articles.title: Xbox aurait réclamé 800 millions de dollars à Netflix pour adapter ses jeux en films et séries
articles.text:
Netflix aurait proposé 500 millions de dollars pour exploiter les personnages les plus populaires de Xbox pendant sept ans, avec une exclusivité sur ses films et séries. Microsoft en aurait demandé 300 millions de plus, et les négociations auraient finalement échoué.
Les adaptations de jeux vidéo séduisent de plus en plus les plateformes de streaming : The Last of Us sur HBO, Fallout sur Prime Video ou encore Arcane sur Netflix. Mais obtenir les droits des licences les plus convoitées peut souvent coûter cher. Selon une enquête de Puck, Netflix aurait ainsi proposé un accord de sept ans à Xbox pour adapter ses personnages emblématiques en films et en séries. Les deux entreprises ne seraient toutefois pas parvenues à s’entendre sur le montant.
Netflix et Xbox n’auraient pas trouvé d’accord sur le prix
D’après trois sources proches du dossier citées par Puck, Netflix aurait mis 500 millions de dollars sur la table pour obtenir les droits d’exploitation des propriétés intellectuelles de Xbox pendant sept ans. L’accord prévoyait une exclusivité sur la plateforme pour les productions concernées. Microsoft aurait cependant réclamé 800 millions de dollars, soit 300 millions de plus que l’offre initiale de Netflix.
Les discussions n’auraient finalement pas abouti. Si Netflix n’a pas souhaité commenter ces informations auprès de Puck, de son côté, Xbox a confirmé avoir reçu un intérêt important pour ses licences, sans donner de détails sur les négociations avec la plateforme de streaming.
« Nous avons reçu un intérêt sans précédent pour nos propriétés intellectuelles », a déclaré l’entreprise, qui qualifie Netflix de « partenaire de confiance ». Xbox indique également attendre avec enthousiasme la sortie prochaine de ses séries animées Minecraft et Diablo, ainsi que d’autres adaptations réalisées avec la plateforme.
Xbox privilégierait désormais plusieurs accords
Plutôt que de confier ses personnages à un seul partenaire dans le cadre d’un contrat global et exclusif, Xbox chercherait maintenant à conclure des accords plus modestes avec plusieurs acteurs. La firme de Redmond aurait d’ailleurs finalement abandonné son projet de partenariat unique envisagé avec Netflix.
Par le passé, Microsoft a déjà travaillé avec Paramount sur l’adaptation en prises de vues réelles de la licence Halo. Lancée en 2022, la série a eu droit à une deuxième saison en février 2024, avant son annulation en juillet de la même année.
Netflix a quant à elle multiplié les adaptations issues du jeu vidéo ces dernières années. Parmi elles, Arcane (League of Legends), Castlevania, Tomb Raider ou encore Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, qui compte parmi les productions les plus réussies de la plateforme. Netflix prépare également un film adapté de Gears of War, l’une des licences phares de l’écosystème Xbox.

articles.title: The VZMORE AX9 Max AI is a stylish AI-ready mini PC with a hefty price tag
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
At the top end of standard form-factor mini PCs, the AX9 Max, with its Ferrari-styled logo, it promises speed, luxury, and exceptional performance. Sure enough, the full metal casing, powerful processing engines, and detailing all add up. It features AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 graphics and a dedicated NPU to maximise its AI potential. SSD and RAM upgrades also offer plenty of flexibility, so the platform can expand with your needs. However, if you want it to meet its full potential, then that comes at a hefty price.
Reasons to buy
- + Excellent CPU benchmark performance.
- + Fast SSD performance.
- + Plenty of connectivity options.
Reasons to avoid
- - Premium pricing.
- - Integrated graphics limit demanding GPU workloads.
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
VZMORE AX9 Max AI: 30-second review
The AX9 Max instantly feels premium, with a full metal build and a huge array of ports on the front and back. However, as you look closely at the embossed detailing around the edges and a logo that seems to blend the old Cadillac and Ferrari logos, something about the aesthetics starts to looks a little less premium.
Aesthetics aside, the build quality is solid enough and well finished, with the most impressive aspect being the sheer volume of ports that have been fitted around the exterior. On the front, there’s a selection of USB Type-A ports and the usual headphone jack; around the back, there are even more connectivity options, including two USB4 ports.
To handle the potential power draw of the devices you can hook up to the box, it packs a powerful AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 processor which is supplied with the 120W power supply. The processor is relatively new, launched at the start of 2026, so it has had a good amount of time to bed in and now has a proven track record. This is supported by an integrated GPU and a dedicated NPU for all those new AI workloads.
As the test progressed, the machine's speed in Microsoft Office apps and the Adobe Creative Suite highlighted its potential. During video editing, the internal SSD kept pace with high-resolution edits without issue. However, a little more headroom on the 1TB capacity would have been beneficial.
Storage and RAM are the two interesting points of this machine. While both are modest in my review sample, maxing them out could turn this from a powerful mini PC into something that will hold great interest for anyone looking to run offline AI and larger LLMs, although that potential does come at a huge monetry cost.
Throughout the test, the creative applications and handling of video and image files were limited by the 32GB of RAM and 1TB SSD. However, with two USB4 ports, I could at least boost the storage capacity. For most HD and 4K edits, the machine handled rough cuts and transitions in Premiere Pro quickly and without issue, though more RAM would have helped.
The most interesting test was running LM Studio and a few local models; while general performance was good, especially for models that utilised the NPU, I could see where the 32GB RAM limit restricted what the machine could potentially do, limiting it as the best mini PC specifically for AI workloads.

For gaming, at mid settings in most games like Cyberpunk 2077 and Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, the machine was more than capable of supplying the power needed for the action. However, again, a little more RAM would have smoothed some of the minor slowdowns in gameplay, especially in Cyberpunk 2077 where quality settings had to be lowered.
This is a machine with potential, and while undoubtedly expensive for a mini PC with a 1TB SSD and 32GB RAM, that money is invested in that powerful CPU, GPU and NPU combo and the ability to expand the storage to a far greater degree than I have seen on the vast majority of other mini PCs of this size and type.
VZMORE AX9 Max AI: Price and availability
- How much does it cost? From $1,349
- When is it out? Available now
- Where can you get it? Directly from VZMore and online retailers.
At present, the UK price is £1,349 for the 32GB RAM and 1TB SSD configuration I’m looking at in this review.
At the time of review, the US site is down (maybe it's just me?), however, it's available on Amazon for $1,399.
- Value: 4 / 5
VZMORE AX9 Max AI: Specs
Processor: AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 470
Graphics: AMD Radeon 890M
NPU: AMD Ryzen AI, up to 55 TOPS
Memory: 32GB DDR5
Storage: 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD
Operating System: Windows 11 Pro
Front ports: 5 × USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A, 3.5mm Audio
Rear ports: 2 × USB4, USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A, USB 2.0 Type-A, 2 × HDMI 2.1, 2 × 2.5Gb Ethernet
Wireless: Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4
Card Reader: SD 4.0
Power Modes: Silent 45W, Balanced 54W, Performance 65W
Dimensions: Approx. 134.9 × 131.8 × 57.7mm
Weight: 777.5g
Power Adapter: 120W
VZMORE AX9 Max AI: Design
Unpacking the compact AX9 Max, the metal casing and detailed plastic base of this mini PC instantly reinforced its price point. Only after carefully checking the detailing and the large, shiny logo on top did I start to question whether this was a premium machine or just one trying to look premium.
Checking the specifications and that the price point was justified, but there’s still something about the design that feels a little over the top. The rest of the design is solid, and at 134.9 × 131.8 × 57.7mm and 777.5g, it’s a great size and weight for this style of machine.
Around the casing, there are four USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A ports and a 3.5mm stereo headphone jack. On the left side of the casing is an SD 4.0 memory card slot, while the back has two USB4 Type-C ports, a USB 2.0 port, two HDMI 2.1 ports, two 2.5Gb RJ45 sockets, a USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A port, and the DC-in port.
Despite the number of ports, they’re well laid out, and testing with multiple accessories, SSDs, and other card readers showed the port selection offered enough space to easily plug in and remove cables when needed.
You access the inner workings of the mini PC through the base, and while it's designed to be upgraded, initial access proved tricky, but only because of the four small rubber plugs covering the screw holes.
Once these are removed, removing the base is easy, and thankfully there are no easily detachable wires to get in the way of speedy progress.
- Design: 4 / 5
VZMORE AX9 Max AI: Features
The aesthetics of this machine are quite run-of-the-mill despite the premium metal build. However, as I checked the specifications, I found plenty that’s quite exciting. First, it features the AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 with 12 cores and 24 threads, plus Radeon 890M integrated graphics. That’s a powerful combo, especially with the dedicated NPU rated at 55 TOPS.
To keep up with this processing power, the machine has a substantial cooling system; flip it over, and the base design suddenly makes sense, as it, along with the huge venting on the back, is designed to keep the machine cool.
VZMORE has its own cooling system called V-Cooling, which uses a vapour chamber and a 360º air intake on the base, and the company claims it provides 65W of sustained TDP output while keeping things quiet. In testing, this claim held up: the cooling seemed effective and quiet for the most part until it was put under heavy load and even then while the fans are audible they’re still well managed.
As mini PCs go, one of the first notable features is the sheer volume of ports across the body. This is far more than most, with wireless connection options including Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4.
There are also three selectable power modes, including 45W Silent mode, 54W Balanced and 65W Performance. Through this test, I turned it to Performance mode.
This machine is aimed at creatives, those looking to use AI and gamers- all high-demand applications. As I reviewed the specifications, a couple of points stood out. First, the internal SSD was limited to 1TB in the review sample, and given the machine's price, I expected at least 2TB.
The other point is that the SSD is PCIe Gen 4 x4, which still provides plenty of speed, as I saw in the benchmarks, but I would have expected an upgrade to PCIe Gen 5. The other point is that there are two M.2 slots: one pre-installed with an M.2 2280 module and one M.2 2230, slot that can only take up to 1TB. That’s still 5TB in a relatively small box, but for this price, I would have expected a little more.
the main point here is that CPU, GPU and NPU combo is an expensive choice and that’s what you’re paying for here.
Then comes the real surprise, the RAM. This is 32GB of DDR5 SO-DIMM, split into dual-channel. That in itself isn't unusual, but since AI is one of the machine's key selling points, this 32GB can be upgraded to 256GB. However, at the time of writing, the most that I could find was 128GB in two 64GB modules for the cool price of £1,999. This could be possible, but would you really want it?
In this test, I’ve run Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B through LM Studio.
- Features: 4 / 5
VZMORE AX9 Max AI: Performance
CrystalDiskMark Read: 6047.65MB/s 
CrystalDiskMark Write: 5058.87MB/s 
Geekbench 6 CPU Multi: 15845 
Geekbench 6 CPU Single: 2997 
Geekbench 6 GPU: 44325 
Geekbench 7 CPU Multi: 17377 
Geekbench 7 CPU Single: 2723 
Geekbench 7 GPU: 35288 
PCMark Overall: 8910 
Cinebench R23 CPU Multi (Threads): 21568 
Cinebench R23 CPU Single (Threads): 2076 
Cinebench 2026 CPU Multi (Threads): 5074 
Cinebench 2026 CPU Single (Threads): 493 
Fire Strike Overall: 9027 
Fire Strike Graphics: 9842 
Fire Strike Physics: 32446 
Fire Strike Combined: 3340 
Time Spy Overall: 4275 
Time Spy Graphics: 3857 
Time Spy CPU: 11109 
Wild Life Overall: 24408 
Steel Nomad Overall: 770 
Windows Experience Overall: 8.2 
Procyon: 1179
The machine arrives with Windows 11 Pro pre-installed and only needs the final steps of the installation to be completed. However, this takes a good 10–15 minutes, rejecting each of the many packages on offer. Once in, Windows 11 Pro runs smoothly, and the Microsoft Office suite is fast, as is interaction with Windows as a whole. Word, Excel, and PowerPoint are all well within its capabilities.
Moving on to Photoshop and Lightroom, the machine's power is evident, but the limits of 32GB of RAM are quickly apparent. The applications load quickly, and photos load into Photoshop and Lightroom are easily adjusted. It’s only when I do batch updates in Lightroom or select files in Adobe Bridge that I started to notice the limitations. On a machine at this price, I really expected a little more performance, and checking the Device Monitor showed the RAM topping out.
Again, loading Premiere Pro and some HD and 4K video, the initial HD footage ran smoothly, with the AX9 Max handling the video files with ease. 4K video was handled just as well, but again, RAM limits meant that as the edit grew more complex, it was best to give the machine a few seconds to catch up with the renders. Still, a good 5-minute 4K edit is well within the limits, and again it’s the RAM that holds the machine back. Another point was that I needed to connect an external SSD to one of the USB4 ports because of limited storage.
Overall, the machine is exceptional for heavy office use and more than able to keep up with the demands. What stood out was how easy it was to connect multiple accessories and screens, thanks to the port support around the case.
For creative applications, the machine performed well and handled most task with relative ease, although I would definitely boost the RAM to 64GB for video work.
To really test the machine’s potential, I loaded Indiana Jones and the Great Circle and was pleased to see that, with settings at moderate, it was more than capable of delivering smooth gameplay and stunning graphics. However, when I switched to Cyberpunk 2077, the gameplay faltered, and I had to dig into the settings and dial everything back to near-base levels to get the smooth gameplay I prefer.
The final test was to run a few LLMs locally and run a series of tests on the machine. The results here were mixed as I switched between two models, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B. On the initial run, I noticed that as the five tests I ran, technical writing, programming, reasoning, image understanding, and review analysis, became more intensive, the machine slowed down and the available RAM maxed out.
Using the installed models in LM Studio provided decent performance, with the chat flowing easily and responses coming back relatively quickly, in 2 to 5 seconds. However, as complexity rose, so did processing times and machine noise.
First, with every request, RAM maxed out between 95% and 99%, leaving little, if any, headroom for the machine to do anything else. The first test, writing a short 200-word technical piece with the Qwen model, took 4.38 seconds to get the first response, at 19.1 tokens per second, requiring 5920 output tokens, for a total run time of 316.7 seconds. Far slower than online models, but still all done completely offline.
Less complex models completed this task far faster, with less finesse in the wording.
Running a Python coding task to read and organise a folder of image files, again using the Qwen model, maxed out the machine across the board, with the fans kicking in to keep things cool. Time to first token was just over 1 second, with 18.84 tokens per second; 7653 output tokens took 407.36 seconds to complete the task. This was more impressive as the folder contained 2,764 images. The Python script could then be run to create a CSV file containing the file information. This is base-level organisation.
As I started pushing more complex image-analysis models, the machine's limits were hit, with processing times running in excess of ten minutes, mainly due to limited RAM.
However, the local LLMs available in LM Studio are surprisingly good, but they aren’t a replacement for online or higher-end models.
- Performance: 4 / 5
VZMORE AX9 Max AI: Final verdict
The VZMORE AX9 Max AI Mini PC is a powerful mini PC with plenty of potential and a premium build. The aesthetics and large logo on top feel a little out of place for a machine at this price and for its intended audience; I usually associate that type of styling with entry-level models.
It is undoubtedly a powerful machine with a CPU, GPU and NPU that make light work of most Copilot and app-initiated AI tasks, and even with 32GB of RAM, it handles all office and most creative tasks without issue. What surprised me was that it struggled with some AI processing through LM Studio, with longer-than-expected processing times because the 32GB limit pushed the RAM to near 100% for extended periods.
Likewise, while most games played back smoothly, Cyberpunk 2077 struggled with the graphics, and the quality options and resolution had to be dropped to get smooth gameplay. Other games, such as Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, played well.
Creative use was also mixed, again held back by that 32GB of RAM, which topped out in Premiere Pro, causing slight slowdowns when editing 4K Log footage. Editing standard 4K and HD was fast, though I still needed to attach an external SSD to expand storage.
The point is that the machine supports up to 256GB of RAM, far more than I’ve seen in any other mini PC. However, as I couldn’t find 128GB modules in the UK, and the maximum available at this time is 2 × 64GB, costing between £1,500 and £2,000, this value seems to be theoretical rather than a reality.
As it is, this is a powerful mini PC, but while it offers upgrade options and plenty of connectivity, it feels like it overpromises; to reach its full potential, you’ll need to invest more in upgrades. At present what makes this machine the price it is, is that CPU, and in order for you to see it’s full potential this machine needs far more investment.
Should I buy the VZMORE AX9 Max AI?
| Value | This mini PC sits at the top of the premium mini PC price range, and I would have expected more RAM and a larger-capacity SSD | 4 | 
| Design | Initial impressions of the build and materials are good, but some of the styling is a little over the top. | 4 | 
| Features | The feature set is impressive, but it feels like it supports potential rather than out-of-the-box performance. | 4 | 
| Performance | In general use, this small box packs in performance, but without a major investment, it’s still a long way from its full potential. | 4 | 
| Overall | A decent enough premium mini PC with plenty of potential if you’re willing to invest. | 4 | 
Buy it if...
You need a compact PC with CPU performance.
The AMD CPU, GPU and NPU combine to offer impressive performance across the board.
You need high-speed external connectivity.
With dual USB4 and LAN, you get plenty of fast and standard connectivity options.
Don't buy it if...
You need a dedicated GPU for demanding graphics or 3D workloads.
The USB4 port lets you connect to an eGPU, but if you need that processing contained in this small box, this won’t be the solution.
You need local AI performance.
To reach its potential, you’ll need to invest in additional RAM, which is incredibly expensive.
For more professional-grade desktops, we've tested the best business computers.
Alastair is a photographer, filmmaker and tech writer who has been working in the publishing industry since the late 1990s. For more than 25 years he has covered photography, video and technology across Future's photography, technology and gaming brands. He runs a photography and video production company and lectures in TV and film. He can usually be found testing mini PCs or prototyping and prop building with the aid of 3D printing.

articles.title: The Frontier X2 heart rate monitor is accurate, useful, and might even replace your Fitbit entirely
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Frontier X2 from Fourth Frontier is a very good heart rate monitor. It’s accurate, providing a continuous ECG functionality through its electrodes and matching readings from top-of-the-range wrist-based wearables, just like the Polar H10. The screen and physical button are incredibly helpful when it comes to making sure the device is on and connected, a constant pain point for some puck-based heart rate monitor users. Its premium price will put many users off, but those who shell out will reap the rewards.
Reasons to buy
- + Highly accurate HR compared to other wearables
- + ECG livestream functionality super useful
- + Screen and tactile button enormously helpful
- + Rechargeable
Reasons to avoid
- - No ANT+
- - Very premium price tag
- - Some features locked behind subscription paywall
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Frontier X2: One minute review
While the Polar H10 chest strap is used by athletes the world over as a heart rate monitor accuracy benchmark, one of its biggest pain points can be its connectivity issues. It’s hard to know whether it’s going to drop out, or you need to replace or clean the strap, until you actually start a workout. There’s also no interface or control on the heart rate monitor itself, and the app is cluttered and outdated. I like using the Polar H10 for its accuracy, but when it doesn’t work for me, it’s not always obvious until after the fact — which, when testing multiple devices simultaneously, is a frustrating experience.
Frontier X2 from Fourth Frontier offers a different chest strap experience: a more modern app and a USB-chargeable device, with a screen and a button allowing you to manually start a workout and receive haptic feedback. That haptic feedback also triggers when you cross heart rate zone thresholds.While you can’t view the screen while wearing it on your chest of course, it does make workout preparation and phone connection so much easier than Polar’s offering. Guessing the heart rate monitor is working, even checking your phone to make sure heart rate is streaming correctly, only to have it drop out halfway through and lose my data due to a poor connection or crap strap, is an experience I’d like to leave in the past.
The Frontier X2 uses heart rate information to calculate Whoop-style metrics like a Strain score, Stress score, Heart Rate Variability (HRV), Breathing Rate, and estimates calories burned. That last metric is somewhat outdated, as research from Stanford University found that calorie estimates based on heart rate are unreliable as they measure effort rather than energy expended. A premium tier subscription costs an additional $119.99 / £109.99 per year, adding a Readiness score, VO2 Max and even sleep stage analysis. As an already-expensive device, I wouldn’t recommend this unless you’re planning to make Frontier X2 your privacy fitness tracker, and accuracy is hyper-important to you.
The continuous electrocardiogram, or ECG, can livestream an ECG scan for yourself or a medical professional to the Frontier app. Not only is this useful for spotting irregular heart rate rhythms over time, but I most often used it to check the HRM is streaming data correctly before starting working out in earnest, which is recommended, as the scan flags up in the app if there’s insufficient data due to poor connection.
In terms of accuracy, I had no complaints. I took it for a test run against the Apple Watch Ultra 4 (which offers a redesigned Health Sensing System said to be ‘the most accurate ever on a wearable’) and the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro, which uses Garmin’s Elevate V5 that I’ve already tested against the Polar H10 and found to be very accurate.
The results of the Frontier X2’s test run were excellent, with just 2 bpm separating the Frontier X2 from the Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Garmin Fenix 9 Pro’s average heart rate readings, a clear indication that all three devices are telling the same story about my body, and thus all three are very likely to be accurate. After some more solo runs and workouts, I feel like I could certainly recommend the Frontier X2, if you don’t mind paying the hefty premium price.
Frontier X2: Price and availability
- $599 / £449 / AU$775
- Very expensive for a HRM
- Not competitively priced compared to the industry standard
The Frontier X2 can be found on storefronts like Amazon for $599 in the US and £449 in the UK. In Australia, it’s more difficult to locate, but Selfridges’ AU storefront lists it for AU$775. The optional subscription for premium features on top is tough to swallow at this price.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
This is a lot for a device that fundamentally only measures heart rate, and although the Frontier X app can interpret strain, readiness, training load, specific workout profiles and other metrics, it’s still a lot to ask for compared to the $89.95 / £79.50 / AU$139 Polar H10.
However, it does address quite a few of Polar’s pain points, notably including a micro-USB charger rather than a replaceable coin battery, and a screen for an easier indicator of connection. The continuous ECG is a nice touch too, offering a way to test the monitor’s connection in addition to providing reliable ECG data for a medical professional. All in all, it’s an excellent package, but I wouldn’t call it excellent value.
- Value score: 3.5/5
Frontier X2: Specifications
| Component | Frontier X2 | 
| Dimensions | 73mm x 24mm x 13mm | 
| Weight | 25g without strap | 
| Case material | Plastic | 
| Connectivity | Bluetooth | 
| Water resistance | IP67 | 
| Accelerometer | Yes | 
| Battery | 14 days typical usage | 
Frontier X2: Scorecard
| Category | Comment | Score | 
| Value | A premium product with more to recommend it over Polar, but not enough to stretch your budget. | 3.5/5 | 
| Design | So many pain points addressed. | 4.5/5 | 
| Features | More than most HRMs, but limited. | 4/5 | 
| Performance | Accurate and reliable with little friction. | 4.5/5 | 
Frontier X2: Should I buy?
Buy it if…
You want the best heart rate monitor
If money is no object, the Frontier X2 won’t let you down.
You want a rechargeable battery
Don’t want to faff around with coin batteries? The Frontier X2 uses standardised micro-USB.
You want ECG
The Frontier X2 is as good for people watching their heart health as it is for serious athletes.
Don’t buy it if…
You’re running a triathlon
The Frontier X2 isn’t for use in saline water.
You’re on a budget
Just get a Polar H10 instead, although you’ll have to put up with its app and the odd connection dropout.
Also consider
Coros Heart Rate Monitor
While not electrical, but optical like a smartwatch, this arm-mounted HRM performed incredibly well during testing.
Read our full Coros Heart Rate Monitor review
How I tested
I took the Frontier X2 on test runs, gym sessions and meditations, draining the battery down and wearing it consistently. I used its continuous ECG functionality, compared its in-app metrics to competitor wearables, and cleaned the band after each use.
First reviewed: October 2026
Matt is TechRadar's expert on all things fitness, wellness and wearable tech.
A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.
He is the author of the upcoming book The Health Data Heist, set to be published by Bloomsbury in 2027. When he’s not training or writing about health and fitness, he can be found reading doorstop-thick fantasy books with lots of fictional maps in them.

articles.title: Après les réseaux sociaux, les affiches générées par IA envahissent nos villes et la riposte s’organise
articles.text:
Les comités des fêtes et les petits commerces ont confié cet été à des générateurs d’images leurs annonces de vide-greniers et leurs menus, reconnaissables entre mille par leurs ressemblances. Quelques mairies tentent maintenant de freiner le mouvement avec leurs panneaux d’affichage et l’argent qu’elles versent aux associations, sans toujours montrer l’exemple.
À Igny-Comblizy, dans la Marne, la secrétaire du comité des fêtes ne regrette rien. « C’est efficace », a-t-elle confié à la presse régionale, en admettant qu’elle obtient rarement le bon résultat à la première tentative. Dans la Manche, la responsable d’une friperie associative se félicite de produire des affiches colorées, là où sa structure se contentait auparavant d’une publication sur les réseaux sociaux. Ces bénévoles ne retirent rien à un graphiste. Sans budget de communication, ils fabriquaient leurs affiches sur un traitement de texte, ou se passaient d’affiche.
Les générateurs d’images gratuits ont changé cette équation. Une phrase tapée sur un téléphone donne un visuel coloré, avec le titre de l’événement intégré à l’image. Terence Renaudeau, patron du restaurant Le Cercle à Brétignolles-sur-Mer, en Vendée, fabrique ses menus et ses annonces avec la version payante de ChatGPT. Avant, il dessinait ses visuels sur Canva sans jamais faire appel à un graphiste, et l’argent économisé l’aide à garder son établissement ouvert toute l’année et à payer une salariée en CDD chargée des réseaux sociaux.
Le défaut de ces affiches tient moins aux mains à six doigts qu’à leur ressemblance. Selon Alberto Romele, maître de conférences à la Sorbonne Nouvelle, cette esthétique lisse est due aux banques d’images qui ont servi à entraîner les modèles. Le graphiste Thomas Prouvost, fondateur de l’agence Les Lunettes créatives à Féron, dans le Nord, retrouve sur chaque affiche générée des compositions et des effets identiques, qu’elle annonce une brocante ou un cabinet dentaire. À ses yeux, une affiche doit répondre au besoin précis de son commanditaire.
De retour d’un voyage en van sur la côte Atlantique, Léa Pixels avait vu trop de flyers générés dans les rues et les magasins. Le 25 août, cette dessinatrice messine a dessiné sur Instagram deux personnages décidés à bouder tout événement dont l’affiche sort d’une IA. Son dessin a dépassé 1,2 million de vues en trois jours, d’après Le Monde Pixels. Les internautes dénoncent désormais des images bien réelles, collées sur des vitrines et parfois sur les panneaux des mairies. Les associations gagnent du temps et de l’argent, les graphistes perdent des commandes, et des élus découvrent qu’ils peuvent freiner le mouvement autant qu’ils l’ont nourri.
Une affiche gratuite en deux minutes, l’argument des petites structures
À Igny-Comblizy, dans la Marne, la secrétaire du comité des fêtes ne regrette rien. « C’est efficace », a-t-elle confié à la presse régionale, en admettant qu’elle obtient rarement le bon résultat à la première tentative. Dans la Manche, la responsable d’une friperie associative se félicite de produire des affiches colorées, là où sa structure se contentait auparavant d’une publication sur les réseaux sociaux. Ces bénévoles ne retirent rien à un graphiste. Sans budget de communication, ils fabriquaient leurs affiches sur un traitement de texte, ou se passaient d’affiche.
Les générateurs d’images gratuits ont changé cette équation. Une phrase tapée sur un téléphone donne un visuel coloré, avec le titre de l’événement intégré à l’image. Terence Renaudeau, patron du restaurant Le Cercle à Brétignolles-sur-Mer, en Vendée, fabrique ses menus et ses annonces avec la version payante de ChatGPT. Avant, il dessinait ses visuels sur Canva sans jamais faire appel à un graphiste, et l’argent économisé l’aide à garder son établissement ouvert toute l’année et à payer une salariée en CDD chargée des réseaux sociaux.
Le défaut de ces affiches tient moins aux mains à six doigts qu’à leur ressemblance. Selon Alberto Romele, maître de conférences à la Sorbonne Nouvelle, cette esthétique lisse est due aux banques d’images qui ont servi à entraîner les modèles. Le graphiste Thomas Prouvost, fondateur de l’agence Les Lunettes créatives à Féron, dans le Nord, retrouve sur chaque affiche générée des compositions et des effets identiques, qu’elle annonce une brocante ou un cabinet dentaire. À ses yeux, une affiche doit répondre au besoin précis de son commanditaire.
Les graphistes voient fondre les petites commandes
Thomas Prouvost a publié à la mi-juin une vidéo vue plus de 4 millions de fois. « On vit la pire époque du design », lance-t-il dès les premières secondes. Il ne pense pas avoir perdu de contrats à cause de l’IA, mais il observe un fossé entre deux familles de clients, ceux qui soignent leur image et ceux qui veulent un visuel rapide et gratuit.
Les graphistes installés en dehors des grandes villes ressentent plus nettement la seconde catégorie. Marie Corbel, graphiste à Lachapelle depuis bientôt dix-sept ans, reçoit des clients qui arrivent avec une image générée, trop pixélisée pour habiller un camion. Son travail se limite alors à reprendre l’image d’un autre, et elle a le sentiment de n’être plus qu’une exécutante, a-t-elle confié à Sud Ouest. Sa consœur marmandaise Mélanie Duprat accepte en revanche que les associations sans budget se débrouillent seules, et sent chez ses clients une envie d’originalité après un été saturé d’affiches générées.
L’illustratrice strasbourgeoise Clémence Dupont a vu baisser depuis trois ans les commandes ponctuelles des festivals et des médiathèques. Certains clients lui apportent même des images générées à partir de ses dessins, et elle se sent « dépossédée de mon travail artistique », a-t-elle raconté au Blog du Modérateur. Le Conseil supérieur de la propriété littéraire et artistique, rattaché au ministère de la Culture, admet que les règles actuelles ne garantissent pas assez l’autorisation et la rémunération des auteurs dont les œuvres nourrissent ces modèles.
À Rouen, la colère est passée de la plainte individuelle à la mobilisation. Un illustrateur a repéré à l’automne 2025 des personnages déformés et des perspectives incohérentes sur l’affiche de Rouen givrée, les festivités de fin d’année de la ville. La directrice de la communication, Karine Divernet, parle aujourd’hui d’un simple test. Une quarantaine d’artistes réunis dans le collectif Autrices & Auteurs Rouen ont écrit au maire, Nicolas Mayer-Rossignol, puis rencontré les services de la Ville et de la Métropole en février et en juin 2026. Les deux collectivités préparent depuis une charte interne destinée à écarter l’IA générative de leurs visuels, mais le texte n’était toujours pas adopté début octobre.
Sète, Vallorcine, Strasbourg et Agde, quatre réponses très différentes
Hervé Marquès, maire de Sète, a annoncé début octobre que la ville ne relaierait plus sur ses supports de communication les visuels associatifs entièrement générés par IA. L’élu refuse de diffuser « des images sans histoire, sans âme, sans une touche d’humanité ». La mairie continuera d’imprimer gratuitement les affiches et les flyers des associations, soit près de 200 000 impressions par an, et accepte un recours partiel à l’IA, pour trouver une idée ou compléter une illustration. Une association sétoise garde donc le droit de coller une affiche entièrement générée chez un commerçant, mais elle ne profitera plus de la communication municipale.
La commune de Vallorcine, en Haute-Savoie, frappe au portefeuille. Dans ce village d’environ 400 habitants, les associations devront signer une charte avant de toucher leur aide. La mairie interdit dans ce texte les propos racistes ou sexistes, et le recours à l’IA pour organiser ou promouvoir un événement, sous peine de suspendre la subvention. « Nous subventionnons les êtres humains et leur travail, et non celui des machines », justifie la municipalité, qui examinera les prochaines demandes au printemps 2027. Le bénévole qui fabriquait son affiche en deux minutes devra alors payer un graphiste ou dessiner à la main, et une petite association devra trouver de l’argent ou des heures de bénévolat en plus.
Strasbourg a vécu l’inverse, avec une mairie prise en défaut en plein festival des Rencontres de l’illustration. Pour l’affiche du carnaval 2026, l’agence Welcome Byzance avait proposé trois pistes, dont deux produites par IA, et la direction de la communication a retenu l’une d’elles faute de budget. Un nouveau visuel IA signé Welcome Byzance a relancé la polémique au printemps. Pierre Jakubowicz, adjoint chargé de la culture, refuse depuis dans ses services l’usage d’« un outil qui nuit à l’écosystème de la création », a-t-il expliqué à Pokaa. Le carnaval relève toutefois d’un autre service, et l’élu travaille à étendre ce refus à toute la collectivité.
À Agde, les habitants ont reproché à la mairie un tout autre défaut. Dans son magazine du 31 juillet, puis à l’entrée des plages, la commune a diffusé une image générée de trois hommes autour d’un narguilé, avec le slogan « Ta chicha et ta musique, on n’en veut pas ! ». Accusée de stigmatiser des jeunes d’origine maghrébine, la municipalité a retiré les affichettes et les a remplacées par le texte de l’arrêté municipal, qui interdit les chichas sur le sable depuis 2014. Ici, l’outil n’a pris le travail d’aucun artiste. Il a fourni en quelques secondes un cliché que personne à la mairie n’a corrigé.
À Saumur, six illustrateurs ont eu carte blanche
Le service communication de Saumur a pris le chemin inverse, sans rien interdire. Il a confié tout l’été la rue Molière à six illustrateurs, libres de représenter la ville à leur manière sur des panneaux grand format. Toutes les œuvres de l’exposition « Saumur par » ont été réalisées sans IA générative. Valentine Halbert, apprentie au service communication et exposée parmi les six, a vu dans le projet l’occasion de « redonner de la valeur à la création humaine », selon le Kiosque saumurois.
Une mairie dispose ainsi de deux leviers à sa portée, ses commandes et ses panneaux. Bruxelles impose peu de transparence aux affiches de quartier. Avec l’article 50 de l’AI Act, applicable depuis le 2 août, les éditeurs de générateurs d’images doivent marquer leurs créations d’un signal lisible par les machines. Les associations n’ont en revanche aucune mention à apposer sur une affiche de vide-greniers, sauf si l’image fait passer une scène inventée pour réelle. Devant une vitrine, les passants doivent encore compter sur leur œil pour repérer une affiche sortie d’un générateur.

articles.title: I’ve driven this miniature Porsche 550 — and the 80%-scale Spyder tribute is exactly as fun as it looks
articles.text:
I've driven the tiny, electrified Hedley Studios Porsche 550 J — and this miniature motorsport legend is exactly as fun as it looks
It might only be to 80% scale but it's 100% hilarious to drive
There has been an increase in demand for compact electric vehicles as city streets get more congested and drivers feel the urge to move away from bloated, heavy SUVs that don’t fit in with daily life.
But Hedley Studios, formerly known as the Little Car Company, has taken this thinking one step further — dedicating its life to producing perfect miniaturized replicas of some of the most famous and sought-after cars on the planet.
Far from simply being a purveyor of toys for kids who never grow up, the company says it stands at the “intersection between art and automotive excellence,” crafting hand-built, electrified interpretations of the Bentley Blower, a 75% scale iteration of the Bugatti Type 35, and a baby Bond Aston Martin DB5, to name but a few.
Now, the British company has signed up its sixth official partner in Porsche, and it has turned its hand to arguably one of the most iconic models in its back catalog: the 550 Spyder.
Shaped like a silver speeding bullet, the 1950s roadster took a class win at Le Mans, dominated Italy’s infamous Targa Florio, and, sadly, became the last car Hollywood megastar James Dean ever drove.
Parking “Little Bastard” for the time being, the Hedley Studios 550 J (the ‘J’ standing for junior) is a 2.9m-long and 1.2m-wide, 80% scale interpretation of a 550 Spyder and 550A that swaps a raspy 1.5-liter four-cylinder boxer engine for a 48-volt electric powertrain producing 8kW (11 hp) in the standard version and 16kW (21 hp) with the optional RS Pack selected.
Oh, the car is limited to just 250 units, and prices start at £69,500 (around $95,000 / AU$135,000), making it more expensive than many adult-size Porsches.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
To question why is almost missing the point, as Hedley Studios boss Ben Hedley tells me that most of the owners of the original multimillion-dollar Porsche 550 Spyders have already been in contact to carefully personalize their miniature interpretations.
A personal project
We’ve already established that anything coming out of Hedley Studios most definitely isn’t for children, with the company’s owner revealing that most of the time, his creations never actually get driven and serve only to look good next to Damien Hirsts and highly collectable classic cars.
Which is a shame, because the effort the team has gone to in order to replicate both the look and feel of the originals is astonishing.
In fact, Porsche allowed the team full access to its very private archives, so engineers could pore over original technical drawings. They even took a 3D scan of an original 550A when designing the chassis.
As a result, carbon-fiber bodywork sits over a steel spaceframe, while Brembo brakes borrowed from a Ducati Diavel motorcycle provide stopping power behind the bespoke 13-inch wheels.
All cars receive adjustable Bilstein coilover dampers, while those teeny wheels are shod with Continental tires also used by the Renault Twizy.
Inside, the 550 J leans heavily on the original car’s motorsport heritage rather than chasing modern digital excess.
A bespoke three-spoke, wood-rimmed Nardi steering wheel, which Ben Hedley says cost an “extortionate” amount of money to design, develop, and produce, sits ahead of a period-correct three-dial instrument panel.
Personalization is key here, with customers able to trim their interiors in whatever material they like, but the RS Pack switches things up to Alcantara, while further personalization options include tan or red leather, navy finishes, and Pepita-inspired upholstery.
Tiny car, enormous fun
Clambering inside the 550 J isn’t exactly the most elegant of exercises, but Hedley Studios has had the foresight to include a removable steering wheel.
Once nestled into the gloriously period-correct interior, it’s a case of inserting a small key, which doubles as the driving mode selector, to power up the 48-volt electric powertrain.
There are Normal, Sport, and Sport+ modes to select from, while the main reverse, neutral, and drive toggle has been lifted directly from a modern electric Porsche.
Organ stops operate the lights, and a race-inspired fly-off hydraulic handbrake prevents it from rolling away.
With just two pedals to contend with, driving the 550 J really is child’s play, but it’s impressive how much it feels like a very small mid-engined sports car.
There’s no wild EV acceleration, but speed builds to a very reasonable 40mph swiftly. Considering the general lack of space, drivers are forced to employ race-inspired left foot braking, which only makes the whole experience feel more sublime.
Cars with the optional RS Pack are even more focused and raise the top speed to 50mph, while it is surprisingly easy to have the rear end gently slide out during the tighter, faster turns. It’s just healthy, analog driving fun.
To be honest, you probably wouldn’t want to be going much faster, although Ben Hedley says many customers have already asked to have speed restrictions lifted, as there have been suggestions of a one-make race series among particularly well-heeled collectors. Sign me up.
But unlike the Hedley Studios Bentley Blower Junior, you can’t drive this pocket-sized Porsche on the road. Let's be real, it’s not going to replace the family runaround anytime soon, is it?
This is the sort of glorious whimsy the world needs right now, and if Santa delivers one to your doorstep this Christmas, you must have been exceptionally well-behaved. Or just have more money than sense.

Currently, EVs are the focus of his attentions, but give it a few years and it will be electric vertical take-off and landing craft. articles.title: MacBook Neo : Apple résiste mieux que ses rivaux à la crise du PC
articles.text:
Le marché du PC décroche, mais Apple parvient à limiter la casse. Alors que les livraisons mondiales ont plongé de 21 % au troisième trimestre 2026, le MacBook Neo aurait aidé la marque à résister bien mieux que ses principaux concurrents.
Le marché mondial du PC traverse définitivement une mauvaise passe. Au troisième trimestre 2026, seuls 57 millions d’ordinateurs ont été livrés, soit 21 % de moins qu’un an plus tôt, selon le dernier rapport de Counterpoint Research publié hier. Pourtant, Apple encaisse le choc mieux que ses concurrents et gagne même des parts de marché. Une performance que le cabinet attribue en partie au MacBook Neo.
Le MacBook Neo aide Apple à gagner des parts de marché
Le géant de Cupertino a livré 5,6 millions de Mac au troisième trimestre, soit un recul de 11 % sur un an. Malgré cette baisse, sa part du marché mondial est passée de 8,7 % à 9,8 %, selon le rapport publié par Counterpoint Research. Le cabinet attribue en partie cette meilleure résistance au MacBook Neo, qui aurait contribué à amortir le repli des livraisons.
Apple se classe ainsi au quatrième rang mondial, derrière Lenovo, HP et Dell, mais devant ASUS. Du côté de la concurrence, la chute est bien plus brutale : Lenovo a vu ses livraisons diminuer de 23 %, HP de 31 % et Dell de 25 %. ASUS limite davantage le recul, avec une baisse de 7 %.
Pour Minsoo Kang, analyste senior chez Counterpoint Research, Apple et ASUS ont mieux résisté que le marché dans son ensemble grâce à « des portefeuilles de produits différenciés et à un positionnement concurrentiel ». Le rapport ne détaille toutefois pas la contribution exacte du MacBook Neo aux résultats d’Apple.
La flambée des composants pèse toujours sur la demande
Le rapport attribue une partie du recul du marché à la hausse du prix de la mémoire et des autres composants. Face à des ordinateurs plus chers, les consommateurs reportent le renouvellement de leur machine, ce qui pèse fatalement sur la demande dans l’ensemble du secteur.
La hausse se mesure déjà dans les prix des composants. Au troisième trimestre 2026, le prix contractuel des modules de mémoire vive DDR4 de 8 Go a augmenté de 24 % par rapport au trimestre précédent. Celui des SSD NVMe de 1 To a progressé de 29 % sur la même période.
La situation ne devrait d’ailleurs pas s’améliorer d’ici la fin de l’année. Le cabinet prévoit une nouvelle hausse des prix de la RAM de 13 % au quatrième trimestre 2026, puis de 15 % au premier trimestre 2027. Les SSD devraient également augmenter de 11 % au dernier trimestre, avant une potentielle stabilisation début 2027.
Source : 9to5Mac

articles.title: FinBursa unveils AI-native platform to streamline private markets operations
articles.text: FinBursa has launched FinBursa 360, an AI-powered platform designed to integrate investment management workflows, deal execution, fundraising and investor relations for private markets firms. Founded in 2024 and co-founded by Ismail Badereldine, a former BlackRock director, FinBursa provides an integrated platform combining investment CRM, deal management, virtual data rooms (VDR), investor onboarding, fundraising and reporting tools for private equity, venture capital, private credit and other investment firms. The newly launched platform features five specialised AI agents and a coordinating orchestrator, enabling firms to analyse deal pipelines, identify potential investors or buyers, support due diligence and generate research insights using data from across their operations. FinBursa 360 allows firms to automate workflows while maintaining human oversight, with AI-generated investor outreach requiring approval before being sent. The platform also supports custom branding and can be deployed within days, according to the company. Press release: FinBursa launches FinBursa 360 – the intelligent front office for private markets, built to run a firm end to end: investment CRM, deal management from origination to execution, virtual data rooms (VDR), fundraising campaign management, investor onboarding, investor reporting, and portals for investors and counterparties, all on one system of record used by both the sell side and the buy side. Until now, a private markets firm's technology has been a mix of legacy systems and disconnected tools. FinBursa resolves this challenge with one system, under one contract, that holds the firm's relationships, deals, documents, and the counterparties it works with, with AI built in by design. "Most private markets firms have spent heavily on AI and say it isn't delivering yet. AI is only as useful as the information it can access and the actions it is permitted to take. For many firms, that information sits in five or six systems," said Ismail Badereldine, co-founder and CEO of FinBursa. "Building or buying an AI layer across those systems is expensive and slow. Every new feature means more integration work, the firm has to keep permissions consistent across all of them, and it needs constant maintenance as each vendor changes its own system. We built FinBursa differently: one system for relationships, deals, and documents, and the investors, buyers, and advisers the firm works with, with AI built in. The orchestrator agent sees the full record and acts within one set of permissions and one audit trail, without another layer of technology to pay for or maintain.” AI Built Into The Platform, Not Wrapped Around It FinBursa's AI comprises five live specialized agents covering relationships, deals from origination to pitch, due diligence and execution, data rooms, fundraising and research – supported by an orchestrator that coordinates them across the firm's record. Rather than operating inside isolated applications, the orchestrator draws on connected information across the firm's front office, including emails and meetings, deal histories, data room activity and questions, fundraising and investor activity, documents, notes, and any pertinent news. It uses this context to answer questions and provide source-backed insights for deal origination, preparation, due diligence, fundraising, and investor relations; and rank daily priorities for the team. A firm can ask the agents to identify investors or buyers suited to a deal. Drawing on previous deals, data room activity, and CRM history, the agents can suggest matches and draft the outreach for the team to review. Nothing is sent without human approval. Built For Where Private Markets Are GoingFinBursa was co-founded by Ismail Badereldine, a former BlackRock director with more than two decades of experience in financial markets and investment technology, including at eFront, alongside investment banking and private markets veterans. Its leadership team has specialized experience building and running the industry's leading institutional platforms. "Private markets are growing and getting more competitive: more investors to serve, more deals to manage, and more data and compliance requirements," said Badereldine. "AI can carry much of that work, but only if it can see the firm's data and act within its permissions. By bringing those capabilities into one system, we are enabling firms of all sizes to move faster and compete more effectively without adding complexity.” Live in Days, Not Months FinBursa 360 can be configured to each firm's workflows and branding, allowing clients to operate under their own brand. Firms can go live in days rather than months. FinBursa is ISO 27001:2022 certified and SOC 2 Type 1 attested.

articles.title: 'The beginning of The Matrix': Unitree is developing an AI system that will let humanoid robots self-improve — and Tesla should be worried
articles.text:
Unitree says its 'self-evolving robots' are the next big leap for humanoids — as Tesla Optimus production ramps up to hit 20,000 robots a week
The robots are (still) coming
It's an exciting time in robotics, with a lot of progress in a short space of time: these machines are getting better and better at carrying out tasks, navigating around the world, and interacting with people, and making fewer and fewer glaring errors.
Across the past few days, we've had big updates from three of the biggest companies in robotics — Unitree, Tesla and Figure — so there's a lot to catch up on when it comes to where these robots are now. The good news is that they'll be tackling the major jobs first: tidying up after us.
Robots, upgraded by robots
The news from Unitree this week (via the South China Morning Post) is that it's developing an AI system that will enable its humanoid robots to effectively improve on their own, without any input from human engineers. This "self-evolving" feedback loop will lead to robots writing their own code and simulations, Unitree says.
"In the past, every robotics engineer had to write code and debug manually, which is relatively inefficient," Unitree founder Wang Xingxing said at an AI conference hosted by his company. "As AI models improve, we expect them to take on more of the planning and iteration, reducing the need for human intervention."
The project has been called Unitree Rehearsal, and while humans will still be involved in terms of providing feedback and assessing performance, the ultimate goal is to make the upgrade process as automated as possible, Wang says. That would in turn accelerate the development of algorithms controlling robots out in the real world.
With that acceleration, Wang says Unitree robots could be cleaning rooms as early as next year. Commenters over on Reddit have been less optimistic about the robot-controlling future looming into view, saying that the move represents "the beginning of The Matrix", where robots are running code that humans don't understand.
Optimus production underway
Over at Tesla, Elon Musk (via Interesting Engineering) says the Optimus robot production lines are now up and running in Fremont, California, after an electric vehicle factory was repurposed. According to Musk, production could be ramped up to some 20,000 robots per week by 2027, though that will require further engineering work.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The news was disclosed as part of the third-quarter 2026 update for Tesla shareholders, and the reports of progress will be encouraging for those who have invested in the company. At the same time, Musk acknowledged that engineers are still working on the robot's design to improve safety and reliability.
Then there's software support, which brings us back to the points Unitree's Wang Xingxing has been making. At the moment, Musk acknowledges, the Optimus robots struggle to complete varied tasks independently — requiring careful coordination between assessing environments, planning movements, and then carrying out those movements and the tasks they're associated with.
Tesla is still riding high on the buzz of its latest Roadster demo, in which the upcoming car performed several demos of flying through the air and accelerating at high speeds. It was impressive stuff, even if there have been multiple questions since about how realistic all of this is (and whether these features will ever appear on a road-ready vehicle).
The roadmap 'completely changed'
Finally, Figure CEO Brett Adcock has shared a recording of his company's latest all-hands meeting online, saying that the roadmap has "completely changed" over the last year. Work is progressing towards Figure's fourth-generation humanoid, while the production run of Figure 03 is now in four figures.
Some of the biggest changes will come in fingertip tracking, which is now down to millimeter-level precision, and gets these robots closer to humans in terms of dexterity. Figure is continuing to collect masses of data through an app called Index, which records human activities to train robots on how to do them — and some 37.5 million videos have now apparently been uploaded to the platform.
Durability upgrades are arriving as well. A Figure 03 bot recently walked for nine days straight on a treadmill at Figure headquarters, the latest evidence that stability is improving over time, and that these humanoids are better at working (or at least exercising) without any human input.
With more training data and constantly updated algorithms, the robots produced by Unitree, Tesla, and Figure are only going to get better — and this time next year, you might even be able to buy one to tidy up after you and do your laundry.

articles.title: Des années que ce n'était plus arrivé : ASUS relance des cartes graphiques estampillées Intel
articles.text:
Il n'est pas encore question de trouver des cartes ASUS/Intel dans les boutiques, mais le revirement reste réel.
Pas moins de cinq ans après sa dernière carte graphique conçue autour d'une puce Intel, voilà qu'ASUS se décide à renouer avec le groupe américain en commercialisant l'ASUS UGen Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB. Un modèle qui n'est toutefois pas destiné au grand public.
En mars 2021, ASUS lançait une carte graphique baptisée DG1-4G. Il s'agissait alors d'un modèle orienté entrée de gamme pour lequel la firme avait retenu le petit GPU Iris Xe d'Intel.
Aucune ambition particulière pour ce modèle qui est toutefois « rentré dans l'histoire » comme signant la dernière collaboration entre ASUS et Intel. Une collaboration qui reprend donc quelque cinq ans plus tard à la faveur du lancement de l'ASUS UGen Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB. Un nom à rallonge pour un modèle finalement assez semblable à la carte de référence Intel.
Au revoir les 80 unités d'exécution et les 4 Go de LPDDR4 de la DG1-4G, la nouvelle carte ASUS embarque le GPU BMG-G31 avec ses 32 cœurs Xe2 et ses 256 unités XMX. Comme son nom l'indique, la nouvelle carte dispose aussi de 32 Go de mémoire vidéo, de la GDDR6 ECC, avec une interface 256-bit.
Nous le disions, autant de caractéristiques parfaitement semblables au modèle de référence d'Intel. D'ailleurs, les fréquences de fonctionnement annoncées par ASUS sont également identiques (2 800 MHz).
Il y a toutefois un « détail » qui pourrait changer pas mal de choses. En effet, ASUS annonce une consommation qui peut grimper jusqu'à 310 W quand les modèles traditionnels sont bloqués à 230 W. Une telle augmentation doit laisser plus de « liberté » au GPU et permettre de maintenir les fréquences de fonctionnement les plus élevées sur de plus longues périodes.
Cela dit, cela ne change finalement pas grand-chose à l'affaire pour nous autres, clients lambda. En effet, ASUS lance une carte graphique, Intel certes, mais surtout dotée de 32 Go. Alors, bien sûr, il n'est pas question de GDDR7, mais même la GDDR6 est onéreuse et il y a donc bien peu de chances que cette carte se retrouve un jour dans votre machine.
ASUS lui-même en parle d'ailleurs comme d'un modèle « PRO » qu'il destine avant à l'intelligence artificielle : « ready for Workstation and AI workload ». Des premiers tarifs évoqués par Wccftech, on peut d'ailleurs conclure que la carte n'est clairement pas faite pour nous : au moins 1 700 dollars, donc sans doute près de 2 000 euros, si elle débarque en France.
Source : Wccftech, VideoCardz

articles.title: Criptomonedas: valor de las principales divisas digitales hoy sábado 24 de octubre
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 80.684,55 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de -0,481% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de -0,339% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 2.376 dólares.
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de 0%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 737,1 dólares, con un cambio de 0,91%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 56.679 dólares, tras una variación de -3.5357509.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,08 dólares tras presentar un cambio de -0,81% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Su avance en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Behind Node.js RCE Also Affects Bun, Python and Other Widely Used Software
articles.text:
A memory-corruption flaw in Google's Brotli decoder sits in many programs that unpack Brotli-compressed data, among them Bun, the Python Brotli and brotlicffi packages, and Envoy proxies set up to decompress Brotli.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, the flaw allows crafted compressed data to overwrite past the end of a buffer and corrupt a program's memory, potentially causing a crash, a memory leak, or the execution of attacker-controlled code.
Imperva researchers have shown that code can run on one unpatched Node.js build. The same has not been demonstrated on the other software, and no real-world attacks have been reported.
The flaw was first disclosed on October 21, when Node.js and Google shipped fixes, and more have followed product by product since. Because the bug is in Google's decoder and each program ships its own copy of it, every one has to update that copy on its own.
Brotli is a compression format from Google, used across the web to shrink pages and other traffic. The bug is in the C code that unpacks a Brotli stream, so it travels into anything that reuses that code, from language runtimes to proxies to Python packages.
Which Software Is Affected
| Product | Affected | Fixed in | Exposed when | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Google Brotli (C library) | 1.0.3 to 1.2.0 | 1.0.10, 1.1.1, 1.2.1 | code decodes untrusted Brotli | 
| Node.js | 22.x, 24.x, 26.x before the fix; 20.x and older (end of life) | 22.23.4, 24.22.1, 26.12.1 | fetch() of a br response, or Express or body-parser br bodies | 
| Bun | 1.4.3 and earlier | 1.4.4 | fetch() of a br response, or node:zlib | 
| Envoy | 1.39.2, 1.38.5, 1.37.7, 1.36.11 | 1.40.0, 1.39.3, 1.38.6, 1.37.8, 1.36.12 | only if the Brotli decompressor is configured | 
| Istio | 1.31.0 to 1.31.1, 1.30.0 to 1.30.5, 1.29.0 to 1.29.8 | 1.31.2, 1.30.6, 1.29.9 | only if Brotli decompression is enabled | 
| Python Brotli | 1.2.0 and earlier | 1.2.1 | installed, and an HTTP client decodes br | 
| Python brotlicffi | 1.2.0.x and earlier | 1.2.1.0 | installed, and an HTTP client decodes br | 
| cdxgen | standalone binaries and images, 13.4.0 and 12.8.8 and earlier | 13.5.0, 12.8.9 | standalone binary or image scanning untrusted input | 
A program is exposed only if it decodes Brotli data that someone else controls. For Node.js and Bun, that happens when the built-in fetch() reads a response sent with Content-Encoding: br, or when request-body code such as Express 5 and body-parser 2 unpacks a Brotli upload. A plain Node.js HTTP server does not decode request bodies on its own.
Envoy and Istio are affected only when Brotli decompression is enabled, for example, through an Envoy filter. Where it is off, the flaw cannot be reached.
In Python, the risk comes from the Brotli or brotlicffi package being installed at all. Once either is present, HTTP clients such as requests, urllib3, httpx, and aiohttp decode Brotli responses on their own, so an application can be exposed without ever importing Brotli in its own code.
A web application firewall helps only so far. Vercel, which added firewall rules on the day of disclosure, said those rules do not cover "responses your functions fetch from other servers." For that path, only updating the runtime or library closes the hole.
How far the flaw can be pushed depends on the software. Imperva's Red Team, which calls its work Node2Shell, ran attacker-supplied code on an unmodified Node.js 24.22.0 build for Linux on ARM64, delivering it both as a fetched response and as an Express request body. The exploit took several tries, has not been released, and was not tested on other builds.
OpenAI, whose Codex Security team reported the flaw, describes it as enabling unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli and lists Node.js, Bun, and Envoy as affected software. In its account, the flaw works both ways:
an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as "curl --compressed") could be taken over by a malicious server.
No in-the-wild exploitation has been reported. CISA's October 23 assessment recorded exploitation as "none" and automation as "no," and Red Hat said there is no reliable public proof-of-concept for running code.
Severity ratings differ by who is scoring. Google, which assigned the CVE, rates it 9.2, or critical, on the CVSS 4.0 scale. Node.js calls it high, and Red Hat rates it 8.1, or important.
The fix has an unusual history. The change that closes the flaw was added to Brotli's source code on February 27, but no new Brotli release carried it until October 21. OpenAI said the root cause "was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn't known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli."
Node.js credits Khai Tran and Sylvie Mayer of OpenAI's Codex Security for reporting the flaw, and maintainers Matteo Collina and Antoine du Hamel for the fix.
What to Do Now
Update to a fixed version from the table above, then restart the service and rebuild any container image, because a running process keeps the old decoder until it restarts.
Where you cannot update yet, stop decoding untrusted Brotli. OpenAI's disclosure page and the security firm Aikido both recommend:
- Reject incoming requests with Content-Encoding: br before any proxy or parser decodes the body.
- Turn off automatic Brotli decoding in HTTP clients, and reject Brotli responses before they are decoded.
- In Python, uninstall the Brotli and brotlicffi packages so clients fall back to gzip and deflate.
Dropping br from the Accept-Encoding header does not help on its own, because a server can send Brotli whatever the client asks for. For Node.js, no workaround has been published, so updating the runtime is the only fix.
System packages are being fixed at different times. Debian fixed its brotli package for Debian 13 (trixie) on October 23 in version 1.1.0-2+deb13u1. Amazon Linux 2023 still listed its brotli and Node.js 24 packages as pending a fix as of October 22.
Dependency scanners may not flag the Python packages yet. The CVE record names Google's Brotli repository, not the PyPI packages, and GitHub's advisory still lists no affected package, which is what Dependabot reads. Advisory entries for the two Python packages, PYSEC-2026-4322 and PYSEC-2026-4323, were added on October 23, so check the installed versions manually as well.

articles.title: Un mois après sa sortie, l’Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni passe à 649€
articles.text:
Un mois après son lancement à 799 €, le nouveau robot laveur milieu de gamme d’Ecovacs passe 50 € sous le prix de sa promotion de lancement. Le Deebot T90S Pro Omni est à 649 € chez Amazon, vendu par la boutique officielle de la marque : voici ce qu’apporte son rouleau laveur, et pourquoi son prédécesseur, moins cher, reste une alternative sérieuse.
Présenté fin septembre, le Deebot T90S Pro Omni prend la relève du T90 Pro Omni dans la série T, le milieu de gamme d’Ecovacs. Il reprend la recette du rouleau laveur, avec une aspiration portée à 40 000 Pa et une station qui lave, rince et vide le robot. On trouve actuellement l’Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni à 649 € chez Amazon, en coloris noir, vendu par la boutique officielle de la marque et expédié par Amazon. La version blanche reste affichée à 799 € sur la même boutique, et Darty vend le pack Care Kit à 799,99 €.
Le Deebot T90S Pro Omni est à 649 € chez Amazon, contre 799,99 € pour le pack Care Kit du même robot chez Darty.
Pourquoi choisir l’Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni ?
- Un rouleau rincé en continu : L’OZMO Roller 3.0 de 27 cm tourne à 220 tours par minute et reçoit de l’eau propre sous pression pendant tout le cycle. Il évite ainsi d’étaler la saleté ramassée.
- Une aspiration taillée pour les poils : 40 000 Pa et 16 litres d’air par seconde, avec une brosse ZeroTangle 4.0 conçue pour limiter l’enroulement des cheveux. Un argument concret pour les foyers avec animaux ou cheveux longs.
- Une station qui espace l’entretien : Elle lave le rouleau à l’eau chaude, rince son propre plateau et nettoie le réservoir d’eau sale. Avec 4 litres d’eau propre et un sac de 2,5 litres, vos interventions se raréfient.
Du parquet du salon aux tapis de la chambre
Sur carrelage ou parquet, le rouleau frotte plutôt qu’il n’essuie, ce qui sert contre les traces sèches et les taches du quotidien. Le système TruEdge 3.0 déporte ce rouleau vers les plinthes et sous les meubles, là où un robot laisse souvent une bande sale. Sur un tapis, le rouleau se soulève de lui-même pour ne pas le mouiller. Le robot franchit des seuils de 2,5 cm et deux obstacles consécutifs de 4 cm, selon Ecovacs.
Le T90S Pro Omni s’adresse d’abord aux foyers avec animaux : l’application permet de définir des zones prioritaires, et la brosse anti-enroulement limite la corvée des poils. La recharge PowerBoost, qui récupère 10 % de batterie en trois minutes pendant les lavages du rouleau, vise les grandes surfaces sans interrompre le cycle. Il est moins pertinent dans un logement très encombré : le site allemand inside-digital, qui l’a testé, conseille de ranger les câbles avant son passage. Sur le T90 Pro Omni, notre test relevait une navigation parfois chaotique, un défaut que le T90S doit encore corriger.
Face à son prédécesseur et à la concurrence
Le T90S apporte surtout un rouleau plus long, 10 000 Pa d’aspiration en plus et une promesse de silence : Ecovacs annonce 60 dB en fonctionnement, un chiffre que nous n’avons pas encore pu mesurer. Son prédécesseur, le T90 Pro Omni à 30 000 Pa, figure dans notre comparatif des meilleurs aspirateurs robots comme le meilleur rapport qualité/prix du milieu de gamme, autour de 599 €, et nous l’avons déjà relayé à 479 € chez Amazon. L’écart de prix reste donc réel, pour des progrès qui relèvent encore de la fiche constructeur.
✅ Les points forts
- Rouleau OZMO Roller 3.0 de 27 cm rincé en continu
- Aspiration de 40 000 Pa et brosse anti-enroulement
- Station qui lave le rouleau à l’eau chaude et rince son plateau
- Rouleau qui se relève sur les tapis et se déporte vers les plinthes
- 150 € de moins que la version blanche sur la même boutique
❌ Les limites
- Pas encore passé entre nos mains : silence et lavage restent des chiffres constructeur
- Son prédécesseur, que nous recommandons, coûte nettement moins cher
- Sac à poussière jetable de 2,5 litres à racheter
- Assistant Yiko qui ne nous avait pas convaincus jusqu’ici
Ce prix concerne le coloris noir vendu par la boutique officielle Ecovacs sur Amazon : la version blanche du même robot y reste affichée à 799 €.
À 649 €, le Deebot T90S Pro Omni passe sous le tarif de sa promotion de lancement, un mois à peine après sa sortie. Il réunit ce qu’on attend d’un robot laveur récent : rouleau rincé en continu, aspiration élevée, station qui gère l’entretien courant. Pour un appartement ou une maison aux sols surtout durs, avec un chat ou un chien, la proposition tient debout.
Reste la question du budget. Si vous cherchez avant tout un robot endurant et efficace au lavage, le T90 Pro Omni, notre choix malin du milieu de gamme, fait le travail pour moins cher. Le T90S se justifie si vous voulez la génération la plus récente et ses promesses sur le bruit. Gardez en tête que ni sa navigation ni son silence n’ont encore été vérifiés par notre rédaction.
