articles.title: Reino Unido creará un laboratorio de bioseguridad con IA financiado con OpenAI y Anthropic
articles.text:
El gobierno del Reino Unido anunció la creación de un Laboratorio de Bioseguridad con Inteligencia Artificial, respaldado con 100 millones de libras esterlinas de fondos públicos y hasta 200 millones más en compromisos de OpenAI y Anthropic, para detectar y responder a amenazas biológicas.
El Cabinet Office británico presentó la iniciativa el 24 de octubre como la primera organización del mundo dedicada por completo a aplicar inteligencia artificial a la bioseguridad. Funcionará como entidad independiente y sin fines de lucro, dentro de una Iniciativa Nacional de Bioseguridad con IA más amplia.
El objetivo declarado es usar modelos de IA para entender, prevenir, detectar y responder antes a brotes biológicos. En una primera etapa, el laboratorio se concentrará en detectar señales tempranas de amenazas emergentes y acelerar el desarrollo de vacunas y tratamientos.
OpenAI aportará 100 millones de libras en capacidad de cómputo y créditos de uso de sus modelos a través de su programa Rosalind Biodefense, además de acceso privilegiado a sus sistemas más avanzados relevantes para biodefensa, según detalló el comunicado oficial.
Anthropic, por su parte, pondrá a disposición hasta 100 millones de libras en créditos de uso de sus modelos, acceso confiable a esos sistemas y apoyo técnico dedicado. El Gobierno aclaró que estos aportes son compromisos de las empresas y no financiamiento público adicional.
Dos socios tecnológicos más se suman al proyecto
Google DeepMind colaborará con el laboratorio en investigación conjunta y buscará dar acceso confiable a sus modelos Gemini y a herramientas científicas especializadas. Basecamp Research, una empresa británica de inteligencia artificial aplicada a las ciencias de la vida, aportará sus propios modelos de biología y asistencia técnica.
Kanishka Narayan, el ministro de Inteligencia Artificial, dijo que el objetivo es que el laboratorio se convierta en “una institución global que reúna experiencia científica de primer nivel para proteger a las personas de amenazas biológicas emergentes”.
El laboratorio también trabajará junto a la Agencia de Seguridad Sanitaria del Reino Unido, la Agencia de Salud Animal y Vegetal y el Laboratorio de Ciencia y Tecnología de Defensa, las instituciones públicas que hoy lideran la respuesta del país ante riesgos biológicos.
El anuncio forma parte de un paquete mayor de gasto en IA
La creación del laboratorio se dio a conocer antes del presupuesto que el canciller presentará esta semana en el Parlamento, y forma parte de un paquete de cerca de 600 millones de libras, equivalentes a unos 800 millones de dólares, orientado a defender al país frente a riesgos de salud y seguridad vinculados con la inteligencia artificial, según informó la agencia Reuters.
Dentro de ese paquete, el Gobierno destinará otros 65 millones de libras al desarrollo de contramedidas contra patógenos y sumará 120 millones de libras adicionales al Instituto de Seguridad de IA, el organismo estatal que evalúa los riesgos de los modelos más avanzados desde su creación en 2023.
El resto del paquete incluye fondos para reforzar la defensa cibernética de infraestructura crítica, una línea de inversión en empresas británicas que usan IA en robótica y manufactura, y recursos para estudiar cómo la tecnología transformará el empleo en el país.
El Gobierno indicó que el laboratorio contará con un comité científico asesor, con integrantes de la academia, la industria y el sector social, cuyos detalles se darán a conocer más adelante, una vez avance la puesta en marcha de la organización.

articles.title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
articles.text:
LiteLLM on Friday revealed that an Agent Platform master key accidentally published to a public GitHub repository in late May 2026 ultimately allowed the threat actor to push a malicious version of the popular Python package.
"On May 27, 2026, a configuration file was committed to the public LiteLLM-Labs/lite-harness repository which inadvertently contained the master key to a deployment of the LiteLLM Agent Platform, an open source tool we use for orchestrating agents," LiteLLM's Oliver Jensen and Mateo Wang said.
"The error was quickly identified, the commit force-pushed over, and we identified the exposed keys as requiring revocation. However, key revocation did not occur for the master key."
LiteLLM said the unknown attacker (operating from "69.48.229[.]143") used this unrevoked key on October 10, 2026, to gain access to the Agent Platform and extracted a GitHub CLI OAuth token the service was configured with to allow self-hosted cloud agents to file pull requests to GitHub repositories.
The token, per the developers of the open-source large language model (LLM) gateway, was "not scoped down" and associated with its GitHub organization owner's account.
Gaining access to the token allowed the attacker to possess owner-level access to all repositories across the organization and perform additional credential exfiltration. The sequence of actions performed by the threat actor following this step is as follows -
- October 10, 2026, between 10:11 and 10:12 p.m. UTC: Author commits into throwaway branches on internal repositories to run workflows (BerriAI/litellm and BerriAI/litellm-auto) designed to acquire GitHub CLI Oauth tokens associated with two engineers with maintainer privileges via an attacker-controlled webhook[.]site endpoint. The two runs are deleted minutes later.
- October 21, 2026, between 10:08 and 11:08 a.m. UTC: Override branch protection and alter the release pipeline with the source set to the lookalike repository "Berri-AI/litellm" rather than "BerriAI/litellm."
- October 21, 2026, between 11:39 and 11:40 a.m. UTC: LiteLLM version 1.107.0 gets published to PyPI on
- October 21, 2026, 11:46 a.m. UTC: Docker Hub and GHCR images are published.
- October 21, 2026, between 11:53 and 11:54 a.m. UTC: Production and staging run records are deleted.
- October 21, 2026, 12:06 p.m. UTC: Supply chain attack reported by Upwind researcher Lidor Machluf.
- October 21, 2026, 1:23 p.m. UTC: PyPI quarantines LiteLLM version 1.107.0.
- October 21, 2025, 2:20 p.m. UTC: Docker Hub tags v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, and main-stable are removed or repointed to verified clean images.
"In typical operation, building and publishing a release requires being kicked off by an authorized engineer and being approved by a special account locked to a physical device in our office," LiteLLM said.
| Leaked master key in May 2026 | 
"This restriction was relaxed earlier this week to accommodate the temporary push for more frequent releases and bugfix backports, allowing any two engineers to trigger and approve a release. As such, the threat actor used one of the tokens to trigger the release (after having repointed the deployer to their malicious repository), and another to approve it."
In addition, the project maintainers noted that the threat actor could have very well loosened this restriction (or removed it entirely) themselves given that they were already in possession of a token belonging to an organization owner. It's suspected that this was not done to evade detection.
LiteLLM also said the workflows are designed to identify and exfiltrate additional keys and tokens, specifically focusing on upstream inference API tokens. In response to the incident, the company said it's working to revoke each and every token associated with every internal system and vendor platform.
More Details About the Workflows Emerge
Socket, which published its own investigation into the malicious workflows, said it recovered two malicious commits that each added a workflow at ".github/workflows/cache.yml." The first commit was made on October 10, 2026, at 10:11:45 p.m. UTC. It was followed by a second commit on October 12.
"Neither commit was pushed to a branch that still exists," Socket security researcher Karlo Zanki said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "Both were pushed to short-lived branches named ci-tmp-<hex> that were created, used, and deleted within minutes, which is why the activity leaves almost nothing behind in the repository's ordinary history."
According to the application security firm's analysis of the repository's activity log records, both commits rely on a legitimate commit as the branch base to make the push look seemingly harmless -
- Create a throwaway branch named "ci-tmp-<hex>" (namely, ci-tmp-a351cc and ci-tmp-4d8517) from a recent legitimate commit on the repository.
- Push a commit adding ".github/workflows/cache.yml" with the same subject, "ci: bump cache config."
- The workflow is configured to be run every time a commit or tag is pushed (i.e., "on: [push]"), causing it to be triggered.
- Delete the branch.
Both workflows, as highlighted by LiteLLM, are equipped to harvest GitHub tokens and API keys for the organization's Linear workspace, LiteLLM deployment, and Together AI, along with the identifier and signing key of a GitHub App.
The October 12 run extends the collection to more secrets, including API keys for Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Tavily, and GitGuardian's secret-scanning tenant. It also captures Playwright storage state, PostgreSQL database information (connection string, account name, password), Redis endpoint address, port, and authentication password.
The data gathered from the two workflows is exfiltrated to two different webhook[.]site endpoints -
- webhook[.]site/65a42464-3cfa-4b02-a18c-17a6d7b86f37
- webhook[.]site/4da03473-a3e7-4dc2-a087-9c564b4208e1
"A GitHub token and a GitHub App private key are credentials for the platform hosting the repository, not for a third-party service," Zanki said. "GITGUARDIAN_API_KEY is a credential for the secret-scanning platform itself, which gives an attacker visibility into, and potentially control over, the alerts that would surface this activity.
"E2E_LINEAR_STORAGE_STATE_B64 is serialized browser session state used by Playwright for end-to-end tests; a valid storage state permits authenticated access to the associated Linear account without a password and without satisfying multi-factor authentication."
The findings rule out LiteLLM's initial hypothesis that the GitHub CLI OAuth tokens were stolen from the logs of an internal LiteLLM deployment. "The investigation was a process in which we continually learned additional information, meaning some of our assumptions and beliefs were later proven to be inaccurate or incomplete," Jensen acknowledged.
What the Malicious Version of the Package Does
Multiple reports have revealed that the files bundled with LiteLLM version 1.107.0 are engineered to execute automatically when Python starts, even if an application did not import LiteLLM.
The malware features two execution paths: a credential harvesting module that targets authentication material across developer tools, AI applications, cloud environments, and web browsers, and a Unix-oriented backdoor that's launched as a background process to fetch and execute arbitrary code supplied by the attacker every one hour.
| Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 execution flow | 
The stealer also collects system information, SSH files, Git and GitLab credentials and tokens, environment variables, and tokens associated with npm, PyPI, pip, Yarn, Maven, Gradle, Composer, RubyGems, and Cargo. The data is then compressed and sent to "litellm[.]dev/healthcheck" using an HTTP POST request. The domain was registered on October 13, 2026.
"Together, these mechanisms extended potential exposure beyond active LiteLLM deployments: simply starting Python in an affected environment could activate the malicious code, even when LiteLLM itself was never imported," the Microsoft Security Research team said.
"Because the startup files resided outside the LiteLLM application directory, removing only the application files could leave the malicious startup components behind."

articles.title: ICYMI: the 7 biggest tech stories of the week, including our iPhone Duo review and the recent PHP crisis
articles.text:
ICYMI: the 7 biggest tech stories of the week, including our iPhone Duo review and the recent PHP crisis
Seven more days of non-stop tech news
Well, it's been another eventful week for the world of tech, to say the least, and as always, we're bringing you the top stories from TechRadar in one easy-to-read place — just in case you haven't been able to keep up with our coverage over the last seven days.
When it comes to this week's ICYMI (In Case You Missed It) roundup, there's something for everyone, whether you come to us for updates on all things audio or if you've been affected by another tech crisis. That said, Apple has also been in the spotlight with the launch of the iPhone Duo — which we finally managed to get our hands on. So, let's recap this week.
7. Apple teases 'Pro and Tell' event
Hot on the heels of Apple's anticipated iPhone Duo keynote and the announcement of its first smart display, the company teased its upcoming 'Pro and Tell' event, which is scheduled for October 28 in LA. While we're not expecting a formal keynote, we imagine there will be plenty of hands-on time.
So what's new for Apple? Well, the main device we're expecting to see is the company's first touchscreen MacBook in 14-inch and 16-inch editions. This will likely be an OLED display packing the same vibrant, rich viewing experience as an OLED iPhone or iPad Pro, all within a redesigned, slimmer notebook.
It doesn't end there; Apple is also tipped to unveil upgrades for its iPad lineup, though we're not expecting them to be the cheapest of devices.
6. Spotify cracks down on Premium Family plan sharing
Spotify is clamping down on account sharing for those who are signed up to its Premium Family plan, and the platform has started enforcing a new QR code verification system, which has started rolling out to a number of users if they’re not at the same address as the account manager.
The QR code, which appears on the account holder’s device, requires members under the same plan to scan it in order to verify that they're living in the same household. This code updates every few seconds, therefore making it harder for you to use screenshots to bypass the process.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
If you receive a verification prompt, you’ll have a 7-day window to complete the scan, but failure to comply comes with consequences. Spotify will boot you back to ad-listening on the free tier, as well as banning you from joining another Premium Family or Duo plan for 12 months. It really does feel like a prison sentence.
5. The ultimate retro music system landed for nostalgists
Start-up audio company Trettitre has launched its new Retro Ambient Audio System, which raised $2 million on a goal of $3,000 on Kickstarter. Essentially, it's an all-in-one physical media machine: a combined record player, CD player, and cassette player, designed to let you listen to any kind of physical media at home.
The full MSRP of the device is $899, and you can buy the components separately if you wish, but the magnetic wall-rack is where the fun is at. Trettitre's marketing videos show users removing the record player from the wall, carrying it via a handle, plugging in some IEMs, and listening to vinyl on their kitchen table, because this turntable has an onboard battery that charges when you put it back on its wall mount.
The only thing that's missing is a speaker, which you'll unfortunately have to purchase separately.
4. Unitree revealed its 'kung fu' robot bodyguard
Robot vacuums are great, but how about owning a personal Robocop that fends off burglars with its black-belt martial arts skills? That’s the kind of smart home tech we can all get behind, and Chinese robotics giant Unitree teased it this week in the form of its H2-X humanoid.
Unitree’s teaser video (above) is like a trailer for a budget sci-fi movie. The H2-X is seen leaping from four-meter platforms, defending someone from a knife-wielding attacker, and (rather violently) pushing a child out of the way of an oncoming car.
Sadly, there’s very little in the way of specs, and the robot would find it nigh-on impossible to clear consumer certification hurdles to make it to market. Still, it’s an impressive demo that keeps our robot bodyguard dreams alive.
3. A free, lossless music streaming app won us over
This week, Audiophile.fm launched its own app for iOS and Android after being limited to the web browser for some time. It's hi-res and completely free to use.
It's hard to believe that, in today's age of digital streaming, a platform can exist without there being a huge catch. But as far as we can see, this is the case for Audiophile.fm. The app and website connect you to internet radio stations, which are all broadcast in FLAC at CD quality or better. While the app is ad-free, some stations do weave in the occasional ad to pay the bills.
There's also no algorithm feeding you endless variations of the songs you already like, so you can end up with truly random listening.
2. We reviewed the iPhone Duo
The wait is over. Not only did Apple finally reveal its first folding device, but now we finally have our extensive review of the iPhone Duo. The flexi-phone proved expertly designed and engineered in a way only Apple could do. It opens flat and hides the crease under a unique nano-texture display. It features the powerful A20 Pro chip, two excellent 48MP cameras, and exciting versatility. The big screen supports split-screen multitasking (though we wish we could do more than two apps), and the large display will soon support the Apple Pencil. It has all-day battery life and performance that easily supports console-grade gaming.
Is it perfect? Not quite. The outer screen loses too much space to the dock, many apps are still not optimized, and it is thicker and heavier than the competition. Still, we’ve liked it enough to consider making the iPhone Duo our daily driver.
1. The PHP crisis sparked an internet meltdown
Aside from ‘Duo’, the three-letter phrase that dominated the tech news this week was ‘PHP’. Slightly less fun than a folding phone, this security flaw in the programming language that’s used in about 70% of the world’s websites hit countless sites as they scrambled to deploy patches. And that might only be the start.
High-profile sites that temporarily went dark to roll out fixes included Wikipedia and the Internet Archive, and security experts have warned that the ‘PHP2Shell’ flaw is now being “broadly exploited in the wild”.
Fortunately, for now the impact appears to be relatively minor. But with AI helping bad actors find and exploit these kinds of security vulnerabilities, it’s a taste of the kinds of stories we can expect to see a lot more frequently.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Rowan is an Editorial Associate and Apprentice Writer for TechRadar. A recent addition to the news team, he is involved in generating stories for topics that spread across TechRadar's categories. His interests in audio tech and knowledge in entertainment culture help bring the latest updates in tech news to our readers.
- Mark Wilson Senior news editor
- Lance Ulanoff Editor At Large

articles.title: Microsoft veut fermer Arkane Lyon : 217 emplois menacés chez le studio de jeux vidéo
articles.text:
Il avait suffi d’un courriel interne, en mai 2024, pour que Microsoft ferme Arkane Austin au Texas. À Lyon, le groupe doit d’abord chercher un repreneur pour l’autre studio Arkane, où 217 emplois sont menacés, et les syndicats réclament du temps pour que cette recherche aboutisse.
Les salariés d’Arkane Lyon, le studio de Dishonored et de Deathloop, ont appris en juillet que Microsoft projetait de fermer leur studio. Ils ont encaissé un « coup de massue », raconte notre confrère Le Monde Pixels, et Simon, délégué syndical de Printemps écologique dont le prénom a été modifié, évoque une « stupeur » vite changée en « très grande colère ». Quelques jours plus tôt, Asha Sharma, directrice générale de Xbox, avait lancé 3 200 suppressions de postes et cédé quatre studios, sans se prononcer sur Lyon. Microsoft ne peut pas fermer un site français d’un trait de plume. Toute entreprise de plus de 1 000 salariés doit, en vertu de la loi Florange de 2014, chercher un repreneur pendant trois mois avant de fermer un établissement en France. Avec ce délai, les salariés gagnent un sursis, mais Microsoft n’a aucune obligation de vendre.
Microsoft tenu de répondre à chaque offre de reprise
Selon les syndicats, Microsoft cherche un repreneur depuis le milieu de l’été, en parallèle de la consultation du comité social et économique (CSE) et de la négociation d’un plan de sauvegarde de l’emploi (PSE). Le groupe n’est pas tenu de trouver un acheteur, seulement de le chercher sérieusement. Il doit présenter le studio aux candidats potentiels et apporter une réponse motivée à chaque offre reçue. Avant de valider le PSE, l’administration du travail vérifie qu’il a joué le jeu. Si ce n’est pas le cas, elle peut refuser le plan, et le préfet peut exiger le remboursement des aides publiques touchées par l’établissement.
Mais dans un accord signé cet été avec Printemps écologique, la direction d’Arkane parle noir sur blanc du « projet de cessation totale et définitive des activités de la société ». D’après un autre document interne cité par Le Monde, la fermeture serait mise en œuvre entre la fin de l’année 2026 et le premier trimestre 2027. Simon garde malgré tout l’espoir d’un rachat, car « plusieurs formes de reprise sont envisagées », et son syndicat a demandé un report des échéances. La consultation du CSE doit se terminer le 13 novembre, date à laquelle Microsoft devra trancher.
Marvel’s Blade presque terminé, l’atout des syndicats pour une reprise
Arkane Lyon apporterait à un repreneur une équipe rodée et un jeu en fin de course. Le studio développe Marvel’s Blade, un jeu d’action-aventure consacré au chasseur de vampires de Marvel, dont la production « est plutôt sur la fin », selon Simon. Printemps écologique espère rallier les joueurs à sa cause. « Ce serait un gâchis monumental, artistique, humain, commercial », prévient le délégué.
Microsoft entretient le flou. Auprès du Monde, le groupe dit rechercher « activement un partenaire pour accompagner la prochaine phase de développement et permettre la commercialisation du projet », sans préciser s’il parle de Marvel’s Blade ni confirmer la fermeture.
Les deux syndicats contestent aussi le motif économique de la fermeture. « C’est en contradiction totale avec ce qu’on nous dit en CSE depuis des années sur la situation économique de l’entreprise », affirme Simon, qui n’exclut pas de porter l’affaire devant un tribunal. Pendant les négociations sur le PSE, prévues jusqu’au 30 octobre, Printemps écologique réclame des reclassements au sein de Microsoft, car les perspectives d’embauche dans le jeu vidéo sont très faibles. Le Syndicat des travailleurs et travailleuses du jeu vidéo (STJV), qui suit le dossier, envisage de son côté une grève si rien ne bouge.
En juillet, Asha Sharma avait promis qu’aucun jeu annoncé publiquement par les studios de Xbox ne serait annulé. Marvel’s Blade est l’un de ces jeux, et le studio qui le développe pourrait fermer d’ici la fin du premier trimestre 2027.

articles.title: El director de Google Argentina habló sobre YouTube: “La gente es la que hoy dicta el prime time en TV”
articles.text:
Juan Vallejo, director general de Google Argentina, habló con Infobae en el marco de Brandcast, el evento anual de YouTube donde se presentan las principales novedades, métricas de audiencia y herramientas comerciales para anunciantes, agencias de publicidad y creadores de contenido.
Según datos de Kantar presentados durante el evento, el 86% de los espectadores encuestados en Argentina afirma que YouTube es la plataforma de video en la que más confía.
“Que los usuarios estén diciendo que ocho de cada diez argentinos tienen más credibilidad y reconocen más a los creadores que a estrellas de cine o televisión es otra cosa”, afirmó Vallejo, quien fue recientemente nombrado en el cargo de Google.
“Es definitivamente un cambio de paradigma”, agregó.
El crecimiento de YouTube en Argentina y el nuevo “prime time” definido por el usuario
YouTube alcanzó a más de 33 millones de personas en Argentina en marzo de 2026, según datos de Comscore. Para Vallejo, esa cifra responde al contenido que hoy se genera dentro de la plataforma.
“Hoy día, no solamente en Argentina, sino a nivel global, se está dictando la pauta, es el barómetro cultural”, explicó.
Vallejo trazó un paralelo con su propia experiencia como colombiano. Recordó que su generación seguía el rock argentino de artistas como Gustavo Cerati, Soda Stereo, Los Fabulosos y Fito Páez, y ese fenómeno cultural hoy se replica dentro de YouTube. Citó como ejemplos a Bizarra Music Sessions y El Quinto Escalón, de donde surgieron artistas que actualmente llenan estadios.
“La audiencia sigue al contenido”, resumió Vallejo. Esa misma dinámica, dijo, se extiende al ámbito deportivo y al género del streaming.
El directivo describió un cambio en los hábitos de consumo. Explicó que antes el horario de mayor audiencia estaba fijado por los medios tradicionales, entre las siete y las once de la noche.
“Hoy día nosotros somos las personas que estamos dictando cuál es ese prime time”, afirmó. “Tú eres tu propia creadora y tu propia curadora del contenido”. Esa autonomía, sumada a la atención real que capta la plataforma, explica el alcance masivo que registra YouTube, según el directivo.
YouTube vs. la televisión tradicional: alcance en connected TV y streaming local
El consumo de YouTube es complementario a los medios tradicionales cuando se trata de grandes eventos como un Mundial.
Según datos de Comscore, siete de cada diez argentinos utilizan YouTube, una medición realizada en marzo pasado. El crecimiento, dijo, no se limita a dispositivos móviles.
YouTube alcanzó a más de 19 millones de personas mayores de 18 años en Argentina a través de televisión conectada en mayo de 2025, de acuerdo con datos internos de Google.
“No solamente tenemos el pulso del dispositivo personal, sino también estamos ganando terreno en lo que es el corazón de los hogares, que es el living”, afirmó el directivo.
Sobre el papel creciente de los canales de streaming locales y los formatos de clips, Vallejo vinculó ese fenómeno con la capacidad de monetización.
“Cuando un programa, llamémosle un programa o un formato, no está siendo acompañado por las audiencias, no puede monetizar”, explicó.
El directivo citó un estudio de una firma especializada en medición de atención a través de seguimiento ocular, resultados de negocio y dispositivos, utilizado por Google para comparar plataformas.
Según ese estudio, los formatos de YouTube Select en televisión conectada generan un 20% más de atención que las nueve plataformas de CTV más importantes. En formato corto, YouTube Shorts registra casi un 50% más de atención real que otras redes sociales.
La métrica de la atención real: la diferencia entre alcance, atención y resultados
Vallejo marcó una distinción entre el consumo en redes sociales de scroll infinito y el consumo en YouTube.En los feeds de otras plataformas el compromiso es con la interfaz, no con el contenido publicitario.
“Te quedas así todo el día en el feed y realmente cuando pasa el anuncio ni siquiera le das bola”, afirmó. En YouTube, dijo, existe en cambio fijación visual real por parte del usuario.
Esa diferencia, es la razón por la que Google impulsa la medición de atención como métrica central, por encima de las impresiones publicitarias tradicionales.
“La idea de un plan de medios o el éxito de un plan de medios no es simplemente comprar impresiones vacías”. Según él, un plan de medios exitoso debe combinar tres variables: alcance, atención y resultados.
Vallejo explicó qué ocurre cuando falta alguna de esas tres variables. “Muchísimo alcance sin atención es básicamente prender lo que tenga que prender y es básicamente background noise”, afirmó.
Confianza y autenticidad: por qué los usuarios creen más en los creadores que en las estrellas tradicionales
Vallejo destacó cifras de credibilidad que marcan un cambio de paradigma en el vínculo entre audiencias y creadores. El 66 % de los espectadores encuestados considera que los creadores de YouTube son los más auténticos. Vallejo citó datos sobre la percepción de las marcas que pautan en la plataforma.
“Los mismos usuarios, un poquito más de siete de cada diez, realmente dicen que las marcas que están en la plataforma se ven mucho más genuinas”, explicó. Para el directivo, ese dato representa otro cambio de paradigma en la relación entre marcas y consumidores.
Sobre el rol de Google frente a los medios tradicionales, Vallejo lo definió como un socio de amplificación.
Generación Z y el riesgo de la viralidad vacía
Vallejo describió un panorama etario balanceado entre los usuarios de YouTube en Argentina. Según el directivo, la Generación Z posiciona a la plataforma como la número uno en consumo de video.
“Si elegirían una aplicación en su televisor, básicamente siempre se volcarían por YouTube”, afirmó, en referencia a los usuarios de entre 18 y 28 años de edad. Esa preferencia convive con un crecimiento sostenido en franjas etarias de mayor edad.
“Lo que antes pensaba la gente, que éramos más hacia demográficos mucho más jóvenes, realmente hoy se expande a través de demográficos comercialmente hablando muy importantes”, explicó.
Consultado sobre si la competencia por la atención de la audiencia termina privilegiando únicamente los contenidos más virales, Vallejo remitió nuevamente a la distinción entre alcance, atención y resultados. Para el directivo, esa combinación de métricas es lo que evita que la plataforma se reduzca a la viralidad vacía.
Contenido en pantalla grande y el futuro de los formatos regionales
El directivo habló sobre los tipos de contenido que impulsan el consumo en pantalla grande. Sobre los formatos que consume en Connected TV, habló como espectador. Mencionó música, video y la extensión de eventos deportivos como contenidos centrales.
Como ejemplo, citó los partidos del Bayern Múnich, que sigue luego en formato diferido para ver al jugador colombiano, Luis Díaz. “Si bien es cierto que me gustaban los goles, a mí me gustaban los goles es en la televisión grande, no en la televisión chiquita”, afirmó.
Consultado sobre la posibilidad de acceder a canales de streaming de otros países sin recurrir a herramientas como las VPN, puse como ejemplo el caso de Caze TV, un canal brasileño de streaming de fútbol.
“Desde el lado técnico no sé en qué aspecto estamos en este momento para develar o abrir esas barreras”, respondió. Sin embargo, afirmó que la compañía trabaja de manera constante en traer formatos similares a nivel local.
Así las cosas, podemos quedarnos con dos datos claves de estos cambios en Argentina:
- Según datos de Google e Ipsos presentados durante el evento, Google y YouTube concentran mayor confianza entre los usuarios de Argentina durante procesos de compra que las principales redes sociales.
- Según Kantar, entre el 6 y el 20 de agosto de 2026, YouTube es la plataforma de video número uno a la hora de tomar decisiones de compra complejas, por encima de Facebook, Instagram, TikTok y X.

articles.title: Google Says Gmail and Photos Data Shared With AI Search Could Be Used for Targeted Ads
articles.text:
Google has updated its privacy policy to spell out that using personalized artificial intelligence (AI) features in Search or Gemini could allow the company to serve targeted ads to users based on their activity on other connected Google services.
"You may choose to allow certain Google services, including services like Search or Gemini Apps, to access data from other Google services you use, such as Google Photos and Workspace apps like Gmail and Drive, in order to provide you with a more personalized experience, subject to the policies and settings of the accessing service," reads a policy update effective October 16, 2026.
"For example, Search may process some of the data that you allow Search to access to personalize content, including ads."
Google also notes in its revised policy that "We don't show you personalized ads based on your content from Drive, Gmail, or Google Photos, unless you choose to make data from these services available to other Google services that support personalized ads."
News of the policy update was first reported by Android Authority.
Personal Intelligence, unveiled by Google in Gemini in January 2026, allows users to connect other services like Gmail, Google Photos, and YouTube as a way to provide tailored answers in combination with their chat history preferences.
The feature is currently rolling out as a beta to eligible users over the age of 18 globally, except in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, the U.K., and Nigeria.
It's worth noting that the policy states it doesn't use content from Gmail, Drive, or Photos to personalize ads by default. However, that changes should users opt to share photos or emails with AI Mode and other Search tools via the Personal Intelligence feature.
In other words, if users interact with AI Mode or Gemini while Personal Intelligence is enabled, the data that informs those answers (i.e., content from Gmail or Photos) could be used as a signal to serve targeted ads. The privacy policy aims to make it clear that feeding personal data into its AI tools could contribute to ad personalization.
Users should be mindful of the privacy trade-off when connecting their apps to enable AI features. Those who prefer to opt out can do so by selecting the apps they want to disconnect from Personal Intelligence or disable Personalized Recommendations entirely via the Search Services Personalization settings ("www.google[.]com/search-personalization").
In January 2026, OpenAI began showing ads to logged-in adult U.S. users in both the free and ChatGPT Go tiers, while emphasizing that users' data and conversations are protected and never sold to advertisers. It has also said the ads do not influence responses from the chatbot, and that users are in control of the experience.
Earlier this week, the AI company said it's expanded advertising on ChatGPT to 26 more countries, bringing the total to 89. This includes 14 more Latin American countries and several markets across Europe, Africa, and Asia.
"We keep conversations private from advertisers and do not sell customer data," OpenAI stressed. "Ads in ChatGPT are clearly labeled and separate from ChatGPT's answers, and advertising does not influence the answers ChatGPT provides."

articles.title: Test Logitech G Pro X3 Superstrike : le plaisir du clic haptique à près de 190 euros
articles.text:
Légère, parfaitement équilibrée et toujours aussi redoutable avec ses clics haptiques, la nouvelle souris gaming de Logitech m’a fait forte impression. Mais les améliorations restent modestes face à l’excellente X2 alors que son tarif plane toujours.
Meilleurs prix
- Légèreté, mobilité et efficacité
- Équilibre impressionnant
- Molette crantée précise
- Confort et précision des clics haptiques
- Excellent capteur optique
- Recharge trop longue
- Prix stratosphérique
- Aspect cheap de la molette ajourée
- Décoration pas discrète
Difficile de revenir à une souris classique après avoir goûté aux clics haptiques de la Logitech G Pro X3 Superstrike. Nous avions déjà été séduits par cette technologie lors de notre test de la X2, en février dernier. Avec la nouvelle version de cette souris gamer, le fabricant suisse ne révolutionne pas sa formule, mais apporte quelques retouches qui rendent l’ensemble encore plus agréable à utiliser. Suffisant pour justifier les 190 euros demandés ? Ça, c’est une toute autre histoire.
Le déballage et la mise en route
Au premier regard, difficile de distinguer cette X3 de ses aînées. Logitech reste fidèle au dessin très épuré de sa gamme G Pro, sans éclairage tapageur ni artifices esthétiques. Des lignes qui me conviennent parfaitement sur une souris destinée avant tout à la performance. Niveau sobriété de la déco, je serai toutefois plus mesuré.
Rien de bien foufou dans une boîte de souris à 190 euros. ©Nicolas Guyot pour Clubic
La première bonne surprise se révèle dès la prise en main. Avec ses 61 grammes, la X3 est d’une légèreté étonnante, au point de presque se faire oublier sous les doigts. La molette détonne légèrement dans cet ensemble pourtant soigné, tout comme les multiples inscriptions X3, Logitech G et Superstrike, qui viennent rompre la sobriété du design. Son dessin ajouré et sa bande de caoutchouc lui donnent un aspect franchement cheap, assez difficile à comprendre sur un périphérique aussi coûteux.
Première impression : cette souris est légère et plutôt bien équilibrée. ©Nicolas Guyot pour Clubic
La mise en route ne réserve aucune difficulté. On branche le récepteur Lightspeed et la souris est immédiatement opérationnelle. Un passage par G Hub reste néanmoins indispensable pour exploiter tout son potentiel.
Le logiciel permet notamment de régler la sensibilité du capteur, mais surtout de personnaliser les clics en ajustant leur profondeur de déclenchement, leur réarmement et l’intensité du retour haptique. De quoi passer un peu de temps dans les menus avant de trouver les sensations qui vous conviennent.
L’utilisation au quotidien
Ce qui impressionne le plus avec la X3, ce n’est finalement pas son poids, mais la manière dont il est réparti. Logitech a revu l’agencement interne pour recentrer les masses, et cela se ressent immédiatement. La souris glisse avec une facilité déconcertante, répond au moindre mouvement et conserve un équilibre remarquable. Même lors des déplacements rapides, elle donne l’impression de toujours tomber juste.
La X3 Superstrike à la loupe. ©Nicolas Guyot pour Clubic
Mais la véritable vedette reste le système H.I.T.S., inauguré sur la précédente génération. Pour les deux boutons principaux, les microswitchs traditionnels cèdent la place à des capteurs inductifs qui mesurent l’enfoncement des boutons. De petits actionneurs produisent un retour haptique pour simuler le clic.
Et le résultat est toujours aussi convaincant. Sous l’index et le majeur, la sensation est à la fois précise, agréable et étonnamment naturelle. On prend même un certain plaisir à multiplier les clics, simplement pour apprécier leur réponse. Le Rapid Trigger permet également de réarmer les boutons dès leur remontée, selon le réglage choisi. Une fonction particulièrement intéressante pour les joueurs qui enchaînent les actions rapides.
Évidemment, les propriétaires d’une X2 connaissent déjà ces sensations. Logitech a surtout peaufiné une formule qui fonctionnait remarquablement bien.
Le capteur optique Hero 2 progresse lui aussi avec une sensibilité maximale portée de 44 000 à 48 000 DPI. Le taux d’interrogation peut désormais atteindre 8 000 Hz aussi bien en filaire qu’en sans-fil. Des caractéristiques impressionnantes même si les bénéfices concrets de telles valeurs resteront imperceptibles pour une grande partie des joueurs et des utilisateurs.
Quant à cette molette qui m’avait laissé une impression mitigée au déballage, elle prend une belle revanche à l’usage. Ses crans sont francs, bien marqués et permettent un défilement particulièrement précis.
Presque tout est réglable sur cette souris. ©Nicolas Guyot pour Clubic
J’apprécie également le mode BHOP, déjà présent sur la X2 (mais que mon collègue Matthieu n’avait pas trouvé convaincant dans son test), qui permet de limiter les activations involontaires de la roulette. En attendant une seconde impulsion dans un délai personnalisable, la souris évite qu’un mouvement accidentel déclenche un saut ou un changement d’arme au pire moment. Il faut simplement prendre le temps d’apprivoiser ce fonctionnement, qui modifie légèrement la réponse habituelle de la molette.
Enfin, Logitech annonce jusqu’à 135 heures d’autonomie, contre 90 heures pour la génération précédente, grâce notamment à son nouveau contrôleur NxLOGI. De mon côté, j’estime l’autonomie de la X3 entre 7 et 10 jours (avec une bonne dizaine d’heures d’utilisation par jour et un taux d’interrogation à 1 kHz). J’ai en revanche trouvé le temps de recharge franchement long, puisqu’il faut compter environ 1h30 pour retrouver une batterie pleine. La souris reste utilisable avec un câble USB Type-C pendant l’opération de charge et peut profiter du tapis de charge Powerplay 2, vendu séparément la bagatelle de 110€.
Logitech G Pro X3 Superstrike : l’avis de Clubic
La Logitech G Pro X3 Superstrike est une excellente souris gaming, et son confort d'utilisation figure clairement parmi ses plus grandes qualités. Sa légèreté impressionne, son équilibre frôle la perfection et ses clics haptiques m'ont conquis.
Mais cette nouvelle génération ressemble davantage à une évolution bien maîtrisée qu'à une véritable nouveauté. Si vous possédez déjà une X2, je ne vois aucune raison sérieuse de la remplacer. Pour les autres, la question du prix risque rapidement de refroidir vos ardeurs.
À 190 euros, cette souris s'adresse avant tout aux joueurs professionnels, semi-professionnels ou aux passionnés prêts à investir beaucoup d'argent dans leur périphérique favori. Pour un usage plus polyvalent ou moins intensif, une MX Master 4 ou une souris gaming à moins de 100 euros feront amplement l'affaire.
- Légèreté, mobilité et efficacité
- Équilibre impressionnant
- Molette crantée précise
- Confort et précision des clics haptiques
- Excellent capteur optique
- Recharge trop longue
- Prix stratosphérique
- Aspect cheap de la molette ajourée
- Décoration pas discrète
Les alternatives à la Logitech G Pro X3 Superstrike :
- Clic haptique HITS innovant et silencieux
- Très confortable en jeu
- Excellente précision (HERO 2, 8000 Hz)
- Prise en main très confortable
- Revêtement granuleux agréable
- Boutons bien placés et endurants
- Une souris pensée pour des mains plus grandes...
- Double connectivité RF 2.4 GHz / Bluetooth
- Molette 4D débrayable
- Capteur HERO 2 ultra-précis
- Switches optiques réactifs
- Design ambidextre très bien pensé

articles.title: Los robots pato de Nvidia que duermen y juegan, tuvieron 20.000 pedidos de preventa en un día
articles.text:
Un video del director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, jugando en un escenario con pequeños robots con forma de pato se volvió viral esta semana y disparó las preventas del producto a más de 20.000 unidades en apenas 24 horas, según informó el director ejecutivo de Hugging Face, Clément Delangue, en una publicación en la red social X.
Los robots, llamados Microduck, caminan dando pasitos, emiten pequeños sonidos parecidos a los de R2-D2, se sientan, se dejan caer como si durmieran una siesta y hacen una voltereta cuando reciben la orden por voz. Huang los hizo actuar durante su discurso principal en la conferencia GTC de Nvidia en Berlín, Alemania, el 21 de octubre.
Microduck es el segundo robot de Hugging Face, después del también pequeño Reachy Mini. Lo fabrica Pollen Robotics, la empresa francesa que Hugging Face compró en 2025 y que, por lo tanto, pasó a formar parte de Nvidia luego de que la fabricante de chips adquiriera la plataforma.
Esa compra se cerró el 2 de septiembre de 2026: Nvidia pagó alrededor de USD 12.930 millones por Hugging Face, según confirmó la propia empresa en un comunicado y una presentación ante la Comisión de Bolsa y Valores de Estados Unidos. El monto incluye un programa de retención en acciones de hasta USD 1.000 millones para empleados que se sumen a Nvidia.
Hugging Face es una plataforma usada por más de 18 millones de desarrolladores para compartir modelos y conjuntos de datos de inteligencia artificial de código abierto. Nvidia prometió mantenerla abierta y no exigir el uso de sus propios chips para operar en ella.
El Microduck se viralizó tres meses después de su lanzamiento
Microduck salió a la venta en agosto a un precio de USD 399 por unidad. Mide unos 25 centímetros y pesa menos de 800 gramos. Sus movimientos básicos —caminar, sentarse, pararse— se entrenaron primero con simulaciones de aprendizaje por refuerzo y luego se transfirieron al robot físico.
En ese momento, Delangue había dicho que los robots más vendidos del mercado rondaban las 20.000 unidades y que esperaba que Microduck superara esa marca. También señaló que llegar a 50.000 unidades sería “un gran éxito” y representaría un negocio de unos USD 20 millones en ingresos, a razón de USD 400 por robot.
Dos meses después, la aparición de Huang jugando con los Microduck sobre el escenario de GTC Berlín aceleró ese objetivo. Según Delangue, las preventas superaron las 20.000 unidades al día siguiente de la demostración, un salto que atribuyó directamente a la viralización del video.
Los pedidos llegan a tiempo para la Navidad
Los Microduck comprados ahora se entregarán antes de Navidad, lo que los coloca como candidatos a convertirse en uno de los juguetes tecnológicos más buscados de la temporada. Delangue sugirió que el producto podría terminar siendo el robot más vendido del año, y no solo entre el público infantil.
Los videos promocionales de Pollen Robotics muestran a adultos jugando con los Microduck, y la propia demostración de Huang tuvo ese tono: le pidió a los robots que se sentaran, que hicieran una siesta y que dieran una voltereta, y los trató como mascotas más que como productos industriales.
En su discurso, Huang explicó que los Microduck fueron entrenados en la nube con supercomputadoras de Nvidia y que aprendieron sus movimientos en un gemelo digital dentro de la plataforma Omniverse antes de ejecutarlos en el mundo físico. Pollen Robotics permite además que los propietarios enseñen trucos nuevos a sus robots y los compartan con otros usuarios.
El episodio contrasta con el resto de la semana para la industria de la inteligencia artificial, marcada por una serie de ataques informáticos que distintos medios vincularon con el uso de IA. El video de los robots pato circuló, en ese contexto, como una nota de color dentro de una conferencia centrada en infraestructura de cómputo para empresas europeas.
Pollen Robotics, con un equipo de alrededor de diez personas, deberá ahora responder a una demanda que multiplicó varias veces el ritmo de ventas previo a la demostración en Berlín. Delangue no precisó cuántas unidades adicionales se vendieron desde entonces ni si la compañía ajustará su meta original de 50.000 robots, pero confirmó que las entregas de diciembre ya están en marcha para cumplir con los plazos de la temporada navideña.

articles.title: Researchers Push Over 2 Million Updates to Remotely Disable Popcorn Time Updater That Could Fuel a Botnet
articles.text:
Between November 2025 and March 2026, the Dutch security firm Eye Security pushed more than 2 million updates to computers it did not own to switch off a background updater that it said could have allowed an outsider to take over the machine.
The updater belongs to Time4Popcorn, an abandoned copy of Popcorn Time, a free app that streamed pirated films and TV over BitTorrent.
Popcorn Time was popular about a decade ago, and the original shut down in 2014, but several copies kept running under the same name. A separate, legal project that took the Popcorn Time name in early 2025 is unrelated to it.
Eye Security, which monitors client networks for threats, found the updater during a routine threat hunt: a program called Updater.exe on one client's laptop kept trying to reach a web address that was no longer registered.
The firm registered the address itself to see what would connect, and about 50 requests a second poured in. It later laid out the operation, which it named Operation IXIM, in a write-up and a talk at Hack.lu on October 22.
Over six months, those requests carried more than 3.8 million different hardware IDs. The IDs proved an unreliable way to count machines, because some Windows PCs shared one and some Macs changed theirs, so Eye revised its estimate to 2.5 to 3 million Windows computers and 250,000 to 350,000 Macs.
The updater ran in the background on Windows and Mac from the moment the computer started. It checked for new versions over an unencrypted connection and installed whatever it was sent, at the highest privilege level, called SYSTEM on Windows and root on Mac, without checking who sent it.
Because the web addresses it called had been abandoned, Eye said, anyone who registered the right one could have served their own program to every machine still calling it.
On a machine with that access, an attacker could install ransomware, steal saved passwords, or pull the computer into a botnet, Eye said. Mapping a sample of the connecting addresses, the firm said it saw home users around the world, as well as machines on government, military, and corporate networks, though it added that it is "hard to draw conclusions" from that.
Eye had disclosed the flaw, now tracked as CVE-2026-30612, in June. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency rates it 9.8 out of 10. It affects three versions of the Time4Popcorn software:
- Windows, up to and including 6.2.1.18
- Mac, up to and including 6.2.1.17
- Android, up to and including 3.5.0.173
Turning the Updater Against Itself
With no company left to fix the software and no patch coming, Eye decided to use the updater against itself. After taking legal advice, it served the machines an update that does one thing: it stops and disables the updater, deleting no files and collecting nothing.
Eye compared the step to Operation Ladybird in 2021, when Dutch police pushed an update to computers infected with the Emotet botnet to disable the malware on them.
The difference, Eye said, is that Emotet's victims never chose to be infected, while Popcorn Time's users installed the app themselves. Still, the firm said, "none of them chose to have a forgotten updater running in the background for years."
Soon after the updates began, someone uploaded Eye's update to VirusTotal, and antivirus engines started flagging it as malware, a fair description of a program that disables a Windows service. Because every product that blocked it left the vulnerable updater running, Eye reworked the update until only one scanner continued to flag it.
By December 2025, Eye had updated more than 1 million systems and cut the traffic to its web addresses by about 90 percent. By March 1, it was sending about 5,000 updates a day, a 98 percent reduction. Judging the remaining numbers too small to interest a botnet operator, Eye stopped, having sent more than 2 million update downloads in all.
In late March, Eye handed the 15 web addresses it controlled to the Shadowserver Foundation, a non-profit that takes abandoned and malicious domains out of circulation, so a trusted party would hold them rather than Eye.
Public registration records for one of them, popcorntimeupd[.]xyz, now point to Shadowserver's sinkhole servers, with a transfer dated March 20, 2026. Other addresses the updater calls were never Eye's to take and remain with outside owners, the firm said, so machines that reach those are still exposed.
Eye found no sign that anyone else was serving code through the addresses: the ones already registered by other people were parked or up for sale, not pushing updates to the machines calling them. The flaw is not listed in CISA's catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities as of October 23, 2026.
What Popcorn Time Users Should Do
Switching off the updater does not make the app safe. Eye said Popcorn Time runs on a 2014 browser engine with its security sandbox turned off, loads content over unencrypted connections, and pulls in code from other abandoned web addresses.
Eye registered those abandoned addresses too, which it said would have let it run its own code on every machine that opened the app. It did not, but it built a working proof of concept, so the risk is real. The update only changed the updater, so the rest of the app remains dangerous for anyone who keeps using Popcorn Time.
Eye's advice is to uninstall Popcorn Time. The updater can also be turned off by hand: on Windows with two commands that stop and disable its "Update service," and on a Mac with one that unloads the PT.updd helper. Removing the app is the safer step, because disabling the updater leaves the rest of it in place.
- Windows: sc.exe stop "Update service"
- Windows: sc.exe config "Update service" start= disabled
- Mac: launchctl unload -w /Library/LaunchDaemons/PT.updd.plist
On Android, the updater is built into the app and cannot be turned off on its own, and it installs only if the user taps to accept, so Eye did not send updates to Android devices. Removing the app is the only fix there.
To check a network, defenders can look for the two updater files, Updater.exe on Windows and PT.updd on Mac, and for traffic to the web addresses in Eye's write-up, which lists all 20 domains and the file hashes.

articles.title: Controlling two PCs with one keyboard and mouse? Here's the hardware I recommend
articles.text:
This is the hardware I recommend to controlling multiple computers with one keyboard and mouse
Talk about a productivity boost
In my last column, I described how to control two or more PCs with a single set of input devices using software. While these applications can work over wired Ethernet, they more typically use Wi-Fi and can get tripped up in environments with public Wi-Fi like many offices.
Fortunately, a number of USB-based devices can provide a reliable alternative. Some can also work on devices such as Chromebooks, which prevent installing low-level drivers, and allow you to control a computer before it has gotten past the login screen and the software has loaded. However, a few still require a software installation.
First off, many vendors offer simple keyboard-mouse switches that can instantly switch control among multiple PCs using USB connections. KVM switches can also work; just don’t attach other monitors to the switch if they are connected to other PCs.
The trade-off is that these baseline devices can’t do seamless mouse handoffs across computers. On most switches, you must either press a button on the device itself or a remote. (Some use wired remotes while others use infrared). Some higher-end KVM switches allow assigning a hotkey on a keyboard to switch among PCs being controlled.
Going through a wormhole
As for more specialized hardware, perhaps the company with the broadest range of products for traversing multiple PCs is J5Create, which has trademarked the function as Wormhole in nine products, including two docking stations and two hubs.
But the heart of the lineup are four simple cables with USB-A connectors on each end. They range from the $15 JUC100 to the $80 JUC700 which, like the Stardock’s Multiplicity software, can also press one of the PCs into service as a second display.
Curiously, the lowest-end and highest-end product work only with Windows, but the two middle-tier variants can work with MacOS. Regardless, both computers must be running the software that installs from a volume embedded within the cable. The software supports sharing Clipboard content.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The company’s newest and most novel Wormhole product is the Aero Drop CrossLink, a small USB-A device that comes packaged in a small astronaut figure. Once freed from its plastic space suit, it allows a PC-connected keyboard and mouse to control an iPhone, iPad, or Android device over a Bluetooth connection. Unlike the company’s wired products, though, connections to a Mac or even another PC aren’t supported.
Perfect pairings
The next two products came into the market via Kickstarter campaigns. Asuizo Crossys is a bit like the generic keyboard-mouse switching products, but with a few twists.
First, its cables to connect two computers are permanently attached. Second, like the J5Create products, the device includes software that must be installed on the Mac or PC being connected. The Mac version, though, is a faceless app that requires access to the Mac’s accessibility features.
Finally, the LoopMotion device is the only intelligent switch in the lot that requires no software installation, billing itself as the only “location-aware” KM switch. Simply connect a cable to each of its USB ports (labeled L and R) and start seamlessly controlling one with the keyboard of another.
The device is not without its options, though. Pressing a key combination mounts a drive with an HTML page listing more key combinations for modes optimized for gaming and other tasks as well as one that will keep the PC it’s activated awake.
LoopMotion is one of the few options in the class that works out of the box with Linux. However, Chrome OS is a no-go, leaving mechanical switches as about the only option. Another limitation is that, unlike products that use software, Loopsmart won’t allow integrated laptop touchpads to move the cursor between PCs. However, this isn’t all bad, at least as an option, as it can be helpful to keep the cursor contained for some tasks even when two laptops are bridged.
A controlling interest
If you’re looking for the simplest free option, Microsoft’s Mouse without Borders is still the best choice. Although its initial codes are cumbersome and it is limited to four Windows PCs, the software avoids having to enter IP addresses but still provides some extra useful features such as Clipboard sharing and file transfers. Plus, it comes along for the ride if you're into the PowerToys collection.
Stepping up from there, Synergy and its open-source cousin DeskFlow can also bridge Macs and Linux machines. Meanwhile, Multiplicity has the highest degree of customizability and a unique audio-sharing feature If a network-based solution doesn’t work in your environment.
Synergy and Multiplicity offer enterprise configuration and management support, which is particularly appealing for software that stretches across the network. If that’s not an option in your environment, it’s tough to beat the simplicity of Loopmotion. Go with a solution like Crossys, though, if the application demands Clipboard sharing or you’re bridging laptops and don’t want to attach a separate keyboard or mouse.

Ross Rubin is the founder and principal analyst at Reticle Research, a technology research and advisory firm. Ross has been an industry analyst focusing on innovation in products, services, and enabling infrastructure in the tech, media and telecom markets for more than 30 years, writing columns for Engadget, ZDNet, and Fast Company, among other publications. articles.title: Tempête Austen : plus de 400 antennes mobiles en panne dans l’Ouest, comment vérifier la vôtre et ce que vous pouvez réclamer
articles.text:
Deux jours après la longue panne d’Orange, plus de 400 sites mobiles de l’Ouest avaient au moins un service coupé ou dégradé au passage de la tempête Austen. Si votre téléphone ne capte plus, vous pouvez vérifier l’état de l’antenne la plus proche sur une carte publique, mais votre opérateur ne vous remboursera pas forcément.
Des abonnés d’Orange et de Sosh ont perdu appels, SMS et données mobiles pendant une dizaine d’heures le 21 octobre, à cause d’« une défaillance d’un équipement au niveau de notre cœur de réseau mobile », a expliqué l’opérateur. Les clients de l’Ouest ont à peine eu le temps de souffler. Des rafales de 120 à 140 km/h ont été relevées en Bretagne et dans l’ouest de la Manche dans la nuit du 22 au 23 octobre, et près de 290 000 foyers étaient privés d’électricité à la mi-journée. Privées de courant, les antennes relais tiennent peu de temps sur leurs batteries. Résultat, 412 sites avaient au moins un service hors d’usage à 11 heures, dont 204 en Bretagne, d’après un relevé de DegroupTest. Dans les communes encore sans courant, les abonnés devront sans doute patienter tout le week-end avant de retrouver du réseau. En attendant, on vous livre quelques conseils pour garder le fil. Enfin, le réseau.
Vérifier l’antenne la plus proche et téléphoner sans elle
Les quatre opérateurs publient chaque jour la liste de leurs sites en panne ou en maintenance, et DegroupTest a tiré son décompte de ces fichiers. L’Arcep reporte ces données sur une carte de son service Mon réseau mobile, mise à jour quotidiennement, qui couvre les deux dernières semaines. Si une antenne en panne apparaît près de chez vous, regardez à quel opérateur elle appartient. Chaque point correspond à un site chez un seul opérateur, et un voisin abonné ailleurs peut très bien capter normalement.
Si votre box fonctionne toujours, vous pouvez continuer à téléphoner. Activez les appels Wi-Fi dans les réglages de votre smartphone, et vos appels et vos SMS passeront par votre connexion fixe. Dans le Morbihan, 15 communes n’avaient plus ni téléphone fixe ni internet à la mi-journée du 23 octobre, et les habitants dont la ligne passe par leur box ne pouvaient plus appeler, selon un point de l’association des maires du département, établi à partir des réponses de 98 communes. En cas d’urgence, composez le 112. L’appel passe alors par l’antenne de n’importe quel opérateur à portée.
Dans les zones privées d’électricité, le réseau mobile ne sera rétabli qu’après le courant. Enedis comptait encore 146 000 foyers sans électricité le 24 octobre à 7 heures, dont 65 800 en Bretagne. « Depuis le pic de la tempête, nous avons déjà réalimenté 264 000 clients », a indiqué Laurent Perrault, directeur de crise d’Enedis, cité par Tendance Ouest. Orange prévient que certaines de ses installations ne peuvent être remises en service que par un technicien, même une fois le courant revenu.
Réclamer un dédommagement à votre opérateur
Aucun texte n’oblige un opérateur à vous indemniser automatiquement après une coupure. Chez Orange et Sosh, un remboursement au prorata n’est possible que si l’interruption « dépasse 10 % de la durée du mois ou dure plus de 48 heures consécutives », selon les conditions générales de l’opérateur citées par MoneyVox. Les dix heures de coupure du 21 octobre étaient loin de ce seuil. Dans certaines communes, les abonnés pourraient en revanche le franchir avec Austen. Orange prévoyait de remettre en service la plupart de ses antennes en panne depuis la tempête entre le 24 et le 26 octobre, d’après les dates de fin déclarées par les opérateurs, et SFR attendait le 22 novembre pour cinq de ses sites. Pour une tempête, votre opérateur peut en outre invoquer la force majeure, que le Code civil réserve aux événements imprévisibles et inévitables.
Les opérateurs décident donc seuls de leurs gestes commerciaux. Lors des incendies de cet été, Free a ajouté 200 Go valables trente jours sur les lignes de ses abonnés dans cinq départements touchés par les feux. Orange et Bouygues Telecom avaient offert 200 Go quelques jours plus tôt à leurs clients de la Gironde et des Landes, sans démarche à faire, et SFR les avait imités, d’après DegroupTest. Les quatre opérateurs n’avaient fait aucune annonce de ce genre après le passage d’Austen, le 24 octobre au matin.
Si la coupure s’éternise chez vous, notez les dates et faites des captures d’écran. Dans sa fiche pratique, l’Arcep conseille d’« informer le service clients de votre opérateur » quand les perturbations durent, puis de « saisir le médiateur des communications électroniques et des postes » si la réponse tarde. Dans les zones boisées, les réparations prendront du temps. « Les conditions d’accès demeurent difficiles du fait de la chute d’arbres et branches », a prévenu Enedis.

articles.title: CISA Flags Two Actively Exploited Critical Flaws in Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added two vulnerabilities impacting Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), citing reports of active exploitation in the wild.
The critical-severity vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-110447 (CVSS score: 9.2) - An operating system command injection vulnerability in Collabora Online – Built-in CODE Server (aka richdocumentscode) when used within the NextCloud platform that could allow remote code execution via "proxy.php" when the CODE local document server isn't running. (Fixed in September 2026 in version 26.4.303)
- CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS score: 9.9) - An SQL injection vulnerability in on-premise versions of Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator that could allow a remote attacker to access privileged internal functionality. (Fixed in October 2026 in versions 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.2.12)
As reported by The Hacker News, threat actors have been observed exploiting CVE-2026-110447 to backdoor Nextcloud servers with a web shell so as to conduct reconnaissance and search for credential stores, password manager artifacts, and cryptocurrency wallets.
As for CVE-2026-114625, successful exploitation requires an attacker to have network access to the VCO web interface and a valid authenticated session on the VCO portal. The minimum user role required is Enterprise Read Only.
Although Arista has acknowledged that the vulnerability is "known to be actively exploited," it has not attributed the activity to a particular threat actor or provided technical details on how the vulnerability is being exploited and what actions the attackers took after privilege escalation. The company also has not disclosed the number of affected organizations.
However, it has shared two IP addresses geolocated to Japan as responsible for driving the activity -
CVE-2026-114625 is the third vulnerability in the same product to have been weaponized in the wild since July 2026, following CVE-2026-16812 (CVSS score: 10.0) and CVE-2026-93952 (CVSS score: 10.0).
In light of active exploitation, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are recommended to apply the fixes by October 26, 2026, to secure their networks.

articles.title: Estas son las principales novedades de Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5
articles.text:
CD Projekt Red lanzó Update 2.5 de Cyberpunk 2077 apenas dos días después de haberlo anunciado.
El estudio reveló la actualización el 20 de octubre de 2026 con la intención de mantener en secreto la lista de funciones hasta su salida, pero creadores de contenido que recibieron acceso anticipado filtraron los detalles antes de la fecha oficial de lanzamiento, el 22 de octubre. El parche, bautizado con el subtítulo Edgerunners 2, incorpora cambios en el combate, soporte para mods, nuevas misiones, elementos cosméticos y una estación de radio adicional.
V puede empuñar dos pistolas al mismo tiempo
La incorporación central de la actualización es la ventaja Double Trouble, ubicada dentro del árbol de habilidades de Frío. Esta mecánica permite al protagonista del juego, V, usar dos pistolas de forma simultánea durante los combates. Se trata de una función que los jugadores reclamaron desde el lanzamiento original del título y que ahora se integra como una mejora directa para quienes construyen a sus personajes en torno a esa rama de habilidades.
Dos nuevos contenidos narrativos vinculados a Edgerunners 2
La actualización suma dos piezas de contenido relacionadas con la temática del anime Edgerunners. Clampdown es un nuevo encargo asociado a Edgerunners 2, mientras que NC Tour es una misión secundaria cuyos detalles no se revelaron antes del lanzamiento del parche. Ninguna de las dos se presenta como una expansión de historia de gran escala, pero ambas ofrecen objetivos adicionales para los jugadores que ya completaron la campaña principal del juego.
El control de campo de visión llega finalmente a consolas
Los usuarios de PC contaban con un control deslizante de campo de visión (FOV) desde el lanzamiento del juego, una opción que los jugadores de consola no tenían disponible hasta ahora. Con Update 2.5, esta función se habilita también en consolas y permite ampliar o reducir la perspectiva de la cámara.
El cambio representa una mejora de calidad de vida para jugadores sensibles al movimiento o para quienes prefieren un campo visual más amplio durante los enfrentamientos.
Soporte integrado para mods en la mayoría de plataformas
La actualización incorpora soporte nativo para mod.io en las plataformas principales donde está disponible Cyberpunk 2077, con la excepción de Nintendo Switch 2. Esta función permite buscar e instalar mods oficiales directamente desde el cliente del juego, sin necesidad de recurrir a herramientas externas o a la gestión manual de archivos.
Los jugadores de PC disponían de un ecosistema de mods desarrollado desde hace años, por lo que esta incorporación reduce la distancia con el público de consola.
Nuevas opciones de personalización visual
Entre los añadidos cosméticos de Update 2.5 se encuentran los Glamdocs, un objeto que permite modificar la apariencia visual del ciberware de brazo sin alterar sus estadísticas de combate. A esto se suman cinco nuevos conjuntos de ropa y nuevos peinados disponibles tanto para V masculino como femenino.
También se incorporaron diseños exclusivos para vehículos Quadra, accesibles a través de Twitch drops que requieren ver transmisiones afiliadas en los canales oficiales del juego.
Una estación de radio con música de Edgerunners
La lista de emisoras de Night City se amplía con una nueva estación de radio dedicada a la banda sonora del anime Edgerunners. Esta incorporación se suma al contenido ya existente vinculado a esa producción dentro del universo del juego.
Disponibilidad en todas las plataformas
Update 2.5 llega a todas las plataformas donde está disponible Cyberpunk 2077. La única función con una excepción de compatibilidad es el soporte para mod.io, que no está disponible en Nintendo Switch 2. articles.title: From the bins, back to business: We take a tour of HPE’s Technology Renewal Centre to see how it's giving old tech a second life
articles.text:
From the bins, back to business: We take a tour of HPE’s Technology Renewal Centre to see how it's giving old tech a second life
We see how HPE is giving old technology a new lease of life
If you’ve ever spotted a laptop or printer with a label that describes it as “reconditioned” or “refurbished” and wondered exactly what that means, read on.
Hidden away a short drive from Glasgow Airport, HPE’s Technology Renewal Centre (TRC) at Erskine is one of the world’s leading e-waste processing facilities.
Initially opened in the late 1980s as part of Scotland’s famed ‘Silicon Glen’, the TRC has gone through a number of rebirths before evolving into what it is today, and TechRadar Pro was lucky enough to be invited on a tour of the facility - here’s what we saw.
Back to life
The 240,000 square foot facility is a huge space, and with the sun shining in on what Jackie Rafferty, TRC Operations Manager and our guide told us was an uncharacteristically nice Scottish October day, TechRadar Pro was part of a pan-European media tour around the TRC.
Since its opening on December 8 1987, when it built 286 computers under the legendary Compaq brand, the site has now been a renewal center since 2011, along with a sister site in Andover Massachusetts.
Its 200+ staff, all of whom have undergone Ministry of Defence-level security clearance, are largely local to the area, with the TRC offering a fantastic employment opportunity, with Rafferty noting how members of the same families are often employed together.
The TRC now plays a key role for HPE’s Financial Services division, offering a more affordable way for customers to make sure they have the latest hardware, and that their older devices don’t end up in landfill.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The company currently provides what it calls HPE 90/9 Advantage, a loan offering where you don’t pay anything for the first 90 days followed by nine months at 1%.
At Erskine, the team is able to process around 150,000 assets a month, with 85% of servers and 97% of workstations and PCs it receives sanitised, tested and processed on site, ready to sell on.
Overall, HPE estimates that 84% of assets processed at Erskine and Andover are refurbished and returned to active use, with the rest responsibly recycled.
These aren’t just HPE assets - in order to maximize the recycling potential, customers are able to send in kit from other vendors - with only over 60% of data center, and close to 70% of workplace assets are HP or HPE branded .
Rafferty's tour took us around every step of the reconditioning process, from inbound deliveries ready to be sanitized, ready for stripping for parts or refurbishment, to rows of shelving containing individual components, all set for their new lease of life - with our guide pointing out assets such as a shipment of reconditioned HPE ProLiant servers set to be shipped out to a customer in France.
The TRC uses a customized version of Microsoft Dynamics 365 that acts as its own ERP system for every component of every asset it receives, allowing the company to track it from end-to-end.
With demand for AI computing forcing companies of all sizes to rethink their technological capabilities, the TRC is increasingly confronted with server racks and other high-end hardware, all of which can still be reconditioned and reused.
We see a huge line of racks full of reconditioned hardware being tested and checked before re-entering the enterprise world, with the hum of fans almost deafening as you get up close.
As the process continues, we see rows of laptops and workstations being formatted and wiped, and multiple workbenches stripping out individual components from older devices designated for re-use, with shelves full of kit ready to be re-assigned at a later date.
Once reassembled, newly-created items are put through a series of rigorous tests to ensure they meet HPE's high standards, and that the buyers receive a device able to cope with all their key workloads.
Security is obviously paramount when it comes to pre-owned hardware, and all drives are formatted and rewritten in accordance with the highest standards.
Despite many users or organizations wiping their SSDs before sending the device to HPE, the company uses extra software to ensure the hardware is clean. HPE estimates it has overwritten around 1.6 million drives this way, with 1.7 exabyte of data securely sanitized – the equivalent of watching around 97 million years of HD movies.
Sustainability is unsurprisingly another key watchword, with HPE keen to extol the environmental impacts the TRC has caused.
Along with the sanitization and recycling, we were shown how HPE has even revolutionized the packaging it uses to send out refurbished items, with the exterior made of 100% recycled corrugate, the majority of which comes from reconstituted inbound return packaging, with the interior protective foam is made of a 100% biodegradable starch-based foam replaced polystyrene which can be dissolved in water.
Overall, HPE estimates over 8.4 million kg of e-waste has been prevented from going to landfill, the equivalent of the annual e-waste generated by over a million people.
So it seems the messaging is true - buying pre-loved or second-hand kit really can be as good as the real thing, so long may HPE's efforts continue.

Mike Moore is Deputy Editor at TechRadar Pro. He has worked as a B2B and B2C tech journalist for over a decade, including at one of the UK's leading national newspapers and fellow Future title ITProPortal. When he's not keeping track of all the latest enterprise and workplace trends, he can most likely be found watching, following or taking part in some kind of sport.
