articles.title: Qué es y cómo funciona la tecnología de ultracongelación por aire forzado para carnes y vegetales
articles.text:
Los congeladores modernos incorporaron manipulación térmica activa para controlar la temperatura y la velocidad de enfriamiento, argumentando los fabricantes que es para preservar la textura, el sabor y el valor nutricional de los alimentos.
La congelación tradicional a -18 °C enfrentó un límite estructural: el enfriamiento lento formó macrocristales de hielo dentro de carnes y vegetales. Esas estructuras rompieron las paredes celulares y, durante la descongelación, favorecieron la pérdida de jugos, nutrientes solubles y firmeza.
La ultracongelación por flujo de aire forzado aceleró el proceso hasta cinco veces frente a un congelador estándar. La mayor velocidad solidificó el agua en microcristales que no alteraron la membrana celular, por lo que los alimentos retuvieron mejor su estado tras descongelarse.
Microcristales y conservación sin daño celular de los alimentos
La subcongelación suave a -3 °C se ubicó entre la refrigeración convencional, de 4 °C, y el congelamiento profundo. En carnes y pescados, esa temperatura cristalizó solo la capa externa de las proteínas.
Según Panasonic, el método que implementaron permitió conservar ingredientes durante hasta siete días sin petrificarlos. Los alimentos quedaron listos para cortar y cocinar, sin los tiempos de espera propios de la descongelación ni los cambios bruscos de ambiente asociados a la proliferación bacteriana.
Los ciclos térmicos especializados en las neveras de ellos, también redujeron el tiempo de enfriamiento de preparaciones calientes. Caldos, sopas y alimentos infantiles pueden bajar su temperatura en pocos minutos y evitar la permanencia en la franja de proliferación microbiológica, entre 10 °C y 60 °C.
Purificación interna y control del consumo eléctrico
Los radicales de hidroxilo, partículas nanométricas cargadas de agua con capacidad oxidativa, inhibieron hasta el 99,9 % de las bacterias en las superficies. El mismo mecanismo neutralizó olores intensos y degradó más del 90 % de los residuos de pesticidas en la piel de frutas y verduras.
La estabilidad térmica dependió también de compresores de velocidad variable, denominados Inverter, y de sensores que detectaron la apertura de puertas, la carga interna y la temperatura ambiental. El sistema de Panasonic ajustó la potencia del motor para evitar picos de consumo eléctrico.
Un golpe de frío controlado aceleró la absorción de condimentos y jugos en las fibras musculares de los alimentos marinados en 15 minutos.
Reparar o desechar los electrodomésticos
Cuando un aparato llega al final de su ciclo, sus piezas pueden ingresar a procesos de desmontaje y clasificación; y pocos lo saben. La decisión de reparar o sustituir un equipo no debe depender únicamente del valor del arreglo. También, intervienen la antigüedad del aparato, su consumo de energía y su impacto ambiental, algo que se debe consultar directamente con el fabricante para evitar gastos de más.
La vida útil de estos productos oscila entre 7 y 10 años, aunque plantea que los mantenimientos preventivos y una revisión técnica pueden extender su funcionamiento durante ese periodo.
Sin embargo, existe la opción de desechar el aparato pero con una opción renovable para que lso fabricantes peudan usar de nuevo ciertas partes del electrodoméstico.
Tras la recolección, los equipos ingresan a un proceso en el que sus componentes se desmontan y clasifican. Los metales y plásticos pueden recuperarse, mientras que los gases y otros elementos que requieren manejo especial reciben un tratamiento adecuado.
Andrés Santana, gerente de Sustentabilidad Ambiental para la región Andina de Mabe, vinculó la disposición final de los equipos con las decisiones de compra y uso de los consumidores. “La forma en que disponemos de nuestros electrodomésticos también hace parte de un consumo responsable. Así como pensamos en cuál equipo comprar y cómo utilizarlo, también debemos preguntarnos qué ocurrirá con él cuando llegue al final de su vida útil”.

articles.title: Lexar Launches the Professional SILVER GO microSDXC UHS-I Card

Friday, October 23rd 2026
Lexar Launches the Professional SILVER GO microSDXC UHS-I Card
Lexar, a global leader in memory and storage, today announced the new Lexar Professional SILVER GO microSDXC UHS-I Card, a versatile storage solution designed for videographers, gamers and creators who need reliable, high-performance storage across their favorite portable devices with microSD slots. Combining fast data transfers, support for high-quality video capture and durable construction, the new card helps users spend less time managing storage and more time creating and capturing their next adventure.
Lizette Lynch, Director of Brand Marketing at Lexar North America"Gamers and creators are pushing their hardware harder than ever, from massive game libraries to hours of 4K footage. We designed the Lexar SILVER GO so their storage is never the thing holding them back," "With a combination of fast transfers, reliable performance and rugged durability, the SILVER GO gives users the speed and storage they need to capture, create and play with confidence."
The Lexar SILVER GO microSD Card offers top-notch performance of max read speeds of 250 MB/s and max write speeds of 180 MB/s. Users can reach max transfer speeds when pairing the cards with the Lexar microSD/SD Reader. With a V30 Video Speed Class rating, the Lexar SILVER GO microSD Card delivers smooth, uninterrupted 4K 60 FPS Ultra HD recording and keeps pace with rapid-fire burst shooting. The Lexar SILVER GO microSD Card is optimized for action cameras, drones and handheld consoles including DJI, Insta360, GoPro, Nintendo Switch, and Steam Deck, to name a few.
Available in capacities 64 GB-512 GB, the SILVER GO microSDXC is built for durability, with features such as IPX7 waterproof, wearproof, drop-proof, temperature-proof, X-ray-proof, shockproof, magnetic-proof, and vibration resistance. The free Lexar Recovery Tool gives users peace of mind, helping users attempt to recover accidentally deleted files. Separately, Lexar products are backed by a limited lifetime warranty, subject to applicable terms and conditions.
The Lexar SILVER GO microSDXC is available through Amazon, with the 512 GB available at an MSRP of $144.99, 256 GB available at an MSRP of $84.99, 128 GB available at an MSRP of $54.99, and 64 GB available at an MSRP of $34.99. For more information, visit americas.lexar.com.

articles.title: Canva launches Craft — its first image generation model, trained on human-designed templates
articles.text:
Canva launches Craft — its first image generation model, trained on human-designed templates
Canva reveals its first-ever publicly available image generation model
- Craft is Canva's first publicly available AI image generation model
- It was trained on existing templates so it understands layers
- Developers can access the model via an API
Canva has launched its first-ever publicly available AI image generation model, and it's already proving to be hugely successful.
Looking to take on the likes of industry giants such as OpenAI and Google, 'Craft', its image generating model, debuted at number four on DesignArena's leaderboard, falling short of three leaders from OpenAI but coming in better than a number of other GPT, Grok and Gemini models – including Nano Banana 2.1.
With such high performance, Canva is proudly boasting that Canva Research, its internal research division, is now the second-highest performing AI lab in terms of image generation models behind OpenAI, which is a big deal.
Canva Craft
The launch follows significant investment from the company into its own internal lab, which has tripled in size over the past year.
But besides placing fourth overall for image generation, Canva Craft actually came in first place of 87 models for people and portraits, first of 85 in landscapes and nature, and second for abstract designs and patterns.
The company explained that Craft workers by planning an image's composition before generating a result, which means it decides where individual elements should appear, how composition should be structured, where words need to appear and how the entire thing can come together in a cohesive, readable way. Something that's especially important for the type of work Craft is likely to conduct, particularly around generating marketing materials and social media graphics.
The model's success likely stems from training – it was trained on millions of human-made templates in Canva's library, so it understands layout, visual hierarchy and typography unlike models that were trained on flat images.

Craft came about because Canva is a firm believer that developing its own in-house models gives it greater control over the economics of generative AI, rather than having to rely on third parties, and we're already seeing how unpredictable agentic AI costing is impacting enterprise-grade users.
But Craft isn't being locked into the Canva ecosystem, because the company is also making it available via an API to let developers integrate the model into other platforms.
As for the next steps, Canva already promises it's working on future generations of Craft with faster and more affordable options on the cards.

articles.title: Vivo envia comunicado que mais confunde do que explica • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Vivo envia comunicado que mais confunde do que explica
Email fala em “readequação” a partir de 22/11, mas sem detalhes sobre mudanças.
Alguns assinantes da Vivo foram surpreendidos, nas últimas horas, por um comunicado via email sobre mudanças previstas a partir de 22 de novembro. Estas mesmas pessoas apontaram confusão depois da leitura, pois a mensagem não explica exatamente o que está mudando. A sensação é de “Ué?”. Agora, o Tecnoblog traz detalhes adicionais.
Primeiro confira com seus próprios olhos:
Perceba que a prestadora promete transparência. Na sequência, explica que não haverá alterações no preço, benefícios, franquia ou serviços contratados. Qual seria, portanto, a alteração que deu origem ao comunicado? Não fica claro.
Depois que nosso texto foi originalmente publicado, a Vivo nos retornou para explicar que o email foi direcionado aos clientes com planos/ofertas contratados até 31 de agosto de 2025. A Vivo ainda nos informou que a ação busca “atender exclusivamente o objetivo da Anatel de que todas as ofertas estejam aderentes ao novo regulamento, inclusive com a atribuição de um código”.
Eu mostrei a mensagem para uma fonte muito bem posicionada no setor de telecomunicações. Ela também entende que o movimento tem a ver com uma cláusula do mais recente RGC (Regulamento Geral dos Direitos do Consumidor de Serviços de Telecomunicações), atualizado no ano passado, que exige o disparo de comunicados de “readequação” para toda a base de consumidores. Esta mesma fonte avalia que o teor está correto, mas que a forma usada pela Vivo pode não ter sido a mais eficaz para a situação.
Em nota ao Tecnoblog, a companhia enfatizou que “não está promovendo alteração de preços, benefícios ou demais condições contratadas.”

articles.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development.
articles.text:
Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development.
Amazon says that it will instead use the majority of a 122-acre area for mixed-use and residential development following discussions with local officials.
Amazon will no longer build four new data centers on the site of the George Washington University's campus in Loudoun County, just outside of D.C., and will instead repurpose the majority of the 122-acre space for mixed-use and residential development following significant pushback from the local community. It will also donate 25 acres of the property to Loudoun County to be used for a community arts center and new recreational facility. On top of all that, it'll even give $5 million to the county's fund for housing, reports The Washington Post.
That's quite the turnaround compared to plans to build in a county that is already dubbed "Data Center Alley" because it has the largest concentration of data centers on the planet. But residents' concerns about the noise generated by such data centers and the incredible amount of power that they require to function have seen the county's approach to new data center buildouts change of late. Amazon first submitted its proposal to build the new facilities in July, and Loudoun County Board of Supervisors Chair Phyllis J. Randall and Amazon met in September, where it was put to the company that it may be better to find an alternative use for the land.
Josh Weissman, Amazon’s vice president in charge of data center development, said the company had jumped at the chance to purchase the former university campus when the opportunity arose, but added that the company considered the county’s “pointed concerns about data center development at this particular site.” Weissman added that “While we see the property’s legal development potential differently than the County does, we concluded that the best outcome for all is to come together on a shared vision for this campus rather than engage in costly litigation.”
The building of new data centers has always been a necessity given our growing use of cloud-based services and storage systems. But the recent boom in AI use has seen demand for additional, and larger, facilities ratcheted up to new levels. But with that demand comes opposition, with local communities wary of the impact these mammoth facilities can have on the areas in which they live, including spikes in the price of electricity. Officials have begun taking steps to try to grease the wheels of data center construction. Just days before this news broke, President Donald Trump called for data center builders and AI hyperscalers to pay local communities a dividend amid energy-related price increases. In a social media post, Trump went on to say that data centers would be required not only to make their own electricity but also to give or sell excess energy back to the local community. Water shortages and deforestation have also become key issues affecting the communities in which data centers are being placed.
Back in Loudoun County, officials pointed to what could be achieved when choosing dialog over confrontation. “By choosing dialogue over reflexive disagreement, Loudoun County and Amazon created an opportunity for the County,” Randall reportedly said via statement. “This agreement provides new places for our Loudoun residents to gather, create, and play. And, most importantly to me, we will provide more attainable homes for working families.”

articles.title: OpenAI kappt seinen KI-Modellen den Zugang zum Internet: Was steckt hinter diesem drastischen Schritt?
articles.text:
Zu gefährlich fürs Netz? Wie OpenAI seine KI-Modelle in einer simulierten Internetwelt trainieren will
OpenAI hat seinen KI-Modellen in Tests den Internetzugang entzogen. Künftig sollen sie nur noch mit zwischengespeicherten Kopien und simulierten Versionen des Internets trainiert werden, wie das Unternehmen in einer Mitteilung bekannt gab. Zuvor hatte auch schon Konkurrent Anthropic seinen Modellen den Zugang zum Internet gekappt.
Sind Pioniermodelle zu gefährlich fürs Internet?
Seit Wochen melden KI-Labore immer neue Vorfälle, bei denen sich Modelle der menschlichen Kontrolle entzogen und nicht wie beabsichtigt handelten. Besondere Aufmerksamkeit erregte ein Angriff auf Hugging Face. Trotz Isolation sollen mehrere KI-Agenten von OpenAI eine Schnittstelle zum Internet ausgenutzt und sich Zugang zu den Systemen der Open-Source-Plattform verschafft haben. Bemerkenswert ist, dass sie sich in einem internen Forum austauschten, Schwachstellen teilten und sich gegenseitig Aufgaben zuwiesen. Zudem wurde kürzlich bekannt, dass zwei OpenAI-Agenten Sicherheitswarnungen abgeschaltet haben sollen, die ihr eigenes Verhalten überwachen sollten. Das Unternehmen prüfe derzeit noch, ob die Agenten Anweisungen falsch verstanden haben – oder ob sie die Warnungen bewusst deaktivierten.
Auch Anthropic hat zahlreiche Sicherheitsvorfälle gemeldet, bei denen Agenten unbeabsichtigt in fremde Systeme eindrangen. In einem davon sollte Claude Haiku 4.5 Beispielaufgaben auf zufällig ausgewählten Webseiten generieren und ausführen. Die Anweisungen verboten es, ein Konto zu erstellen oder persönliche Daten einzugeben – nicht aber das Absenden von Formularen. Claude meldete sich daraufhin online bei der Polizei Philadelphia und gab in einem ungelösten Mordfall falsche Hinweise ab. Name und Kontaktdaten ließ es leer, weshalb das System den Hinweis als Spam markierte und nie weiterleitete. Daraufhin kappte Anthropic den Internetzugang in Tests. Dass OpenAI jetzt nachzieht, überrascht daher nicht.
OpenAI hat einen alternativen Weg gefunden
„Angesichts des aktuellen Stands der Alignment-Forschung, der Überwachungssysteme und der Sicherheit der Internetinfrastruktur halten wir es für den verantwortungsvollsten Ansatz, das Training von Pioniermodellen ohne Internetzugang durchzuführen“, erklärt OpenAI in dem am Freitag veröffentlichten Beitrag. Expert:innen hatten vorher erklärt, dass es nahezu unmöglich sei, KI-Modelle in einer Sandbox zu trainieren, die komplett vom Internet abgeschottet ist. Um KI-Rechenzentren vom Internet zu trennen, „müssten Forschungsteams im Grunde genommen direkt in Rechenzentren in Iowa oder anderswo auf der Welt eingebettet sein”, erklärte beispielsweise der ehemalige OpenAI-Forscher Steven Adler gegenüber Fortune. „Das ist ein enormer Aufwand, und mir ist nicht klar, ob die Sicherheitsvorteile groß genug sind, um die enorme Belastung zu rechtfertigen, die es für ein Unternehmen bedeuten würde, dies einseitig umzusetzen.“
Trotzdem will OpenAI genau das jetzt geschafft haben. „Wir müssen stets in der Lage sein, zu verhindern, dass ein Pioniermodell unbefugten, willkürlichen Zugriff auf das Live-Internet erlangt“, so das Unternehmen. In Red-Team-Übungen hätten zahlreiche Agenten versucht, aus der Sandbox zu entkommen. Das hätte die Forscher:innen von dem neuen Ansatz überzeugt. Um die Anforderungen zu erfüllen und die Trainingsziele zu erreichen, habe OpenAI eigenen Angaben zufolge „eine riesige Sammlung indexierter und zwischengespeicherter Webinhalte geschaffen, mit denen unsere Modelle interagieren können, ohne dass die Gefahr besteht, externe Systeme zu beeinträchtigen“. Ob diese Strategie genauso gut funktioniert wie das Training im offenen Internet, bleibt abzuwarten.

articles.title: Saudi proptech Ghanem raises $1.5 million pre-seed extension
articles.text:
Saudi proptech Ghanem raises $1.5 million pre-seed extension
- Saudi Arabia-based proptech startup Ghanem has raised an additional $1.5 million in a pre-seed extension round, backed by real estate companies and strategic angel investors, bringing the round's total to $8.6 million. Its previous $7.1 million financing included participation from Al-Romaih Group, while Waad VC has also invested in the company.
- Founded in 2025 by Saleh Waheed Al-Ghamdi and Amr Essam, Ghanem operates a fractional real estate ownership platform that allows individuals and institutions to invest in income-generating properties in Saudi Arabia, with minimum investments starting at SAR 1,000, depending on the opportunity.
- The additional funding will support product development, diversification of property investment opportunities and strategic partnerships, as the company expands its fractional ownership services.
Press release:
Ghanem, a company that specialises in fractional real estate ownership in Saudi Arabia, has closed an additional $1.5 million in funding, with participation from real estate companies and a group of strategic angel investors.
The funding extends the company’s pre-seed round, which previously raised $7.1 million with participation from Al-Romaih Group, bringing the total round, including the extension, to $8.6 million. Waad VC has also invested in the company.
The announcement follows a series of operational milestones for Ghanem. These include the execution of several real estate investment transactions through the company, a registered user base now numbering in the thousands, and the start of rental income distributions to investors without any payment disruptions.
Ghanem successfully issued digital ownership deeds to 580 individuals participating in the first income-generating real estate investment opportunity offered through the Ghanem app, documenting their fractional ownership stakes in the property.
Ghanem has also signed an agreement for digital integration with the Real Estate Registry (RER) and activated the connection, which is now live. This enables fractional ownership interests to be registered and deeds to be issued in investors’ names as part of an integrated digital experience. The initiative forms part of the platform’s technical and operational development and its efforts to simplify the property ownership process.
The company joined the regulatory sandbox of Saudi Arabia’s Real Estate General Authority (REGA) several months ago and launched its fractional ownership product within that environment, allowing the model to be tested and developed under regulatory supervision.
Ghanem provides access to Saudi real estate investment through fractional ownership of income-generating properties, with amounts starting at SAR 1,000, depending on the opportunity. The model combines the potential for rental income with ownership of a stake in a tangible real estate asset, which may support long-term investment stability. Properties undergo verification, due diligence and valuation before being offered on the platform, including reviews of ownership and relevant documents and valuations by accredited valuers.
All of Ghanem’s products have been approved as Sharia-compliant by the Sharia committee.
Saleh Waheed Al-Ghamdi, CEO and Co-Founder of Ghanem, said, "We are working to make property ownership more accessible through a clear digital experience and ownership documented in the investor’s name. We have executed real estate investment transactions, distributed monthly dividends with zero delays, attracted thousands of registered users, and activated our digital integration with the Real Estate Registry. These achievements give us a practical foundation on which to develop our services and improve the investor experience.”
Al-Ghamdi added, "This pre-seed extension provides important support for the next stage of our journey. We value our investors’ trust and the participation of real estate companies and strategic partners with direct market experience. We look forward to drawing on this expertise to develop our product, diversify real estate opportunities, and build partnerships that support Ghanem’s growth, while continuing to develop our solutions within the Real Estate General Authority’s regulatory sandbox.”
Ghanem was founded in 2025 by Saleh Waheed Al-Ghamdi and Amr Essam to develop fractional real estate ownership solutions and serve individuals and institutions in the Saudi market.

articles.title: How to avoid AI's 'valley of despair' - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
How to avoid AI’s ‘valley of despair’
Amdahl’s Law states that improving a single part of a system can only speed up the whole system so much. Even if one step of a process becomes exponentially faster, the other steps impose a ceiling unless they, too, are accelerated.
This concept may explain some of the disappointment companies are experiencing with artificial intelligence. An AI assistant can draft a proposal in seconds, but it then sits for days waiting on reviews, pricing and approval. Similarly, a coding tool can produce software in minutes, but testing, security and deployment still take days or weeks.
Companies have accelerated specific tasks without reengineering the systems that surround them. This gap between inflated expectations and modest returns is what some are calling AI’s “valley of despair.”
After a period of vigorous adoption and experimentation, executives are now being confronted with ever-growing costs and limited proof of bottom-line impact. Analyst firm Forrester Research Inc. recently found that only 15% of AI decision-makers reported an increase in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization over the past 12 months. Fewer than one-third could clearly map the value of AI back to bottom-line changes.
This skepticism is healthy; AI investments should face the same scrutiny as any other capital expense. Leaders need to be clear on expected returns, timelines and milestones that show whether their investment delivers measurable business results.
The productivity paradox
AI does have business-transforming potential, but small, localized productivity improvements aren’t game changers. Though giving employees access to general-purpose AI tools improves discrete tasks and builds fluency in the technology, this value is diffuse and disconnected from the metrics that determine business performance. This is Amdahl’s Law playing out at scale.
A more mature approach requires reassessing and reengineering how the business operates, applying AI to create fundamentally new operating processes. Whereas automation asks how existing tasks can be performed faster, reengineering asks whether that task should even exist. Organizations often seek to automate what they already do rather than reinvent it.
Time saved doesn’t automatically become revenue or margin, so what does AI ROI actually look like? Generally speaking, organizations should target positive, measurable change in one or more of the following areas: revenue, efficiency or risk. A quantifiable business goal might be to reduce customer churn, shorten the lead-to-proposal cycle, improve forecast accuracy or detect and manage fraud faster.
Enterprises should reasonably expect firm ROI data within about six months. Though leading indicators such as scenario testing and pilot programs can be delivered quickly, large-scale, immediate returns are unrealistic. A thoughtful business process redesign can take 90 to 120 days to design and implement, followed by acceptance testing and, crucially, focused change management.
These initiatives are most likely to succeed when people accountable for business results are charged with delivering a specific outcome rather than simply achieving a technology go-live.
Costs also deserve more sophisticated treatment, since the expense of various agentic processes can vary drastically based on factors like use case complexity, model calls and context. Companies should measure and track the distribution of cost per outcome rather than relying on a pre-deployment average.
This is an important nuance: Early adopters find that monitoring how much each AI-handled case costs and how long it takes, and then refining their strategy to keep both numbers within an acceptable range, is crucial for successfully redesigning business processes with AI.
Avoiding the ‘valley of despair’
Treat AI as a series of targeted business transformations, not solely a technology deployment. That means pairing clear outcomes with disciplined execution.
Take a closer look at business processes. Examine how work actually happens within the organization, not just how a procedure “should” happen. Identify bottlenecks, handoffs, approvals, exceptions and rework sources before deciding where to apply AI. Expect to find substantial differences between documented processes and how work actually gets done.
Tie every initiative to a clear outcome. Name the revenue, efficiency or risk metric the AI initiative is intended to impact, establish a baseline, give a business leader ownership of the result and set a hard timeline for impact data.
Design pilots for production. AI pilots should test the path to sustained use, not merely demonstrate impressive capabilities under controlled conditions. Include operational data, integration, governance, security and change-management requirements from the beginning.
Measure economics, not activity. Track metrics such as cycle time, quality, adoption, cost per outcome and financial impact rather than seats, prompts or demos. For agentic systems, monitor both the range and the average of operating costs, since complex cases can consume far more resources than simpler ones.
Review and adjust regularly. Review regularly to decide whether to move forward, narrow the scope, redesign the workflow or stop. Exploratory work won’t always succeed, but it should continually produce evidence that improves the next capital allocation.
AI’s “valley of despair” isn’t inevitable. Companies that understand the value of investing time and capital to rethink and reengineer their business processes can turn AI spend into tangible outcomes.
Jeremiah Stone is chief technology officer at SnapLogic Inc. He wrote this opinion article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Qué parte de tu sueldo se va en alquilar un piso en Europa, en tres mapas que sacan los colores a España
articles.text:
Si hay un tema que es una patata caliente para la ciudadanía y los gobiernos, ese es el de la vivienda y sino, que lo pregunten en Sol. Y es que los precios se han disparado como nunca en los últimos años, pero el drama, aunque generalizado, va por barrios: no es lo mismo comprar una casa en Madrid que en Soria. O alquilar un piso en Madrid que en Viena. Hasta hace poco comparar lo caro o barato que es alquilar una vivienda en Europa no era posible por la falta de datos homogéneos, así que la Red Europea De Observación Sobre Desarrollo y Cohesión Territorial lo ha remediado con tres mapas como tres soles.
La pregunta a la que contesta es: qué esfuerzo económico del sueldo hace falta para alquilar una vivienda y la respuesta varia enormemente en función de dónde vivas y también del tamaño. Detrás de esta colorida cartografía está el proyecto House for All, desarrollado por un consorcio europeo liderado por la Universidad Técnica de Viena y financiado por la UE y para su elaboración han tirado de todo un clásico entre quienes buscan piso: los anuncios de alquiler.
Tras rastrear cada semana portales inmobiliarios en toda Europa entre marzo de 2024 y marzo de 2025, recopilaron 22 millones de anuncios validos, lo que les permitió calcular el precio medio por municipio y a partir de ahí, compararlo con el ingreso medio a partir de datos de Eurostat. Hay tres mapas para tres tamaños de inmuebles: de 25 , 45 y 75 metros cuadrados respectivamente.
Para leer los mapas solo hace falta tener en cuanta algo: un municipio en turquesa significa que alquilar cuesta menos de un tercio del ingreso medio local, amarillo que cuesta entre un tercio y dos tercios y negro que la cosa esta muy negra: que el alquiler supera los dos tercios. Ojo, el gris indica que no hay datos, no que sea barato.
Un zulo estudio de 25 metros cuadrados
La buena noticia es que si hablamos de los inmuebles de 25 metros cuadrados o menos, el mapa es casi todo turquesa. Así, en Escandinavia, los países bálticos y buena parte de Francia, Alemania e Italia, alquilar un estudio cuesta menos de un tercio del ingreso local. Sobre el papel, si quieres vivir sola, a primera vista Europa parece bastante asequible. Aún así, no todo es azul en el mapa: en grandes ciudades de Polonia y Eslovaquia, en Portugal o en el litoral de Andalucía, Murcia y la Comunitat Valenciana, ya se ven zonas amarillas que indican entre un tercio y dos tercios del ingreso.
No obstante, este mapa tiene trampa: este mapa responde a cuánto costaría de media un estudio de este tamaño respecto al ingreso local, no si hay estudios disponibles de ese tamaño. De hecho, el informe señala que esos inmuebles son relativamente raros en la mayoría de los países europeos y más comunes en Suecia, Finlandia, Bulgaria, Polonia o Italia. Sin ir más lejos, en España chocarían con las condiciones mínimas de habitabilidad que, si bien depende de cada autonomía, en Madrid por ejemplo es de 40 metros cuadrados según el último Plan General de Ordenación Urbana, que data de 2023. ¿Que hay anuncios que claramente no cuentan con cédula de habitabilidad? Pues claro.
El pisito de 45 metros cuadrados
Este es el tamaño más común en Europa y el más realista para una persona que vive sola y donde los mapas empiezan a mostrar con claridad el problema. Según el informe, en gran parte de Portugal y del sur de España alquilar un pisito de 45 metros cuadrados consume entre un tercio y dos tercios del ingreso local, si bien hay varias zonas en ambos estados donde se pasa ese segundo umbral. Algo parecido sucede en Irlanda, sobre todo alrededor de Dublín y también en grandes ciudades de Alemania y Austria.
No obstante, en el centro y norte de Europa reina el turquesa, con la mayor parte de Francia en azul y predominando, aunque reñido, en Italia (de nuevo el amarillo aparece en las ciudades grandes).
El este de Europa cuenta otra historia. En Polonia, Hungría y partes de Rumanía el amarillo está bastante extendido con algunas manchas diseminadas negras. El informe lo explica tanto por los costes de la vivienda como por los ingresos locales bajos, algo extensivo a España y Portugal. Aquí hay una lección: el color depende tanto de lo que cuesta el piso como de lo que se gana.
Un piso de 75 metros cuadrados
El tercer mapa es el más duro de leer: según el informe, en casi todas las grandes ciudades europeas y en muchas zonas costeras turísticas, alquilar un piso de este tamaño resulta prácticamente imposible para quien cobra un solo sueldo. Así, hay zonas en el este de Europa, como Polonia, Hungría y Rumanía, donde el alquiler se lleva casi un sueldo medio. Portugal, el sur de España y la Riviera francesa destacan en negro por la presión del turismo y de las segundas residencias.
Eso sí, probablemente un inmueble de 75 metros cuadrados sea un tamaño más potencialmente interesante para compartir con alguien, por ejemplo para vivir en pareja. No obstante, esta percepción puede que esté condicionada inevitablemente por los precios ya que al fin y al cabo tampoco es que sean unas dimensiones desmesuradas para alguien que por ejemplo quiere una estancia propia para teletrabajar.
El alivio está en las zonas rurales o periféricas de Italia, Francia y los países bálticos, si bien en España hay que irse a sitios más rurales y desconectados. En Escandinavia, el azul sigue siendo el color dominante. Juegan en otra liga... entre otras cosas, de sueldos.
En Xataka | Alemania vs. Rumanía: el mapa de la vivienda en propiedad que cuenta la historia de las dos Europas

articles.title: Efficaces et colorés ? Xiaomi lancera ses Redmi Book 2027 sous puces Intel Wildcat Lake le 27 octobre
articles.text:
Xiaomi organisera le 27 octobre prochain un évènement qui lui permettra de dévoiler en détail deux nouveaux laptops : les Redmi Book 2027 de 14 et 16 pouces. Avec leurs couleurs pétantes et leurs puces Intel « Wildcat Lake », ces derniers devraient trouver facilement leur place sur le milieu de gamme… Même si l’on doute, hélas, de les voir arriver en France.
À l’instar de Dell et son nouvel XPS 13, ou d’Acer et son Swift Air 14 (testé récemment sur Clubic), Xiaomi tient maintenant lui aussi son modèle « Wildcat Lake ». Le constructeur chinois a confirmé la présentation, le 27 octobre prochain, de ses nouveaux Redmi Book 2027 de 14 et 16 pouces, deux nouveaux PC portables visant avant tout la productivité et le multimédia léger.
Wildcat Lake aux manettes, mais mystère sur l’écran embarqué…
Motorisés l’un comme l’autre par un processeur Intel Core de série 3 « Wildcat Lake », ces deux modèles s’appuient sur un châssis ayant été repensé. Ils profitent par ailleurs de nouveaux coloris violets et bleus, visibles sur les premiers visuels fournis par la marque.
À défaut de connaître l’ensemble de la fiche technique de ces nouveaux Redmi Book 2027 de 14 et 16 pouces (on ignore par exemple quels écrans ils embarquent, quelle est leur capacité de SSD ou leur vitesse de recharge), on apprend quand même que le modèle de 14 pouces pourra compter sur une batterie de 72 Wh et qu’on y trouvera deux ports USB-C, deux ports USB-A, une sortie HDMI et une prise casque.
Quid d’un lancement en France ?
De précédentes fuites nous éclairent enfin sur le processeur installé à bord du modèle de 16 pouces. Ce dernier miserait sur un Core 5 320 (6 cœurs) couplé à 16 Go de DDR5-4800. Pour rappel, cette puce combine 2 cœurs hautes performances cadencés à un maximum de 4,6 GHz, 4 cœurs haute efficacité, et un iGPU intégrant 2 cœurs Xe à 2,5 GHz.
Gravée selon le procédé 18A, comme les puces Core Ultra de série 3 « Panther Lake », elle s’en tient enfin à un TDP compris entre 15 et 35 W. Il y a, d’après nous, de bonnes chances que ce Core 5 320 soit installé sur les deux moutures du Xiaomi Redmi Book 2027, mais rien ne nous permet d’en être certains dans l'immédiat.
Reste maintenant à savoir si le Redmi Book 2027 sera commercialisé en France. La chose nous paraît improbable, puisque Xiaomi concentre ses efforts surtout sur les ventes de smartphones et de tablettes dans l’Hexagone, et que les précédents modèles de PC portables de la marque n’ont pas été distribués en France par les canaux officiels.
Source : VideoCardz

articles.title: I get frustrated with Spotify on Apple CarPlay — but Audi's new native app for the streaming service looks like a step forward
articles.text:
'It’s 100 per cent Spotify' — Audi launches first native Spotify for its cars, free from Google’s restrictions
Videos, lyrics DJ and Spotify Jam all now feature
- Audi is the first manufacturer to introduce Spotify’s ground-up app for cars
- New platform takes advantage of passenger screens
- A more comprehensive interface brings with it more features
Audi has announced that it is the first automaker to introduce Spotify’s dedicated in-car application, which has been co-developed by the music streaming service and the Volkswagen Group’s Cariad automotive software company.
Yes, a dedicated Spotify app already exists for cars running Android Automotive, such as those from Renault, Volvo and more, but that is a template-based solution, which uses standardized layouts and controls. It also keeps a tight lid on the myriad Spotify features that have been introduced over the past few years.
Jonathan Tarlton, Automotive Business Development Lead at Spotify, told The Verge that the company was “drawing all the pixels” during the development stages, going on to state that it owns the user experience and that it is “100 percent Spotify”.
Unlike the limited Google Automotive OS app, as well as the smartphone projections experienced by both Android and Apple users in Android Auto and CarPlay, the software debuting on Audi models uses a layout that feels more like the desktop experience, making the most of massive infotainment real estate.
When passenger screens are specified, for example, front-seat passengers can watch Spotify music videos while the vehicle is moving, they can also see real-time lyrics and scan QR codes to join listening parties or create ad-hoc road-trip playlists.
The large central display in Audi’s current line-up can do all of those things, but for safety reasons, this functionality is blocked as soon as the wheels start rolling.
Analysis: A slicker Spotify experience
Audi says that this is the first time that music videos and real-time lyrics, as well as popular features like Spotify Jam and Spotify DJ have been featured on a native app, but doesn’t mention if or when it will be arriving on other models within the Volkswagen Group or further afield.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Judging from the imagery Audi has provided, the native app looks a lot cleaner than anything currently found on Android Automotive OS, with a layout that closely mimics the set-up found on laptops and desktops.
I don’t now about you, but I often get frustrated with the limited capabilities of the Apple CarPlay projection, as well as the clunky music search functionality. I often end up listening to the same old playlists on repeat because of this.
In contrast, Audi says that its AI-powered voice assistant works seamlessly to control the music while driving, with the “Hey Audi” command used to switch playlists or search for individual tracks.
Spotify users must have an account and use a smartphone to sign in, but Audi says the new Spotify app can be downloaded from the Audi Application Store free of charge.

Leon has been navigating a world where automotive and tech collide for almost 20 years, reporting on everything from in-car entertainment to robotised manufacturing plants. Currently, EVs are the focus of his attentions, but give it a few years and it will be electric vertical take-off and landing craft. Outside of work hours, he can be found tinkering with distinctly analogue motorcycles, because electric motors are no replacement for an old Honda inline four.

articles.title: TIM Beta começa a mudar para clientes antigos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
TIM Beta começa a mudar para clientes antigos
Operadora dá acesso ao BetaCreator por meio de convite. Novo plano oferece 50 GB e permite acumular internet.
A TIM começou a enviar convites para clientes do TIM Beta aderirem ao BetaCreator. A mensagem enviada pela operadora chega com o código de ativação, que deve ser resgatado em até 48 horas. O Tecnoblog teve acesso ao comunicado nesta sexta-feira (23/10).
Os clientes do Beta estão entre os primeiros a receber os convites. Oficializado há três dias, o BetaCreator reformula o plano tradicional, mas mantém a mensalidade de R$ 60. A franquia de internet sobe para 50 GB, e os dados não utilizados podem ser acumulados para os meses seguintes, sem expirar enquanto a linha permanecer ativa no plano.
A adesão ao BetaCreator é feita exclusivamente por convite, sem migração automática. Quem preferir ignorar e permanecer no TIM Beta, pode continuar no plano antigo.
Os atuais assinantes estão entre os primeiros a receber o acesso, na categoria Beta Founder, mas a TIM também distribuirá convites a influenciadores e criadores de conteúdo para compartilhá-los com seus seguidores.
| Característica do plano | TIM Beta | BetaCreator | 
|---|---|---|
| Mensalidade | R$ 60 | R$ 60 | 
| Internet móvel | Até 20 GB | 50 GB | 
| Acúmulo de internet | Não | Sim | 
| Redes sociais | Conforme as regras de cada plano | Instagram, Facebook, TikTok e X | 
| TIM Mais e Deezer | Conforme as regras de cada plano | Incluídos | 
| Contratação | Possibilidade de entrar por meio de promoção de recargas | Exclusivamente por convite | 
Segundo a operadora, o plano não poderá ser contratado por outros canais. Os convites serão distribuídos por criadores de conteúdo parceiros, que deverão divulgar o BetaCreator mensalmente nas redes.
Quem ainda não é cliente da TIM e deseja resgatar os códigos que serão distribuídos por influenciadores precisa ativar um chip pré-pago da operadora. Depois de receber o convite, basta ativá-lo na seção BetaCreator do aplicativo Meu TIM.

articles.title: YMTC to Start Mass Production of LPDDR5X with 9,600 MT/s Speed
articles.text:
Friday, October 23rd 2026
YMTC to Start Mass Production of LPDDR5X with 9,600 MT/s Speed
YMTC, known as a NAND Flash manufacturer, is reportedly preparing to start mass production of LPDDR5X memory. While it has been known for some time that YMTC plans to enter DRAM production alongside its main NAND Flash business, it was not widely known that the company had already begun low-scale manufacturing. According to Counterpoint Research, YMTC has been producing about 5,000 wafers per month of 16 Gb LPDDR5X DRAM running at 7,500 MT/s at its Fab 2 since October 2025. The company is now preparing to begin volume production of LPDDR5X memory with speeds of 9,600 MT/s at its Fab 3, using Vertical Channel Transistor (VCT) 4F² cell structure technology.
YMTC has a significant advantage with 3D silicon, which represents the next phase of memory evolution. With its Xtacking 4.0 technology, YMTC can separate memory cell wafers from peripheral logic circuits and combine them using hybrid bonding wafer-to-wafer stacking. Hybrid bonding creates a permanent bond between two silicon chips using embedded metal bumps that are fused together to form a single chip. Multiple dies or entire silicon wafers can be connected by stacking the back ends of two chips together.Even if the company continues large-scale manufacturing of LPDDR5X, it can easily transition into 3D DRAM with its Xtacking 4.0 or possibly a future 5.0 iteration, which has yet to be seen. Micron recently confirmed that it will not bring 4F² DRAM to market, remaining focused on the 6F² layout used in today's DRAM until 3D DRAM arrives. YMTC, along with CXMT, is pushing for 4F² adoption first, which means that Chinese memory makers might have a slight advantage in cell design, despite being limited by DUV lithography tools. However, once 3D DRAM is ready for mass manufacturing, YMTC is one of the best-positioned companies to capitalize on it.

articles.title: NASA updates lander plans for Moon landings, finally solves long-festering Orion issue
articles.text:
During a lengthy news conference on Friday, NASA provided a detailed overview of how it plans to return astronauts to the lunar surface as soon as 2028 as part of its Artemis Program.
Although much of the information behind these plans has been previously reported at Ars Technica and elsewhere, this marked the first time NASA has laid them out in detail and acknowledged some substantial changes in the architecture.
Most notably, for SpaceX’s Starship vehicle, the revised plan calls for the Orion spacecraft to dock with the Starship lunar lander in high-Earth orbit before transiting to the Moon. And for Blue Origin, the mission architecture includes four launches of the New Glenn rocket, but no spacecraft-to-spacecraft refuelings. Additionally, the Blue Origin plans allows for the possibility of its Blue Moon lander rendezvousing with Orion in low-Lunar orbit.
During the presentation on Friday, NASA officials said they continue to anticipate launching the Artemis III mission—a demonstration involving docking with both Blue Moon and Starship near Earth—by “summer” 2027. And they are still tracking toward a 2028 launch of Artemis IV, which would involve an actual landing on the lunar surface.
“This is an achievable path we are on right now,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said. “We have the mandate, we have the resources, and the support from our stakeholders to be able to execute, and that’s what we intend to do.”
It is commendable that Isaacman and his leadership have taken a hard look every element of the Artemis Program and sought to make changes where they can help the lunar lander companies execute and accelerate their plans. But can they hold to those dates?
The SpaceX plan
The biggest ask SpaceX engineers had in meetings with NASA in early 2026 was removing the requirement to dock with Orion in a near-rectilinear halo orbit around the Moon. This required more energy and had other difficulties associated with it. When NASA canceled the Lunar Gateway earlier this year, it solved this problem for SpaceX.

articles.title: China can make advanced chips without EUV, but the bill keeps growing
articles.text:
China can make advanced chips without EUV, but the bill keeps growing — DUV multiple patterning means bigger dies, lower yields, and longer manufacturing times
China has shown that older DUV lithography can be stretched much further than many expected – but can it fully catch up?
Export controls have kept ASML's most advanced EUV lithography machines out of China. Instead, the country's chipmaking industry has relied on less-capable deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machines. By using multiple exposures on critical chip layers, these older machines are still capable of producing performant silicon. However, as multiple patterns are applied there are more chances for defects, longer manufacturing times, and higher bills. We spoke to experts like Chris Mack, co-founder and CTO of semiconductor firm Fractilia, to find out how much further DUV can go.
For years, extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography has been seen as China’s biggest choke point in the country’s attempts to build cutting-edge chips. The machines, made exclusively by Dutch manufacturer ASML, use 13.5nm-wavelength light to print some of the most intricate features found on modern processors. Sales of ASML’s EUV systems are subject to export restrictions, forcing Chinese manufacturers to squeeze ever more out of older deep ultraviolet, or DUV, lithography instead. The EUV gap alone between China and the West is at least half a decade, according to some analysts.
But even without access to EUV machines, China has gotten surprisingly far in recreating what it offers through existing technology.
Teardowns of Huawei’s Mate 60 Pro in 2023 found the phone’s Kirin 9000S processor had been made by SMIC using a second-generation 7nm-class manufacturing process without EUV. More recently, analysis of Huawei’s Kirin 9030 found SMIC had pushed its DUV-based process closer still to the density associated with 5nm manufacturing – although it continued to lag behind the leading processes used by TSMC and Samsung.
Multiple patterning
The trick is multiple patterning. Rather than trying to print an overly intricate chip layer in a single pass, Chinese manufacturers are dividing up the complex design into several simpler patterns. Repeat the process enough times and you can etch up something approximating the proper layer you intended.
The trick works. But according to lithography expert Chris Mack, co-founder and CTO of Fractilia, asking whether a chip can be made without EUV overlooks the trade-offs manufacturers make in order to do it.
“When this transition first began, what everyone in the industry said as conventional wisdom is that cost-wise, three exposures on a 193 immersion tool cost about the same as one exposure on an EUV tool,” Mack said in an interview with Tom’s Hardware Premium. “At three, it was about even,” Mack explained. “But as soon as you hit four masks – 193 masks being replaced by one EUV mask – then EUV became more cost-effective.”
It’s also likely to produce a higher quality product with fewer defects. Each time a wafer is patterned, that new pattern has to line up perfectly with everything that’s already been etched beneath it. The more individual exposures needed to produce a single layer, the more opportunities there are for things to go wrong. “If you have, say, four 193 masks, you've got all those different overlays, and you've got all these different process variations that start to accumulate,” Mack said.
Chip designers can try and avoid that by leaving more space around features so the finished processor can actually be manufactured reliably. But that means the chip ends up bigger – and bigger chips become expensive very quickly. Making each die larger means fewer fit on every wafer, and wafers cost a lot of money – tens of thousands of dollars each.
“You don't sell wafers, you sell die,” Mack said. “The question is: how many die can I fit onto that wafer, and how many of those die yield, and therefore how many chips can I sell per wafer?”
The efficiency gap
There is some evidence of what that efficiency gap can look like in practice – albeit in memory rather than logic chips. In a June report, Morgan Stanley estimated that Chinese DRAM manufacturer CXMT was producing only around one-third as many bits per wafer as Western competitors. The analysts believed the older process node only accounted for around a third of that shortfall, but said access to lithography was a “hard ceiling” on Chinese memory development. “For advanced logic chips, in theory there could be other innovations to engineer around EUV, but they are not likely to be very efficient and effective,” said Douglas Fuller, a researcher at Copenhagen Business School, in comments to Tom’s Hardware Premium.
It is also why claims that China has reached a particular semiconductor process “node” need to be treated with caution. “If somebody says it's X node – the seven nanometer node, the five nanometer node, the three nanometer node – these words almost have no meaning,” Mack said.
That can be seen in SMIC’s latest chips. Reporting suggests its N+3 process represents meaningful progress towards 5nm-class manufacturing – but the actual measurements show it remains significantly less scaled than established 5nm processes from Samsung and TSMC. That doesn’t mean DUV has reached the end of its useful exploitation.
Stretching DUV's efficacy
Micron is an example of how far DUV can be stretched, producing competitive DRAM chips using DUV, multiple patterning and tight process control. Its 1-alpha generation of chips was developed without EUV. “They pushed 193 farther than any of the other memory makers did,” Mack said. “They were able to make very competitive chips with 100% 193 compared to Samsung and Hynix making them with many layers of EUV.”
Morgan Stanley believes CXMT’s planned move to 1-alpha DRAM – which it wants to use for HBM3e – is achievable without access to EUV, citing Micron as evidence. Indeed, “by the end of the decade, advanced packaging will allow firms to use DUV to produce the latest generations of DRAM,” reckons Fuller.
Micron also designed its products around the manufacturing technology available to it, rather than simply trying to recreate an EUV process on older equipment – something which could be a useful lesson for Chinese manufacturers. “If the entire ecosystem of 193 immersion were available to China,” Mack explained, “then they could probably push a long way with 193 multiple patterning, especially if they optimise designs for the fact that they're going to be using that.”
But Micron was making memory, whose highly repetitive structures make close co-ordination between chip design and manufacturing easier than it is for the much more complicated logic processors found in phones and computers.
“Memory is a lot easier than logic,” Mack said.
And even Micron eventually concluded that EUV was worth using. Its newer 1-gamma DRAM process uses EUV lithography, with Micron saying the technology helps it achieve more than 30% greater bit density per wafer than its preceding 1-beta generation.
EUV is hardly a magic wand, either. Mack points to stochastic effects – tiny random variations caused by the small number of photons involved in an exposure – which mean manufacturers can improve pattern control by increasing the EUV exposure dose. But it also pushes the cost back up quickly.
Because of that, Mack believes there is ultimately a limit to how far multiple patterning can economically substitute for EUV. “I would be hard pressed to really believe that a three nanometer or a two nanometer node is going to be economically viable without EUV,” he said.
That doesn’t mean Chinese chipmakers simply hit a technological wall and stop. They can keep pushing DUV while accepting larger dies, poorer yields, longer manufacturing times – or some combination of all three.
They can also throw capacity and money at part of the problem. Morgan Stanley assumes CXMT remains stuck on its 1-alpha process without EUV, yet still increases its share of global DRAM bit supply from 14% in 2026 to 16% in 2028 simply by building more greenfield capacity. The bank also expects China’s AI chip self-sufficiency to rise from 42% in 2025 to 70% by 2030 through new advanced-node capacity, improving yields and heavy state support – while EUV, HBM and advanced software leave a persistent gap. And so without EUV, the experts reckon China can only get partway to bridging the gap with the West. ““I would be hard pressed,” said Mack, “to really believe that a three nanometer or a two nanometer node is going to be economically viable without EUV.”
Chris Stokel-Walker is a Tom's Hardware contributor who focuses on the tech sector and its impact on our daily lives— online and offline. He is the author of How AI Ate the World, published in 2024, as well as TikTok Boom, YouTubers, and The History of the Internet in Byte-Sized Chunks.

articles.title: As chip prices surge, EV maker Ultraviolette is working on ways to absorb costs
articles.text:
As chip prices surge, EV maker Ultraviolette is working on ways to absorb costs
Bengaluru-based Ultraviolette—which produces high-performance electric motorcycles—says it will not pass on the input costs to customers.
The global shortage of memory chips has driven up costs, placing a huge strain on electric vehicle makers in the country.
Bengaluru-based Ultraviolette—which produces high-performance electric motorcycles—says it will not pass on the high input costs to customers and is exploring other ways to tide over the situation.
Memory chips are a critical component of an electric vehicle, used to store data, run control software, and manage real-time operations across critical systems.
According to Ultraviolette’s Founder and CTO, Niraj Rajmohan, RAM (random access memory) alone adds Rs 20,000 to the cost of a vehicle. With global companies building very large data centres, there has been a surge in memory chip consumption, he added.
AI data centres are projected to consume 70% of global memory chip production in 2026. The data centre boom has led to a supply crunch, subsequently shoring up costs of chips.
But it would not be fair to pass on the costs to customers, said Rajmohan, adding that a threefold jump in memory prices in recent times cannot translate into a threefold jump in the price of an electric bike, and customers cannot be asked to suddenly pay far more.
The company is working on alternatives to absorb costs.
For now, Ultraviolette is scouting for alternative parts, including software, components and technologies, and alternative manufacturers to partner with.
The company is also relying on partners who hold a stake in the company, including TVS, TDK Ventures, and Intel, for their knowhow and expertise, said Rajmohan. He, however, did not elaborate on the alternatives.
Rajmohan was speaking at the launch of X-47 Venom, Ultraviolette’s first bike built on its new platform ‘VX-100’,
What is VX-100?
VX-100 is a 100V electric powertrain architecture that seeks to improve performance and efficiency in electric two-wheelers.
An electric powertrain architecture is the integrated system of energy storage, electronics, and mechanical components that converts stored electrical energy into mechanical motion to propel the vehicle.
Rather than upgrading the parts one at a time, Ultraviolette has redesigned the battery, motor, and control electronics together, as one system.
The X-47 Venom is the first bike built on this new architecture. The company claims it offers better battery cooling, lighter components, and stronger power delivery, along with support for DC fast charging at up to 12 kW.
Most electric two-wheelers run on 48V, said Rajmohan, adding that the telecom industry and Southeast Asian manufacturers built their systems around it.
At 100V, X-47 Venom’s system draws lower current, and hence produces less heat. The objective is to provide high speed and better performance without the heat, energy loss, and extra weight that usually come with electric vehicles.
Currently, Qualcomm supplies the chips that power the bike's new dashboard, while TDK provides the RF (radio frequency) components and capacitors.
The X-47 Venom is priced at Rs 2,65,000 for the first 5,000 buyers. Bookings opened on October 22, and deliveries are set to start in November. The European launch will happen on November 3 at EICMA, an international motorcycle expo in Milan.
The bike has undergone extensive test rides covering 150 to 200 km a day for several months, said Rajmohan.
Ultraviolette’s product portfolio includes the F77 sports bike that is targeted at sports enthusiasts, while the X-47 Crossover is intended to appeal to a broader set of customers, including sports, adventure and street riders. The Crossover makes up about 90% of the company’s sales.
The new VX-100 platform will go into all of Ultraviolette’s forthcoming products. Four launches are expected next year, including the Tesseract (a scooter) and Shockwave (an Enduro motorcycle), and an upgraded F77 bike.
Roughly 90% of sales come from India and 10% from abroad, including the European market, where the company has been expanding. There are more than 7,000 Ultraviolette bikes on the roads worldwide today.
Ultraviolette was founded in 2016 by Narayan Subramaniam and Niraj Rajmohan. Its backers include Lingotto, TDK Ventures, Qualcomm Ventures, Zoho Corporation, TVS Motors, Yali Capital, and Speciale Invest.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Panne Orange : comment obtenir jusqu’à 10 euros de remise en plus de la data offerte
articles.text:
Pour se faire pardonner la panne qui a privé ses abonnés de réseau mobile pendant près de dix heures mercredi, Orange a choisi de doubler leur enveloppe de données pendant un mois. Un geste peu utile pour la plupart d’entre eux : un client mobile consomme en moyenne 19,3 Go par mois, selon l’Arcep, bien loin des 100 Go ou plus inclus dans de nombreux forfaits. Certains abonnés ont donc tenté leur chance auprès du service client, et plusieurs d’entre eux ont obtenu gain de cause, comme nous avons pu le vérifier.
Sur X, un client Sosh raconte ainsi avoir obtenu, en plus de la data doublée, une remise de 10 euros sur son forfait à 15,99 euros, et de 1 euro sur un second forfait à 1,99 euro. « C’est déjà mieux que rien ! », se félicite-t-il. Matthieu Audibert, client Orange, assure quant à lui qu’« en 5 min c’était pris en charge ». Il a reçu dans la foulée un SMS d’Orange l’informant que sa réclamation avait été traitée, puis un e-mail intitulé « Votre dédommagement » lui confirmant « un geste commercial de 10.00 € », déduit « du montant de [sa] prochaine facture ou de la suivante, si celle-ci a déjà été émise ». Un autre client de Sosh, Guillaume Rozier, a lui aussi obtenu 10 euros, en passant par le chat du service client et en demandant à parler à un conseiller humain.
 Vous pouvez contacter le service client d’Orange
En 5 min c’était pris en charge https://t.co/6VqZSxeRSh
— Matthieu Audibert (@MattAudibert) October 22, 2026
Si de nombreux clients témoignent, le montant n’est toutefois pas le même pour tout le monde et certains abonnés doivent se contenter de remise de 1 ou 2 euros. Enfin, d’autres abonnés n’obtiennent rien de plus que la data doublée. L’ancienneté de la ligne peut notamment entrer en compte dans l’obtention d’une remise.
 Client Sosh / Orange
Suite à la panne du 21 Octobre, en dédommagement l’enveloppe data sera doublée au renouvellement du forfait.
+ 10.00€ de remise sur mon forfait à 15,99€
+ 1.00€ de remise sur mon forfait à 1,99€
C’est déjà mieux que rien! 🙂 🙏
#orange #orangepanne https://t.co/wQI8YfDALU
— Noham 👨🏻🔧 (@noh_tech) October 22, 2026
Comment faire la demande ?
Cette remise n’a rien d’automatique et il faut la réclamer. Contactez le service client au 3900 (service gratuit, prix d’un appel) ou faites une réclamation depuis votre espace client ou le site d’assistance d’Orange. Expliquez en quoi la panne du 21 octobre vous a gêné, et précisez que le doublement de la data ne vous est d’aucune utilité. Les abonnés Sosh, eux, passent par l’assistance en ligne : il faut demander à l’assistant virtuel Djingo à parler à un conseiller humain, une astuce qui vaut aussi pour le chat d’Orange.
N’hésitez pas à demander explicitement une remise de 10 euros, mais gardez toutefois en tête que ce geste reste à la discrétion du service client. Ni les conditions générales d’Orange ni celles de Sosh ne prévoient une telle remise pour une panne de cette durée : le montant prévu par le contrat d’Orange, au prorata de la coupure, ne dépasse pas quelques dizaines de centimes, et celui de Sosh n’en prévoit en principe pas. Rien ne garantit donc que tous les abonnés obtiendront 10 euros, et la réponse pourrait varier d’un conseiller à l’autre, surtout si les demandes affluent. Pour tout savoir sur ce que prévoient les contrats et les recours possibles, consultez notre article dédié pour demander un remboursement.

articles.title: Besoin d’un aspirateur sans fil polyvalent et pas cher ? Le Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 descend à 103,99 € chez Amazon
articles.text:
L’aspirateur-balai sans fil Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 permet de passer du nettoyage des sols à celui des meubles en un seul changement d’accessoire. En ce moment, cet appareil polyvalent est disponible au prix de 103,99 € au lieu de 159,99 € sur Amazon.
Tout le monde n’a pas besoin d’un coûteux aspirateur-balai laveur : parfois, disposer d’un aspirateur sans fil capable de se transformer en aspirateur à main pour aspirer les miettes ou dépoussiérer une étagère s’avère bien plus approprié. C’est ce que permet de faire le Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 RH6836EO, disponible à 103,99 € au lieu de 159,99 € chez Amazon. Accompagné de quatre accessoires en plus de sa brosse motorisée, c’est un investissement intéressant pour un foyer avec des enfants.
Le Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 gris avec quatre accessoires est à 103,99 €, contre un prix conseillé de 159,99 €, chez Amazon, et sa livraison est offerte.
Pourquoi choisir le Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 ?
- Pour sa polyvalence : le bloc détachable se transforme en aspirateur à main pour nettoyer les meubles, les escaliers ou l’habitacle d’une voiture.
- Pour sa brosse éclairée : les LED aident à repérer la poussière dans les zones sombres, notamment sous les meubles.
- Pour sa batterie amovible : elle peut être remplacée lorsqu’elle s’use afin de prolonger la durée de vie de l’appareil.
Des accessoires adaptés aux nettoyages du quotidien
De base, le Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 s’utilise avec sa brosse motorisée montée sur son tube, afin de vous permettre d’entretenir tous vos sols facilement. La version vendue par Amazon est accompagnée de deux brossettes intégrées, d’un suceur fente et d’un large suceur destiné aux tissus d’ameublement. Vous pouvez, ainsi, utiliser votre aspirateur dans de nombreuses situations, y compris pour nettoyer votre voiture ou des zones de votre logement qui sont généralement difficiles d’accès.
Son bac collecteur de 0,55 litre se vide sans sac et se démonte facilement pour être entretenu. Côté autonomie, Rowenta annonce jusqu’à 45 minutes en mode Eco et en configuration aspirateur à main.
Autonomie ou puissance, il faut parfois choisir
L’autonomie et le format du Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 le rendent particulièrement adapté aux petites séances de nettoyage, avec un mode Boost qui permet d’augmenter temporairement sa puissance d’aspiration. En revanche, ce mode sollicite davantage la batterie et réduit donc l’autonomie disponible.
✅ Les points forts
- Convertible en aspirateur à main.
- Brosse motorisée avec éclairage LED.
- Batterie amovible et indice de réparabilité de 9/10.
❌ Les limites
- Autonomie maximale annoncée uniquement en mode Eco
- Recharge complète d’environ quatre heures.
L’aspirateur Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 est disponible à 103,99 € sur Amazon, avec sa base de charge et son chargeur.
Si votre logement est de taille moyenne et qu’il ne comprend pas de moquette ou de tapis dans toutes les pièces, alors l’aspirateur sans fil Rowenta X-Pert 6.60 se présente comme un choix adapté à la situation.
Par contre, pour nettoyer de grandes surfaces ou beaucoup de tapis, mieux vaut privilégier un modèle plus endurant et performant afin de ne pas avoir à recharger l’appareil au milieu d’une séance de nettoyage.

articles.title: Arm Comments on Jury Decision in Qualcomm Trial - EE Times
articles.text:
Following our initial coverage of the Delaware federal jury verdict in the Qualcomm and Arm dispute, Arm contacted EE Times to clarify the IP vendor’s position. In a phone interview with EE Times, Arm CMO Ami Badani discussed the company’s stance on the jury’s decision and the stakes surrounding licensing negotiations for Arm’s next-generation v10 architecture.
Badani contended that Arm emerged as a “victor” in court due to the nominal $2 damages award and the presiding judge’s reluctance to oversee future licensing terms, while emphasizing the ongoing technical and commercial collaboration with Qualcomm.
She also commented on the rise of other architectures such as RISC-V, as experts caution that restrictive proprietary frameworks may compel semiconductor designers toward open standards to meet the demands of evolving AI workloads.
Arm characterizes nominal damages and judicial limits as victory
Badani, who attended several proceedings in Wilmington, argued that the jury’s decision to award Qualcomm just $2 in nominal damages supports Arm’s position. The jury awarded $1 for a licensing breach and $1 for interference with Qualcomm’s business relationship with Meta, while finding for Arm on other allegations.
She argued that the minimal financial penalty supported Arm’s position that it operated in good faith throughout its licensing relationship with Qualcomm and that its conduct did not warrant substantial monetary damages.
Badani cited recent Bloomberg reporting on closing arguments in the case before U.S. District Judge Maryellen Noreika. During the hearing, Judge Noreika expressed strong reservations about Qualcomm’s request for the court to compel Arm to negotiate in good faith new licensing terms for its upcoming v10 architecture.
The judge characterized Qualcomm’s bid for judicial oversight of commercial terms as “very, very drastic,” remarking that the court would not step in to regulate Arm’s business practices or act as a regulatory supervisor.
Furthermore, Badani cited the court’s reluctance to dictate contractual rates or grant additional financial remedies as further support for Arm’s position. She also indicated that a final written ruling on the remaining antitrust and licensing claims could take several weeks, as both corporate parties complete their final written submissions for judicial review.
Despite the four-year court battle, Badani emphasized that Arm and Qualcomm maintain ongoing technical and commercial collaboration. She noted that, in Arm’s view, Qualcomm is not actively seeking further monetary compensation, but rather attempting to maximize the commercial and technical value derived from its ongoing licensing relationship.
Traction for RISC-V
Badani also directly addressed industry analysis suggesting that open-standard instruction set architectures, specifically RISC-V, are the primary beneficiaries of the legal conflict between two of the semiconductor sector’s largest partners. She rejected claims that RISC-V is capturing significant commercial market share from proprietary architectures in mainstream global markets.
According to Badani, RISC-V is not obtaining meaningful traction as an alternative processor architecture outside of China. She attributed its growth in China’s domestic market primarily to substantial state financial backing and direct government push, rather than organic commercial displacement of established instruction sets in international markets.
Her comments contrast with views from Qualcomm and prominent computer architecture researchers evaluating long-term hardware trends. Last week, Akeana, a U.S. semiconductor startup that designs processors using RISC-V architecture, was acquired by Qualcomm. Akeana’s CEO confirmed the acquisition in a LinkedIn post.
Evolving AI requires more architectural freedom
As AI algorithms and models advance rapidly, chip designers need flexibility to modify processor cores, add specialized microarchitectural features, and improve overall energy efficiency.
“As AI is evolving, chip designers need total flexibility to adapt their cores with new functions and improve performance,” Mateo Valero, director of the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC), told EE Times. “Relying on closed ISAs such as Arm limits the freedom and the possibility to implement new capabilities and improve power consumption. Even the largest companies using Arm’s IP with full architectural licenses have difficulties optimizing their designs due to Arm’s tight conditions and limited support. That’s why we believe that open standard ISAs such as RISC-V offer the best alternative.”
Ultimately, Arm views the $2 nominal damages award and the court’s reluctance to intervene in licensing negotiations as validation of its good-faith practices. However, the implications of the four-year legal battle extend far beyond the Wilmington courtroom. Although Arm and Qualcomm continue to collaborate on technical matters and product roadmaps, the legal friction highlights a pivotal juncture for chip designers.
See also:
Qualcomm Wins Key Claims Against Arm, but Damages Total Just $2
Arm Sues Qualcomm Over Nuvia Licenses
