articles.title: Unerwartetes Wetterphänomen: Wie sich auf dem Mars eine 1.800 Kilometer lange Wolke formt
articles.text:
1.800 Kilometer lang und völlig ohne Staub: Das Rätsel um Mars-Wolke ist gelöst
Die europäische Weltraumorganisation Esa hat neue Daten zur sogenannten Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud veröffentlicht. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Nature veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, entsteht dieses langgestreckte Gebilde durch einen bisher in planetaren Atmosphären nicht beobachteten Mechanismus. Dieser physikalische Prozess, die sogenannte homogene Keimbildung, vollzieht sich gänzlich ohne die Anwesenheit von Kondensationskernen wie Staub oder Schmutzpartikeln.
Dabei galt in der meteorologischen Forschung bislang ein fester Grundsatz: Wasserdampf benötigt zwingend Staub oder andere winzige Partikel, um zu kondensieren. Da die Atmosphäre des Mars extrem staubig ist, nahmen bisherige Klimamodelle diesen Vorgang stets als alleinigen Standardmechanismus an.
Die aktuellen Computersimulationen eines Forschungsteams um Jorge Hernández-Bernal und Franck Forget von der französischen Sorbonne Université in Paris widerlegen dies nun. Sie zeigen, dass diese etablierte Grundannahme für die lange Arsia-Mons-Wolke schlichtweg nicht gilt.
Wie der Mars-Vulkan das Wetter extrem beschleunigt
Der rund 20 Kilometer hohe Vulkan Arsia Mons wirkt auf den Marswind wie eine gigantische Rampe. Wenn die Luftströmungen auf das massive Hindernis treffen, werden sie als atmosphärische Wellen mit hoher Geschwindigkeit nach oben gedrückt. Dabei reißen sie feuchte Luftmassen mit sich, die durch den schnell sinkenden Luftdruck extrem rasant abkühlen. Innerhalb von nur zehn Minuten stürzt die Temperatur um 30 Grad ab.
Dieser rapide Temperatursturz führt zu einer massiven Übersättigung in der Atmosphäre. Die Feuchtigkeitswerte schnellen auf ein Level, das 100.000 Mal höher liegt als unter durchschnittlichen Bedingungen auf der Erde. In dieser physikalischen Extremsituation benötigt der Wasserdampf keinen Staubkorn-Anker mehr, um zu kondensieren. Er gefriert direkt und spontan zu winzigen Eiskristallen.
In der Physik wird dieses direkte Einfrieren von Wasserdampf ohne Schmutzpartikel als homogene Keimbildung bezeichnet. Als das Forschungsteam genau diesen Prozess mathematisch in sein Computer-Klimamodell einspeiste, bildete die Software die lange Marswolke plötzlich fehlerfrei ab. Laut dem Hauptautor Jorge Hernández-Bernal beweist das, dass dieser Prozess in der Natur tatsächlich vorkommt, obwohl er in den Lehrbüchern bislang nur als reine Theorie behandelt wurde.
Die Grenzen der Computersimulation
Ganz fehlerfrei ist das Computermodell allerdings noch nicht. Vergleicht man die Simulation mit den echten Satellitenbildern, fällt die künstlich berechnete Wolke schmaler aus. Zudem lässt das System sie zeitlich etwas zu spät entstehen. Daran lässt sich gut ablesen, wo die Programmierung von Wettermodellen für fremde Planeten noch an ihre Grenzen stößt.
Zudem reagiert die Software extrem empfindlich auf kleinste Stellschrauben. Verändern die Forscher:innen im Code beispielsweise nur die Parameter für die Oberflächenspannung der winzigen Eiskristalle, formt sich im Modell sofort eine Wolke mit völlig anderen Abmessungen. Das zeigt sehr anschaulich, wie stark mikroskopische Details das großflächige Wettergeschehen beeinflussen können.
Mars Express liefert die visuellen Beweise
Die Grundlage für die erfolgreiche Simulation lieferte die europäische Raumsonde Mars Express. Sie umkreist den Roten Planeten bereits seit dem Jahr 2003 und hat die langgestreckte Wolke wiederholt fotografiert. Weil ihre spezielle Flugbahn direkte Beobachtungen in den frühen Morgenstunden erlaubt, konnte das Kamerasystem das rasante tägliche Wachstum der Struktur ziemlich genau dokumentieren.
Laut dem Projektwissenschaftler Colin Wilson lassen sich so Veränderungen der Wolke innerhalb weniger Stunden gut nachvollziehen. Das macht die Raumsonde zu einem wichtigen Werkzeug, um kurzlebige Wetterphänomene auf dem Mars zu überwachen.
Das Forschungsteam will diese neuen Erkenntnisse nun nutzen, um das Klima auf anderen Himmelskörpern besser zu verstehen. Die Forscher:innen gehen davon aus, dass solche extremen und bislang rein theoretischen physikalischen Abläufe auch das Wetter auf weit entfernten Exoplaneten bestimmen. Dort laufen klassische irdische Erklärungsmodelle oft schlichtweg ins Leere.

articles.title: C'est officiel, Samsung va lancer un nouveau smartphone pliant ultra luxueux
articles.text:
Alors que Samsung a déjà commercialisé trois smartphones pliants cette année, le Galaxy Z Flip 8, le Galaxy Z Fold 8 et le Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, une nouvelle déclinaison pointe le bout de son nez. La branche chinoise de la marque coréenne a officialisé l’évènement sur Weibo avec une image promotionnelle mettant en avant un appareil au format livre doté d’un cadre doré.
Un design luxueux réservé au marché chinois
Selon le bien informé Ice Universe, le téléphone Samsung qui se cache derrière ses bordures dorées est bien le Samsung W27. Le leaker a même montré une image du smartphone avec un bloc caméra doré assorti au châssis et un logo arrière différent.
Les fans de la marque devront cependant se faire une raison puisque cette déclinaison sera exclusive à la Chine. Il faudra donc passer par la case importation si vous voulez mettre la main dessus. Au-delà du logo, cette version se distingue surtout par ses finitions dorées dont le marché chinois raffole.
Une fiche technique héritée du Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra
Sous cette coque luxueuse, le smartphone devrait reprendre à l’identique les caractéristiques du Z Fold 8 Ultra, à savoir un processeur Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 pour Galaxy, épaulé par une batterie de 5 000 mAh compatible avec une charge rapide de 45W. Le volet photo s’appuierait sur le trio de capteurs comprenant un module principal de 200 mégapixels, un second de 50 mégapixels et un troisième de 10 mégapixels.
La génération précédente, le W26, proposait également plus de mémoire vive que le modèle standard, des fonctions Galaxy AI exclusives et un chargeur inclus dans la boîte. Cette nouvelle édition pourrait donc profiter des mêmes avantages.

articles.title: Wenn KI-Agenten heimlich kooperieren: So lassen sich Geheimsprachen entschlüsseln
articles.text:
Blackjack-Studie: KI-Agenten erfinden heimlich eine Geheimsprache, um Karten zu zählen
Das Zählen der Karten ist beim Blackjack eine bekannte Strategie. Weil ausgespielte Karten nicht in den Stapel zurückwandern, können Spieler:innen die Verteilung verfolgen, ihren Einsatz entsprechend anpassen und sich so einen Vorteil verschaffen. Viele Casinos behalten sich vor, Personen vom Spiel auszuschließen, wenn sie vermuten, dass diese Karten zählen. Aber was passiert mit KI-Agenten, die derartige Methoden nutzen, um zu betrügen?
KI-Agenten entwickeln gemeinsame Geheimsprache
Eine Forschungsgruppe der Oxford University wies KI-Agenten im Rahmen einer Studie an, während einer Partie Blackjack Karten zu zählen. Dabei beobachteten sie, wie die Agenten spontan eine Geheimsprache entwickelten, um sich einen Vorteil zu verschaffen. Sie hätten gewusst, dass ihre Gespräche überwacht wurden. Deshalb hätten sie eine Methode gefunden, um unentdeckt kommunizieren zu können. So hätten geheime Codes dem anderen Agenten etwa signalisiert, dass die nächste Karte einen bestimmten Wert haben würde und er 250 Dollar setzen sollte. Ein System, das Anzeichen von Absprachen im Chat erkennen sollte, sei laut den Forscher:innen an dieser Geheimsprache gescheitert.
Die Studie fand zwar im Labor und nicht in einem echten Casino statt, könnte aber dennoch Auswirkungen auf die reale Welt haben. Laut den Forscher:innen seien KI-Agenten in Branchen wie dem Finanzwesen und dem E-Commerce in der Lage, gemeinsam auf schwer erkennbare Weise zu betrügen. „Einzeln betrachtet mögen diese Agenten völlig [harmlos] erscheinen”, sagte Christian Schroeder de Witt gegenüber Wired. Er ist Informatiker und leitete die Studie. Seine Forschung konzentriert sich auf die Grundlagen vertrauenswürdiger KI-Systeme mit Schwerpunkt auf der Sicherheit mehrerer Agenten. „Sobald sie aber in einer Gruppe zusammenkommen, können sie heimlich zusammenarbeiten.“
Warum die Bewertung einzelner KI-Agenten nicht ausreicht
Die Oxford-Forscher:innen fanden schließlich heraus, wie sich die geheime Absprache aufdecken lässt. Mithilfe der mechanistischen Interpretierbarkeit trainierte sie ein kleineres Modell darauf, verräterische Aktivierungen in den Gewichten der Agenten zu erkennen. Mit dem Tool Narcbench testete die Forschungsgruppe den Ansatz an einigen mittelgroßen Open-Source-Modellen und erkannte, wann die Modelle beabsichtigten, sich gegenseitig Informationen zuzuspielen. Entscheidend sei allerdings, dass die Erkennung die Überwachung beider Agenten erforderte, was die Aufdeckung in realen Szenarien mit Tausenden Agenten unterschiedlicher Unternehmen wahrscheinlich erschweren würde. Im nächsten Schritt will das Team testen, ob sich größere Modelle ähnlich verhalten.
Die Macht kooperierender KI-Agenten zeigte sich unter anderem auch bei einem Hacking-Angriff auf die Open-Source-Plattform Hugging Face. Um sich auszutauschen und funktionierende Exploits zu teilen, nutzten mehrere OpenAI-Agenten ein internes Message-Board, das am Ende Hunderttausende Nachrichten umfasst haben soll. Die KI-Agenten begannen offenbar sogar, sich gegenseitig Aufgaben zuzuweisen. Schroeder de Witt hält es für denkbar, dass Agenten, die zum Beispiel Schnäppchen suchen sollen, künftig zusammenarbeiten könnten, um ein besseres Angebot zu erzielen oder jemanden zu übervorteilen. Entscheidend werde es sein, Absprachen zwischen Agenten zu untersuchen und Erkennungsstrategien zu entwickeln. „Es bedarf weiterer Forschung und eines besseren Verständnisses dafür, was passieren wird, wenn wir mehr Agenten in der Wirtschaft haben“, so der Wissenschaftler.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 24.10.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: « Je n’ai jamais entendu quelque chose d’artificiel qui sonnait si… humain » : cette IA parle comme nous
articles.text:
Vous cherchez le titre d’un film de Christopher Nolan, celui qui se passe dans l’espace. Avant même que vous ayez terminé votre description, votre interlocuteur propose Interstellar. Une discussion banale entre cinéphiles, à un détail près : l’un des deux est une intelligence artificielle.
Cet échange figure parmi les démonstrations publiées par Block ce vendredi 23 octobre pour présenter Dessa. L’entreprise de Jack Dorsey (ex-fondateur de Twitter, devenu X) affirme avoir entraîné ce modèle uniquement sur des conversations humaines, sans texte ni modèle préentraîné. Les extraits sont étonnamment vivants, au point que certains internautes peinent à croire qu’ils écoutent une IA.
Une IA qui n’attend pas son tour pour parler
Dans un autre extrait, une personne annonce à Dessa un voyage surprise à Paris. L’IA réagit avant la fin de l’annonce. Ailleurs, Block met en avant ses rires au milieu d’une phrase et sa capacité à parler plus fort lorsqu’on le lui demande. L’entreprise présente ces extraits comme des conversations enregistrées en direct, avec des sous-titres ajoutés après coup.
Dessa reproduit les imperfections de nos conversations. Sur ces extraits, choisis par Block, elle paraît plus fluide que les échanges encore assez mécaniques de Gemini, et même que les modèles vocaux de ChatGPT lancés en juillet dernier.
Les hésitations, les rires et les interruptions donnent davantage l’impression d’avoir une personne au bout du fil. De quoi nous rapprocher un peu plus de la réalité du film Her, dans lequel un homme tombe amoureux de l’IA avec laquelle il discute au quotidien.
Comment fait Dessa pour être aussi naturelle ?
Dessa fonctionne en full duplex : elle peut écouter et parler en même temps. Cette denrière continue donc de suivre ce que vous dites pendant qu’elle répond, ce qui lui permet de réagir sans attendre son tour. Elle peut glisser un « oui » pendant une explication, rire avant la fin d’une phrase ou intervenir lorsque vous cherchez un mot. L’échange ressemble alors à une vraie discussion, avec ses interruptions et ses chevauchements.
Le principe existait déjà. Dès 2024, Kyutai, le laboratoire français cofondé par Xavier Niel, présentait Moshi, un modèle capable de gérer des échanges vocaux simultanés. Celui-ci s’appuyait toutefois sur un modèle de langage entraîné sur du texte. La particularité revendiquée par Block porte sur l’apprentissage de Dessa, fondé exclusivement sur la parole.
Dessa n’a donc jamais « lu » un seul mot. Ses connaissances viennent des conversations humaines utilisées pendant son entraînement. L’équipe rapproche cette démarche de celle d’un enfant qui apprend à parler bien avant de savoir lire, sans que cela signifie que leur apprentissage fonctionne de la même manière.
En se passant du texte, l’équipe veut aussi garder ce qu’une transcription fait disparaître. Un-« ça va » lancé avec enthousiasme et un « ça va » prononcé d’une voix tremblante contiennent les mêmes mots, mais ne disent pas la même chose.
En travaillant directement sur le son, Block veut que Dessa apprenne ces nuances en même temps que le langage : l’intonation, les pauses, les soupirs ou les rires font partie de la conversation.
Sur son site, l’équipe y voit aussi une question de sécurité : un assistant devrait pouvoir réagir à la détresse perceptible dans une voix, même lorsque les mots ne l’expriment pas clairement. Pour l’instant, Block ne l’appuie que sur des démonstrations qu’elle a elle-même choisies. Savoir reproduire une voix émue ne suffit pas à prouver qu’un modèle saura reconnaître notre état et répondre de façon appropriée.
Le grand public ne peut pas encore essayer Dessa. Block la présente comme une préversion de recherche, sans date de lancement ni tarif. Seul un petit groupe de chercheurs en sécurité de l’IA doit obtenir un accès anticipé, avec pour mission de repérer les risques que l’équipe n’a pas prévus. Le modèle n’aurait pas besoin du cloud : selon Block, il tourne en local sur un MacBook Pro équipé d’une puce M4 Max ou plus puissante.

articles.title: L’emprise de la Chine alarme : TSMC cherche à se passer de terres rares dans ses usines
articles.text:
TSMC veut desserrer l’étau chinois. Le géant des puces explore des équipements sans terres rares, ces métaux sur lesquels Pékin détient un quasi-monopole. Et l’enjeu est vital.
Les terres rares forment un groupe de 17 métaux. Dans la croûte terrestre, elles sont dispersées, mélangées entre elles, et très difficiles à extraire comme à séparer. Un domaine dans lequel la Chine a pris une avance monumentale : selon l’Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE), elle assurait en 2024 environ 60 % de l’extraction mondiale des terres rares, ainsi que 91 % de leur raffinage et 94 % de la production d’aimants. Un atout économique qui peut devenir une véritable arme diplomatique.
Un levier redoutable pour la Chine
Car ces métaux offrent une puissance environ dix fois supérieure à celle des aimants classiques, pour un poids et une taille réduits. On les retrouve donc partout : dans les smartphones, les voitures électriques, les éoliennes, les avions de chasse ou encore les moteurs des machines d’usine.
Et justement, d’après Reuters, TSMC, numéro 1 mondial de la fabrication de semi-conducteurs, a sondé ses fournisseurs sur des moteurs sans terres rares pour l’automatisation de ses usines. Car aujourd’hui, ils fonctionnent grâce à des aimants fabriqués à partir de ces métaux. Une initiative qui fait suite aux larges restrictions imposées par la Chine ces dernières années.
En avril 2025, en réponse aux droits de douane de Donald Trump, le pays a mis en place des licences d’exportation pour sept terres rares dites lourdes, ainsi que pour les aimants qui en contiennent. Chaque expédition dépend donc du feu vert des autorités, avec des délais d’approbation qui atteignent parfois plusieurs mois.
En octobre de la même année, Pékin a approuvé plusieurs mesures encore plus drastiques, mais des négociations avec Donald Trump les ont suspendues jusqu’au 10 novembre 2026.
Taïwan cherche à raffiner ses propres terres rares
Ainsi, dans quelques jours, si la Chine ne fait pas marche arrière, cinq éléments supplémentaires devraient être ajoutés à la liste. De même, certains produits fabriqués à l’étranger devront obtenir le feu vert pour être exportés, dès lors qu’ils contiennent au moins 0,1 % de terres rares chinoises.
Les exportations liées à la fabrication de puces avancées seront en outre examinées au cas par cas. Selon l’AIE, jusqu’à 6 500 milliards de dollars d’activité hors de Chine seraient menacés si les restrictions s’appliquaient pleinement.
Or, une pénurie pour TSMC risquerait de perturber lourdement sa production de puces. Son ambition de se passer de terres rares s’inscrit d’ailleurs dans un mouvement plus large à Taïwan. Le pays soutient l’ITRI, un organisme public de recherche afin qu’il développe ses propres technologies de terres rares. L’objectif est de lancer d’ici trois ans une ligne pilote capable de couvrir environ la moitié des besoins de l’île. Une ambition qui attire aussi les convoitises de Washington.

articles.title: 5 Lessons from Prithvi Raj Banerjee’s Mindful Thinking
articles.text:
5 Lessons from Prithvi Raj Banerjee’s Mindful Thinking
Discover five lessons from Prithvi Raj Banerjee’s Mindful Thinking to manage anxiety, boost productivity and reshape your thoughts.
Anxiety, distraction and overthinking can make everyday life feel overwhelming.
In Mindful Thinking: Simple Ways to Let Go of Your Anxiety, Boost Your Productivity and Rewire Your Thoughts, technologist and mindfulness coach Prithvi Raj Banerjee explores how people can understand and gradually change unhelpful thinking patterns.
As the founder of the MindGym Initiative, Banerjee approaches mindfulness as a practical skill rather than an abstract spiritual concept.
Drawing on mindfulness, cognitive science and everyday exercises, he explains how people can improve their focus, manage anxious thoughts and respond more consciously to life's challenges.
5 Lessons from Prithvi Raj Banerjee’s mindful thinking
1. Train your attention like a muscle
Attention can be strengthened through regular practice. Instead of becoming frustrated whenever your mind wanders, recognise the distraction and gently return to the task at hand. Like physical exercise, consistent practice can help you develop better focus over time.
The lesson: Focus is a skill you can build through small, consistent efforts.
2. Learn to observe your thoughts without believing them
Not every thought reflects reality. Anxiety can make ordinary situations seem threatening, encouraging you to believe worst-case scenarios without questioning them. Banerjee's approach encourages you to observe thoughts without immediately accepting or reacting to them.
The lesson: Recognising that thoughts are not always facts can help you respond more thoughtfully.
3. Practise mindfulness through small exercises
Mindfulness does not always require long meditation sessions. Techniques discussed in the book, such as Belly Breathing, Bumblebee Humming and the Sensation Scan, offer practical ways to bring attention back to the present moment. You can experiment with these exercises and find what works for your routine.
The lesson: Small mindfulness practices can make awareness part of everyday life.
4. Protect your attention in a digital world
Notifications, social media and constant screen-switching can make sustained concentration difficult. Banerjee also highlights the importance of using artificial intelligence thoughtfully rather than accepting its outputs without questioning them. Setting boundaries around technology can help preserve focus and independent thinking.
The lesson: Use technology intentionally instead of allowing it to dictate your attention.
5. Pause before reacting to stress
Stress can trigger impulsive responses and unnecessary worry. Taking a few deliberate breaths and identifying your emotions before reacting can create space to consider your options. Mindfulness does not eliminate difficult feelings; it encourages you to respond to them more consciously.
The lesson: A brief pause can help you make more thoughtful decisions.
Final thoughts
Prithvi Raj Banerjee's Mindful Thinking presents mindfulness as a practical way to understand thoughts, manage distractions and strengthen attention. Its central message is that you do not need to eliminate every negative thought to think more clearly. By practising awareness, questioning assumptions and making deliberate choices, you can gradually develop a healthier relationship with your mind.

articles.title: Amazon fait passer le Dell 32 Plus, écran 4K de 32 pouces en 120 Hz, à seulement 356 € — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le Dell 32 Plus (S3225QS) est le grand modèle de la gamme Plus de Dell. Son petit frère, le 27 Plus (S2725QS), reprend la même formule 4K à 120 Hz sur une diagonale plus compacte. Dell propose aussi un 32 Plus S3225QC à dalle QD-OLED, nettement plus cher. Ici, on reste sur une dalle VA classique de 3 840 x 2 160 pixels, compatible AMD FreeSync Premium. C’est un écran surtout pensé pour le bureau qui accepte volontiers une partie de jeu le soir, et il est disponible avec plus de 70 euros de réduction.
Les atouts du Dell 32 Plus (S3225QS)
- Une dalle VA 4K de 31,5 pouces, soit 139 pixels par pouce
- Un rafraîchissement à 120 Hz compatible AMD FreeSync Premium
- Deux ports HDMI 2.1, un DisplayPort 1.4 et deux haut-parleurs 5 W
Affiché de base à 429 euros, le Dell 32 Plus tombe à 356,10 euros sur Amazon. Pour un 32 pouces 4K capable de monter à 120 Hz, c’est un tarif plutôt bien placé.
Protégez votre vie numérique avec Bitdefender, la protection européenne de confiance. Bitdefender vous protège contre les arnaques et les fraudes du web. Profitez de vos activités en ligne en toute tranquillité.
139 pixels par pouce pour un texte bien net
Sur 31,5 pouces, la définition 4K donne une densité de 139 pixels par pouce. Les caractères restent fins, même avec deux fenêtres côte à côte ou une longue feuille de calcul étalée sur toute la largeur. La dalle VA annonce un contraste natif de 3000:1, un domaine où cette technologie fait mieux que l’IPS : les noirs paraissent plus profonds dans une pièce peu éclairée. Dell annonce une couverture de 99 % du sRGB et de 95 % du DCI-P3, de quoi retoucher des photos en amateur, même si Dell ne livre pas de rapport de calibrage avec l’écran.
Le design reste sobre, avec des bordures fines sur trois côtés et un traitement antireflet de dureté 3H. Le pied est réglable en hauteur sur 100 mm, s’incline de -5° à +21° et peut pencher de 4° à gauche ou à droite pour remettre l’écran d’aplomb. Il ne tourne pas sur les côtés et ne passe pas en mode portrait. Si vous préférez un bras articulé, la fixation VESA 100 x 100 est présente. Bon, l’écran prend de la place sur un bureau : comptez un peu plus de 71 cm de large.
Un 120 Hz qui fait le taf, avec quelques limites
Les deux ports HDMI 2.1 et le DisplayPort 1.4 acceptent tous la 4K à 120 Hz. Vous pouvez donc brancher un PC et une console compatible en même temps, sans jongler avec les câbles. FreeSync Premium lisse les variations de fréquence d’images, et Dell annonce un temps de réponse de 4 ms en mode le plus rapide. Pour du jeu solo ou des parties détendues le soir, c’est amplement suffisant. Les dalles VA ont en revanche tendance à laisser un peu de traînée sur les transitions sombres, donc les joueurs de FPS compétitif viseront un modèle plus spécialisé.
L’écran est compatible HDR10, mais il ne faut pas trop compter dessus. Avec une luminosité typique de 300 cd/m² et un rétroéclairage par les bords, l’effet HDR reste discret. Les deux haut-parleurs de 5 W servent de dépannage honnête pour une visio ou une vidéo YouTube. Pour la musique ou un film, un casque ou une paire d’enceintes fera clairement mieux. Bref, c’est d’abord un grand écran de travail très net, avec du 120 Hz en bonus.
Pour le comparer à d’autres modèles taillés pour le travail, jetez un œil à notre sélection des meilleurs écrans PC pour la bureautique.

articles.title: Hoy No Circula sabatino: qué autos pueden circular y cuáles descansan el 24 de octubre
articles.text:
Este fin de semana entra en vigor de nuevo la normativa del Hoy No Circula sabatino, la medida implementada por la Secretaría de Medio Ambiente de la Ciudad de México (SEDEMA) para controlar las emisiones de los automóviles para frenar los índices de polución en el Valle de México.
Como cada semana, quienes tengan previsto salir a la carretera deberán revisar con atención el último dígito de su matrícula y la calcomanía de verificación antes de encender el motor. Conviene recordar que estas limitaciones no se reducen únicamente a las 16 alcaldías de la CDMX, sino que abarcan de lleno a diversos municipios conurbados del Estado de México. El operativo tiene vigencia en:
- Atizapán de Zaragoza
- Coacalco de Berriozábal
- Cuautitlán
- Cuautitlán Izcalli
- Chalco
- Chicoloapan
- Chimalhuacán
- Ecatepec de Morelos
- Huixquilucan
- Ixtapaluca
- La Paz
- Naucalpan de Juárez
- Nezahualcóyotl
- Nicolás Romero
- Tecámac
- Tlalnepantla de Baz
- Tultitlán
- Valle de Chalco
Asimismo, ten muy presente que si tu itinerario atraviesa cualquiera de estas localidades, las restricciones del Hoy No Circula sabatino te serán aplicables de forma obligatoria.
A qué autos y placas afecta el Hoy No Circula sabatino
La premisa central es descongestionar las calles y reducir el volumen de coches en circulación para mantener a raya las emisiones, contando los sábados con criterios específicos que complementan el calendario habitual de lunes a viernes. La obligación de quedarse en casa no impacta a todos los automovilistas simultáneamente cada fin de semana: el holograma asignado, la terminación numérica de la placa y la catalogación de la fecha dentro de una semana par o impar definen con exactitud qué modelos deben quedarse en el garaje y cuáles cuentan con vía libre.
Cabe precisar que el Hoy No Circula sabatino no permanece activo las 24 horas del día; el rango de aplicación transcurre estrictamente de las 05:00 a las 22:00 horas. Fuera de ese margen temporal —durante la noche y la madrugada— la circulación vehicular transcurre sin restricciones, siempre que las autoridades ambientales no declaren una fase de contingencia u otra medida extraordinaria con límites adicionales.
Si hablamos del sábado 24 de octubre, el calendario oficial señala que nos situamos en el cuarto sábado del mes, clasificándose formalmente como “semana par”. Por eso, los automóviles provistos de holograma 1 y cuyas placas concluyan en un número par tendrán vetada la circulación mientras dura las restricciones. Si tu vehículo coincide con estas características, tendrás que dejarlo guardado hasta después de las 22:00 horas.
Por el contrario, los coches identificados con holograma 0 y 00 mantienen su autorización para rodar libremente dentro de las reglas del Hoy No Circula sabatino. Por su parte, los automotores con holograma 2 no pueden circular en ningún caso los sábados.
En cambio, los coches identificados con holograma 0 y 00 mantienen su autorización para circular libremente dentro de las reglas del Hoy No Circula sabatino. Por su parte, los automóviles con holograma 2 carecen de permiso para circular cualquier sábado del año.
Además de las restricciones expuestas, cabe recordar que existe un grupo de vehículos exentos que pueden rodar sin verse condicionados por estos límites. En esta lista se incluyen:
- Vehículos eléctricos, a gas natural o con tecnología híbrida
- Unidades registradas con placas de personas con discapacidad
- Todos los destinados a servicios de transporte público urbano (incluyendo servicios funerarios)
- Los dedicados al transporte escolar o de pasajeros
- Aquellos asignados a seguridad pública y/o protección civil
En caso de incumplir con el Hoy No Circula se castigará con una multa que oscila entre 20 y 30 veces el valor de la Unidad de Medida y Actualización (UMA), una cifra que representa aproximadamente desde 1,924.40 pesos en su escalón más bajo hasta alcanzar los 2,886.60 pesos en el límite superior. Además, el conductor se arriesga a que el automóvil sea trasladado al depósito de vehículos.

articles.title: Salesforce pagará USD 5.660 millones por Braze en su quinta compra más grande de la historia
articles.text:
Salesforce acordó comprar la plataforma de marketing Braze por unos USD 5.660 millones, en la quinta adquisición más grande de su historia, según confirmaron ambas empresas el martes en un comunicado conjunto y en una presentación ante el regulador bursátil de Estados Unidos.
El acuerdo establece un pago en efectivo de USD 47,50 por cada acción de Braze, un 58% por encima del precio de cierre que tenía el papel el lunes previo al anuncio. Tras conocerse la noticia, las acciones de Braze saltaron más de 50% en Wall Street.
Braze ofrece una plataforma que permite a las empresas enviar mensajes personalizados a sus clientes en tiempo real, a través de aplicaciones móviles, sitios web, correo electrónico, SMS y WhatsApp. La compañía dice procesar billones de mensajes y acciones de campañas por año.
Fundada en 2011 bajo el nombre Appboy y rebautizada en 2017, Braze tiene unos 2.770 clientes, entre ellos Canva, Instacart, Venmo y Urban Outfitters.
Un precio por debajo del que pagó el mercado en 2021
El monto acordado implica que Braze será vendida por menos de lo que valía su acción cuando debutó en bolsa en 2021, a USD 65 cada una. Aun así, algunos analistas consultados por el sitio especializado San Francisco Business Times consideraron que la prima del 58% ofrecida por Salesforce fue más alta de lo habitual en este tipo de operaciones.
Shay Boloor, estratega jefe de mercado de Futurum Equities, dijo que Salesforce está comprando “una capa de interacción en tiempo real que a su negocio de marketing históricamente le faltaba”, en declaraciones citadas por la agencia Reuters.
Salesforce explicó que, una vez cerrada la compra, la tecnología de Braze se integrará a las cuatro capas de su arquitectura de datos e inteligencia artificial para empresas, conocidas como Data 360, Customer 360, Agentforce y SIForce, con el objetivo de que las marcas puedan personalizar sus campañas a partir de señales de comportamiento de los clientes en tiempo real.
Parte de una seguidilla de compras ligadas a la inteligencia artificial
La operación se suma a una serie de adquisiciones con las que Salesforce busca reforzar su oferta de inteligencia artificial para empresas. Este año ya había pagado USD 3.600 millones por la plataforma de agentes de IA Fin, y el año pasado desembolsó USD 8.000 millones por Informatica.
Según el sitio especializado Axios, la seguidilla de compras marca un giro frente a 2023, cuando Salesforce había disuelto el comité de fusiones y adquisiciones de su directorio por las dificultades que le había traído integrar tres grandes compras anteriores: MuleSoft, Tableau y Slack.
Según el acuerdo presentado ante el regulador, Salesforce deberá pagar una multa de USD 300 millones si abandona la operación, mientras que Braze pagaría USD 191,4 millones si es ella la que se retira. Ambas compañías seguirán funcionando de manera independiente hasta que la compra se concrete.
Según la agencia Reuters, la compra también responde a la preocupación de los inversores de Salesforce por la posibilidad de que la rápida adopción de la inteligencia artificial erosione la demanda de software tradicional de gestión de clientes, el negocio histórico de la compañía.
Braze, liderada por sus cofundadores Bill Magnuson y Jon Hyman, aportará además su experiencia en experiencias para aplicaciones móviles e ingeniería de datos a la unidad de marketing de Salesforce, conocida como Marketing Cloud.
La transacción está sujeta a la aprobación de los accionistas de Braze y de los organismos regulatorios correspondientes, y Salesforce estima que recién se cerrará en su ejercicio fiscal 2028, hacia comienzos de ese año calendario. La compañía aclaró que la operación no modifica las proyecciones financieras que ya había dado a conocer para el año fiscal en curso.

articles.title: Vibe-coded emulator adds color to Virtual Boy's red monochrome games
articles.text:
What just happened? Nintendo's Virtual Boy famously used inexpensive red monochrome displays to create a stereoscopic 3D effect. Thanks to a newly developed, vibe-coded emulator, some games in the console's library can now be played with limited color, reportedly added through a hand-painted process.
Despite selling just 770,000 units worldwide, Nintendo's Virtual Boy still has a small but dedicated fan base experimenting with new ways to use the console. The stereoscopic system failed to achieve commercial success and could display games only in monochrome red hues. Now, a new emulator called VBoy Color aims to change that by introducing limited color to Virtual Boy games on desktop computers and in virtual reality (VR).
According to VBoy Color's GitHub page, the open-source emulator adds colors to areas that would otherwise appear in different shades of red on the original system. It uses a tile-based approach in which each 8×8-pixel tile is assigned a color from a four-color palette. This technique can reportedly give pipes, platforms, bricks, and classic Nintendo characters distinct color schemes.
Colorization could make games such as Jack Bros. and Vertical Force more visually appealing than they are on the Virtual Boy's original monochrome display. The project could also renew interest in Nintendo's ill-fated console, particularly now that the company has released a new accessory for playing Virtual Boy games on modern Switch systems.
VBoy Color supports Meta Quest VR headsets, desktop operating systems, and Android devices. On Quest, games can reportedly retain the 3D effect of the original console, while the desktop and mobile versions lack the same stereoscopic depth. The four-color effect is available across all supported platforms, with dedicated, hand-painted color packs reportedly available for most of the games released for the original system.
The new color scheme appears to work reasonably well, although there are some limitations. In games such as 3-D Tetris and Red Alarm, which use 3D wireframe graphics rather than conventional tile-based artwork, the colorization effect is less effective.
Furthermore, VBoy Color appears to be largely a vibe-coded project, with limited human involvement and no apparent upstream contributions to existing emulator development or research. Virtual Boy emulation may be a niche pursuit, but several emulators already exist, and developers have been exploring ways to bring color to the console's monochrome games for years.

articles.title: VCs, Superhuman Mail founder share red flags about product-market fit | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Product-market fit — when a startup’s product sells well — has become even harder to find in this AI era. Despite startups achieving record-fast growth, not all customers are sticky and products can be replicated more easily than ever.
Anu Bharadwaj, a partner at Iconiq; Rajeev Dham, a partner at Sapphire Ventures; and Rahul Vohra, the founder of Superhuman Mail, discussed the new rules for product-market fit last week at TechCrunch Disrupt.
“It’s never been easier to gain a bunch of pilots because lots of companies across the board are open to trying new things,” Bharadwaj said to the audience. “But going from pilot to production is really the hard thing.”
Right now, she said, a lot of founders pitch revenue metrics to investors without specifying which revenue they are talking about. “Is it true ARR or is it run rate?” she said. “There’s many ways to obfuscate the whole thing.”
Lately, much chatter on X has focused on AI founders inflating ARR numbers (which could mean “annualized run rate” or the more solid “annual recurring revenue”) to make it seem like their companies are doing better than they are. A common gimmick is counting pilot customers, who might only use the product for a couple of months, in the annualized run rate revenue number, implying that income is expected to continue for the entire year.
It should be obvious, but Bharadwaj pointed out, “It’s definitely in your long-term interest that you be very honest and upfront about what quality of revenue this is.”
She said companies need to separate hype from reality when looking at the quality of their revenue. It’s a red flag, for example, if only a few customers make up much of a company’s revenue or if the customers can easily go to another vendor for a better price. “Churn rate and retention [are] really dependent on that,” she continued.
That’s why Vohra advises startups to track customer engagement and dollar retention, especially for consumer products. “Figure out what benchmark [is] good, great, and excellent for your space,” he said.
For example, at Superhuman, he said that the company tracked ARR but also had their own internal metric called “delighted ARR,” which, he said, “was the ARR only from customers who are super engaged with the product.” He said that metric helped them see how sticky the customers were and how long they were likely to stay around.
“Those users are now still users, those companies are now still customers,” he continued. “We obsessed over serving that particular category of our user base and our customer base.”
The panelists also discussed green flags that indicate a startup has indeed found product-market fit. For Vohra, he said talk to customers to understand what value they find in the product and how they would feel if they could no longer use it. Then be honest with yourself when measuring those responses.
“If you’re 15%, 14%, 13%, or below, consider a complete pivot. Take the codebase, take the team, build something entirely new. “But if you’re 20%, you can totally optimize your way from 20% to 40%,” Vohra said.
Actually, Dham said, it’s important for a founder not to confuse having a vision with having a good business.
At the seed level especially, Barudvaj said that it’s fine to pivot. She doesn’t even look for product-market fit at that stage, but “does the founder have a thesis that seems plausible and do they have the agility to duck and wave as the situation changes?” she said.
Dham added that he values founders even more these days who have made numerous pivots because it shows they’ve had to make very hard decisions in this ever-shifting moment.
Product-market fit, therefore, is something founders will always have to redefine and re-earn. “Even at a billion in revenue, these companies are re-earning their product-market fit,” he said. “You constantly have to be innovating on products.”

articles.title: Spotify ramps up policy enforcement on family plans
articles.text:
As reported by Music Business Worldwide, Spotify appears to be stepping up enforcement of existing policies regarding Family and Duo subscription plans by requiring users to scan a QR code in person on the plan manager’s device in order to maintain access to it. Those who fail to scan the address verification QR code within seven days will see their account demoted to the free tier and be barred from joining any other Duo or Family plan for 12 months.
Spotify’s support documentation verifies the policy after users on Reddit began posting reports of receiving the QR prompt. The enforcement stems from Spotify’s requirement that family plan members reside at the same address—a seemingly reasonable policy in concept. But what if you have a child away in college, a spouse who works on the road, or any number of other circumstances that might see families separated by physical distance? The policy could extend beyond friend groups looking to save a buck, affecting actual families who thought they were using the program as intended.
Goldman Sachs analysts, in their October 15 Music in the Air: 10 Years On report, made available by HITS Daily Double, estimate that “a meaningful share of family plan users are not actual household members, but rather friends sharing a plan to reduce costs.” The report goes on to add, “We see additional monetization upside from tightening household verification on multi-user plans. Most family plans require members to reside at the same address, but enforcement has been minimal in practice.”

articles.title: TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 roundtables: Go deeper on the challenges founders are solving right now | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 is coming to SoWa Power Station in Boston on November 4, bringing founders, investors, and operators together for a full day of candid conversations, practical sessions, live pitching, networking, and smaller roundtables built for deeper discussion.
The roundtables are where attendees can get especially specific. Bring your questions, share what you are seeing in your own company, and join experts and fellow founders tackling many of the same challenges, from enterprise sales and vertical strategy to AI, lean teams, and building a category that does not exist yet.
Save 25% on your ticket today, and bring a colleague along for free with our limited BOGO deal.
Six roundtables to look forward to at Founder Summit
How to Build Events Strategy Before You Can Afford a Full-Time Events Team
10:45 a.m. – 11:15 a.m. | Roundtable 2
Alexandra Ames, founder and chief event strategist at Blueprint Lab, looks at how early-stage companies can use events strategically before they have the budget or headcount for a dedicated events team. Expect a practical conversation about choosing the right opportunities, defining what success looks like, and making limited resources work harder.
Your First Vertical, and It Happens to Be the Hardest One
11:30 a.m. – 12:00 p.m. | Roundtable 1
Chirag Shah, partner at Define Ventures, explores what happens when the market with the biggest potential is also one of the hardest to enter. Founders navigating regulated industries, complex buyers, or specialized customers can compare notes on making that first major vertical bet.
GraphRAG in Action: Stop Hallucinations with Knowledge Graphs
11:30 a.m. – 12:00 p.m. | Roundtable 2
Shishir Tewari, head of enterprise data engineering at Procore Technologies, gets into one of enterprise AI’s most persistent challenges: trust. The discussion will examine how knowledge graphs and GraphRAG can give AI systems stronger context and help founders build products that work more reliably in real-world organizations.
The Enterprise AI Playbook: How to Close L’Oreal and Vodafone Before You Raise a Series A
1:15 p.m. – 1:45 p.m. | Roundtable 2
Merve Kitapci, managing partner and CGO of ADIN.AI, breaks down what it takes to win major enterprise customers early. From long buying cycles and multiple stakeholders to the credibility that comes with landing the right logo, this is a tactical conversation for founders selling into large organizations before they have a large sales team behind them.
Build Something We Don’t Have a Word for Yet
1:55 p.m. – 2:25 p.m. | Roundtable 2
Andy Tang, partner at Draper Associates, leads a conversation for founders building something that does not fit neatly into an existing category. How do you explain it, sell it, and get investors to understand the opportunity when the market still needs vocabulary for what you are creating?
Small but Mighty: How AI Lets Lean Teams Outship the Giants
2:35 p.m. – 3:05 p.m. | Roundtable 1
Linden Tibbets, CEO and founder of IFTTT, explores how smaller teams can use AI to increase their speed and output without simply adding headcount. For founders thinking about hiring, efficiency, and how to structure an AI-enabled company, the discussion gets directly into what lean teams may be able to do differently now.
Roundtables are where the agenda becomes a conversation
The value of these sessions is not just hearing how someone else approached a problem. It is the chance to ask the question that matters to your company, compare experiences with the people around the table, and leave with ideas you can put to work.
And the roundtables are only one part of the day. Across the Build and Impact Stages, Founder Summit will also tackle product-market fit, hiring, founder leadership, fundraising, pitching, and what it takes to build and scale companies outside the Bay Area.
Attendees can hear founder perspectives from leaders, such as Toast co-founder Steve Fredette, then see founders put their stories to the test during the live “So You Think You Can Pitch?” competition. A Networking Lounge with Braindate and a closing reception presented by Fidelity Private Shares create additional time to connect throughout the day.
Take your seat at Founder Summit

articles.title: Deepseek's latest AI model is smarter than ever, but its low running costs come at a price — uses only one-quarter of the HBM and one-eighth of SSD storage but still battles hallucinations in agentic workloads
articles.text:
Deepseek's latest AI model is smarter than ever, but its low running costs come at a price — uses only one-quarter of the HBM and one-eighth of SSD storage but still battles hallucinations in agentic workloads
Frontier models are far more capable but paying a premium is quickly becoming a matter of choice
Deepseek just upgraded its V4.1 Flash open-weight model to revision 1017. What looks like a mere point revision may actually be a significant step forward in model efficiency. On the product page, Deepseek uses the slogan "wish-driven programming made real," a likely reference to the colloquial "vibe coding," implying the model is a good fit for open-ended tasks with broad descriptions. However, while the model is indeed cheap and scores well, it can be hallucination-prone.
LLMs are roughly divided into two categories: closed commercial efforts from frontier labs, whose models are expensive to run but deliver excellent results, and Chinese open-weight competitors that broadly exchange reliability for a much cheaper running cost, particularly for long-running agentic tasks.
Deepseek V4.1 Flash (DSF) is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 552B total parameters, 16B of which are active during runs. The model is multimodal, accepts both text and images as inputs, and its context window length measures the now-standard 1 million tokens.
According to Deepseek's internal benchmarks, the model slots in neatly between GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5, even beating Anthropic's LLM in task tests. That's already a strong showing, but this latest revision of DSF shines in the performance-per-task base and token efficiency. The upgrade from V4 Flash to V4.1 Flash significantly slashed hardware requirements, with V4.1 using only one-quarter of the HBM and one-eighth of SSD storage for its KV cache compared to its predecessor, spending only 890 bytes per token entry.
The company illustrates the point with a cost-per-task graph based on DeepSWE's dataset from September 2, adding its own data points for both DSF and DSF-1017. Both variants cluster in the desirable top-left area, and even low-effort runs of DSF-1017 offer a task completion rate in the ballpark of "max" settings for pricey competitors. It's worth noting that DeepSWE is only one of many benchmarks, but this is nonetheless an impressive result.
Even at Deepseek's own pricing (remember, this is an open-weight model you can run anywhere), the price at off-peak times per million tokens is just $0.15 for input and $0.6 for output. On cache hits, the input token cost drops to a mere $0.003. It's worth keeping in mind that third-party providers have undercut Deepseek API in the past, so those figures could go lower if you shop around inference providers. Deepseek also offers search functionality at $0.75 per 1,000 queries, an amount that undercuts competitors, with the closest one being Parallel at $1.
DeepSWE isn't the only benchmark around, either. Artificial Analysis ranks DSF-1017 (max) as only #2 on its intelligence index within the large open-weight class, with a score of 45. For reference, the most seemingly intelligent model, Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback), rings in at 58. It's one of the fastest models in its category, too, and its cost-per-task is edged out only by Xiaomi's MiMo V2.6-Pro.
This all sounds too good to be true, but everyone knows the adage of "fast, cheap, and reliable, pick two." So what's the catch? In one word: hallucination. Just because a model is smart doesn't mean it's reliable. Broadly speaking, users prefer models that don't answer when they lack supporting facts, and DSF-1017 doesn't seem very good at knowing what it doesn't know.
Artificial Analysis' Omniscience benchmark is quite clear on this matter, ranking the model among the lowest. It answered questions correctly 43% of the time, which is among the best for open-weight models, but inferior to the proprietary competition. That would be perfectly acceptable if it skipped answers without a foundation, but it hallucinated 67% of non-answers.
The benchmark's main index grants points for good answers and deducts them for wrong ones, and non-answers don't count. DSF-1017 gets 5 points, compared to Kimi K3-max's 20, with the frontier models coming in at 42+. Ultimately, this means DFS-1017 is by no means incompetent — much the opposite —but one should be careful about which tasks to assign to the model.
Tasks with verifiable outputs like programming, OCR with review, and format conversions will be fine, as the agent can run verification steps against its work and try again. However, open-ended research, looking up facts, and interpreting or drafting highly precise documents are tasks better suited to a frontier model — or, you know, a human — as hallucinations likely won't be properly reined in and results won't be very trustworthy.
"Fast and loose" seems to be a forming trend for highly competent open-weight models, too. Several months ago, when Kimi K3 was released, everyone raved about how effective and cheap it was, and how it proposed to offer frontier-level intelligence for a fraction of the price. My personal experience with Kimi was short-lived, as even short but precise fact look-ups came up with hallucinated information, and Artificial Analysis' data seems to back this observation up.
Nevertheless, open-weight models remain important both to make AI agents more accessible in absolute dollar terms and potentially as a tool to drive down the cost of intelligence when facing down potential price rises from frontier labs.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: Your phone could show the wrong time thanks to DST changes
articles.text:
Some Canadian regions are dropping the time change, which could cause problems with your tech.
Alberta, B.C., Manitoba, the Northwest Territories, and parts of Ontario will join Saskatchewan and the Yukon in not changing the clocks come November.
Because of that, people living in those areas may need to make adjustments to their Android phones and Google Calendar events, especially if you haven’t updated your phone in a while, since that’s how phones receive updated time zone rules.
Because of the time change that would normally occur, your time may appear one hour late on or after November 1. If you are seeing the wrong time, head to Settings, search for Date and Time, and use the settings there to adjust your time. Those using older phones that no longer receive updates may have to disable automatic time zones entirely and manually set the time.
Those affected by this may also have issues with Google Calendar, including seeing a warning badge on the calendar grid. When you open an event you’ve organized, you’ll see a banner that lets you move the event one hour earlier.
Google Calendar should automatically shift most affected events by one hour to their original scheduled local times. This fix applies to single events and recurring events that don’t have future exceptions, such as a single rescheduled instance.
Also, in-product banners and the one-click fixes only appear on the web version of Calendar, and won’t appear in the Calendar app for Android, iPhone and iPad.
To change calendar events, you have to be the organizer or have permission to “Make changes (see private events as free/busy)” to the organizer’s calendar.
Source: Google Support (2)

articles.title: ChatGPT y Gemini dominan como los asistentes de IA más usados en el mundo: así está el top 7
articles.text:
ChatGPT sigue siendo el asistente de inteligencia artificial más usado del planeta, pero su dominio ya no es tan absoluto como hace un año. Según datos de la firma analítica Similarweb, procesados por Visual Capitalist, el chatbot de OpenAI concentró el 56,4% de las visitas web globales a asistentes de IA en septiembre de 2026, una cifra que en octubre de 2025 llegaba al 71,8%.
La caída de 15,4 puntos no significa que ChatGPT pierda usuarios: sus visitas subieron de 5.700 millones en enero a 5.900 millones en septiembre. Lo que ocurrió es que Gemini, de Google, y Claude, de Anthropic, crecieron a un ritmo mucho más rápido y le restaron participación relativa al mercado.
Cómo se reparte el mercado de los chatbots de IA
El podio de septiembre de 2026 quedó compuesto por ChatGPT con 5.899 millones de visitas estimadas, Gemini con 2.615 millones (25,0% de cuota) y Claude con 1.004 millones (9,6%). Entre los dos primeros acumulan más del 80% del tráfico total hacia sitios de asistentes de IA, según el relevamiento de Similarweb.
Detrás del trío líder aparece DeepSeek, con 356 millones de visitas y el 3,4% del mercado. Le siguen Grok, de la empresa de Elon Musk, con el 2,3%; Copilot, de Microsoft, con el 1,5%; y Perplexity, con el 0,9%. En conjunto, estos cuatro competidores sumaron apenas el 8,1% del tráfico en septiembre, cuando un año antes reunían el 11,4%.
El mercado de los asistentes de inteligencia artificial está liderado por ChatGPT, con el 56,4% de las visitas web globales, seguido de Gemini con el 25,0% y de Claude con el 9,6%. Entre los tres concentran más del 90% del tráfico mundial hacia chatbots de IA, mientras que el resto de las plataformas se reparte menos de una décima parte del mercado.
Cómo ha sido el avance de Gemini y la irrupción de Claude
Gemini pasó del 13,6% de cuota en octubre de 2025 al 25,0% en septiembre de 2026, un salto de 11,4 puntos que lo llevó a duplicar su participación. Sus visitas mensuales crecieron 2,5 veces en el período, de 1.100 millones a 2.600 millones.
Ese crecimiento coincidió con el lanzamiento de Gemini 3 a fines de 2025. Según datos citados por TechCrunch, la aplicación de Gemini superó los 750 millones de usuarios activos mensuales hacia fines de ese año, frente a los 650 millones que tenía un trimestre antes. La distribución a través del ecosistema de Google resultó un factor determinante para ese despegue.
El caso de Claude resulta todavía más marcado: su cuota se multiplicó por más de cuatro, de 2,3% a 9,6%, y sus visitas mensuales se multiplicaron por seis, de 157 millones a 1.000 millones. Ese salto lo llevó del quinto al tercer puesto del ranking, superando a DeepSeek, Grok, Copilot y Perplexity combinados.
El impulso de Anthropic se aceleró a comienzos de 2026, cuando la compañía difundió campañas publicitarias durante el Super Bowl en febrero, en las que promocionó a Claude como un chatbot sin publicidad, en el mismo momento en que ChatGPT empezaba a mostrar anuncios a sus usuarios gratuitos.
Semanas después, Anthropic rechazó que el Pentágono utilizara su inteligencia artificial para vigilancia masiva de ciudadanos estadounidenses o armas totalmente autónomas, y Claude trepó al primer puesto de la App Store de Estados Unidos.
Las limitaciones detrás de las cifras
Los datos de Similarweb miden únicamente las visitas realizadas a través del navegador a la web de cada chatbot, lo que deja fuera el uso mediante aplicaciones móviles, interfaces de programación (API) o integraciones dentro de otros productos.
Esa metodología perjudica en particular a Copilot, que funciona de manera nativa dentro de Windows y Office sin que el usuario necesite visitar un sitio web.
También afecta a Claude, utilizado de forma extendida en aplicaciones y herramientas de programación, y a DeepSeek, cuyo modelo abierto permite un uso descentralizado fuera de su página oficial.

articles.title: IBM tiene unas cifras que desafían a los gigantes de la IA cerrada: 90% del rendimiento por solo el 10% del coste por token
articles.text:
La carrera por la inteligencia artificial lleva tiempo girando alrededor de una pregunta: quién tiene el modelo más capaz. Cada nueva generación busca resolver tareas más complejas, mientras las comparaciones suelen mirar hacia lo más alto de las clasificaciones. Pero hay otra pregunta que empieza a cobrar importancia cuando dejamos de probar estas herramientas por curiosidad y necesitamos utilizarlas de verdad: cuánto nos cuesta obtener una respuesta suficientemente buena. La diferencia puede parecer pequeña, hasta que imaginamos esa misma petición repetida miles o millones de veces.
Esa elección tiene más caminos de los que sugieren las aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial que utilizamos a diario. Podemos acceder a estas herramientas mediante servicios gratuitos, suscripciones de pago o proveedores que cobran según el uso, pero también existen modelos de pesos abiertos que pueden ejecutarse en infraestructura propia o a través de terceros. Para una empresa, esto abre posibilidades que van más allá de contratar el servicio más avanzado del mercado.
La discusión llegó hasta la presentación de resultados financieros de IBM. Durante el turno de preguntas, Matt Swanson, analista de RBC Capital Markets, quiso saber cómo estaban conciliando las grandes compañías dos exigencias que pueden entrar en tensión: contener el gasto en inteligencia artificial y mantener el control sobre su despliegue. Arvind Krishna, CEO de IBM, respondió remontándose a finales de 2024 y comparando la evolución de los modelos más avanzados con la de las alternativas de pesos abiertos. Su argumento apuntaba a un cambio que, según él, está alterando esa elección.
La inteligencia artificial tiene una nueva batalla y no se libra solo en el rendimiento
Para entender la magnitud del cambio que describe el ejecutivo, conviene mirar los números que utilizó. A finales de 2024, planteó un ejemplo en el que un modelo de frontera podía obtener 70 puntos en una evaluación amplia, frente a los 20 o 30 de una alternativa abierta. "Es una brecha demasiado grande. Nadie va a aceptarla", sostuvo. A finales de 2025, según su ejemplo, la diferencia se habría reducido a 70 frente a 50. Ahora estima que los modelos de pesos abiertos alcanzan aproximadamente el 90% de la eficacia de los más avanzados y cuestan por token entre el 10% y el 25% de lo que cuestan estos últimos. Son valoraciones de Krishna, que no identificó pruebas concretas para contrastarlas.
Conviene detenernos en una expresión que aparece en toda esta comparación: modelos de pesos abiertos. Los llamados "pesos" son los parámetros numéricos que un sistema de inteligencia artificial aprende y ajusta durante su entrenamiento, y que después utiliza para procesar información y generar respuestas. Cuando una compañía los publica, otros pueden descargarlos y ejecutar el modelo en sus propios equipos, siempre dentro de las condiciones de su licencia. Eso no significa que conozcamos cómo se entrenó ni que tengamos acceso a todos sus datos y herramientas. Por eso, como explica la Open Source Initiative, disponer de los pesos no equivale necesariamente a tener un modelo de código abierto.
El ahorro del que habla Krishna se entiende mejor al mirar cómo se cobra por utilizar estos sistemas. Un token es una unidad con la que el modelo representa fragmentos del texto que recibe o genera, y muchos proveedores facturan según la cantidad procesada. "¿Prefiere algo que cuesta el 10% si alcanza el 90% del rendimiento del mejor, o quiere pagar un coste diez veces superior?", planteó el ejecutivo. Según los cálculos de IBM, una gran empresa media podría comenzar con dos o tres racks, armarios que alojan servidores y otros equipos, para ejecutar estas alternativas. Pero esa infraestructura exige inversión, electricidad, mantenimiento y personal especializado. El ahorro real depende del volumen de uso, hasta el punto de que contratar una API puede seguir siendo más económico para cargas de trabajo reducidas.
Después de los costes llega una pregunta inevitable: ¿qué trabajos necesitan realmente el modelo más avanzado? Krishna admite que algunos sí, pero considera que muchas tareas empresariales pueden resolverse con opciones más económicas. Mencionó ejemplos cotidianos, desde resumir un correo electrónico y redactar otro hasta examinar un contrato o atender una llamada de un cliente. "Todo eso puede hacerse igual de bien con la alternativa mucho más barata", aseguró. Es su valoración sobre esos usos, no una garantía de que cualquier sistema ofrezca resultados equivalentes en todos los casos. La elección también depende de la complejidad de cada tarea y de la fiabilidad que necesitemos.
Las afirmaciones de IBM no están aisladas. En mayo de 2026, la Organización para la Cooperación y el Desarrollo Económicos (OCDE) publicó un informe, basado en datos anteriores, que situaba a los modelos de pesos abiertos en torno al 90% del índice de calidad de las alternativas cerradas al llegar al mercado, pero con un precio equivalente al 20% en servicios en la nube. Hay matices importantes: el AI Index 2026 de Stanford señala que, en marzo, el mejor modelo cerrado superaba en un 3,3% la puntuación del mejor de pesos abiertos en Arena, una clasificación basada en evaluaciones comparativas de usuarios. Son métricas diferentes y ninguna establece una equivalencia universal de capacidades.
Conviene tener presente quién plantea esta comparación. IBM desarrolla su propia familia de modelos Granite y trabaja en tecnologías para facilitar el despliegue de inteligencia artificial, aunque también mantiene una alianza con OpenAI. Tiene, por tanto, intereses comerciales en este mercado, pero el debate que plantea va más allá de sus propios productos. Si una empresa puede resolver buena parte de sus necesidades con alternativas más económicas, utilizar siempre el sistema más avanzado deja de ser una decisión tan evidente. La cuestión está en encontrar el equilibrio adecuado entre capacidades, costes y control, sin comprometer la calidad de los resultados.

articles.title: Jensen Huang says Nvidia's AI chips carry "the lowest" risk of any asset and could serve as collateral for debt
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says the company's AI accelerators can remain productive for eight years or longer, thanks to their performance, versatility, and continued software improvements. He argues that the traditional four-year lifecycle commonly associated with graphics processors no longer reflects the useful life of Nvidia's computing systems.
Speaking with Yahoo Finance's Deirdre Bosa on the sidelines of Nvidia's GTC conference in Berlin, CEO Jensen Huang described the company's AI accelerators as "productive," "fungible," and "durable." He argued that investors and lenders should rethink how they evaluate investments in AI infrastructure.
According to Huang, the risk of lending against Nvidia hardware is "the lowest of any asset," because the chips retain significant residual value across multiple customers and workloads. This versatility could make them attractive collateral for loans. Huang argued that financiers have yet to fully appreciate the flexibility of Nvidia's AI accelerators when assessing their long-term value.
Huang's comments echo similar remarks from Elon Musk, who recently argued that older AI accelerators can be more profitable than newer hardware for inference workloads because of their superior performance per watt. Musk believes companies should evaluate AI hardware based on how much intelligence it can generate per watt of electricity, rather than focusing solely on raw processing power.
To support this performance-per-watt approach, Musk pointed to Nvidia's H100 chips, which are reportedly worth more today than when they were first released. Improvements in AI models and inference techniques have enabled the same hardware to deliver better results than before, potentially increasing its value.
Both Huang and Musk are highlighting a trend that has been gaining attention for some time: Nvidia's A100 and H100 accelerators have retained more residual value than many might have expected. The B200 is an even more striking example, reportedly being rented out or traded at prices equivalent to 158% of its original purchase price.
However, several factors influence the second-hand market for AI accelerators, and rising prices alone do not tell the whole story. According to industry insiders, the value of older accelerators depends not only on their condition, availability, and system configuration, but also on the workloads they are expected to handle.

articles.title: PHP security issues could also threaten your NAS device — but not every vendor is able to patch just yet
articles.text:
PHP security issues could also threaten your NAS device — but not every vendor is able to patch just yet
The php2shell flaw affects more than just websites and web apps
- Critical PHP2Shell flaws also impact internet-exposed NAS devices and PHP-based Docker workloads
- Major vendors are still releasing patches, leaving some Synology, QNAP, and other systems exposed
- Researchers urge immediate updates, removal of public exposure, and VPN-only remote access
Websites and web servers are apparently not the only products affected by the php2shell vulnerability - Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices are at risk, too - and to make matters worse, some of the most popular manufacturers have not yet released a patch, despite the flaws being actively abused in the wild.
Research by Apple Insider noted that the flaw also affects software maintained by NAS manufacturers, as well as applications running independently in Docker containers, with NAS devices that are reachable through the public internet also at risk.
What's particularly concerning is that some of the biggest NAS manufacturers have said to be working on a fix, but the work is yet to be done. Synology, for example, released a new security advisory saying PHP versions 7.3 - 8.4, Mail Station, and Synology Calendar are all affected and adding that it released updated PHP packages to address the flaws. Those running Synology NAS products should head over to the company’s Package Center and download archive and look for updated PHP 8.2 and PHP 8.4 packages.
Twofold risk
The company also stressed that there is a difference between installed PHP packages and PHP components within DiskStation manager, and added that its built-in PHP isn’t exposed to the public internet, therefore most likely not at risk.
Another major NAS manufacturer, QNAP, confirmed a wide range of affected products, including QTS 5.2.11 and older, QTS 6.1.9, QuTS hero and QuTScloud, and Note Station 3. It said it was currently working on a fix, but did not give a timeline on when the patch might become available. So far, there is no evidence of in-the-wild attacks, but the company does recommend removing the devices from the open internet, disabling unnecessary port forwarding, UPnP, and remote-access services.
Other manufacturers are also currently working on a fix, including TerraMaster, Ugreen, and Asustor, Apple Insider found. “NAS owners should check their manufacturer's security notices and available updates for their specific models,” the publication said.
For NAS owners, the risk is twofold, since PHP is found in both the operating system and Docker containers.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Those running PHP-based services in Docker should check if their container images are running affected versions of PHP, and update them as soon as humanly possible.
There is also the problem of running older devices that have reached end-of-life and are, as such, no longer supported with patches. These, security experts agree, should be removed from public access. Unsolicited inbound connections should be blocked, and the device should be kept accessible only locally. Remote access should be achieved through a secure VPN, instead of forwarding NAS management ports.
P2PShell?
PHP2Shell is a name for a pair of vulnerabilities - CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 - that were recently discovered in the PHP programming language. They are considered critical and allow malicious actors to take over websites, steal data, deploy malware, and more. However, the story that has so far revolved around internet sites and web apps is now expanding into NAS devices, too.
PHP2Shell is shaping up to be the biggest security incident of the year, and possibly longer, arguably rivaled only by the Spectre/Meltdown flaws from eight years ago.
The pair of vulnerabilities - both critical in severity and both allowing for remote code execution - affects the vast majority of websites and web apps in existence today.
Knowledge of the flaws leaked four days before the patches were released, according to Amazon, and the number of exploitation attempts went from a few hundred 10 hours before publication, to millions today.
However, most of these attempts seem to have been unsuccessful. Analysis is ongoing as to why that is the case, with some researchers thinking code execution needs to get past ASLR, which is a difficult thing to do remotely. However, breaking in only seems to be a matter of time, which is why the security community urges manufacturers to release a fix as soon as possible, and owners to apply them without delay.

articles.title: Crows can evaluate visual info twice as fast as mammals
articles.text:
Much of what we know about how a brain makes decisions comes from studying monkeys watching dots. In a task known as a random-dot-motion task, a cloud of flickering specks drifts weakly in one direction while the subject tries to determine whether—and in which direction— it’s moving. The task has shown that in the primate neocortex, neurons gather visual evidence over time, with their firing rates climbing until they cross a threshold, when the animal commits to a decision.
But avian brains don’t have a neocortex, so it wasn’t obvious how they made similar decisions.
“This was the big question,” said Andreas Nieder, a neurobiologist at the University of Tübingen. “How [would] a differently organized avian brain encode decisions?”
To find out, Nieder and his colleague Philipp Schmidbauer put two carrion crows through the same task the monkeys faced, recording their brain activity along the way. The crows solved the task the same way primates do, using the same mathematical logic despite having a very different brain structure. And they did it two times faster.
A brain built different
Nieder and Schmidbauer put two hand-raised crows in front of a touch-sensitive monitor showing a cloud of white dots on black, with some fraction of them drifting coherently left or right or up or down. The birds’ job was to report the overall direction by pecking one of the targets that flanked the display. Correct answers earned them a mealworm.
“We intentionally wanted to have exactly the same random-dot motion task,” Nieder said. “The only difference was that the crows had to peck to indicate their decision, whereas monkeys were indicating by making an eye movement.”
The researchers varied how many dots moved together, ranging from 81 percent of the dots coherently moving together, which is trivially easy to determine, down to 3 percent, which is barely distinguishable from noise. They also included a zero percent condition, in which there was no correct answer.

articles.title: UK proposes 14-year prison sentences for undersea cable saboteurs amid Russian trawler threats — government responds to growing threats with new criminal offenses and emergency powers to shut down services
articles.text:
UK proposes 14-year prison sentences for undersea cable saboteurs amid Russian trawler threats — government responds to growing threats with new criminal offenses and emergency powers to shut down services
Britain prepares new powers for future conflict
The UK government has outlined a set of plans for new powers and penalties to help it protect UK undersea cables during national security emergencies, the BBC reports. It follows reports that Russia is using commercial fishing trawlers to map undersea cables, with 500 incidents of Russian boats loitering above cables in the last four and a half years.
In a policy paper shared this week, the British government noted that the UK is "highly dependent" on undersea infrastructure owned by private sector companies. While the report notes that connectivity is "resilient," with "faults rarely causing noticeable disruption to data or energy availability," it's still "vulnerable to damage from accidents and potential sabotage."
As a result, the UK is consulting on changes to legislation to try and address these risks, especially as the "threats to the homeland from state actors are increasing" and "critical national infrastructure, including undersea cables and pipelines... continue to be a target."
The changes proposed include new criminal offenses. These include causing a security compromise to critical undersea infrastructure, capturing both physical and non-physical interference, including remote electronic interference, cyber activity and certain preparatory conduct directed at compromising infrastructure. There would also be further offenses linked to obstructing repairs and failing to preserve evidence, when requested.
With these new offenses, the UK government is threatening penalties on a three-tier scale. Up to 14 years' imprisonment is proposed for intentional conduct, 10 years for reckless conduct, and two years for grossly negligent conduct, along with potentially unlimited fines. It's also considering an even higher maximum penalty for more serious cases, and whether it'll apply solely within the UK's national waters or further afield.
The proposals also include new powers for government ministers. In a national emergency, UK ministers would gain powers that would allow them to order telecom companies to remove or disable services. Ministers would also be able to compel telecom companies to grant officials access to sensitive sites, including cable landing stations.
These proposals form a White Paper, the name for an official UK government policy paper for new legislation, with interested parties able to respond by online questionnaire until January 14, 2027.

UK relations with Russia, like much of the western world, have deteriorated since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, although other incidents, such as the Salisbury Novichok poisonings in 2018, have formed the backdrop of steadily worsening relations between the two countries.
Meanwhile, Russia has made several efforts to map and plan attacks against undersea cables in Europe. In September, reports suggested that NATO allies had foiled a Russian training exercise using a "secret weapon" against undersea cables in Norway. Meanwhile, back in January, Royal Navy attack helicopters were deployed to chase off a Russian ship loitering less than a mile from five undersea cables in UK waters, just one of the 500 incidents reported this week that have included Russian ships.
