articles.title: Cambridge Analytica's fallout is still costing Meta, this time $25 billion in New Mexico
articles.text:
No Big Enough: A few weeks after a jury found Facebook liable in the Cambridge Analytica case, a judge in Santa Fe imposed an unprecedented fine on its parent company. Meta will, of course, appeal, while New Mexico's attorney general insists that no Big Tech company is too powerful to be held accountable.
Santa Fe District Court Judge Francis J. Mathew recently imposed a $25 billion fine on Meta, Facebook's parent company. The ruling follows a jury verdict in September that found the social network had deprived New Mexico residents of their privacy and their right to know how major technology companies use their personal data.
According to New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez, the massive $25 billion civil penalty represents a "historic financial victory" for the state. New Mexico's authorities sued Meta over the Cambridge Analytica scandal, one of the most significant privacy controversies in modern internet history. The British consulting firm has long since gone bankrupt, but the fallout from the scandal continues to create major legal headaches for Meta.
A month ago, the jury found that Facebook had violated New Mexico's consumer protection laws more than 43 million times. The company allegedly provided third-party apps with unlawful access to users' data, mishandled hate speech, and knowingly profited from misinformation.
Torrez said Judge Mathew's penalty order demonstrates that such violations can have serious financial consequences for businesses. The attorney general's office successfully took on one of the world's largest corporations, and the ruling underscores the principle that no company is too powerful to be held accountable under the law.
The size of the fine highlights the importance of state consumer protection laws as a means of holding technology companies accountable, according to Torrez's office. However, the financial consequences for Meta could have been even greater. The judge determined that the company could have faced a fine of as much as $219 billion under New Mexico law, while a local attorney had sought a penalty ranging from $35 billion to $40 billion.
Meta had asked the court to cap the fine at $3.45 billion. The judge ultimately imposed a penalty between the maximum amount allowed and the sum Meta had sought, although the ruling still represents a substantial financial hit for the company. Torrez said the outcome "reinforces a fundamental principle: companies that do business in our state must follow our laws and respect the rights of our people."
According to Gil Luria, an analyst at D.A. Davidson & Co., the New Mexico ruling carries a hefty price tag, but Meta remains a company valued at nearly $2 trillion. Meta, whose business relies heavily on digital advertising, warned that the verdict could significantly affect its ability to operate in New Mexico. The company has said it will appeal the ruling.

articles.title: Nintendo Switch 2 é desbloqueado via software pela primeira vez • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Nintendo Switch 2 é desbloqueado via software pela primeira vez
Pesquisador identificou falha que permite rodar aplicativos não oficiais e modificar jogos no console.
O Nintendo Switch 2 foi desbloqueado pela primeira vez via software, pouco mais de um ano após o lançamento. Batizado de ns2jb, o método permite executar código não autorizado sem instalar modchips ou realizar modificações físicas no console.
A descoberta foi apresentada pelo pesquisador Sammy Hajhamid, conhecido como “pepsipu”, e funciona na versão 23.0.1 do sistema, atualmente o firmware mais recente do Switch 2. O jailbreak, no entanto, possui limitações e não oferece o mesmo nível de acesso que usuários conseguiram ao desbloquear o Switch original.
O processo é feito apenas por software e não exige abrir o videogame ou soldar componentes na placa. Segundo o pesquisador, o ns2jb aproveita falhas encontradas no SmileBASIC 4, aplicativo de programação criado para o primeiro Switch e executado no Switch 2 graças à retrocompatibilidade.
Uma das vulnerabilidades permite executar código não autorizado e alcançar componentes privilegiados do sistema, incluindo o módulo responsável pelo gerenciamento de arquivos, permissões bloqueadas para desenvolvedores independentes.
O método ainda é complexo e precisa ser executado de novo sempre que o Switch 2 é reiniciado. Relatos desta quinta-feira (22/10) indicam que o SmileBASIC 4 foi removido de algumas regiões da Nintendo eShop, especialmente na Europa, enquanto ainda aparecia disponível em outros mercados.
O método abre possibilidades para pesquisas e desenvolvimento de softwares não oficiais, conhecidos como homebrew. Entre os recursos identificados estão a execução desses programas, o backup de arquivos de salvamento, a modificação de jogos e a análise do hardware e do sistema do Switch 2.
Essa técnica também permite acessar diversos periféricos do console, o que pode contribuir para o desenvolvimento de ferramentas e projetos experimentais. Para demonstrar o funcionamento, o pesquisador modificou Mario Kart World e adicionou personagens que não fazem parte do jogo original.
A situação lembra os primeiros passos da cena de desbloqueio do Switch original. Em 2018, uma falha no chip Tegra X1 acabou abrindo caminho para homebrew e emulação no console da Nintendo, uma das empresas mais ativas contra a pirataria digital.
O jailbreak atual não oferece controle completo, não instala um firmware personalizado e não consegue executar cópias de jogos comerciais. O método é classificado como “tethered”, ou seja, as alterações desaparecem da memória e o sistema volta ao normal quando o console é desligado ou reiniciado.
O desenvolvimento também chamou atenção pelo uso do Codex, da OpenAI. Agentes de IA ajudaram a analisar o console enquanto recebiam imagens da tela e enviavam comandos remotamente, contribuindo para identificar vulnerabilidades.
Isso não significa que a tecnologia tenha desbloqueado o console sozinha. O próprio pesquisador esclareceu que o jailbreak exigiu cerca de duas semanas de trabalho. Já a modificação de Mario Kart World usada na demonstração foi desenvolvida com ajuda de IA em um dia.
Vale lembrar que o desbloqueio do console é um método não oficial. O acordo de uso do Switch 2 proíbe explicitamente tentativas de contornar ou modificar as proteções do console e prevê que alterações não autorizadas podem fazer com que o aparelho ou parte de seus recursos fique inutilizável.
Isso não significa que a Nintendo esteja banindo usuários do ns2jb, ao menos por enquanto. Ainda assim, testar o jailbreak em um aparelho conectado à eShop ou aos serviços online envolve riscos.

articles.title: US banks scramble to restrict AI agent activity — agents detected accessing customer accounts or even attempting to make transactions in breach of policy
articles.text:
US banks scramble to restrict AI agent activity — agents detected accessing customer accounts or even attempting to make transactions in breach of policy
Banks can't determine if AI agents are working under user instructions or going rogue.
A new report claims that major U.S. banks have now detected AI agents accessing customer accounts, and that some are even attempting to make transactions. Axios reports that it’s hard to differentiate between an actual human and an unauthorized bot, which is why some institutions, including Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan, and Wells Fargo, are blocking the technology and changing their terms of service to account for this.
While an AI agent or AI assistant can access an account with a user’s permission and through the use of their login credentials, this often goes against bank policy that requires users to maintain control of their account and not share it with anyone else. One of the fears that executives have is when an AI agent with login access takes unauthorized steps, like spending money or moving funds around without the explicit instructions of the account owner. There have even been situations where an AI agent called the bank directly and took actions independent of direct user command. Even though it wasn’t explicitly told to do that transaction, it considered it a crucial step to accomplish the task assigned to it.
One hypothetical example of this is when a user tells an AI agent to purchase an item but gives it a credit card with no available limit. The AI agent could then have accessed the user’s bank account to move some funds from whatever account it sees that has available funds to then effect the transaction, even if the user did not explicitly tell them that they could use the money in that said account. This is just one example where an AI agent’s transaction could go wrong, which is why several U.S. banks are now restricting third-party AI agents from accessing their platforms. Nevertheless, they still recognize that their customers might want to use tools like AI agents to monitor their finances. This is why some institutions have given or are moving towards read-only access for AI agents, which is something that they’ve been doing for years already.
The move comes against a background of burgeoning AI agent use, coupled with the risk that agents can and often do act beyond their remit, making mistakes or performing tasks without instruction, often with disastrous results. An unsupervised AI agent recently deleted a TV show's entire edit weeks before broadcast, forcing the program off air. AI agents are notorious for deleting databases and directories, making it a small leap to imagine they cause some havoc with unfettered access to a bank account.
Financial institutions have deep experience when it comes to employing new technology while ensuring that their critical infrastructure remains safe — something that AI labs lack, according to a former OpenAI safety employee. Despite that, banks are still concerned about the speed at which AI technology is developing, fearing that the technology’s capabilities might outrun their ability to control it, which is why they’re preparing for worst-case scenarios and even planning for “day after” scenarios after a catastrophic AI event.

articles.title: Exclusive: Star Trek is bringing a Red Tolarian Terror to Magic: The Gathering, and we have yet another Green Landfall Commander to show-off too
articles.text:
Exclusive: We've got a first look at two new Star Trek Magic: The Gathering cards, including a Red Tolarian Terror that I'm very glad isn't Common
Not one, but two Uncommon previews for Star Trek
Magic: The Gathering is ready to boldly go where it has never gone before with its upcoming Star Trek Universes Beyond set, and I have a pair of cards from it to showcase for you today!
Let’s start with Jake Sisko, War Correspondent. A mono-Green Commander with Landfall is nothing new, though I see them working much better in the 99 given their ability, especially in more budget-friendly or color-restricted decks after somewhat reliable card draw.
I’m coming back around on incidental lifegain, especially on cards like this where it’s not the only reward for your chosen strategy — in this case, playing as many lands as possible. In more grindy, elongated games, it can help you cling to life for a turn or two more to eke out a win, and can offset any life loss afflicted by your value engines.
The Clue reward for your second land drop each turn isn’t as useful as a full card, but in a deck with access to plenty of mana (which Landfall decks tend to be) and especially in such decks without the card draw efficiency afforded by Blue, it’s not a terrible alternative.
Tireless Tracker sees play for this reason, and while Jake Sisko is arguably worse given the restrictions on its Clue generation, it does offer a little redundancy.
If you do want to build Jake Sisko, War Correspondent out as a Commander, I’d recommend including cards like Academy Manufactor, Stridehangar Automaton, and Tippy-Toe, Terrific Partner which each turn you Clue into a Clue and other tokens — Tippy-Toe will also turn even one Landfall trigger into card draw on your end step. You’ll also want cards like Captain Kathryn Janeway, Exploration, and Asuza, Lost but Seeking to help you consistently play two lands a turn.
Turning to Ravenous Cosmozoan, a Red Tolarian Terror that gives up protection and some stats for Flying and Haste — lending itself to a more immediately aggressive approach the turn it comes down.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
At Uncommon, the Cosmozoan won’t see the Pauper play of its predecessor, but I fear it may mimic Terror’s low Standard play rate.
There are some notable differences. Flying and Haste should help the Cosmozoan pressure opponents more aggressively the turn it comes down — even if it packs a softer punch — and notably it cares about all nonland, noncreatures in your Graveyard, not merely your Instants and Sorceries.
We’ll have to wait and see if that’s enough to save it, though.
The best (perhaps only) place for it may unfortunately be Limited. If the environment is more grindy and games tend to go a little longer, it shouldn’t cost more than a couple of mana in the late game, and a few of these could swing over an opponent’s board to steadily chip them down to zero — perhaps as a surprise attack thanks to its Haste.

articles.title: RFK Jr.’s vaccine injury clinic could damage NIH hospital, board warns
articles.text:
At a recent meeting of the board that oversees the National Institutes of Health’s Clinical Center Research Hospital, chair Jack Leslie opened with cheerful introductions and gregarious chatter—then diverted from the agenda of the regularly scheduled meeting. He spent the next six minutes delivering a pointed rebuke of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, warning that his anti-vaccine activities could tarnish the venerable hospital, often called the “house of hope” for patients with rare conditions or those who have exhausted all other options.
Leslie took issue with a recent stunt Kennedy had pulled at the hospital, which involved making a surprise appearance for a ribbon-cutting ceremony to open his signature vaccine injury clinic. The ceremony included a panel with people claiming to have been injured by vaccines. They sat behind placards reading “vaccine injured” and spoke with Kennedy and other high-ranking Trump administration officials.
Leslie prefaced his comments by noting that some might prefer he not speak out against Kennedy’s efforts. “But I think that that would be a failing as an advisory board if we were silent,” he said. Leslie also noted that he has no concerns about studying potential injuries from vaccines. “Serious reactions are rare, but real,” he said, and people who believe they’ve been injured should “be taken seriously.”
In fact, the NIH already has a center that studies vaccine injuries, and Kennedy’s splashy new clinic does not come with more funding or clinic space. The hospital’s CEO, Jonathan Green, who sat next to Leslie at the meeting, chimed in to confirm that “the NIH has conducted research on the safety and efficacy of vaccines for decades in the past, and it ongoes.” Green described Kennedy’s vaccine injury clinic as merely a new, individual “protocol” for the hospital.

articles.title: Tempête Austen : pourquoi votre smartphone peut-il perdre tout réseau mobile alors qu’il a encore de la batterie ?
articles.text:
Tempête Austen : pourquoi votre smartphone peut-il perdre tout réseau mobile alors qu’il a encore de la batterie ?
Alors que la tempête Austen balaie le nord-ouest de la France, des centaines d’antennes-relais tombent en panne, privant soudainement les smartphones chargés de tout accès au réseau.
Depuis la soirée du jeudi 22 octobre, la tempête Austen frappe durement la façade ouest et le nord de l’Hexagone avec des rafales dépassant localement les 140 km/h. Face au risque de coupure électrique, le premier réflexe consiste à recharger intégralement son téléphone portable pour rester connecté. Pourtant, de nombreux habitants de Bretagne, de Normandie et des Pays de la Loire constatent avec surprise la disparition totale des barres de réseau sur leur écran, qu’il s’agisse de la 4G ou de la 5G.
Des centaines d’antennes-relais privées de courant dans le Grand Ouest
Un smartphone chargé à 100 % ne suffit pas pour passer un appel ou naviguer sur Internet pendant la tempête Austen. Pour acheminer vos communications, votre appareil doit impérativement se connecter à une antenne-relais située à proximité. Or, ces infrastructures fonctionnent grâce au réseau électrique classique, lourdement chahuté par les intempéries. Lorsque les vents violents et les chutes d’arbres provoquent des coupures de courant chez Enedis, les émetteurs des opérateurs s’éteignent eux aussi.
Ce vendredi 23 octobre en matinée, les fichiers officiels d’indisponibilité de Free Mobile, Orange, SFR et Bouygues Telecom recensaient déjà 412 sites mobiles affectés en Bretagne, en Normandie et dans les Pays de la Loire, dont 258 déclarés en panne depuis le début de l’épisode venteux jeudi soir. La Bretagne paie le plus lourd tribut avec plus de 200 installations touchées. Si la plupart des antennes disposent de batteries de secours pour absorber de brèves microcoupures, cette autonomie ne dure généralement que quelques heures.
De plus, le rétablissement de l’électricité dans un quartier ne garantit pas un retour immédiat de la 4G ou de la 5G. Comme le rappelle Orange dans ses consignes dédiées aux intempéries, certains équipements qui se sont mis en sécurité face aux variations de tension nécessitent le déplacement d’un technicien sur place pour être relancés manuellement.
En attendant la remise en état du réseau, inutile d’activer et de désactiver le mode avion à répétition sur votre téléphone pour espérer voir quelques barres de réception. Cette manipulation n’aura aucun effet sur les antennes privées d’alimentation, qui n’émettent de toute façon plus aucun signal. Si votre box internet fonctionne encore et que votre forfait le permet, activez plutôt les appels Wi-Fi dans les réglages de votre smartphone pour rester joignable.

articles.title: Der Deal steht, der Security-Fragebogen nicht: So wird Compliance zum Wachstumstreiber
articles.text:
Security-Fragebogen bremst den Deal? So wird Compliance zum Wachstumstreiber für Enterprise-Vertrieb
Und der Fragebogen ist erst der Anfang: Der nächste Kunde verlangt ISO 27001, ein Automotive-Kunde TISAX, ein US-Kunde SOC 2. Je größer die Kunden werden, desto mehr entscheiden schnelle und belastbare Compliance-Nachweise über den Vertriebserfolg.
Was Enterprise-Kunden wirklich prüfen
Security-Fragebögen sehen auf den ersten Blick nach vielen unterschiedlichen Anforderungen aus, drehen sich inhaltlich jedoch meist um dieselben Fragen:
- Wer darf auf welche Systeme zugreifen (Berechtigungskonzept)?
- Welche Dienstleister verarbeiten Daten (Vendor Management)?
- Wie werden Sicherheitsvorfälle behandelt und welche Löschfristen gelten?
- Welche technischen und organisatorischen Maßnahmen (TOMs) sind konkret umgesetzt?
Bei kleineren Deals reicht oft eine Selbstauskunft. Bei Enterprise-Kunden, regulatorischen Vorgaben (wie NIS2, DORA, dem Cyber Resilience Act oder dem EU AI Act) und branchenspezifischen Standards kommen formale Nachweise wie ISO 27001, SOC 2 oder TISAX hinzu.
Der Kunde fragt dabei nach der Kontrolle und dem Nachweis, nicht nach dem spezifischen Framework dahinter. Viele Unternehmen haben deshalb kein neues Compliance-Problem, sondern ein Wiederverwendungsproblem: Wer jedes Framework als separates Projekt behandelt, beschreibt Controls neu, sucht Nachweise erneut zusammen und dokumentiert Verantwortlichkeiten mehrfach.
Die Antworten existieren meist schon, sie sind nur verteilt
Das Problem sind selten die 200 Fragen selbst, sondern dass Antworten im Unternehmen verstreut liegen: Datenschutz bei Legal, ISO 27001 im ISMS, Richtlinien in SharePoint und technische Docs bei der IT.
Dabei überschneiden sich oftmals die Anforderungen. Ein dokumentiertes Berechtigungskonzept oder ein Incident-Prozess lassen sich für nahezu jedes Framework nutzen. Die Skalierungsfrage lautet daher: Wie nutzen wir einmal erarbeitete Controls und Nachweise für möglichst viele Anforderungen?
Compliance-Dokumentation wird zur technischen Schuld
Aus der Softwareentwicklung ist das Muster als „Technical Debt“ bekannt: Gleiche Logik existiert mehrfach, ohne zentrale Quelle. Wird bei Compliance ein Prozess geändert, aber nur an einer Stelle aktualisiert, tauchen beim nächsten Audit widersprüchliche Versionen auf. Das erhöht den Aufwand und gefährdet Audits.
Unternehmen brauchen eine zentrale Quelle (Single Source of Truth):
- Ein Control wird einmal beschrieben.
- Ein Nachweis wird einmal gepflegt.
- Anschließend wird gemappt, welche Framework-Anforderungen damit erfüllt sind.
Kommt ein neues Framework hinzu, prüft man nur noch die Lücken (Gap-Analyse), statt bei null zu beginnen.
Was sich automatisieren lässt und was nicht
Software eignet sich hervorragend für:
- Automatisches Mapping: Verknüpfung von Überschneidungen zwischen Frameworks.
- Reusability: Systemische Wiederverwendung bestehender Controls und Nachweise.
- Gap-Analyse: Schnelle Identifikation fehlender Informationen.
Vollständig automatisieren lässt sich Compliance dennoch nicht. Ob NIS2 oder der Cyber Resilience Act bei komplexen Unternehmensstrukturen greifen oder wie der Scope einer Zertifizierung gezogen werden sollte, erfordert fachliche Bewertung. Software schafft die Struktur und reduziert Routinearbeit – strategische Entscheidungen bleiben Aufgabe von Expert:innen.
Vom Rechercheprojekt zur Unternehmensinfrastruktur
Mit einem zentralen Fundament verändert sich der Vertriebsprozess fundamental: Security-Fragebögen werden von aufwendigen Recherche-Projekten zur einfachen Abfrage vorhandener Daten. Nachweise lassen sich wiederverwenden und neue Frameworks docken nahtlos an. Compliance wird so zum Enabler für schnelles Enterprise-Wachstum.
Wie heyData diesen Ansatz in der Praxis umsetzt
Entscheidend ist, dass geleistete Compliance-Arbeit wiederverwendet werden kann. Genau darauf ist heyData ausgelegt:
- Zentrale Plattform: Bündelt Datenschutz, Informationssicherheit und AI-Governance an einem Ort.
- Multi-Framework-Ansatz: Controls und Nachweise werden einmalig angelegt und flexibel in verschiedenen Frameworks (z. B. ISO 27001, NIS2, DSGVO) zugeordnet.
- Hybrider Ansatz: Wo reine Software an ihre Grenzen stößt, unterstützen Domain-Expert:innen aus Datenschutz, Recht und Informationssicherheit bei Audits und regulatorischen Einordnungen.
Mehr als 2.500 Unternehmen nutzen heyData bereits, um Compliance nicht mehr isoliert pro Framework aufzubauen, sondern auf einem zentralen Fundament zu bündeln.

articles.title: Google’s Data Agent Kit Hits GA, Splitting Agent Guardrails Between Skills and IAM
articles.text:
Google recently made Data Agent Kit generally available, moving it out of the preview it ran through the summer. It is free, it is open source, and it installs into coding agents Google does not own. It ships two kinds of control, and the difference matters in production.
Data Agent Kit is a set of MCP tools connecting an agent to more than fifteen Google Data Cloud services, plus Google-authored skills that teach it practices like optimizing BigQuery SQL or designing Bigtable row keys. It runs in Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and VS Code-compatible editors, and comes preinstalled in Cloud Shell and Cloud Workstations.
Data Agent Kit sits between the coding agent and Google Data Cloud services as two components: skills carrying best-practice guidance and MCP servers exposing live schema and tools. (Source: Google Blog post)
With the GA release, the company adds BigQuery Graph, Bigtable, and Managed Service for Apache Spark. Product manager Arun Nair and developer advocate Jeff Nelson, who wrote the launch post, pitch it at a gap agents have by default: they write good SQL but know nothing about "which tables exist, how they’re partitioned, which ones your team trusts, or why last night’s job failed."
The plugin repository carries 37 skills under Apache 2.0, each with frontmatter naming Google as publisher. It is versioned properly, with 1.0.0 cut on September 29 and 1.1.0 on October 13, so teams can pin it.
Among those skills is accidental-data-loss-prevention, which exists to stop the agent destroying something. Its description opens "STOP AND VERIFY" and tells the agent it "MUST obtain explicit user consent" before anything irreversible, listing DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, a DELETE missing a WHERE clause or using 1=1, storage deletions against production buckets, gcloud projects delete, and KMS key destruction. The procedure is halt, explain the impact, wait for affirmative consent.
That guardrail is advice. The agent is asked to obey it. A second control is not.
Asked in a LinkedIn post whether read-only investigation could be isolated from tools that modify infrastructure, Nelson answered that it is handled in IAM rather than per agent: run the agent as a read-only service account through impersonation, or use "an IAM deny policy that blocks any MCP tool where tool.isReadOnly is false."
The documentation gives the condition:
api.getAttribute('mcp.googleapis.com/tool.isReadOnly', false) == false
It denies the mcp.googleapis.com/tools.call permission, and applies at the organization, folder, or project level. Companion attributes cover resource.service and tool.name.
Three limits come with it. A blocked tool still appears in tools/list, so the agent sees capabilities it cannot use and finds out only on invocation. The controls cover Google Cloud MCP servers and nothing else. And resource.service and tool.name are gcloud only, absent from the console.
Amel Habira, an AI solutions architect, read the documentation and came away encouraged, noting the short-lived credentials, the read-only attribute, and a warning before agents execute notebook cells. He wrote:
Combine that with branching and time travel on the Iceberg side, and you can imagine containment at both the access layer and the data layer.
Ankit Dongre, an AI engineer at viaSocket, drew the boundary further out:
MCP access is the easy part. The production boundary is permission scope plus repeat-safe execution: what happens when an agent retries a write after a timeout, or when the schema changes mid-run?
IAM and dry runs cover authorization and preflight, he added, "but they do not tell the agent whether a timed-out write committed. A first-class result should carry an idempotency key plus commit status and rollbackability." Data Agent Kit’s tool results do not carry that today.
Microsoft put that decision somewhere else. Its Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management, in public preview, keeps governance intent in a Microsoft 365 admin surface and enforces it at a gateway, where per-tool blocking requires a preview tier and the application key is "gateway-scoped", reaching every model and tool. Google authorizes per tool in the IAM language customers already use, and propagates the user’s identity so row and column security applies.
Operators are sequencing either way carefully. Timon Knapp, founder of the self-hosted workload automation vendor Conductral, wrote:
Connecting agents to live environments like Airflow is powerful. From running production batch for years I would start with read access and suggestions, and let a human confirm anything that changes a schedule or reruns a job. A clean audit trail makes it much easier to give the agent more rights later.
Data Agent Kit costs nothing beyond the Google Cloud services an agent uses. The skills are on GitHub and forkable.

articles.title: Ontario to start consultations on developing digital IDs
articles.text:
The Ontario government is taking the first steps toward introducing digital identification cards, which will give residents the option of keeping their official credentials on their phones instead of relying solely on physical cards.
Keeping your digital credentials on your phone would be completely optional under the proposed changes, which would include permanently guaranteeing that Ontario residents can maintain access to their physical ID cards.
“As we modernize government services, we’re making identification more secure, convenient and cost-effective,” said Minister of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement, Stephen Crawford.
“Digital credentials will provide a trusted and seamless way to present identification, helping protect personal information while retaining every Ontario resident’s right to use physical I.D.”
The province says digital credentials would support a more seamless customer experience while also providing an added layer of security by reducing the risk of lost or stolen identification. Those with digital credentials would be able to store their ID on their mobile devices and use them to access services in person or online.
Starting later this year, the provincial government is set to begin consultations that will help shape the development of digital credentials. Following these consultations, the province plans to introduce a digital version of the Ontario Photo Card, a government-issued photo ID card for residents who do not have a driver’s licence.
Additional consultations and the digital Ontario Photo Card testing are set to support the introduction of optional digital driver’s licences and health cards on a future date.
In late 2027, the Ontario government intends to introduce legislation that would protect Ontario residents’ right to obtain and only use physical ID cards, with digital credentials being optional.

articles.title: UK detective investigated for allegedly using Microsoft Copilot to make decisions in criminal cases
articles.text:
Facepalm: Most people already know that there are some tasks where you really, really shouldn't rely on AI, especially those that deal with sensitive matters. It should come as little surprise, then, to learn that a UK police detective is being investigated over allegations they used Copilot to help make decisions in criminal investigations.
The senior Derbyshire Constabulary officer is facing an investigation by the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) over alleged gross misconduct. According to the BBC, the inquiry began in August, following a voluntary referral from the force on June 23 after an internal review of the detective's AI use.
The allegations go beyond asking Microsoft's assistant to check some sentences for spelling and grammar errors. The officer allegedly used AI to formulate policy decisions, assess and manage risk, and justify decisions during criminal investigations. They are also accused of entering sensitive operational and personal information relating to cases into the tool.
Derbyshire had actually approved Copilot for officers to use in May 2025. It was meant to help with tasks such as drafting reports and summarizing information. However, that permission came with conditions barring the input of operational, sensitive, or personal data.
Emily Barry, the IOPC's director of engagement, said: "These are serious allegations and it's right they are investigated thoroughly and independently."
Investigators will examine the detective's Copilot use between May 2025 and June 2026 to determine whether professional standards were breached. The officer has received a gross misconduct notice, but no finding has been made.
AI has already been making its way into police paperwork elsewhere. It was previously reported that US police departments were adopting Axon's Draft One, which generates report drafts from body-camera audio. Officers were required to check and approve the results, although concerns remained about inaccurate information and an increasing reliance on automated writing.
Earlier this year, there was a bizarre example of AI getting police paperwork wrong. An AI-generated report in Utah claimed an officer had turned into a frog after the software picked up audio from Disney's The Princess and the Frog playing in the background. A human caught the mistake before the report was submitted.
The sensitive-data element also brings to mind Samsung's experience in 2023, when employees submitted confidential code and meeting information to ChatGPT. As reported at the time, attempts to speed up routine work ended up handing company information to an outside service.

articles.title: Clientes do Airbnb não vão mais precisar lavar a louça • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Clientes do Airbnb não vão mais precisar lavar a louça
Mudanças nas regras da casa colocam limites nas exigências dos anfitriões. Além da louça, quem aluga a casa não pode mais ser obrigado a retirar o lixo.
O Airbnb atualizou as chamadas Regras da Casa, orientações gerais dadas aos anfitriões do serviço de aluguel de temporada. No documento, algumas questões polêmicas chamam atenção. Agora, por exemplo, não é mais permitido obrigar os clientes a lavarem a louça e retirarem o lixo, assim como colocar a roupa de cama usada na máquina de lavar.
Os donos das casas e apartamentos também não podem mais impedir os usuários de utilizarem comodidades anunciadas, como ar-condicionado e ventilador, por exemplo. Segundo a empresa, os pedidos devem ser “razoáveis de acordo com a nova política”.
Com as novas regras, anfitriões não podem avaliar negativamente quem deixar o lixo dentro de casa ou a louça suja na pia, por exemplo. Nas redes sociais, diversos usuários repercutiram a novidade, afirmando que lavar a louça e deixar a casa minimamente arrumada são “questão de educação”.
A atualização também trouxe mudanças na interface do serviço, que passa a mostrar as instruções de checkout em uma seção separada. Ao todo, são sete regras padrão disponíveis, além dos pedidos dentro do que é permitido. Segundo o Airbnb, as opções podem ser configuradas no próprio Editor de anúncio.
Por padrão, é necessário informar:
Além delas, os pedidos pontuais dos anfitriões também podem ser incluídos nos anúncios, mas com as novas restrições levadas em conta. Caso essas informações adicionais não sigam a política do app, uma mensagem vai aparecer no próprio Editor destacando os trechos que precisam de ajustes.
A empresa enviará ainda um e-mail com dicas para resolver problemas relacionados, e os clientes podem se deparar com um aviso relacionado a pedidos específicos como as exigências de limpeza. Vale lembrar que, apesar de não ser mais permitido exigir louça lavada e retirada de lixo, os anfitriões podem solicitar que os pratos sujos fiquem na pia ou que os clientes separem lixo orgânico de embalagens recicláveis, por exemplo.

articles.title: Probarse ropa antes de comprarla en internet ya es posible con esta IA de Google
articles.text:
El probador virtual de Google permite anticipar cómo quedará una prenda antes de pagarla en una tienda digital, mediante inteligencia artificial generativa aplicada a una foto personal.
La herramienta, llamada “Pruébalo” o “Try On” en inglés, busca resolver una de las mayores desventajas de comprar ropa por internet: la imposibilidad de probársela antes de recibirla en casa.
Qué es “Pruébalo” y cómo funciona
La función está desarrollada por Google y funciona con un modelo de generación de imágenes especializado en moda. Según explicó la compañía, el sistema “entiende” el cuerpo humano y los matices de la ropa, así como la forma en que los distintos materiales se pliegan, se estiran y se adaptan a diferentes cuerpos.
A diferencia de un montaje simple, la herramienta interpreta la postura, las proporciones corporales y la caída de la tela para generar una representación más realista del resultado final.
“La herramienta conserva estas sutilezas cuando se aplican las prendas a poses en tus fotos, por lo que el resultado te permite ver cómo luciría en ti, en lugar de ver sólo una imagen fija o en un modelo”, detalló Google.
La función permite probar tops, pantalones, vestidos y zapatos, y da acceso a miles de millones de artículos disponibles en el inventario de Shopping de la compañía.
Cómo usar la herramienta de Google paso a paso
Para emplear “Pruébalo”, el primer paso es buscar un producto en Google e ingresar a la pestaña de Shopping, que aparece junto a otras modalidades como “Imágenes”, “Noticias” o “Videos”. También se puede acceder directamente a través del sitio de Google Shopping correspondiente a cada país.
Una vez dentro, los pasos son los siguientes: seleccionar una prenda, tocar el ícono “Pruébalo”, subir una fotografía personal y esperar el resultado generado por la inteligencia artificial.
Se recomienda que la foto sea de cuerpo entero, de frente a la cámara, con los brazos hacia abajo, buena iluminación, fondo limpio y ropa ajustada. También conviene evitar que aparezcan otras personas en la imagen, ya que esto puede afectar la precisión de la simulación.
Una vez cargada la primera foto, el sistema la almacena para no tener que subirla nuevamente en cada nueva prueba. Además, los looks generados pueden guardarse para compararlos más adelante o compartirlos con otras personas.
Si la prenda convence, el usuario puede tocar el botón de compra para ser redirigido al sitio del comerciante y completar la orden.
Requisitos, limitaciones y disponibilidad
La función ya está disponible en Argentina, Chile, Colombia y México, según informó Google al ampliar su alcance en América Latina. Previamente, la herramienta había comenzado a operar en Estados Unidos, Canadá, Reino Unido, Japón, India y Australia, países donde su implementación resultó progresiva.
Para acceder a “Pruébalo” es necesario contar con una cuenta activa de Google, ser mayor de 18 años y tener habilitadas opciones como la Actividad en la Web y la Personalización de la Búsqueda.
La herramienta no admite todo tipo de productos: funciona con partes de arriba, partes de abajo y vestidos, pero excluye lencería, trajes de baño y accesorios. Tampoco está disponible en productos patrocinados.
Google aclaró que las imágenes generadas pueden contener errores en detalles o proporciones, por lo que recomienda complementar la prueba con la revisión de tallas, descripciones y opiniones de otros usuarios antes de concretar una compra.
En materia de privacidad, la compañía indicó que las fotos cargadas no se utilizan para entrenar modelos ni se comparten con terceros, y que no se recopilan datos biométricos durante el proceso. El usuario puede eliminar sus imágenes en cualquier momento.
Cómo usar asistentes de IA para probar ropa
Más allá de “Pruébalo”, los principales asistentes de inteligencia artificial también pueden funcionar como probadores virtuales, entre ellos Gemini, ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude y Meta AI.
Para lograrlo, hay que seleccionar el modo de generación de imágenes, adjuntar una foto de cuerpo entero y una captura de la prenda deseada, y pedirle a la IA que edite la imagen para mostrar cómo luciría el producto puesto.
Para mejorar el resultado, se recomienda incluir en la solicitud el enlace del producto, las medidas corporales exactas en centímetros (pecho o busto, cintura, cadera, hombros y altura) y el talle que se piensa comprar.
Estos asistentes también pueden actuar como asesores de vestuario, con capacidad de analizar talles, tipos de calce, cortes y colores, y ofrecer una recomendación sobre si conviene adquirir esa prenda u optar por otra.

articles.title: Agent cloud startup Daytona hits $1B valuation backed by FirstMark and a who’s who of angels | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Daytona Platforms announced on Friday that it had raised a $60 million Series B round at a $1 billion valuation led by FirstMark Growth. The company says it has now raised a total of $91 million.
The New York-based startup has attracted not just FirstMark (which also led its $24 million Series A in February), but also a host of well-known angels in this latest round. Daytona says they include Stripe’s Patrick Collison, Shopify’s Tobi Lütke, Perplexity’s Aravind Srinivas, Zoom’s Eric Yuan, Datadog’s Olivier Pomel, Quora’s Adam D’Angelo (who is also an OpenAI board member), and Mercor’s Brendan Foody. It also names Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Next, and Okta Ventures as participants.
Three-year-old Daytona is building a cloud specifically for long-running agents, which have different infrastructure needs than yesteryear’s software, the startup contends. “Agents don’t work like the long-lived services today’s cloud was designed for. They spin up thousands of short, stateful jobs nobody planned in advance, and they need a cloud built for that,” founder Ivan Burazin wrote in a blog post announcing the new round. Daytona’s cloud, he said, is like giving every agent its own computer, where agents have access to sandboxed versions of Linux, Windows, macOS, and GPUs, among other services, on the one platform.

articles.title: Kenya’s Spiro rolls out first 100 e-bikes in Ghana as pan-African expansion continues - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Kenyan electric mobility company Spiro has launched its first 100 electric motorcycles in Ghana, introducing its Ekon 450 M1 V3 model and battery-swapping network to the West African market.
Spiro is Africa’s largest electric mobility company, operating the continent’s most extensive and fastest growing network of battery-swapping for electric two-wheel vehicles. It has operational assembling facilities in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Togo, Cameroon and Benin.
The company is positioning the Ekon 450 M1 V3 as an alternative to petrol-powered motorcycles for everyday riders, particularly commercial riders and delivery fleets whose earnings depend on fuel costs and time on the road. It is paired with Spiro’s battery-swapping technology, which lets riders exchange a depleted battery for a charged one at a swap station in around two minutes instead of waiting to recharge.
The Ghana rollout comes as Spiro accelerates its continental expansion off the back of a US$270 million equity funding round, as well as US$18 million in debt financing from the Africa Go Green Fund.
“Ghana represents a major opportunity for electric mobility, with a rapidly growing two-wheeler market and increasing demand from commercial riders and delivery fleets,” said Kaushik Burman, CEO of Spiro.
“With the launch of the Ekon 450 M1 V3, we are bringing a solution that addresses two key barriers to adoption: operating costs and access to charging infrastructure. Our first 100 motorcycles mark the beginning of our ambition to make electric mobility accessible at scale across Ghana.”
Spiro currently operates in seven countries, with more than 156,000 electric motorcycles on the road and over 2,500 battery-swapping stations, including 11 mega swap stations in Kenya and Rwanda. It has facilitated more than 57 million battery swaps to date, covering over 3.1 billion kilometres. It aims to be present in 20 African markets, and is preparing to enter Ethiopia, Malawi, Mali and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

articles.title: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 creative director speaks on Dawn of War influences and on-field reinforcements were almost cut because 'lore-wise it didn't make any sense' and 'it's not something a ton of RTS games have' — 'We actually tried it out and now we love it'
articles.text:
'Maybe you win the battle but lose the war because you put all your resources into one battle' — Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 creative director says King Art Games 'wanted battles to take a while' so borrowed from the original strategy game's systems
The original Dawn of War is the studio's "north star" for inspiration
- Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 creative director Jan Theysen has explained how the original Dawn of War influenced the new game's RTS systems
- Theysen says King Art Games "wanted the battles to take a while" in Dawn of War 4
- He says that the game's on-field reinforcement feature was almost cut because it was "weird," but now the team loves it because it "brings the macro [management] and the economy side into the battles"
King Art Games co-founder and Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 creative director Jan Theysen has described how the game manifests the classic real-time strategy (RTS) experience of the original Dawn of War.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, Theysen explained that the first question the team asked itself was which game it wanted to draw inspiration from for the foundations of Dawn of War 4; it ultimately chose the first game, which was released in 2004, as it was the more "classic RTS" and the game the team refers to as its "north star."
"We basically said, 'Okay, we want to do a new Dawn of War,' but then the question was: 'What are we talking about? Dawn of War 1 or 2?' Which are both great but very different," Theysen said. "Maybe even Dawn of War 3. And we said, 'Okay, let's really go back to Dawn of War 1, which for us was more this classic RTS with base building, with big battles."
King Art looked at how big the battles were and how long they took in the original game, and decided on a larger and longer "time-to-kill" gameplay system for the newest iteration.
"We wanted the battles to take a while, so that you can actually throw more units into the battle, right?" he said. "And maybe you win the battle and lose the war because you put all your resources into this one battle, for example; it was something that we looked into a lot, because you know it's something that different RTS [games] handle very differently.
On-field reinforcements is one of the "weirder" things Dawn of War 4 will feature, which Theysen revealed King Art didn't have initially because it's an old system that not many modern RTS games have. Turns out, when the team tested it, [and they] really liked it.
"We felt like it was a little bit weird, right?" he said. "Lore-wise, it doesn't make any sense, and even gameplay-wise, it's not something that a ton of RTS games have. Maybe it's a weird thing that they had like 20 years ago, and maybe it's not that important, but then we actually tried it out, and now we love it."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The creative director added that "we think it's great" because on-field reinforcement also "brings the macro[management] and the economy side into the battles," as well as the real-time unit control with micromanagement.
"By just auto-healing everything or auto-reinforcing everything, the battles become easier, but actually the economy part suffers, right? Or it becomes harder," Theysen explained. "But if you are more about the macro and more about the big picture, it might be totally fine to just put all your units on auto in battle, and they'll do their stuff.
"While if you're really into micro, you probably say, 'no, I can optimize the battle', and then you spend less time in the macro but more in the micro, and that's also fine, and that is maybe an example you know that we directly took from Dawn of War 1."
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 is slated to launch on PC on December 3.

articles.title: Besoin d’un PC portable pour travailler et vous divertir ? Ce Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 passe à 659,99 € chez Amazon
articles.text:
Le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 est un ordinateur portable dont la configuration est adaptée à la bureautique et aux loisirs du quotidien. Amazon le propose actuellement à 659,99 € au lieu de 899,99 €, et offre même sa livraison.
L’idéal, pour un ordinateur portable avant tout destiné à travailler, c’est qu’il permette aussi de vous divertir pendant vos pauses. Le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 15AMN8 disponible à 659,99 € chez Amazon peut répondre à ces différents usages : il est adapté à la bureautique, mais permet aussi de surfer sur le Web, de regarder des vidéos ou encore d’écouter de la musique de manière confortable. Ce modèle est doté d’un processeur AMD Ryzen 5 40, de 16 Go de RAM et d’un SSD de 512 Go, et il fonctionne sous Windows 11 Famille.
Adapté au télétravail comme au divertissement, le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 passe de 899,99 € à 659,99 € chez Amazon.
Pourquoi choisir le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 ?
- Pour son écran spacieux : la dalle IPS Full HD de 15,6 pouces convient à la bureautique et au visionnage de séries.
- Pour ses 16 Go de RAM : cette capacité laisse de la marge pour utiliser confortablement plusieurs programmes en même temps.
- Pour son SSD de 512 Go : il offre de la place pour installer ses logiciels et conserver ses fichiers sans passer systématiquement par le cloud.
Un ordinateur pour travailler à la maison et ailleurs
Avec son écran de 15,6 pouces doté d’une définition Full HD, le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 donne accès à une diagonale d’écran confortable. Et malgré cela, il reste facile à transporter : son poids avoisine 1,62 kg et, lorsqu’il est fermé, son épaisseur est de seulement 17,9 mm. Ce modèle comprend également un clavier AZERTY avec pavé numérique, une webcam HD et une connectique composée de ports USB-A et USB-C, d’une sortie HDMI et d’un lecteur de cartes SD.
Une configuration bureautique qui garde ses limites
Si le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 se veut adapté aux usages multimédias de base, son processeur Ryzen 5 40 et sa puce graphique intégrée Radeon 610M restent limités pour les jeux récents ou gourmands. Quant aux 16 Go de mémoire vive, ils sont soudés sur la carte mère, ce qui empêche d’augmenter la quantité de RAM.
✅ Les points forts
- Écran IPS Full HD de 15,6 pouces.
- 16 Go de RAM et SSD de 512 Go.
- Connectique variée et lecteur de cartes SD.

articles.title: Confiner l'IA devient un casse-tête : après sa pause de 11 jours, OpenAI explique pourquoi couper Internet ne suffit pas
articles.text:
OpenAI est revenu sur la sécurité de ses modèles dans une communication publiée le 23 octobre. Les cas de « désalignement », ces comportements qui s’écartent de ce que l’on attend des IA, se sont accumulés ces derniers mois avec pas moins de 20 incidents constatés sur l’année 2026.
Chez OpenAI, des agents sont notamment parvenus à pirater Hugging Face pendant une évaluation interne. D’autres ont appris à dissimuler leurs erreurs.
En septembre, un nouvel accès non autorisé à Internet avait conduit l’entreprise à suspendre certains travaux sur ses modèles les plus avancés. OpenAI précise désormais que cette pause a duré onze jours, jusqu’au 1er octobre, pour renforcer ses protections et les mettre à l’épreuve.
Pourquoi faut-il confiner une IA pendant son entraînement ?
Trouver une information, écrire du code, résoudre un problème : pour entraîner une IA, OpenAI (et d’autres) force son modèle à trouver une solution. Le modèle essaie, échoue, recommence, et les essais réussis servent ensuite à renforcer les comportements qui l’ont mené au but. Mais comment s’assurer qu’il ne prend pas un raccourci interdit pour y arriver ?
D’où l’idée de l’enfermer dans un environnement contrôlé, souvent appelé « bac à sable ». L’IA y dispose d’outils pour travailler, mais ses accès sont limités. Un peu comme un terrain d’exercice : elle doit pouvoir s’entraîner sans intervenir sur les systèmes extérieurs.
Or, un modèle peut chercher à contourner ces limites pour terminer sa tâche. En septembre, un agent d’OpenAI devait simplement retrouver l’auteur d’un billet de blog. Ses recherches n’aboutissant pas, il avait profité d’un filtrage insuffisant du DNS (le service qui traduit les noms de sites en adresses) de son bac à sable pour interroger un chatbot extérieur, malgré l’interdiction d’accéder à Internet. Personne ne lui avait demandé de tester la sécurité de son environnement.
Pour OpenAI, les protections actuelles ne suffisent pas encore pour laisser ses modèles les plus avancés accéder au véritable Internet pendant leur entraînement. L’entreprise compte appliquer cette règle tant que la recherche et les outils de surveillance n’auront pas progressé. L’entreprise explique :
« Bien que l’accès à internet puisse aider les modèles à acquérir des compétences utiles, il offre également à un agent compétent mais mal intentionné la possibilité d’influencer des systèmes hors de notre contrôle. », peut-on lire dans le billet de blog d’OpenAI.
Autrement dit, il faut à la fois apprendre aux modèles à respecter les règles et prévoir des barrières techniques au cas où ils les contournent. Les tests menés par OpenAI ces dernières semaines montrent pourtant que couper le réseau ne supprime pas tous les moyens d’échanger.
Même sans réseau, les agents trouvent un moyen de communiquer
Dans une expérience supervisée menée après l’incident de septembre, l’équipe d’OpenAI a voulu vérifier si ses agents pouvaient communiquer malgré les barrières censées les isoler.
Pour cette campagne, OpenAI a mobilisé des équipes d’agents fondées sur ses modèles les plus puissants, dont le futur GPT-6 Astra Cyber, et y a consacré des centaines de milliards de tokens. Les agents disposaient du code source de l’infrastructure, de sa configuration et d’une documentation sur ses failles possibles. Les essais se déroulaient sur des copies isolées des systèmes de recherche.
Les chercheurs ont demandé à des agents IA de communiquer depuis des espaces informatiques séparés, sans réseau ni fichier commun. Mais ces espaces partageaient le même processeur et sa petite mémoire rapide, appelée « cache ». Un agent chassait certaines données de cette mémoire, ce qui obligeait l’autre à aller les chercher, plus lentement, dans la mémoire principale. En chronométrant ses propres opérations, le second détectait ces ralentissements. Avec un code convenu entre eux, ces variations devenaient un message (un peu comme du morse), où les accès rapides et lents remplacent les signaux courts et longs. Aucun fichier ne passait de l’un à l’autre. L’information circulait uniquement par les variations de vitesse du matériel partagé.
On peut imaginer deux personnes dans des pièces voisines du même bâtiment sans téléphone, qui tapent contre la cloison pour se parler. Il leur suffit de convenir d’un code et d’un tempo pour se comprendre. Ici, le matériel partagé joue le rôle du mur, et les différences de vitesse remplacent les coups.
Ces expériences permettent de comprendre jusqu’où peut aller l’IA pour réussir une tâche, mais ici ils n’ont pas désobéi puisque les chercheurs leur demandaient explicitement de chercher ces passages, avec des indications dans la plupart des tests. L’expérience ne montre donc pas des IA décidant spontanément de se coordonner, mais les moyens mis en œuvre pour y arriver dans des conditions très dégradées.
Quelles protections OpenAI met-il en place ?
Après ces onze jours de pause, OpenAI détaille une protection à plusieurs niveaux. Sous Linux, les agents travaillent dans des conteneurs restreints, eux-mêmes installés dans de petites machines virtuelles. Le conteneur limite les fichiers et les processus accessibles. La machine virtuelle ajoute une séparation avec l’ordinateur physique qui l’héberge. L’objectif est de conserver une barrière si l’agent franchit la première.
Autour, les restrictions réseau doivent encore bloquer les accès interdits, même si l’agent prend le contrôle de la machine hôte. Des systèmes de surveillance cherchent à détecter les comportements dangereux et à arrêter automatiquement les travaux concernés.
Pour apprendre à naviguer, les agents disposent d’un « monde hors ligne », constitué de contenus web archivés. L’entreprise ajoute des contrôles contre les communications détournées et poursuit les tests de ses barrières. Elle précise toutefois que son infrastructure n’est pas entièrement déconnectée : son fonctionnement et sa supervision nécessitent encore des connexions extérieures.
Ces connexions peuvent aussi devenir des portes de sortie. Pour les tester, OpenAI a donné à des agents le contrôle d’une machine hébergeant ses environnements isolés. Ils ont trouvé des failles dans presque tous les services examinés qui conservaient un accès limité à Internet. L’un d’eux a notamment réussi à faire consulter une adresse web par un service interne : l’agent ne pouvait pas accéder directement à Internet, mais un intermédiaire le faisait à sa place.
L’enjeu dépasse donc le simple accès au Web. Fermer les portes les plus évidentes ne dispense pas de vérifier ce qui peut encore passer à travers les cloisons.

articles.title: „Es gibt immer noch so viel Unsicherheit“: Die gängige Neandertaler-Theorie gerät ins Wanken
articles.text:
„Es gibt immer noch so viel Unsicherheit“: Die gängige Neandertaler-Theorie gerät ins Wanken
Sie haben wahrscheinlich schon einmal in irgendeiner Form davon gehört: In vielen von uns schlummert eine Art innerer Neandertaler. Vor etwa 45.000 Jahren, als der eigentlich afrikanische Homo sapiens erstmals nach Europa kam, traf er auf Angehörige einer verwandten Spezies: die breitstirnigen, kräftiger gebauten Neandertaler. Eins führte zum anderen, und deshalb tragen manche Menschen noch heute eine kleine Menge Neandertaler-DNA in sich. So die allgemein anerkannte Theorie.
Dieser Text erscheint in der Ausgabe 7/2026 von MIT Technology Review. Darin beschäftigen wir uns damit, wie KI die IT-Sicherheit auf den Kopf stellt. Das Heft ist ab sofort in unserem Online-Shop und im Zeitschriftenhandel erhältlich.
Diese Neandertaler-DNA in unseren Genen ist wohl die berühmteste Entdeckung des 21. Jahrhunderts zur menschlichen Evolution. Sie wurde mit allen möglichen Merkmalen und Gesundheitszuständen in Verbindung gebracht und verhalf dem schwedischen Genetiker Svante Pääbo zum Nobelpreis.
Neandertaler-Gene im Menschen: Forscher bezweifeln die gängige Erklärung
Vor zwei Jahren stellten jedoch zwei französische Populationsgenetiker die Grundlage dieser weit verbreiteten Theorie in Frage. Lounès Chikhi und Rémi Tournebize, damals Kollegen an der Université de Toulouse, schlugen eine alternative Erklärung vor. Das Problem sei, sagen sie, dass die ursprünglichen Belege auf der statistischen Annahme beruhen, dass sich Menschen, Neandertaler – eine Spezies, die sich vor mehr als 400.000 Jahren von der Linie des Homo sapiens abgespalten hatte – und ihre gemeinsamen Vorfahren alle zufällig in riesigen Populationen auf einem Kontinent fortgepflanzt hätten.

articles.title: Consultant comes clean for sparking worldwide panic by accidentally breaking the PHP vulnerability embargo — user says they were unaware of disclosure restrictions, move 'clearly backfired in a pretty wild fashion'
articles.text:
Consultant comes clean for sparking worldwide panic by accidentally breaking the PHP vulnerability embargo — user says they were unaware of disclosure restrictions, move 'clearly backfired in a pretty wild fashion'
The leaks were coming from multiple users, however.
A Hacker News user who shared news about the recent PHP vulnerabilities revealed by ChatGPT Sol before an embargo, which they claimed to be unaware of, has taken to the platform to apologize for the post. According to petecooper, they shared the CVEs because they wanted to alert others who follow the four-week PHP release cycle about the importance and urgency of the matter, but they weren’t aware of the news blackout that went with the two identified vulnerabilities.
The user said they have "No connection or affiliation to any of the organisations involved." Noting, "I am a self-employed consultant for my day job, and a solo founder of a mental health non-profit on the side." Petecooper's original post about the vulnerability was among the first to break the NDA, though they claim they were unaware.
“I posted here about the then-upcoming PHP RCEs related to CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619. I appreciate this has had considerable knock-on effects with the schedule for co-ordinated disclosure, and created additional workload. I am truly sorry. I take full responsibility for my actions,” petecooper wrote on the platform. “It was not remotely my intention to cause any of the subsequent side effects. At the time of posting, I didn’t know about any embargo. My contact had told me there was no embargo, and her contact had told her the same thing.”
CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are two critical vulnerabilities, both scored at 9.2. It seemed that the PHP Foundation planned for a controlled public release, allowing affected websites and applications to be patched before the vulnerabilities became widely known. Unfortunately, it seemed that some recipients of the warning failed to share the embargo that came alongside the CVEs, spreading the news earlier than expected.
It should be noted that petecooper apparently wasn’t the only one who leaked the news early. Multiple leaks had already been circulating on social media and other platforms, which forced the PHP Foundation to move its announcement up by one day. Despite that, the organization mentioned that Chainguard broke the embargo by more than six hours. Dan Lorenc, the co-founder and CEO of Chainguard, defended the move on LinkedIn, saying that he made the call after talking to several other researchers and immediately notified the group after releasing the fix publicly, and not just his customers.
The vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 were bugs in the PHP runtime itself that were discovered using AI tools, not attacks by rogue AI. Still, the abilities of this technology could make it easier for both security researchers and bad actors to find vulnerabilities that could have been lurking in widely used code for years, if not decades. This makes it a race to find and deploy a fix before they can be exploited.

articles.title: Autonomy and control are not opposites, they go together: EY GDS at DevSparks Chennai
articles.text:
Autonomy and control are not opposites, they go together: EY GDS at DevSparks Chennai
At DevSparks Chennai 2026, Arvind Purushothaman of EY GDS made the case that moving agents into production is an engineering problem, not a model problem.
Ask a room of developers about agents today and you will get plenty of answers. Almost everyone has built one, and most have a demo they are proud of.
The harder question is what happens after that, when the agent has to hold up against real customers, real data, and real consequences. At DevSparks Chennai 2026, Arvind Purushothaman, Global Cloud Consulting, Microsoft Practice and Alliances Leader at EY GDS, opened with a version of it. He asked how many people in the room had built an AI agent, and plenty of hands went up. Then he asked how many had built one that made it to production for a business-critical system. "I think that's where the numbers dramatically drop," he said. "Not because of anybody's fault, but that's how it is."
That gap is the whole problem, and it is not a model problem. Cloud, low code tools, and open model APIs have pushed the entry barrier close to zero. What has not changed is the difficulty of industrializing what you build. "Access to intelligence is not the bottleneck, but the ability to industrialize is going to be the bottleneck," said Arvind Purushothaman.
From the nets to the match
Drawing on a cricket analogy, he said that hackathon builds are like net practice, where a few lines of Python and an API key let you rehearse your reverse scoop all afternoon. The match is different. You need 12 runs off six deliveries under pressure, and the strokes only matter alongside the ability to read the situation.
For agents, that pressure arrives when the demo meets regulated data, compliance requirements, integration points, and business-critical workflows. Skip the rigor and the exposure is concrete: a bad transaction, financial loss, reputational damage, security and privacy failures. The question itself changes, Purushothaman said, from does it work in a demo to "can we trust it repeatedly under real operating conditions."
More autonomy means more engineering
Traditional software ran on deterministic rules and stage gates that everything had to clear before production. Agents behave differently. They interpret context, reason about a goal, and decide for themselves which tools to use to reach an outcome.
The instinct is to read it as less work for engineers. Purushothaman argued the opposite. More freedom for the agent means more engineering responsibility for the people around it, because the system has to constrain, restrict, and verify what the agent does. "Autonomy and controls … they are not the opposite of each other in this world," he said.
He offered three maturity levels to locate yourself against. Task-based agents automate specific steps and return an output. Goal-oriented agents are handed an objective, such as how much credit limit a customer should get, and assemble their own data and policies to reach a recommendation. The third horizon is humans and agents as one team, with judgment reserved for critical calls.
Ontologies, controls, and platform
Three foundations make production deployment possible, and they only work together. Domain context and ontologies codify business knowledge, taxonomy, and decision logic, and mature vendors now ship them by industry. Controls evaluate outcomes for quality, bias, and risk, and produce traceability. The platform makes execution repeatable and scalable. Ontologies without controls create chaos, controls without a platform are not repeatable, and a platform without domain context is generic.
The same logic scales up.
The model is only one part of the system, so the engineering has to cover data context, cloud and compute, integration APIs, security and identity, responsible AI, and FinOps discipline around cost. "The outcome is only as strong as the weakest link in your chain," Purushothaman said.
Every agent needs a passport
Take a customer asking a bank to raise their credit limit. The agent has to establish identity, retrieve the applicable risk policy before anything else so it knows which boundary it is operating under, pull the relevant data, and interpret context. The recommendation has to stay inside policy guidelines, and if the risk is high, it should transfer to a human. Every step has to be auditable. Without that preserved history, he said, it is not a production-ready system.
Hence the agent passport. Every agent gets an identity, a named business owner and technical owner, defined permissions covering where it can operate, and escalation points. Organizations already carry deprecated software they cannot account for, and agents will multiply that problem faster. Production systems also need circuit breakers: anomaly detection, the ability to halt execution, roll back, and escalate to humans.
What value actually looks like
Asked how to measure return, Purushothaman pushed back on counting agents deployed and tokens consumed. The number that matters is cost per governed business outcome, counting cloud and agent running costs, the human effort still in the loop, and the risk profile. "You don't want to over-engineer a simple ask, and you don't want to under-engineer a complex ask. It should be right for the outcome."
Testing, he added, has to shift from fixed test cases toward simulating production like runtime conditions. Asked whether robustness holds as attackers keep evolving, he conceded that the how will change while the fundamentals will not. "We talked about the why. We talked about the what. The how will evolve."
He closed on the sharpest line of the session. "Intelligence is abundant, but trust, accountability, and repeatability, we must still engineer."

articles.title: Abandoned Popcorn Time app exposed millions of devices to RCE attacks
articles.text:
Researchers remotely disabled a vulnerable updater in the abandoned Time4Popcorn app, a fork of the Popcorn Time BitTorrent client, closing a security flaw that could have allowed attackers to execute malicious code with elevated privileges on millions of computers.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-30612, affects Windows and macOS updaters that contacted the app's abandoned domain (popcorntimeupd.xyz) over unencrypted HTTP and accepted executables without verifying digital signatures.
Anyone controlling the update domain could manipulate HTTP traffic and execute code as SYSTEM on Windows and as root on macOS.
The Popcorn Time app featured a Netflix-style interface that integrated BitTorrent downloads, allowing users to consume illegal content right directly inside the app.
The project was abandoned for legal reasons but later relaunched as a legitimate content-streaming app. However, forks such as Time4Popcorn emerged under the Popcorn Time name, quickly attracting millions of users.
Researchers at Eye Security discovered the security risk after registering the popcorntimeupd.xyz domain and observed up to 3 million Windows and 350,000 macOS client connections to Time4Popcorn.
Connections came from residential ISPs and corporate, government, and military networks. However, none of the users appeared to be actively using the app, suggesting it had been installed and forgotten.
“If we were able to send an update, we could potentially get code execution on millions of systems,” Eye Securit notes, adding that “the impact would be severe if this were to fall into the wrong hands.”
Following this discovery, the researchers registered 14 more domains associated with the service.
Securing the systems
Between November 2025 and March 2026, Eye used the vulnerable update mechanism to deliver remediation code that stopped and disabled the updater.
Their payload collected no host data or telemetry, and deleted no files on the users’ computers, keeping their actions within a fully legal context.
Eye explains that it had to modify its payload during testing to evade antivirus products that flagged it for disabling a service.
After deploying the remediation, Eye recorded 2 million update downloads, and by March 1 this year, requests to its update domain dropped by 98%.
Following the successful completion of the remediation operation, domain ownership was passed to the non-profit security organization The Shadowserver Foundation.
Despite this success, the researchers warned that the risk is not fully eliminated for users of the app.
First, Android users remain exposed as installing an update would require user interaction, and researchers could not disable the updater remotely for the mobile platform.
Second, the Time4Popcorn app uses a severely outdated Chrome engine from 2014, with no sandbox protections, which could be exploited in attacks.
The best course of action would be for users to remove the software entirely from their systems.

articles.title: Una novela premiada con 20.000 euros resultó estar escrita en un 99% por inteligencia artificial
articles.text:
La novela corta “Donde el agua trabaja”, del escritor peruano David Silva Rojas, fue escrita en un 99% por inteligencia artificial, según el detector Pangram. La obra había ganado en julio el primer Premio Internacional de Novela Breve Almadía Ventosa-Arrufat, dotado con 20.000 euros, según informó este viernes el diario español El País.
El hallazgo llevó a la editorial mexicana Almadía a suspender la presentación del libro prevista para este viernes en Madrid, así como el resto de la gira por Barcelona, Sevilla y Cádiz. El País calificó el caso como el primero de este calibre detectado en la literatura en español.
El premio fue convocado en noviembre de 2025 por Almadía junto a la fundación española Ventosa-Arrufat. Las bases eran explícitas: la participación implicaba declarar que la obra no había sido escrita, ni parcial ni totalmente, con herramientas de inteligencia artificial, bajo pena de descalificación en cualquier fase del proceso.
Entre 2.204 manuscritos enviados desde 22 países, el jurado eligió por unanimidad la novela de Silva Rojas, abogado e investigador de 45 años nacido en Ica. Lo integraron la escritora mexicana Cristina Rivera Garza, la argentina Selva Almada y la ecuatoriana Mónica Ojeda, quienes destacaron “el uso de los silencios” y un lenguaje de oraciones breves que evitaba “la tentación del panfleto”.
Un análisis sobre el libro completo
El País no se basó en fragmentos sueltos: analizó la novela entera, unas 26.000 palabras, con la versión 4.1 de Pangram, la herramienta que la propia investigación del periódico había identificado antes como la más fiable del mercado para detectar texto generado por máquinas.
La compañía detrás del detector sostiene que su tasa de falsos positivos es de apenas uno por cada 24.000 textos escritos por personas. Su consejero delegado, Max Spero, explicó en el pódcast Mixed Signals que esa cifra surge de probar el sistema con millones de textos anteriores a 2022, previos a la existencia de los modelos actuales de IA.
El diario encontró además otras señales. Pangram atribuyó a una IA el 97% de las respuestas que Silva Rojas dio en una entrevista publicada en septiembre por la revista Ulrica, mientras que el texto de la periodista que la firmaba salió calificado como enteramente humano. Un texto autobiográfico de 924 palabras que el autor publicó ese mismo mes en la web de Ventosa-Arrufat obtuvo un 80% de IA.
La respuesta de la editorial
Contactada por El País a primera hora del viernes, la editorial Almadía dijo sentirse sorprendida y aseguró que en ningún momento del proceso había sospechado del autor. El diario compartió con el sello varios de los indicios reunidos y preguntó por la existencia de borradores o registros de versiones anteriores del manuscrito.
Desde Almadía respondieron que la cuestión es compleja y pidieron tiempo para hablar con Silva Rojas y continuar con sus propias averiguaciones. El autor, según el diario, no respondió a nuevas llamadas para ofrecer su versión de los hechos.
El primer sospechoso tras un rastreo más amplio
El hallazgo llega apenas una semana después de que el mismo diario analizara 175 libros populares en España y concluyera que uno de cada tres superventas autopublicados contiene una proporción considerable de texto generado con IA. Ninguno de los libros premiados que había revisado entonces mostraba señales, hasta la aparición de “Donde el agua trabaja”.
El caso también llega dos días después de que se confirmara que el canadiense Thélyson Orélien usó inteligencia artificial para escribir su novela “C’était ça ou mourir”, premiada en Francia, lo que llevó a su editorial a desvincularse del autor tras una investigación interna.
“Donde el agua trabaja” narra la historia de una joven que deja su comunidad para trabajar en una hacienda vinícola de Ica, Perú, y había sido publicada internacionalmente el 13 de octubre, diez días antes de que se conociera el resultado del análisis.
El País advirtió que un resultado de Pangram no prueba por sí solo cómo se escribió un texto, ya que el sistema reconoce patrones estadísticos sin poder distinguir si una persona usó la IA de forma automática o para dar forma a sus propias notas e ideas. La editorial no había anunciado, hasta el cierre de esta nota, ninguna decisión formal sobre el futuro del premio o del libro.

articles.title: The Gentlemen (Netflix) : la saison 3 recrute de nouveaux acteurs et lance son tournage
articles.text:
The Gentlemen (Netflix) : la saison 3 recrute de nouveaux acteurs et lance son tournage
Netflix a annoncé le début du tournage de la troisième saison de la série The Gentlemen, qui verra de nouvelles têtes rejoindre le casting tandis que certains acteurs quittent l'aventure.
Les péripéties d'Eddie (Theo James) et Susie (Kaya Scodelario) vont continuer dans la troisième saison de The Gentlemen, dont le tournage a débuté. Il aura lieu au Royaume-Uni et au Maroc au cours des prochains mois et voit la série Netflix ajouter plusieurs nouveaux visages à sa distribution.
Direction le Moyen-Orient
Dans la saison 3 de The Gentlemen, Eddie et Suzie s'embarquent dans leur projet le plus ambitieux : ouvrir un casino au Moyen-Orient. Mais alors que le danger les attend dans chaque recoin, l'ambition sans borne du Duc va-t-elle enfin trop loin ?
Pour tenir tête à ce duo intrépide dans la nouvelle saison de la série de Guy Ritchie, Netflix a recruté de nouvelles têtes dont Robert Carlyle (Line of Duty), Elijah Wood (Yellowjackets) et Orlando Bloom (Le Seigneur des Anneaux).
Robert Carlyle, Elijah Wood, Orlando Bloom, Dexter Fletcher, Bruna Marquezine, Ed Speleers, Saffron Burrows and Bugzy Malone join the cast of THE GENTLEMEN Season 3.
