articles.title: I’d buy Epson’s entry-level EcoTank ET-2980 for its crisp low cost pages
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Epson’s entry-level all-in-one EcoTank is frustratingly light on features, but crucially, it can auto-duplex crisp and colorful pages at a highly competitive cost-per-page.
Reasons to buy
- + Plenty of inbox ink
- + Bright color prints
- + Motorized output tray
- + Low total cost of ownership
Reasons to avoid
- - No paper input drawer
- - High upfront cost
- - Small display
- - No fax, ADF, or USB Host
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
As the leader in cartridge-free printing, Epson also has the largest range of refillable printers, which now includes this entry-level all-in-one promising ultra low-cost color printing at home.
The white Epson EcoTank ET-2980 has several variants, including the black Epson EcoTank ET-2950 tested here, but it’s essentially a budget tank printer aimed at the small office or anyone who wants to cut their consumables bill by 95%.
Yes, bottled ink is that much cheaper than cartridge ink. But can it compete with the Brother DCP-T580DW and HP Smart Tank 210 to become one of our best ink tank printers?
Epson EcoTank ET-2980: Design and build
Type: color inkjet tank multifunction printer
Functions: Print, copy, scan
Connectivity: USB, Wi-Fi
Data storage slots: None
Max print speed: 15ppm
Max paper size: Letter/A4
Print quality: 4,800 x 1,200 dpi
Memory: unknown
Apple AirPrint: yes
Consumables included: 4 x bottled ink (6,600 black or 5,500 color pages)
Dimensions/Weight: 375 x 347 x 187 mm (WxDxH)/11.4lb/5.2kg
For an all-in-one bulk tank device with an integrated 8.5" x 11" scanner, the Epson EcoTank ET-2950 is reasonably compact. It replaces the outgoing Epson EcoTank ET-2850 and as well as printing a little faster using an improved printhead, I think it looks better too.
The tanks protrude less, and yet they’re still conspicuous enough that it’s easy to see the ink levels at glance. And I’m glad to see the capacity is the same, because Epson’s reservoirs are slightly larger than those of the Brother DCP-T580DW. The sleeker replacement also gets an attention-grabbing LED on top that illuminates usefully when there’s printing in progress.
There’s no touchscreen on this budget model, but the 1.4” color LCD is clear enough and the control panel tilts upwards conveniently. There’s no USB Host port and no paper input tray. Instead, you have to load paper in the rear tray, which can only hold up to 100 sheets. The whole thing weighs little more than 11 pounds making it feel insubstantial, so it’s somewhat surprising to find that the out-tray is motorised. That’s really the only luxury.
Epson EcoTank ET-2980: Features & specifications
We’re so used to seeing cartridge printers packed with features and selling for fifty bucks and less, that tank printers, which are not being subsidized in order to make money from their ink, can seem expensive.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Likewise, the feature set on this US$240 EcoTank could also look slim. As mentioned, there’s no touchscreen, no USB Host port and no paper drawer. There’s no ADF (automatic document feed) either, but these are all non-essential items that Epson has dropped to keep the price competitive.
Crucially, the Epson EcoTank ET-2950 can auto-duplex and has a flatbed scanner, unlike the HP Smart Tank 210, and it has Wi-Fi with AirPrint and Mopria compatibility. It can print on a wide variety of paper up to Letter or A4-size, including quite think cardstock, but its best feature is perhaps the generous amount of ink included in the box. Enough to keep you printing for three years according to Epson.
If you would rather have a printer with a paper input tray and an ADF for copying multiple documents at a time, you should consider the excellent step-up Epson Ecotank ET-3850 for around seventy dollars more. Or, if you don’t need auto duplexing or the scanning feature, you can save money with the economical HP Smart Tank 210.
Epson EcoTank ET-2980: Setup and operation
The Epson EcoTank ET-2950 comes with an easy-to-follow quick-start guide printed on a single sheet, but you probably won’t need it. When you plug in and turn on for the first time, the printer’s on-screen prompts will help you get your new printer online and printing the first test page in a matter of minutes.
Alternatively, you can use Epson’s free companion app for iOS and Android called Smart Panel to avoid having to enter your Wi-Fi password via the printer’s control panel.
Filling up with ink is also stress free as the capacity of the bottles matches that of the tanks. That’s 65ml for CMY and 127ml for black. And the keyed bottle necks mean you can’t pour the wrong color in the wrong tank. In day-to-day use, I’d say this is a user-friendly device, thanks to the reasonably sized color display and the intuitive companion app that really simplifies printing remotely.
Epson EcoTank ET-2980: Performance
The Epson EcoTank ET-2950 printed every test page on every type of media from card to envelopes without a hitch or a jam. It printed slowly but steadily with the quoted print speed of 15ppm for simplex mono printing proving accurate.
That slows to just 8ppm in color. In duplex mode, each page is turned over automatically and quite promptly, so long 2-sided documents can actually be printed out faster than the manual duplexing HP Smart Tank 210 despite its superior 22ppm print rate.
Black and white text pages are printed with crisp dark black characters that are smudge resistant and easy to read at small point sizes. Through the magnifying glass I can see evidence of overrun, but it’s not visible with the naked eye. If you need fast laser precision and rarely print in color, you should consider a mono laser printer like the Brother HL-L5100DN.
Color prints look rich and bright with well contained colors. It’s perhaps a tad too red and also slightly softer than some rivals. Epson is using its energy efficient Micro Piezo technology to deliver ink through a total of 784 nozzles. That’s 65% fewer than the cheaper HP Smart Tank 210 with its thermal inkjet system.
Although nozzle-count doesn’t equate directly with print quality (their quoted print resolutions are exactly the same) I think the Epson achieves less detail when it comes to printing photos at best quality on coated photo paper. For a business-oriented inkjet, its photo printing is perfectly acceptable, but it’s not a strong point.
Where the Epson EcoTank ET-2950 excels is in handling paper. I always find it annoying when there’s no front drawer and you have to load paper in the rear slot where it curls and collects dust. On the plus side, the paper path is straighter this way so the printer can feed through thicker media without causing a jam. I printed on envelopes, stickers and some pretty thick 300g/m² card with great results. The HP Smart Tank 210, for comparison, chokes on anything heavier than 200g/m².
The Letter or A4-sized flatbed scanner makes decent copies at 1,200 x 2,400 dpi resolution and is easy to operate with the dedicated ‘copy’ button. It’s a pity there’s no ADF to go with it, but at least it has a scanner bed, unlike the HP Smart Tank 210 which relies on your phone for scanning.
Epson EcoTank ET-2980: Consumables
The headline feature here is the three years’ worth of ink you’re getting in the box. To be more precise, that’s three 65ml bottles of colored ink and one 127ml bottle of black that should yield up to 5,500 color pages or 6,600 monochrome. That’s about the same as Brother, HP and Canon give away with their entry-level tank printers.
In this case, Epson’s 102 black ink is pigment-based, while the 102 CMY inks are dye-based because the quicker-drying pigment is better for smudge-free handouts. That’s different from the 106 inks Epson supplies with its photo printers which are all dye-based for their superior performance on coated photo paper.
Epson’s bottled ink is around 95% cheaper than its cartridge ink, though there’s nothing to stop you from using even cheaper third party bottled ink.
Epson EcoTank ET-2980: Maintenance
As with any inkjet printer, the printheads are liable to clog if left unused for long periods, but it’s easy to unblock any nozzles by running a cleaning cycle. Just go into the printer’s maintenance menu, choose one and it will automatically flush the nozzles with fresh ink until it can print a clean test page.
That detachable compartment at the rear corner of the printer is the maintenance box that catches any excess ink generated in this way and at some point in the printer’s lifetime, you may need to replace it.
Epson EcoTank ET-2980: Final verdict
Epson’s entry-level EcoTank all-in-one is short on features, but delivers crisp documents, vibrant color prints and exceptionally low running costs, with enough ink included to last three years.
Admittedly, there’s no touchscreen, ADF, USB Host port or even a front paper drawer, just a 100-sheet rear feed and small color display. But crucially, you still get automatic duplex printing, Wi-Fi and a flatbed scanner. Setup is straightforward using Epson’s excellent Smart Panel app, and the keyed ink bottles make refilling painless.
In my tests, the ET-2950 printed reliably on everything from envelopes to thick 300g/m² cardstock. It’s not a fast printer, but automatic duplexing is a welcome convenience. Pigment black ink produces crisp, smudge-resistant text, while dye-based colors look bright and punchy. Photographs are slightly soft and oversaturated towards red, but perfectly acceptable for occasional use.
The biggest attraction is the ink economy. Epson is putting plenty of ink in the box and replacement bottles are cheap. At around $240, the ET-2950 is relatively expensive upfront, but I think its low running costs, reliable performance and essential duplexing feature make it excellent long-term value.

articles.title: 5 cosas que deberías saber de ‘Clayface’ antes de ver la película de DC
articles.text:
Clayface es un experimento arriesgado y uno que demuestra que el Universo de DC está intentando encontrar identidad propia. Por un lado, alejándose de la premisa más colorida y humorística del Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel. Al otro extremo, también de toda la estética, temas y planteamientos del cancelado DCU. Por lo que James Gunn y Peter Safran intentan no solo encontrar una forma madura, original y complicada de contar las historias de la editorial. También, una que rinda tributo a sus largos años de historia y su importancia en la cultura popular y el mundo del cine.
Por ese motivo, la cinta de James Watkins parece continuar lo que Linternas comenzó con buen pie. Un tipo de premisa adulta, compleja y en este caso tenebrosa, que explore en el mítico universo de la editorial de una manera nueva. Una decisión que, además, trae al live-action a una figura lóbrega que ya es icónica en el mundo del cómic. Y la razón es obvia. Clayface es uno de los villanos más complejos de DC, caracterizado por su trágica transformación en un monstruo de barro maleable.
Aunque originalmente debutó en los cómics en 1940 como un asesino sin poderes sobrenaturales, el personaje evolucionó rápidamente. Todo, hasta convertirse en una masa cambiaformas capaz de imitar la apariencia, la voz y el ADN de cualquier persona. Un giro terrorífico que lo hace el candidato perfecto para la primera gran película de terror del estudio DC.
Un personaje complicado llega al live-action
Pero además, se trata de una exploración en el universo que tiene enormes posibilidades. Después de todo, su naturaleza física lo convierte en un enemigo formidable para Batman. Eso debido a que no solo posee una fuerza física colosal, sino que también puede infiltrarse en cualquier lugar sin dejar rastro. Por ese motivo, entender su impacto antes de Clayface es fundamental; explorar varios elementos intrigantes que le rodean.
De su origen teatral, la variedad de identidades que han portado el nombre hasta el drama psicológico que define su existencia. Todo pasando por sus habilidades únicas de combate y su rol dual entre el heroísmo y la villanía en el universo de Gotham. Te dejamos cinco cosas esenciales que saber del personaje para disfrutar mejor la cinta.
Una tortuosa historia de origen para ‘Clayface’
Si es la primera vez que escuchas sobre Clayface (además de sus variadas apariciones en el mundo animado de DC), te gustará saber esto. El Clayface original, Basil Karlo, era un actor de cine clásico. Uno además, que enloqueció al enterarse de que harían una nueva versión de su mayor película de terror sin él. Consumido por los celos y la desesperación, Karlo adoptó la identidad del asesino de la película, Clayface, para asesinar al elenco original.
Por lo que, aunque al principio no tenía superpoderes, esta conexión con el mundo de la actuación y el teatro definió la esencia del personaje. Algo que Clayface refleja en mayor o menor medida. Más interesante todavía. La tragedia de Karlo radica en su obsesión con la identidad y el aplauso. Por lo que convierte su posterior transformación física en una extensión metafórica de su incapacidad para aceptar la realidad y su pérdida de relevancia.
Aunque no es la misma historia, Clayface utiliza este trasfondo para explorar la locura de un artista dispuesto a destruir todo por recuperar su gloria. Que es, de hecho, el centro motor de la premisa de la cinta. Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries), la nueva versión del personaje, deberá luchar para recuperar su rostro y su celebridad. Y lo hará a un altísimo precio que destruirá su vida, su cuerpo y su salud mental.
¿Y quién es realmente ‘Clayface’?
A lo largo de la historia de DC, múltiples personajes han asumido el manto de Clayface. Lo que aporta diferentes matices al mito del villano y a su profundidad psicológica. Después de Basil Karlo, llegó Matt Hagen, quien obtuvo poderes moldeables al interactuar con un estanque de protoplasma radiactivo. Este, siendo la versión más popular y que forma parte de la serie animada de los 90.
Más tarde aparecieron Preston Payne, cuyo toque derretía la carne ajena, y Lady Clay (Sondra Fuller). Esta última, poseedora de habilidades de imitación perfectas. Eventualmente, estos personajes unieron fuerzas en el cómic formando el Sindicato de Barro. Un retorcido equipo en que el propio Basil Karlo los manipuló para absorber sus muestras de sangre. Por lo que terminó mutando finalmente en la gigantesca y monstruosa criatura de lodo viviente que el público general reconoce hoy en día.
De modo que, para crear una única historia de un personaje tan complejo, el guionista Mike Flanagan tomó una dirección interesante. La película toma como inspiración principal el aclamado episodio doble "Feat of Clay" de Batman: La serie animada (1992). Para construir la trama, el escritor mezcló los dos primeros rostros del villano en las viñetas. El nombre y la trágica adicción a una crema modeladora pertenecen a Matt Hagen (quien debutó en Detective Comics #298 en 1961 como un cazatesoros). Mientras que su trasfondo como un actor de Hollywood desfigurado se extrajo de la identidad de Basil Karlo, el Clayface original creado en 1940.
Un héroe complicado para DC
El verdadero peligro de Clayface no radica en su fuerza bruta, sino en su impactante inestabilidad psicológica y su crisis de identidad constante. Al ser capaz de transformarse en cualquier persona, el villano suele perder la noción de quién es realmente. Por lo que olvida su rostro original y termina quedando atrapado en las mentes de los individuos a los que imita.
Esta desconexión de la realidad le genera un sufrimiento interno profundo, convirtiéndolo en un monstruo trágico. Uno además, atrapado en un cuerpo que se derrite constantemente si no mantiene la concentración. Su mente fracturada lo hace un ser sumamente impredecible, capaz de pasar de una profunda melancolía a una ira destructiva en cuestión de segundos. Algo que añade una capa de horror psicológico a sus historias que va mucho más allá de un simple enfrentamiento físico con Batman.
¿Qué habilidades específicas tiene Clayface?
Las habilidades físicas de Clayface desafían las leyes de la biología y lo convierten en una pesadilla táctica para cualquier héroe. Al estar compuesto completamente de un barro denso y maleable, su cuerpo es inmune a los ataques físicos convencionales, como golpes o disparos. Los cuales simplemente lo atraviesan o quedan atrapados en su masa.
Además, puede moldear sus extremidades para crear armas gigantescas como martillos, hachas o picos. Por lo que es capaz de sofocar a sus víctimas envolviéndolas por completo. Además, su destreza para imitar el ADN y las huellas dactilares le permite engañar a los sistemas de seguridad más avanzados del planeta. Lo cual, claro, le hace un villano no solo temible por todo lo que puede hacer, sino porque en determinadas condiciones es virtualmente imparable.
Pero, si te lo estás preguntando, Clayface no es infalible ni tampoco invencible. Su única debilidad real suele ser el agua extrema, que diluye su forma. O en cualquier caso, las temperaturas extremadamente frías, que solidifican su cuerpo y le impiden moverse temporalmente. Algo que Clayface seguramente explorará en alguna parte de su trama.
La redención de un villano temible
A pesar de su monstruosidad, Clayface ha tenido arcos de redención significativos, demostrando que no es un villano unidimensional. En etapas recientes de los cómics, particularmente en la iniciativa DC Rebirth. De hecho, en este último, Batman le ofrece a un arrepentido Basil Karlo la oportunidad de usar sus talentos para el bien. Por lo que lo integra formalmente en los Gotham Knights.
Durante este período, Clayface lucha junto a la Batifamilia. Así que utiliza sus poderes de infiltración para salvar vidas y buscando desesperadamente una cura definitiva para su condición médica y mental. Este rol como antihéroe o aliado trágico añade una enorme riqueza narrativa al personaje. Un giro que probablemente veremos en el futuro cinematográfico de DC, ahora que Clayface ya es parte oficial del universo cinematográfico de la editorial.

articles.title: Laika has spent 20 years building up to Wildwood
articles.text:
Across several decades in Hollywood, Caleb Deschanel has seen a lot. He served as cinematographer on films like The Passion of the Christ and The Patriot, worked on sequences in The Godfather and Titanic, and directed a few episodes of Twin Peaks. Even still, nothing could quite prepare him for his first stop-motion project: working as the cinematographer on Wildwood, the latest release from Coraline studio Laika. While he knew that stop-motion was a long and involved process, he was still surprised by just how much work went into these movies. “When I started I thought it was one thing, and then I quickly found out that it was another thing,” Deschanel says. “It was much more complicated than I expected.”
Laika has spent 20 years building up to Wildwood
How the stop-motion animation studio blends traditional techniques with modern tech.
Laika has spent 20 years building up to Wildwood
How the stop-motion animation studio blends traditional techniques with modern tech.
Wildwood has been a long time coming. Laika CEO Travis Knight originally optioned the rights for the book of the same name, written by Decemberists frontman Colin Meloy, in 2011. But production didn’t begin until a decade later. “I’ve been working on it in some form or another for 16 years,” Knight, who also directed Wildwood, says. “The reason why I stuck with it, the reason why I had to make this movie no matter what, is because of what it meant to me personally. Underneath it all, it’s a story about love and loss and grief, it’s about the impossible things that love asks of us, and that meant something to me personally in a very profound way.”
It’s also the biggest production Laika has ever undertaken. Wildwood tells the story of a young girl named Prue who has to venture into the “impassable wilderness” that surrounds Portland in order to find her baby brother. When she enters the forest she discovers a fantasy realm reminiscent of Narnia, with magical spells, talking animals, and warring factions. It required nearly 50 animators and more than 200 puppets to pull it off, and the film is full of ambitious sequences, like a 12-minute battle with dozens of soldiers and a chase scene through a bustling Portland, where Prue’s brother is carried away by a gigantic murder of crows.
According to head of animation Brad Schiff, the studio’s ethos involves mixing “old-school craft with modern technology.” With each project, he says, Laika develops new techniques. If something works well, they then push the idea even further on the next project. For instance, on Laika’s previous film, Missing Link, the main character was outfitted with a diaphragm so that when an animator turned a screw on the puppet’s back, the diaphragm could expand or contract, creating the illusion that it was breathing. This has since become the standard for puppets in Laika’s films.
These may sound like small details, but over the years they add up. For costume designer Deb Cook, there wasn’t a single innovation on Wildwood that stood out to her, but rather the sheer number of tools she had at her disposal. “Over time we’ve gathered together a library of techniques that we’ve been able to put into practice on this movie,” she says. This was especially important on Wildwood, which features a huge range of costumes; in the city sequences everyone is dressed in modern clothing, whereas in the forest characters have more fantastical looks.
“It was much more complicated than I expected.”
For Wildwood, many of the advancements came down to materials. The costumes made use of more flexible fabrics, for example, and the team also engineered a new process for creating silicone that’s lighter and more durable than what they previously used. “We’ve done this so we can wean ourselves off of foam latex, which is stinky and it shrinks over time, and five years later it kind of just crumbles,” says Oliver Jones, head of characters and practical effects. “There are advantages to rethinking a lot of these materials that were our go-to probably since King Kong.”
The scale of Wildwood has also forced the studio to adopt another seemingly much more boring practice: being better organized. “They’ve been misplaced,” Cook says, when asked if she’s ever lost a puppet. “There’s now a very sophisticated tracking system because there are so many moving parts, and so many stages around the studio.”
And while much has been said about the large and elaborate sequences in the film — Knight says the epic battle scene is “probably the most technically challenging thing that we’ve ever done” — all of these techniques are designed to imbue more humanity into characters that are portrayed by puppets. In that regard, small details like the flow of fabric or the impression of breathing are vitally important.
“We also have really subtle and intimate scenes, quiet scenes that don’t have a lot of flash, that have virtually no sound design or music, where the only thing that you’re experiencing is the grief of a father talking about a secret that he’s been holding on to for 15 years, or a quiet moment of a woman grieving the loss of her son,” Knight explains. “These are moments where you have nowhere to hide and the performances of these little puppets — these little assemblages of steel and silicon and fabric that have no life of their own — completely spring to life because of the hand and the artistry of the human behind it. Those are the moments that I’m most proud of.”
In this way, the long road to Wildwood hitting theaters makes a lot of sense. Laika has been around for just over 20 years, and over the course of each film the studio has innovated to steadily push its craft forward. Knight may have been thinking about the film for 16 years, but creating the version that is coming out in 2026 wouldn’t have been possible without all of the learnings spread across films like ParaNorman and Kubo and the Two Strings.
For Knight, it’s been especially gratifying to bring it to life with a team of both Laika veterans and newcomers, including not only Deschanel but also a handful of young animators for whom Wildwood was their first feature film project. Some were young enough that Coraline, Laika’s very first film, was what inspired them to get into the field in the first place. “I was really moved by that,” says Knight. “It also made me feel old as shit.”
Wildwood is in theaters now.

articles.title: Egyptian ed-tech startup Learning Rockets helps children in Upper Egypt learn English - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian ed-tech startup Learning Rockets is helping children from pre-K to Grade 6 learn English through a connected system of books, a learning app and progress data.
The World Bank estimates that 70 per cent of 10-year-olds in Egypt cannot read and understand a simple text, while the country is rated “low proficiency” in the 2025 EF English Proficiency Index.
“In Egyptian schools, English lives in the school book and stays there,” co-founder and CEO Mariam Soliman told Disrupt Africa. “I saw three problems up close. Practice stops at the classroom door: at home, nothing connects to the lesson a child just learned. The apps parents download are fun, but they teach their own course, not the one the child is tested on. And nobody – teacher, principal or parent – sees how a child is doing until the exam. In Upper Egypt, add weak internet and old devices, and most digital products simply don’t work.”
Founded in Assiut in Upper Egypt, Learning Rockets launched the first prototype of its Bee Degree app in 2023, with the idea for the business having started at home.
“My daughter became fluent in English because we taught it to her at home, and I kept asking myself – why can’t other children in Upper Egypt have the same chance?” Soliman said. “I had spent more than 10 years in business and finance, and I decided to build that chance myself.”
Connecting the classroom and home
The startup brings books, an app and learning data together in one system.
“The app is Bee Degree. Every unit of our books, and of Egypt’s national English course from KG1 to Grade 6, becomes games, quizzes and reading activities that children play in class or at home,” Soliman said. “It works offline and on older, low-cost devices. Children log in with a code printed on a card, so they need no email or password.”
“We also own both sides. We write the books and build the games for the same units, so the classroom and the app never disagree, and we built everything to work offline on low-cost devices,” she said.
The data closes the loop
“Teachers, principals, school groups and parents each have a dashboard that shows how every child is doing, week by week, instead of waiting for exam results. We also train teachers to use the whole system in class,” Soliman said.
She leads the company alongside executive manager George Gamil, who runs day-to-day operations, with a team of 11 curriculum writers, illustrators, developers and trainers.
“Seventy percent of our full-time team are young women from Upper Egypt,” she said. “That matters to me, because good jobs for young women are still scarce here.”
Growing through schools
Schools have driven the startup’s growth. More than 100,000 students now learn with Learning Rockets in over 200 partner schools across all of Egypt’s governorates.
“The clearest sign of trust came this school year. A group of 63 schools joined at once, and we set up every branch, class and student account in September 2026,” said Soliman.
Bee Degree has more than 10,000 downloads on Google Play and a 4.8-star rating, though Soliman said this understates real usage. “Most children reach the app through their school, often on offline copies we install on school tablets and classroom smart panels,” she said.
Schools pay Learning Rockets per student, per school year, for a package including the app, readers, teacher dashboard and printed books. Schools brought in 92 per cent of revenue in 2025, with five per cent coming through a distribution partner and three per cent from parents subscribing directly in the app.
The model is working. In 2025, Learning Rockets made revenue of EGP6.3 million, with a 68 per cent gross margin and EGP1.6 million in net profit.
“So far we have grown mainly on our own revenue, plus non-dilutive prizes,” Soliman said. “We were profitable in 2025, and we are now opening an investment round to fund the next stage.”
Support for the next stage
The startup won the Orange Social Venture Prize in Egypt in 2024, and has taken part in a host of programs, including the Standard Chartered Foundation’s Women in Tech Accelerator, implemented with support from Village Capital.
“The program gave us time to step back from daily operations and work on the business itself: sharpening our pitch, tightening our numbers and planning our growth, alongside mentors and a group of women founders facing the same challenges. The grant went straight back into the business,” Soliman said.
“It also gave us credibility at the right moment. Within a year we were a She’s Next Egypt finalist, joined the UNDP and Flat6Labs accelerator, and were selected for Web Summit.”
Expanding beyond Egypt
Learning Rockets currently operates only in Egypt, but Soliman said there is still plenty of room for growth at home, with the country having about 25 million school students and around 11,000 private schools.
A new version of Bee Degree is heading to Google Play and the App Store, alongside a campaign to bring parents of its school students into the app.
“We are also building Rocket Talk, an offline speech engine that listens to children and scores their pronunciation. The engine is built; the next step is training it on children’s voices,” she said.
International expansion is now on the cards, and Soliman plans to use Web Summit, which will take place in Lisbon in November, to quicken the process.
“At Web Summit we are looking for publishers, distributors and school groups that want a ready book-plus-app system. Our first targets are North and East Africa and the Middle East, and over time we plan to add more languages,” she said.
Building from Assiut
Getting this far has not been easy, with cash flow a key challenge.
“Our revenue follows the school year. Schools pay at the start of the year, and some contracts pay in two installments, in December and April. Banks look for a steady monthly inflow, so even with signed school contracts and a profitable year, getting working capital has been hard,” Soliman said.
The realities of the classroom have also shaped the product.
“Many schools in Upper Egypt have weak internet and old devices, and many teachers had never used a learning app. So we built offline copies, versions for older Android tablets and classroom smart panels, and logged in with a printed card code. We train the teachers ourselves, and we have refurbished 343 devices so schools can use what they already have.”
Then there is the matter of building a startup far from the capital.
“Most of Egypt’s startup ecosystem sits in Cairo, a long way from Assiut,” Soliman said. “The hardest part of being a woman entrepreneur outside Cairo isn’t talent, or even the idea. It’s whether you’re willing to keep showing up anyway.”

articles.title: Les données de 587 000 Français piratées : une cyberattaque frappe à nouveau la Fédération française de tir
articles.text:
Il y a près d’une semaine, un pirate a revendiqué une nouvelle attaque à l’encontre de la Fédération française de tir (FFTir). Comme le rapporte FrenchBreaches, le cybercriminel dit détenir 586 854 fiches de licenciés et des informations sur 1 659 clubs de tir. Selon le hacker, le répertoire volé contient les informations personnelles d’environ 250 000 membres actifs et de 350 000 d’anciens adhérents.
Le butin, mis en vente sur la plateforme, comprendrait aussi 64 000 photos d’identité et près de 19 000 documents confidentiels et sensibles, dont des certificats médicaux. Le pirate affirme s’être glissé dans un compte, dépourvu de double authentification, pour arriver à ses fins. Pour prouver ses dires, le truand a diffusé un échantillon des données. Cet échantillon laisse penser qu’il dit vrai.
 🚨La Fédération Française de Tir piratée deux fois en un an, sans 2FA obligatoire
Alertée par FrenchBreaches, elle confirme une nouvelle cyberattaque touchant potentiellement 580 000 licenciés actuels et anciens, avec 64 000 photos, 19 000 documents et 55 dossiers complets dérobés. https://t.co/EMow3W8CG1
— Seb (@seblatombe) October 22, 2026
À lire aussi : Nouvelle cyberattaque en France – les données de propriétaires de chiens et chats ont encore été volées
La fédération confirme « une nouvelle attaque »
La FFTir a confirmé qu’une cyberattaque a visé ses plateformes EDEN (le portail où chaque licencié gère sa licence et dépose ses documents) et Cibles Couleurs (une école de tir pour les jeunes). Selon les investigations menées par la fédération, le pirate « s’est connecté à l’espace licencié EDEN avec des comptes de licenciés dont il avait obtenu ou deviné les identifiants ». Une fois à l’intérieur, il a copié « le dossier complet » des données à portée de main. Il s’agit bien d’« une nouvelle attaque, distincte de celle de 2025 ». Le pirate ne s’est pas contenté de recycler des informations déjà volées.
« Aucune information sur la possession d’armes n’a été touchée : la Fédération ne détient pas ces informations », précise-t-elle dans un communiqué.
Sans surprise, la Fédération française de tir a prévenu l’Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d’information (ANSSI) et la Commission nationale de l’informatique et des libertés (CNIL). Une plainte a été déposée dans la foulée.
Dans son communiqué, la fédération met surtout en garde ses licenciés contre d’éventuelles arnaques. Elle rappelle que la police, la gendarmerie ou la douane « ne vous appellera jamais » pour venir récupérer des armes à la suite de la fuite. La fédération promet de renforcer sa sécurité avec un système de double authentification obligatoire, des tests d’intrusion, des audits de code, et la réduction des données conservées sur les anciens licenciés.
À lire aussi : Cyberattaques en France : les dernières fuites de données et entreprises touchées
Une fédération déjà piratée en 2025
Ce n’est pas la première fois que la FFTir se retrouve dans le viseur d’un cybercriminel. En octobre 2025, les données de 250 000 adhérents et de 750 000 anciens adhérents avaient déjà été dérobées. Là encore, un compte interne compromis était à l’origine de la fuite. Suite à cette violation massive, plusieurs licenciés avaient été cambriolés à travers la France. Des malfaiteurs se sont servis à plusieurs reprises des adresses volées pour dérober des armes et des munitions. L’auteur présumé de la cyberattaque était un jeune homme de 18 ans. Il a été interpellé en janvier dernier, après des mois d’enquête.

articles.title: China-aligned hackers deploy AI agents in massive ConnectWise supply chain attack — agents attempted sign-ins at more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants, with some of the group's attacks reaching privileged access in under three hours
articles.text:
China-aligned hackers deploy AI agents in massive ConnectWise supply chain attack — agents attempted sign-ins at more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants, with some of the group's attacks reaching privileged access in under three hours
Automated password guessing failed, but stolen app credentials needed no user sign-in at all.
China-state-aligned actor Storm-0940 used ARTEX, an open-source agentic AI penetration testing framework, in its large-scale ConnectWise supply chain attack, Microsoft wrote in its Security blog. After unauthorized access to the multi-tenant application, the group attempted sign-ins at more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants, with stolen ConnectWise app credentials that authenticated as the apps with no interactive user sign-in. Some of the group’s attacks reached privileged access less than three hours after initial targeting.
Automated password guessing, or password spraying, also targeted 327 accounts across eight organizations with more than 151,000 failed logons and no successes. The use of ARTEX, “a system of LLM-driven agents that run an autonomous penetration test,” sped up scanning and reconnaissance, password spraying, and OAuth application abuse. The agents can work around the clock “with little needed human interaction,” at a pace that “leaves defenders with little time to detect and respond.” It’s uncertain how the ConnectWise credentials were stolen or how many tenants were actually compromised.
Storm-0940, active since 2021, is a “China-state aligned actor” with “no known industry aliases,” and its name follows the convention for a developing actor. Industries targeted this time include aerospace and defense, semiconductor, government, and think tanks, with 14 listed in total. The activity “did not result from a compromise of or a vulnerability” in Microsoft’s systems, products, or services.
At its peak on Oct. 11, the password spray engaged in 2,900 attempts, all failures, per minute, at more than 111,000 for that day, with 48 accounts logging more than 1,000 failures each. Almost 98% of this activity was locked out. However, with control of the identities of multiple ConnectWise cloud apps, the attacking AI agents signed in to customer tenants from the same IP range using those apps’ credentials, with more than 200 sign-ins in under four minutes using four application credentials. Operations taken within some tenants include Graph and directory operations, reconnaissance, app credential changes, plus changes to identities, groups, and privileged roles.
In one tenant on Oct. 15, Huntress, a security firm, saw an app add itself to the top administrator role, the behavior behind the Microsoft Defender alert “Application self-assigned Global Administrator role.” Actions included planting new secrets set to expire in 2028. It confirmed unauthorized sign-ins for 162 tenants by Oct. 16 and, a day later, almost 1,000 Entra tenants with sign-in activity from the attacking IP, with more than 300 succeeding. The attack’s sweep through tenants in sorted order, a few seconds apart, indicated “a script working from a target list.”
What differs from many traditional attacks is the use of the open-source pentest framework that, Microsoft says, can use any AI model. Threat actors in multiple regions are using the technology, and public reporting this month tied it to breaches at South Korean financial institutions. CrowdStrike said the suspect in those separate attacks was likely based in China and allegedly used ARTEX with Anthropic’s Claude Code. ARTEX’s developer, who goes by the handle “Autumn-27,” said on GitHub that the ARTEX project “will no longer be updated” and would become closed source, Reuters reported.
ConnectWise noted the unauthorized access and suspended Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) as well as SaaS Security and Cloud Management as a precaution. It has started a phased restoration with recovery expected to take several days and has no indicators to date that partner backup data was compromised. Microsoft notes that an affected app, or even a successful sign-in, doesn’t necessarily mean data was accessed or taken, and advises customers to keep affected app connections disabled until formal restoration instructions are issued, and to review activity from this month where logs allow.

articles.title: Avec ce launcher dopé à l'IA, Ubuntu Linux pourrait s'inspirer de macOS Spotlight
articles.text:
Un ingénieur de Canonical a publié un prototype de launcher qui simule des tâches confiées à une IA locale. Le résultat rappelle un peu Spotlight sur macOS, mais rien ne promet de le voir arriver dans Ubuntu.
Warty-prototype : ce que ferait l’IA depuis la barre de recherche d’Ubuntu
Ici, la fenêtre du launcher s’affiche en cliquant sur un petit logo Ubuntu dans la barre supérieure. L’outil permet d’effectuer plusieurs actions relativement classiques comme insérer un emoji, épingler des fichiers, afficher l’historique du presse-papiers ou retrouver une fenêtre ou un onglet de navigateur déjà ouvert. Chaque résultat propose des actions, comme le fait Spotlight sur macOS.
Mais en y ajoutant un LLM en local, le launcher devient tout de suite plus puissant. Pour l’heure il ne s’agit que d’un concept embarquant des démonstrations avec des cas d’usage simulés. Dans une première simulation, il est possible de retrouver une photo sur le disque, puis de demander au modèle d’en faire le fond d’écran et d’assortir la couleur d’accentuation du système. Dans la deuxième, on cherche une application pour ouvrir un fichier ePub. Le launcher affiche alors des résultats du Snap Store, avec un bouton d’installation. Enfin, dans la troisième, plusieurs éléments copiés dans le presse-papiers sont transformés en itinéraire de visite, qu’on peut ajouter à son agenda.
Chaque action déclenche une vraie notification de bureau, qui explique ce qui se serait passé au lieu de modifier la machine. Le snap de démo ne remplace d’ailleurs pas le launcher d’Ubuntu. Il place sa fenêtre en haut à droite via XWayland, une couche qui permet aux applications conçues pour l’ancien serveur graphique X11 de tourner sous Wayland, son successeur. Sur une session Wayland pure, il fonctionne mais ne peut pas positionner sa fenêtre. Sa licence n’est pas renseignée sur la fiche du Snap Store.
Reste à savoir si Canonical ira plus loin que ce simple concept. Nous rapportions fin avril que Jon Seager, vice-président de l’ingénierie, avait publié une feuille de route IA pour Ubuntu. Elle distingue l’IA "implicite", qui améliore des fonctions existantes comme la dictée vocale (Myna est disponible en aperçu technologique depuis ce mois-ci), et l'IA "explicite", plus proche des agents. Elle privilégie aussi l’inférence locale, c’est-à-dire des modèles qui tournent sur l’ordinateur de l’utilisateur. Ce launcher pourrait relever de la seconde catégorie, mais sa fiche le présente seulement comme un prototype pour discuter du design du prochain launcher.

articles.text:
Medion vend désormais ses PC portables gamer sous le nom Erazer. Ce Beast 16 X1 Ultimate associe un Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX à une GeForce RTX 5090, la puce graphique mobile la plus haut de gamme de Nvidia. Avec la crise de la RAM qui pousse le prix des composants à la hausse, une machine prête à l’emploi devient une option sérieuse pour jouer aux jeux AAA. Ça tombe bien, alors que GTA VI arriverait sur PC début 2027, PC Componentes propose en ce moment ce laptop suréquipé avec 1 500 euros de réduction.
L’Erazer Beast 16 X1 Ultimate, c’est quoi ?
- Un combo Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX et GeForce RTX 5090
- Un écran QHD+ Mini-LED de 16 pouces à 300 Hz
- Un châssis tout en métal et 2 To de stockage SSD
Le Beast 16 X1 Ultimate en RTX 5090 passe de 5 249 euros à 3 704 euros chez PC Componentes, avec la livraison offerte.

Un châssis en métal et un écran Mini-LED à 300 Hz
Medion a nettement soigné la fabrication de son Beast 16 X1 Ultimate. On a droit à un châssis entièrement en métal, avec un style froid et brut et des tranches nettes. Seule fantaisie, une bande LED personnalisable est située à l’avant de la machine. Avec 2,99 cm d’épaisseur et 2,67 kg sur la balance, il reste dans la norme des PC portables gamer de cette taille.
Côté écran, il embarque une dalle Mini-LED de 16 pouces en définition QHD+ (2560 x 1600 pixels). La dalle est certifiée HDR1000 et Trusted Reviews y a mesuré près de 775 nits en SDR, de quoi jouer sans souci dans une pièce lumineuse.
Le taux de rafraîchissement monte à 300 Hz, ce qui rend l’affichage très fluide sur les jeux compétitifs nerveux, à condition que la machine suive en images par seconde.
Une RTX 5090 pour les jeux AAA, avec quelques compromis
La GeForce RTX 5090 est le cœur de cette configuration. Dans sa version pour PC portable, elle embarque 24 Go de mémoire vidéo GDDR7 et peut tirer ici jusqu’à 175 watts (150 watts, plus 25 watts de Dynamic Boost). Nous avons testé la version RTX 5080 de cette machine. Notée 8/10 dans notre test, elle offrait les meilleures performances que nous ayons vues avec ce duo processeur et carte graphique. La RTX 5090 fait mieux, mais Notebookcheck juge que son surcoût face à la RTX 5080 se justifie surtout par sa mémoire vidéo (24 Go contre 16 Go).
Pour accompagner toute cette puissance, la machine utilise le processeur Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX couplé avec 32 Go de DDR5, extensibles à 64 Go, et 2 To de SSD. De quoi encaisser du montage vidéo ou de la 3D en plus des jeux les plus gourmands. En revanche, le logiciel maison d’Erazer nous a déçus.
Côté autonomie, la batterie de 99 Wh (juste sous la limite autorisée en avion) ne fait pas de miracle avec de tels composants, surtout en jeu. Quant à la connectique, on retrouve un port Ethernet, un port HDMI 2.1, un mini DisplayPort, un port Thunderbolt 4, un port USB-C 3.2 Gen 2, trois ports USB-A 3.2 Gen 2, un lecteur de cartes SD plein format et un combo jack. Autre point à prendre en compte avant de commander : la fiche de PC Componentes indique un clavier QWERTY espagnol.

articles.title: Microsoft: Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support in January
articles.text:
Microsoft says Windows Server 2016 will stop receiving security updates after it reaches the end of support in January 2027.
Windows Server 2016 was released in September 2016 at Microsoft's annual Ignite conference and reached general availability one month later, on October 12, 2016
It reached the end of mainstream support in January 2022, and extended support will end in roughly three months, on January 12.
"The January 2027 Windows security update will be the last update available for this version. After this date, devices running Windows Server 2016 will no longer receive monthly security updates containing protections from the latest security threats," Microsoft said in a message center update.
"This end of updates in 2027 applies to all editions of Windows Server 2016: Datacenter, Essentials, MultiPoint Premium and Standard."
On the same date, Microsoft will also stop support for all Windows Server 2016 Essentials features, including Remote Web Access and related Essentials-specific functionality.
Admins advised to switch to Windows Server 2025
Before Windows Server 2016 reaches the end of support, Microsoft advised IT administrators to upgrade to Windows Server 2025, which started rolling out to Windows Insiders in January 2024 and reached general availability in November 2024.
"To help keep your environment protected and supported, plan to upgrade to Windows Server 2025," the company added.
Windows Server 2025 is the latest Long-Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) release for Windows Server. According to Microsoft's lifecycle platform, it will reach the end of mainstream support in November 2029 and receive an additional five years of extended support until November 14, 2034.
Those who want to test Windows Server 2025 before deployment can get a free 180-day Windows Server 2025 trial via the Microsoft Evaluation Center.
More information about Windows servicing dates is available on the Windows Lifecycle FAQ page or via the Lifecycle Policy search tool.

articles.title: Sebi cautions investors against fraudulent stock-tip WhatsApp groups
articles.text:
Sebi cautions investors against fraudulent stock-tip WhatsApp groups
Sebi noted that members are often contacted from a new number and invited to join another group, with operators claiming that the previous group had been banned due to social media platform restrictions.
Markets regulator Sebi has cautioned investors against fraudulent WhatsApp stock-tip groups that use 'astroturfing'–fake endorsements and profit claims–to create a false impression of credibility and lure investors.
In a statement, Sebi said certain unregistered persons were offering stock recommendations to investors through invitation-only WhatsApp groups in the name of free investor education. The operators of these fraudulent groups often use overseas WhatsApp numbers posing as market experts.
“To make these calls look credible, certain members, acting in concert with the operators, post false claims of profit and praise the 'expert'. This practice, known as astroturfing, creates a false impression of genuine support and induces unsuspecting investors to act on the call,” Sebi said.
The regulator also highlighted a tactic used by such groups after enforcement agencies or regulatory bodies take action against them.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) noted that members are often contacted from a new number and invited to join another group, with operators claiming that the previous group had been banned due to social media platform restrictions.
One such message cited by Sebi reads, "Due to social media platform's risk control measures, our previous group has been banned. This new group will provide daily recommendations of quality stock information and trading guidance. Please join the group.”
Advising investors to exercise caution, Sebi said they should not join invitation-only WhatsApp groups operated by unknown persons or individuals claiming to be stock market experts, particularly those using overseas numbers.
Investors have also been advised not to be influenced by messages containing praise, profit claims or trade confirmations posted by other members, as such posts could be planted to create a misleading impression.
The regulator said messages claiming that a group had been suspended, closed or banned, and inviting members to join a new group should be treated as red flags.
It further advised investors against opening accounts on, or transferring money to, trading platforms or applications recommended by such groups.  Investors should also refrain from sharing their investment holdings or trading account details with the operators, the regulator advised.
“Deal only with Sebi-registered intermediaries and use only authentic trading apps,” the regulator said, adding that investors could verify the registration status of intermediaries through its official website.
Sebi said the statement was intended to caution investors against acting on stock tips and trading calls circulated through such closed fraudulent WhatsApp groups and urged them to remain vigilant while dealing in the securities market.

articles.title: Cuánto cuesta la criptomoneda ethereum este viernes
articles.text:
Ethereum es una plataforma digital que adopta la tecnología de cadena de bloques (blockchain) y expande su uso a una gran variedad de aplicaciones, mientras que ether es su criptomoneda nativa. En el mundo de las finanzas digitales es común que la criptomoneda sea llamada como la red, aunque en realidad no son lo mismo.
La plataforma ethereum, creada en el 2015 por el programador Vitalik Buterin, buscaba ser un instrumento para aplicaciones descentralizadas y colaborativas sobre las que se pueden hacer contratos inteligentes (dAPPs)
Al igual que el bitcoin, el valor de ether se disparó en un corto periodo de tiempo. En enero de 2016, ether cotizaba alrededor de un dólar y actualmente tiene un máximo histórico de 4.953,73 dólares.
La cotización de ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 2410.82 dólares, es decir, que la criptomoneda registró un cambio de 0.37 % en el último día.
Por otro lado, registró un cambio de 0.0 % con respecto a su valor hace una hora. En cuanto a su popularidad, se ubica en la posición #2.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Ethereum
La nueva era de Ether
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: Quatre prises secteur et une batterie de 2 048 Wh : l’EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max reconditionnée est à 1 044,05 €

La station électrique EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max de 2 048 Wh reconditionnée est à 1 044,05 € (-15 %)
La station électrique EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max associe une batterie LFP de 2 048 Wh à quatre prises secteur délivrant jusqu’à 2 400 W au total. Cette offre concerne du reconditionné.
Amazon propose la station électrique EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max reconditionnée à 1 044,05 €, contre un ancien prix affiché de 1 229 €. L’économie atteint 184,95 €, soit 15 %. Le prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours est également indiqué à 1 229 €. La station est vendue et expédiée par EcoFlow Germany GmbH.
Une batterie de 2 048 Wh et quatre prises secteur
La station électrique EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max embarque une batterie lithium-fer-phosphate de 2 048 Wh. Ses quatre prises secteur fournissent une puissance cumulée de 2 400 W. Elle peut ainsi alimenter plusieurs appareils simultanément, à condition que leur consommation totale reste dans cette limite. L’autonomie dépend des équipements branchés et des pertes de conversion.
La connectique comprend aussi un port USB-A, trois ports USB-C et une sortie 12 V. L’un des ports USB-C atteint 100 W, notamment pour recharger un ordinateur portable compatible. Le mode X-Boost prend en charge certains appareils jusqu’à 3 200 W ; cette valeur se distingue de la puissance nominale des prises secteur.
Une recharge rapide, mais un poids de 20,3 kg
EcoFlow annonce une recharge de 0 à 80 % en 51 minutes sur secteur, dans ses conditions de mesure. L’entrée solaire accepte jusqu’à 500 W avec des panneaux compatibles, à acheter séparément. L’écran permet de consulter l’état de charge, tandis que l’application donne accès au suivi et aux réglages.
Avec environ 20,3 kg, cette station se destine davantage aux déplacements ponctuels qu’au transport quotidien à pied. Elle présente un intérêt pour disposer d’une réserve d’énergie dans un véhicule de loisirs ou alimenter directement quelques appareils lors d’une coupure. L’offre concerne ici un exemplaire reconditionné : l’état et les conditions de garantie associés méritent donc d’être vérifiés avant commande.

articles.title: Think the iPhone Duo is expensive? Wait until you see how much Apple charges to repair it
articles.text:
Winners & losers: Buyers of expensive Apple products, which, let's face it, includes almost all of them, tend to face a dilemma: should they also hand over the not insubstantial recurring fee for AppleCare. If the person in question is buying an iPhone Duo, then the answer is yes, definitely, especially when its fragile inner screen cost $999 to repair, with other damage reaching as high as $1,499.
Apple's first-ever foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, launches today. With a price ranging from $1,999 to $3,199, it's Cupertino's most expensive phone to date, but buying one without AppleCare could prove even more costly.
Apple has listed some of the estimated repair costs for the iPhone Duo on its repair services page. Repair costs start at $49 for damage to the cover layer, reaching all the way up to $1,499 for "other damage." Here's the full list, along with the price for the same repair if you have AppleCare coverage:
- Cover layer damage: $49 
With AppleCare+: $19
- Back glass damage: $199 
With AppleCare+: $25
- Battery service: $229 
With AppleCare+: Free
- Rear camera damage: $229 
With AppleCare+: $99
- Outer display damage: $379 
With AppleCare+: $29
- Outer display and back glass damage: $509 
With AppleCare+: $58
- Inner display damage: $999 
With AppleCare+: $99
- Other damage: $1,499 
With AppleCare+: $149
It's important to remember that these are prices for repairs carried out by Apple, so they're going to be higher than those charged by most third-party repair shops. It's probably fair to assume that Apple wants users to subscribe to AppleCare, too.
While much improved since they first arrived, foldable phones remain notoriously fragile. This appears to be especially true of the iPhone Duo. Prolific leaker Ice Universe recently posted that the screen around the Duo's crease is soft to the touch and can develop deep wrinkles when pressed with a finger.
 – Ice Universe (@UniverseIce) October 20, 2026
It's speculated that this is related to Apple's rumored variable-thickness ultra-thin glass, which has a thinner central folding region and thicker surrounding areas.
AppleCare isn't cheap. With theft and loss, it's $20 per month or $200 per year ($399 upfront for two years' coverage). But that's still preferable to handing over half the iPhone Duo's price if, or when, it breaks.

articles.title: Las obras del metro de Málaga han destapado una de las mayores necrópolis romanas de España: ya van más de 1.000 cuerpos enterrados
articles.text:
Continúan las obras del metro de Málaga para expandir una nueva línea hacia el Hospital Civil y el futuro nuevo hospital y, ante su avance, nuevos hallazgos en la excavación del túnel que desembocó en el descubrimiento de toda una necrópolis romana. De hecho, una de las más grandes y mejor conservadas de España, según apuntan desde Diario SUR.
La excavación arqueológica lleva meses varada bajo la calle Hilera, en el centro de Málaga, y está reescribiendo lo que los historiadores creían saber sobre la antigua ciudad romana de Malaca.
Un remanente del Imperio Romano. Los arqueólogos han documentado hasta ahora 984 complejos funerarios que contienen a más de 1.000 individuos, según cifras de la Consejería de Fomento de la Junta de Andalucía. Tal y como apunta el medio, el yacimiento data de entre los siglos II y IV d. C. y se extiende a lo largo de unos 400 metros. Lo curioso es que, antes del descubrimiento no existía ningún otro registro previo, pues se creía que era una zona de terrenos ganados al mar en época islámica. Eso habría explicado por qué nunca antes habían aparecido restos anteriores.
Se multiplican. Tal y como comparten desde National Geographic, una excavación de salvamento en los meses previos al verano de 2025 sacó a la luz unas 15 tumbas. El medio informa que en su momento hallaron 274 enterramientos y más de 400 individuos. Ese recuento ya es más de tres veces superior, y todavía queda para rato.
Qué se encontró. Según cuenta Diario Sur, Las tumbas fueron excavadas en arcilla roja y posteriormente sepultadas bajo huertas islámicas y, más tarde, modernas. Presentan múltiples formas, desde marcos de tejas (tegulae) construidos alrededor del cuerpo, cubiertas de tejas a dos aguas, fosas simples, cistas revestidas de piedra, y hasta recién nacidos enterrados en el interior de ánforas.
Algunas tumbas se superponían hasta en tres niveles, indicaba Mario Muñoz-Atanet, consejero autonómico de Fomento, al diario. También señala que habían aparecido numerosas monedas procedentes de distintos lugares, lo que encaja con la historia de Malaca como puerto que atraía a gentes de todo el Mediterráneo.
Un equipo de arqueólogos y antropólogos está estudiando en la actualidad los restos, y su trabajo podría revelar cómo vivían estas personas, qué comían, qué enfermedades padecían y en qué trabajaban. La variedad de tipos de enterramiento también podría arrojar luz sobre las creencias y los vínculos familiares y sociales.
Y qué pasa con el metro. La excavación se encuentra en el primero de los tres tramos del ramal hacia el futuro hospital Virgen de la Esperanza, entre la estación de Guadalmedina y el final de la calle Hilera. La superficie afectada por la excavación se ha reducido de 406 a 250 metros lineales, lo que ha permitido reanudar los trabajos en la losa de cubierta del túnel. Aun así, Muñoz-Atanet contaba al medio que esta fase, cuya finalización estaba prevista inicialmente para noviembre, se prolongará ahora hasta principios de 2027. También promete que, aunque el proyecto haya sido modificado, la fecha general de apertura no se vería afectada, pues los tres tramos se están construyendo de forma escalonada.
Y ahora qué. Los restos irán a parar finalmente al Museo de Málaga. Las piezas más significativas se expondrán en un futuro espacio dedicado junto al túnel de la estación de Guadalmedina, que ya alberga restos del barrio islámico de Attabanim. El consejero indicaba además que una tumba de cada tipo irá destinada al proyectado museo arqueológico del metro.

articles.title: Orchestrating SageMaker AI endpoint auto scaling with AWS CDK | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Orchestrating SageMaker AI endpoint auto scaling with AWS CDK
Updating the Amazon Sagemaker AI real-time endpoint configuration (changing the instance type, instance count, or environment variables) causes deployments through AWS CloudFormation or the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to fail. SageMaker AI requires you to deregister the scalable target before updating the endpoint, but when you deregister it, CloudFormation can’t track the AWS Application Auto Scaling resources.
In this post, we show you how to use a reusable CDK construct with AWS CloudFormation custom resources to orchestrate deregister and register auto scaling automatically during endpoint updates. You can update your endpoint configuration and auto scaling parameters in a single deployment without manual intervention.
Why this problem occurs
When you deploy a SageMaker AI endpoint with native CloudFormation auto scaling resources, then change the endpoint configuration and redeploy, several failure modes emerge. The specific failure depends on what you change and how you work around the issue.
Changing the endpoint configuration with auto scaling registered
CloudFormation tries to update the endpoint while the scalable target is still registered. SageMaker AI rejects the update with the following error:
SageMaker AI blocks the endpoint update before CloudFormation reaches the auto scaling resources.
Manually deregistering auto scaling, then changing only the endpoint configuration
If you deregister the scalable target through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and redeploy with only an endpoint configuration change, the deployment succeeds. However, CloudFormation doesn’t register auto scaling even though it is in the CloudFormation template. Because the auto scaling parameters in the CloudFormation template haven’t changed, CloudFormation doesn’t register the scalable target or re-apply the scaling policy. The endpoint is now running without auto scaling, and there is no error to indicate anything went wrong.
Manually deregistering auto scaling, then changing auto scaling parameters
If you deregister the scalable target through the AWS CLI and redeploy with auto scaling parameter changes, CloudFormation tries to update the ScalableTarget resource that no longer exists:
This failure is notable because the rollback also fails (UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED), leaving the stack in a broken state that requires manual intervention in the CloudFormation console to recover.
Solution overview
You can use this CDK construct to replace the native AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget and AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalingPolicy CloudFormation resources with three custom resources. These custom resources deregister and register auto scaling around the endpoint update with explicit dependency ordering, enforced by node.add_dependency calls in CDK. The full sequence is:
- Deregister (custom resource): Removes the scalable target before the endpoint update begins. On first deploy, no scalable target exists yet, so the handler handles the error gracefully and continues.
- Endpoint update (CDK-managed): CDK updates the endpoint resource normally, swapping to the new endpoint configuration.
- Register Scalable Target (custom resource): Waits for the endpoint to reach InService status, then registers the scalable target.
- Attach Scaling Policy (custom resource): Waits for the scalable target to be queryable, then applies the target tracking policy.
Register Scalable Target and Attach Scaling Policy use the CDK provider’s asynchronous completion pattern. Each custom resource has an on_event handler that returns immediately and an is_complete handler. The provider’s waiter re-invokes the is_complete handler on an interval (every 30 seconds) until its readiness check passes. The provider’s total_timeout (1 hour for Register Scalable Target, 15 minutes for Attach Scaling Policy) bounds the wait, so it isn’t limited by the timeout of any single Lambda invocation.
A ConfigHash property on each custom resource forces CloudFormation to re-invoke the Lambda functions whenever a configuration value changes. The endpoint configuration and auto scaling parameters are defined together because a single ConfigHash drives the auto scaling orchestration.
While the construct defines three custom resources, the deployed stack contains more than three Lambda functions. Each custom resource is backed by a CDK cr.Provider, and the provider framework generates its own helper Lambda functions. A synchronous provider (Deregister) adds one framework function. An asynchronous provider (Register Scalable Target and Attach Scaling Policy) adds three (onEvent, isComplete, and onTimeout) plus an AWS Step Functions state machine that drives the waiter. As a result, the deployed stack contains three custom resources, two Step Functions state machines, and twelve Lambda functions. Five of the resources hold the construct’s own handler code (one for Deregister, and an on_event and is_complete pair for each asynchronous resource), with the remaining seven generated by the provider framework. You don’t write or maintain the framework-generated functions, but they are present in the stack and worth accounting for when you review the deployed resources.
Walkthrough
In this walkthrough, you deploy a SageMaker AI endpoint with auto scaling using the provided example stack, then verify that configuration updates work correctly.
The walkthrough includes the following steps:
- Clone the repository and install dependencies.
- Configure your endpoint and auto scaling settings.
- Deploy and verify.
- Test an update.
The source code is available in the linked GitHub repository.
Prerequisites
For this walkthrough, you need the following:
- An AWS account with permissions for Amazon SageMaker AI, AWS Lambda, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), Application Auto Scaling, and Amazon CloudWatch.
- AWS CDK v2 installed.
- Python 3.12 or later.
- uv for Python dependency management.
- A SageMaker AI model artifact in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) and a container image in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR), or a SageMaker AI built-in algorithm container.
Clone the repository and install dependencies
- Clone the repository:
- Install dependencies:
Configure your endpoint and auto scaling settings
The endpoint and auto scaling settings are defined together in config/config.yaml because a single config_hash drives the auto scaling orchestration. A change to either section triggers the full sequence.
Edit config/config.yaml with your values:
The endpoint parameters map to the SageMaker AI CreateModel and CreateEndpointConfig APIs. The auto scaling parameters map to the Application Auto Scaling RegisterScalableTarget and PutScalingPolicy APIs.
Deploy and verify
- Bootstrap your AWS environment if you haven’t already:
- Deploy the stack:
CloudFormation creates the SageMaker AI model, endpoint configuration, and endpoint, then runs the three custom resources in sequence to register auto scaling.
- Verify that the deployment registered the scalable target:
- Verify that the deployment applied the scaling policy:
Test an update
Change a value in config/config.yaml, for example, update the instance type from ml.m5.large to ml.m5.xlarge, and redeploy:
After the deployment completes, verify that auto scaling is still registered and has the updated values:
Integrating with an existing stack
Use the example stack if you’re starting fresh or want a reference implementation. Use the construct directly if you already have a CDK stack with SageMaker AI resources.
To integrate with an existing stack, copy the sagemaker_autoscaling/constructs/ directory into your project and add the construct alongside your endpoint resources:
How the construct works
This section walks through the key implementation details of SagemakerAutoscalingConstruct.
Deregister
The Deregister custom resource calls deregister_scalable_target before the endpoint update. It handles ObjectNotFoundException for first deployments where no scalable target exists:
The dependency is established in CDK:
Register Scalable Target
Even though CloudFormation treats the endpoint resource as complete once the update is accepted, the scalable target can only be registered after the endpoint reaches InService. Rather than block a single Lambda invocation on that wait, Register Scalable Target uses the provider’s asynchronous completion pattern. The on_event handler returns immediately, and the provider’s waiter re-invokes the is_complete handler on query_interval until the endpoint is InService. The provider’s total_timeout (1 hour) bounds the wait, not the timeout of any single Lambda invocation:
On stack deletion, the on_event handler deregisters the scalable target to clean up.
Attach Scaling Policy
There is a brief window after RegisterScalableTarget returns where the target isn’t yet queryable. Attach Scaling Policy uses the same asynchronous completion pattern: the on_event handler returns immediately, and the is_complete handler reports completion only once the scalable target is queryable, at which point it applies the policy. The provider’s total_timeout (15 minutes) bounds the wait:
On stack deletion, the on_event handler deletes the scaling policy to clean up.
Cleaning up
To avoid incurring future charges, delete the resources:
This removes the SageMaker AI endpoint, endpoint configuration, model, Lambda functions, IAM roles, Amazon CloudWatch alarms created by the target tracking scaling policy, and deregisters the scalable target.
Conclusion
In this post, we showed you how to use a reusable CDK construct to deregister and register auto scaling automatically to orchestrate SageMaker AI endpoint updates. The construct uses three CloudFormation custom resources with explicit dependency ordering and a ConfigHash property to keep auto scaling intact across deployments.
To get started, clone the sample-sagemaker-endpoint-autoscaling repository and follow the setup instructions. The repository includes an example stack you can deploy directly, or you can integrate the construct into your existing CDK stack.
For more information about Application Auto Scaling for SageMaker AI, see Automatically scale Amazon SageMaker AI models. For more information about CloudFormation custom resources, see Custom resources in the AWS CloudFormation User Guide.

articles.title: Nicht das Lager bremst dein Wachstum, sondern die Daten
articles.text:
Nicht das Lager bremst dein Wachstum, sondern die Daten: Was gutes Fulfillment heute ausmacht
Viele traditionelle Third-Party-Logistics-Anbieter (3PL) arbeiten jedoch nach wie vor mit starren Standardsystemen, die durch intransparente Dashboards und teure Zusatzlizenzen für jede neue Funktion limitiert werden. Das Ergebnis für Händler sind fehlende Echtzeit-Einblicke in den Warenfluss und steigende Kosten bei jedem Wachstumsschritt.
Vertikalisierung: Logistik trifft auf Software-Entwicklung
Einige Akteure am Markt brechen mit diesem traditionellen Ansatz, indem sie Software und Logistik-Infrastruktur vollständig vertikalisieren. Der Fulfillment-Dienstleister Monta agiert hier primär als Tech-Unternehmen, das seine Systeme seit 1999 komplett in-house entwickelt. Durch standardisierte Schnittstellen zu allen gängigen ERP- und Shopsystemen sowie eine offene API für individuelle Architekturen ermöglicht Monta eine Live-Schaltung in der Regel innerhalb von ein bis drei Wochen.
Real-Time-Daten statt Kontrollverlust
Herkömmliche Warehouse-Management-Systeme (WMS) bilden Daten häufig erst zeitversetzt ab. Ein proaktiver Steuerungsansatz setzt früher an: Das System von Monta bildet Daten nicht nur passiv ab, sondern ermöglicht das direkte Eingreifen in laufende Prozesse. Erkennt die Software beispielsweise eine fehlerhafte Lieferadresse, wird der betroffene Auftrag automatisch gestoppt. Die Korrektur kann direkt im Dashboard vorgenommen werden, sodass das Paket fehlerfrei das Lager verlässt – was unvorhergesehene Retourenkosten minimiert und die Marge schützt.
Die technologische Differenzierung vom klassischen Markt erfolgt dabei über drei zentrale Säulen:
Monta ist der Fulfillment-Partner für E-Commerce-Unternehmen, die ihr Backend technologisch skalieren wollen. Komplett in-house entwickelte IT, kombiniert mit DHL-Infrastruktur – von der offenen API bis zur paneuropäischen Cross-Border-Logistik.
- Das Labor-Prinzip: IT-Entwickler arbeiten räumlich direkt verzahnt mit den Logistikteams im Lager. Jede neue Funktion und jede API-Kopplung wird sofort im operativen Betrieb getestet. Bottlenecks oder Systembrüche werden dadurch ohne Verzögerung identifiziert und direkt im Code angepasst.
- All-in-One-Software statt Lizenz-Flickenteppich: Viele Wettbewerber arbeiten mit modularen Systemen, die ständige Upgrades erfordern. Monta bietet stattdessen eine extrem umfangreiche Standardsoftware, für die Händler keine teuren Zusatzlizenzen benötigen. Smarte Features wie ein Einkaufsberater-Tool, ein integriertes Retourenmodul und detaillierte Bestandsreportings sind bereits vollumfänglich enthalten.
- Großes Carrier-Netzwerk bei voller Wahlfreiheit: Ohne feste Bindung an einen einzelnen Versanddienstleister bietet Monta Zugriff auf ein breites Netzwerk an Carriern. Dabei bevormundet das System den Händler nicht durch automatische Zuweisungen: Der Shop-Betreiber entscheidet selbst, mit wem er versendet – oder er bietet gleich mehrere Carrier an und überlässt seinen Endkunden im Checkout die freie Wahl des bevorzugten Paketdienstes.
Fulfillment entwickelt sich damit vom reinen operativen Kostenfaktor zum strategischen Wachstumsmotor, der E-Commerce-Unternehmen im Backend den Rücken freihält.
Bereit für ein Fulfillment-Setup, das mit deinen Tech-Ambitionen mitwächst? Lerne jetzt die datengetriebene Logistik-Infrastruktur von Monta kennen.
