articles.title: Dein Ausweis zieht aufs Handy – das musst du über d-you wissen
articles.text:
Was die digitale Brieftasche d-you kann – und wo ihre Grenzen liegen
Die Bundesregierung plant die “digitale Brieftasche” für alle. Für die “d-you” genannte Wallet hat sie Mitte Oktober die gesetzlichen Grundlagen geschaffen, der Bundesrat muss noch zustimmen.
Starten soll die App bereits zum 2.Januar 2027. Damit setzt Deutschland Vorgaben aus der EU um. D-you ist also die deutsche Version der European Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI-Wallet), entwickelt wird sie von SPRIND und Common Codes im Auftrag des vom Bundesministerium für Digitales und Staatsmodernisierung (BMDS).
Die Nutzung ist freiwillig. Wer kein Smartphone hat oder das digitale Angebot einfach nicht nutzen will, kann also weiter auf die physischen Ausweisdokumente zurückgreifen. Nutzen lässt sich d-you ab 16 Jahren und nur auf einem Smartphone mit NFC und Android oder iOS, alternative Betriebssysteme werden nicht unterstützt. Außerdem braucht die Ausweisfunktion eine Internetverbindung. Geht das Handy verloren, muss die Wallet ohne Backup komplett neu eingerichtet werden.
Behörden, die für ihre Online-Dienste einen elektronischen Ausweis verlangen, müssen d-you als Identifizierungsdienst akzeptieren. Ab Ende 2027 sind dann auch Banken, Energieversorger, Telekommunikationsanbieter und sehr große Online-Plattformen verpflichtet, die Wallet zu nutzen. Normale Online-Shops entscheiden dagegen selbst, ob sie d-you integrieren.
Was kann die digitale Brieftasche d-you?
Die Wallet bringt im Prinzip die Möglichkeit, sich online und digital auszuweisen, etwa bei Behördengängen, im Online-Shopping oder bei Vertragsabschlüssen. Das gilt nicht nur in Deutschland: Weil alle EU-Staaten so eine Wallet bereitstellen müssen und die Wallets in allen Mitgliedstaaten gelten, wird man d-you auch im EU-Ausland nutzen können.
Insbesondere das Identifizierungsverfahren soll dann einfacher ablaufen, als etwa beim bisher häufig genutzten Videoident-Verfahren. Während man dabei einem Service-Mitarbeiter den Ausweis vorzeigen muss, werden in der Wallet wenige Klicks genügen, um die eigene Identität zu bestätigen.
D-you baut dabei auf dem Personalausweis mit Online-Funktion auf. Nach einer einmaligen Anmeldung wird eine digitale Kopie der Identitätsdaten auf dem Handy gespeichert, danach muss der Ausweis nicht mehr wie bislang bei jedem einzelnen Vorgang ans Telefon gehalten werden.
Perspektivisch sollst du in d-you alle möglichen behördlichen Dokumente, aber auch andere Unterlagen und Tickets speichern und die App für Behördengänge, die Eröffnung von Bankkonten oder den Abschluss von Verträgen nutzen können. Außerdem soll sie etwa beim Einkaufen eine einfachen Altersnachweis ermöglichen.
Allerdings könnte der Starttermin noch wackeln, das Digitalministerium will „unter Berücksichtigung eventueller Restrisiken” über den Start entscheiden. Sicher ist: Die App wird zum geplanten Start im Januar noch nicht alle Funktionen haben.
„Zum Launch wird es keinen großen ‚Big Bang‘ geben“, sagt Johannes Hollunder, der sich beim Digitalverband Bitkom mit digitalen Identifizierungsverfahren beschäftigt. Es gehe darum, Schritt für Schritt Anwendungen in die Wallet zu integrieren, die wirklich funktionieren. “Das volle Potenzial von d-you wird sich entfalten, wenn mehr Partner ihre Anwendungsfälle in die Wallet integrieren.“
Ein großer Vorteil der Wallet soll darin liegen, dass sich nicht nur staatliche, sondern auch private Dokumente in die Wallet laden lassen, neben Ausweis und Führerschein etwa das Deutschlandticket, die Zugangskarte fürs Fitnessstudio oder ein Konzertticket. Doch diese Funktionen werden erst nach und nach integriert werden. Mit einer großen Einführungskampagne wird das Digitalministerium also wahrscheinlich warten, bis die Wallet auch wirklich viel zu bieten hat.
Anfangs wird auf jeden Fall der digitale Ausweis und dann etwas später auch der Führerschein, Sozialpass oder Rentenausweis verfügbar sein. Außerdem arbeiten rund 40 Partnern wie etwa die Deutsche Post, die Sparkassen, Vodafone und Rossmann an Funktionen für d-you. Ob alle Partner direkt zum Start Funktionen bereitstellen werden, ist noch nicht klar. Die Sparkassen kündigen zum Start immerhin zehn Anwendungen an, etwa zur Identifizierung bei der Eröffnung von Konten und Depots, später sollen auch Freigaben im Online-Banking und von Zahlungen hinzukommen.
Auch in der Verwaltung wird d-you erst schrittweise ankommen. Bundesbehörden müssen ihre Nachweise bis Ende 2027 elektronisch in der Wallet ausstellen können. „Wer ein Dokument von einer Bundesbehörde braucht, kann es also spätestens zwölf Monate nach dem Start elektronisch erhalten“, erklärt Hollunder. Das gilt jedoch nur auf Bundesebene. In den Ländern und Kommunen hängt die Frage, ob und wann diese eigene Nachweise in die Wallet ausstellen, dagegen auch vom Stand der Technik und dem Budget ab.
„Anfangs könnte es also sein, dass eine Kommune Dokumente bereitstellt, während eine andere das noch nicht tut“, sagt Hollunder. Aktuell wird eine zentrale Plattform entwickelt, um diese Dokumente auszustellen. Wie schnell die Kommunen sich daran anbinden, hängt dann von ihren Kapazitäten ab.
Das brauchst du, um d-you zu nutzen
Die Anmeldung bei d-you wird über den Ausweis mit Online-Funktion laufen. Nutzer geben dazu bei der ersten Anmeldung die sechsstellige PIN des Online-Ausweises ein, die App liest die Karte per NFC aus und vergibt dann eine eigene sechsstellige PIN für die Wallet. Für die Übernahme der Identitätsdaten werden dazu Softwarekomponenten der Ausweis-App genutzt.
Das bedeutet allerdings auch: Falls du keinen funktionierenden Online-Ausweis hast oder deine PIN für die Online-Funktion vergessen hast, bekommst du auch keinen Zugang zu d-you.
Für die d-you-Nutzung könnte das zu einer echten Hürde werden. Denn obwohl der Online-Ausweis seit 2010 in jedem neuen Personalausweis angelegt ist, wird er nur von einem Bruchteil der Bevölkerung genutzt. Laut einer Bitkom-Umfrage im April haben nur 18 Prozent der Befragten die Online-Funktion aktiviert und kennen ihre PIN. Weitere 21 Prozent haben die Funktion zwar freigeschaltet, kennen ihre PIN aber nicht mehr.
Wer die PIN vergessen oder die Online-Funktion im Ausweis bislang nicht genutzt hat, kann kostenlos einen Rücksetzbrief anfordern und erhält dann per Post entsprechende Zugangsdaten.
Datenschutz und Sicherheit bei d-you
Die digitale Brieftasche speichert Nachweise nicht nur als bloße Abbilder. Die Dokumente sind kryptografisch signiert und kommen direkt von der ausstellenden Behörde. Anbieter von anderen Funktionen können ihre Echtheit also jederzeit überprüfen. Die Wallet verspricht ein datensparsames Design, soll also möglichst wenig Daten der Nutzer weitergeben.
Beim Altersnachweis etwa im Supermarkt soll die Wallet künftig etwa nur bestätigen, dass jemand volljährig ist, ohne Name und Adresse preiszugeben. Ob das aber zum Start schon funktioniert wird und auch an der Kasse ohne Internetverbindung, ist offen.
Grundsätzlich müssen Partner der Wallet offenlegen, wofür sie welche Daten brauchen. und bekommen nur Zugriff auf diese Informationen. Eine Vorabprüfung, ob Unternehmen nur die Daten abfragen, die sie wirklich brauchen, sieht das Gesetz aber nicht vor. Wer kein biometrisches Passfoto in der Wallet haben will, kann das ablehnen. Außerdem entscheidet der Nutzer vor jeder Übermittlung selbst, ob er Daten teilen will.
Kritiker sehen darin allerdings auch ein Problem. So warnte die Sachverständige Bianca Kastl vom Innovationsverbund Öffentliche Gesundheit in einer Anhörung der Bundestags vor einem „Cookie-Banner 2.0“-Szenario. Wer eine Anfrage vorschnell bestätigt, gibt dann vielleicht mehr preis als nötig. Verbraucherschützer kritisieren außerdem, dass die App zum Start noch keine pseudonyme Nutzung ermöglicht, sie soll erst später kommen.
Fragezeichen gibt es auch noch bei der Sicherheitsarchitektur. Die Daten sollen langfristig im Secure Element des Handys gespeichert werden. Zunächst sollen die Schlüssel aber nicht im Handy, sondern in Hochsicherheitsmodulen auf Servern gespeichert werden. Das Projekt begründet das damit, dass die EU für den digitalen Ausweis das höchste Sicherheitsniveau verlangt und nur wenige Smartphones den dafür nötigen Spezialchip besitzen.
Das Bundesamt für Sicherheits und Informationstechnik (BSI) und der Bundesdatenschutzbeauftragte warnten außerdem davor, dass die staatlich signierte Daten auch nach einem Leck als echt nachweisbar bleiben und damit ein lohnendes Ziel für Datenhändler und Betrüger sind.
Das Digitalministerium hat im Oktober ein Bug-Bounty-Programm gestartet und belohnt das Aufspüren von Sicherheitslücken.
Auch die Deutsche Kreditwirtschaft als Interessenvertretung der Banken forderte zuletzt noch Nachbesserungen, etwa zu Haftungsregeln. Bei Fehlern soll aus ihrer Sicht der Wallet-Anbieter haften und nicht die Bank. Eine Pflicht, Zahlungen über d-you anzubieten, lehnt sie ab.

articles.title: How Bayer Crop Science built an agentic decision engine on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with AWS Unified Operations | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
How Bayer Crop Science built an agentic decision engine on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with AWS Unified Operations
Plant breeding decisions depend on data that spans genomics, field trials, imagery, environmental conditions, and model outputs. Bayer Crop Science runs hundreds of machine learning (ML) model configurations against this data across crops, regions, and teams, and each run needs to be repeatable and governed. To meet that requirement, Bayer built the Connected Decision Engine (CDE), a system for deploying, orchestrating, monitoring, and reusing ML workflows. CDE gives breeders, analysts, researchers, data scientists, and data engineers a consistent way to run analytics while preserving execution history and operational controls.
As adoption grew, the bottleneck moved from running workflows to understanding them. Explaining a result meant piecing together context from APIs, documentation, metadata stores, dashboards, and logs. A user who wanted to know why a workflow failed, what a model did, or where a result came from still had to know which system to inspect. To close that gap, Bayer built the Agentic Decision Engine (ADE), a multi-agent, natural language interface over CDE. A supervisor agent routes each question to a specialist agent, the specialist retrieves context from the relevant system, and the user receives an answer without navigating the operational stack. In its first phase, ADE resolves about 80 percent of user questions without an engineer in the loop.
ADE runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, an AWS service to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale with any framework or model. AgentCore let the team focus on agent behavior instead of building and operating its own agent hosting, session isolation, and tool access layer. Three AgentCore capabilities drove that choice: a managed runtime that isolates each user session, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)-scoped tool access through AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, that keeps authentication and authorization outside agent code, and a framework-agnostic design that let the team bring its own LangGraph orchestration and choice of models.
To prepare for launch and to operate ADE afterward, Bayer engaged AWS Unified Operations. The engagement provided a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM) and a generative AI Domain Specialist Engineer (DSE), who worked as an extension of the ADE team from design through production. The TAM, as Bayer’s strategic advisor, brought an established understanding of Bayer’s operating model and business priorities. The DSE brought generative AI domain expertise on AWS. In three technical standups each week, the team reviewed and made design decisions. The DSE built working knowledge of the ADE workload and how the Bayer team operates, so technical guidance reflected both AWS service behavior and Bayer’s context. This post follows that journey: the ADE architecture, five design decisions made during the build, the work to prepare the platform for production, and how it is operated after launch.
Architecture overview
ADE is organized into four layers: the user experience, agent orchestration, specialist agents, and the tools and data sources those agents call (Figure 1). Users reach ADE through a React web front end, and requests pass through an identity proxy for Microsoft Entra ID before they reach the agents. GitHub Actions builds the agent container images, pushes them to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR), and deploys them to AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime hosts the agents, and because the runtime is framework-agnostic, the team runs its own LangGraph-based orchestration on it directly. The team chose LangGraph for its explicit graph-based control flow and checkpointing for multi-step workflows. LangGraph orchestrates the workflow, with a Supervisor Agent as the entry point that classifies each request, selects a specialist, and combines results when a question spans domains. The data plane is separated by responsibility. Amazon DynamoDB stores LangGraph checkpoint state. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL stores session records, user feedback, and analytics. Amazon ElastiCache caches agent responses with a time to live (TTL). Domain content in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) is embedded with Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 and indexed in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless for Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). Amazon CloudWatch captures runtime and application telemetry. AgentCore Gateway exposes backend APIs to agents as Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools and keeps authentication and authorization outside agent code.
ADE runs 22 specialist agents in production, each scoped to one domain with its own tools and data sources. For example, the Domain Expert Agent answers conceptual questions through RAG. The Operational Agent retrieves live workflow status and results from CDE. The Troubleshooting Agent analyzes operational telemetry. The Visualization Agent generates charts or returns existing dashboards. A customer-specific Models as Skill pattern converts model code and documentation into skill definitions stored in a central registry, so agents answer model-specific questions from the model’s implementation instead of generic model knowledge.
When a breeder asks, “Why did my phenotyping workflow fail yesterday?”, the supervisor classifies the intent and routes the request to the Troubleshooting Agent. That agent reads the workflow’s telemetry in CloudWatch and its status from the CDE API through AgentCore Gateway, identifies the failure point, and returns a diagnosis through the supervisor (Figure 2). The breeder doesn’t search logs directly. With the Troubleshooting Agent, a diagnosis that once took over an hour of manual log-hunting and waiting for engineer support now takes under 10 minutes.
Five design decisions on the path to production
The Unified Operations TAM and DSE took part in the following decisions as members of the working team, not as an escalation point after the fact. That let Bayer test each design against AWS service behavior before committing to it, while keeping ownership of the architecture and the final call.
1. Externalize orchestration state without treating the runtime as stateless
AgentCore runtime provides isolated sessions that preserve execution context across invocations within a session’s lifecycle. That context isn’t a durable store for a multi-step workflow. ADE writes LangGraph checkpoints to DynamoDB so the graph can resume after scale-out events, restarts, or session boundaries without depending on one execution environment remaining available.
Principle: Use the runtime session for active execution, and persist the state required to resume or reconstruct the workflow in a durable service.
2. Separate enterprise identity, gateway access, and downstream authorization
Bayer standardizes on Microsoft Entra ID for user identity, while ADE’s services authorize each other with AWS-native mechanisms. Rather than force one token across every trust boundary, the team gave each boundary its own mechanism.
Entra ID remains the source of user identity. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) authorizes service-to-service calls. AgentCore Gateway outbound authorization handles access to downstream CDE services. A request interceptor AWS Lambda function performs custom validation and passes the authorization attributes that downstream tools require. The team worked through the token contract at each hop with the DSE.
Principle: Identity failures in agent systems cluster at the transitions between user identity, agent identity, and tool identity. Define the issuer, audience, claims, scopes, and credential lifetime at every hop instead of reusing a token that is valid for one boundary at the next.
3. Treat model selection as an interface contract
During the build, the team evaluated a newer model version with reasoning mode enabled. For that version, the combination of tool use and structured output that ADE depends on was not compatible with how its agents were implemented. The DSE confirmed the constraint, and the team retained the current model for the release.
Principle: For tool-using agents, model choice is constrained by the full interface: tool calling, structured output, streaming behavior, reasoning features, latency, quota availability, and model-specific request semantics. A newer model is not automatically a drop-in replacement.
4. Control the tool surface before it controls the prompt
CDE manages more than 500 model configurations. A dedicated MCP server per API would have added deployment, authentication, and version management overhead. ADE instead registers OpenAPI specifications with AgentCore Gateway, which exposes the REST operations as MCP tools. Adding or changing an API becomes a schema and gateway configuration change instead of a new server deployment.
Tool schemas and descriptions also consume input tokens and compete with the user’s request and retrieved context. ADE scopes tools by specialist agent instead of giving every agent the full catalog. For larger catalogs, AgentCore Gateway supports semantic tool search, so an agent can find relevant tools without loading the entire catalog on every turn.
Principle: Scope the tool catalog per agent. Every tool definition adds tokens and widens the model’s decision space.
5. Promote complex capabilities from tools to agents
Visualization started as a tool invoked by other agents. As it grew, it needed its own data retrieval, chart selection logic, retries, error handling, and a decision about whether to generate a chart or return an existing dashboard. The team moved it into a specialist Visualization Agent. The agent generates on-demand charts with matplotlib and Plotly in AgentCore Code Interpreter, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that provides a sandboxed code execution environment, and exchanges data with it through Amazon S3. When a prebuilt dashboard is the better answer, the agent returns the existing Amazon Quick or Power BI asset.
Principle: A tool performs a bounded operation. When a capability starts to own state, retries, planning, policy, or presentation decisions, model it as an agent.
Preparing ADE for production
As the build moved toward launch, the focus shifted from design to operability: detecting agent failures, attributing inference cost, and hardening the deployment.
Observability: Measure task failures, not only exceptions
A supervisor architecture turns one user request into a chain of model calls, tool calls, and agent handoffs. The final answer can be wrong even when every HTTP request succeeded. ADE encountered this directly: application exception handlers caught agent errors and returned responses that monitoring counted as successful. After reproducing the issue with the DSE, the team added custom CloudWatch metrics inside failure paths and alarms on agent-specific conditions: tool call errors, throttling, model timeouts, and structured output validation failures. Traces and invocation logs follow each request across the supervisor and specialists.
Principle: Distinguish transport success from task success. Agent observability should show whether the task completed, which agent or tool changed the outcome, and whether the response used the expected source.
Cost attribution: Combine billing attribution with request-level telemetry
One ADE request can invoke several models and tools, so account-level Amazon Bedrock spend doesn’t explain unit economics. The team designed the attribution approach with the DSE using three mechanisms that answer different questions. Amazon Bedrock application inference profiles attribute billed model usage to an application or workload. Request metadata and model invocation logging associate token usage with a specific agent, feature, or request. IAM principal attribution adds an identity dimension. Together they let the team estimate cost per interaction, identify expensive agents, and determine whether prompts, retrieved context, or tool definitions drive token use. In practice, the Visualization and Operational agents, which rely on MCP tools and multiple tool calls, consumed the most tokens.
The same telemetry surfaced a workload during launch preparation with a large repeated input prefix and no prompt cache activity. For supported models, placing stable instructions and tool definitions in a cacheable prompt prefix reduces repeated input processing, which lowers latency and token cost. For ADE, caching the stable prompt prefix cut input-token cost by 20–30 percent.
Security and launch readiness
IAM roles are scoped to each agent’s responsibility. The Troubleshooting Agent can read the operational data it needs for diagnosis but can’t modify workflows. The Domain Expert Agent can query its retrieval index but cannot call unrelated CDE APIs. In production today, ADE’s agent responses are governed by least privilege, read-only tool access scoped to each agent, structured output validation on agent responses, and answers grounded in retrieved CDE data and telemetry rather than open-ended generation. Bayer also plans to evaluate Amazon Bedrock Guardrails as an additional layer on these controls, complementing the custom safety checks already used in CDE multi-turn workflows.
Before launch, Unified Operations ran a Critical Workload Review and a Well-Architected review with the Generative AI Lens alongside the ADE team. Because the DSE already knew the workload, both reviews targeted ADE’s specific failure modes, capacity risks, and deployment gaps rather than generic best practices. Findings included gaps in failure visibility across the supervisor and specialist agents, mutable container image tags, limited image traceability, and missing vulnerability scanning. The team responded with stronger alarms, immutable versioned images, scan on push in Amazon ECR, and lifecycle policies for unused images.
The DSE also reviewed scaling and quota requirements with the team. Load testing validated both the application and its service quotas and exposed a networking failure mode that returned empty responses, which the team fixed before the production event. By launch, the team had tracked 35 blockers to resolution with Unified Operations.
Launch, operations, and next steps
Bayer launched ADE to a gated group rather than opening it to the whole organization at once. Since launch, more than 100 users across Bayer Crop Science have used ADE, including breeders, analysts, researchers, data scientists, and engineers. Alongside its 22 specialist agents, ADE exposes about 20 API tools and can host third-party agents as it expands. Exposing those APIs through AgentCore Gateway rather than a dedicated server per API cut per-API integration overhead by more than 99 percent. In its first phase, ADE has resolved about 80 percent of user questions without an engineer in the loop.
CDE remains the governed execution layer for analytics. ADE adds a natural language layer over it, so users can ask about workflow status, results, model behavior, and failures without learning the location or interface of each underlying system.
The engagement then shifted from launch readiness to ongoing operations. The DSE continues to meet with the team, so issue triage and operational reviews start from existing knowledge of ADE instead of a new ramp-up. ADE’s critical CloudWatch alarms, including the agent-specific alarms described earlier, are onboarded to AWS Incident Detection and Response. When one fires, AWS Incident Management Engineers engage within 5 minutes and start from the workload’s context rather than from scratch. On the security side, AWS Security Incident Response engineers support the team during potential or active security events, so ADE has AWS monitoring and response coverage for both operational and security issues.
With agent-to-agent communication already in place, Bayer is focusing next on hybrid cloud agent interoperability. The team is exploring how agents running in different environments can discover and communicate with each other without manual configuration.
Conclusion
Bayer didn’t replace its analytics platform with ADE. It made CDE easier to query and operate. Most of the production work sat outside the prompts: durable state, identity boundaries, tool scoping, task-level observability, cost attribution, and launch readiness. Bayer owned the architecture and each of those decisions. Working with a designated DSE and TAM through AWS Unified Operations, the team tested those decisions against AWS service behavior during design and carried the same context into production.
To learn more, explore Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Bedrock cost attribution, AWS Well-Architected Generative AI guidance, and AWS Unified Operations.
The authors would like to thank Sijie Shi, Jorge Gomes, Naveen Reddy, Iago Fonseca, Mateus Silva, and Sushimitha Jarugula for their contributions to the design, development, and launch of ADE.

articles.title: Tonbo Imaging shares make stellar market debut; jump 66%
articles.text:
Tonbo Imaging shares make stellar market debut; jump 66%
The stock made its debut at Rs 1,162 apiece, registering a premium of 66% from the issue price on the BSE.
Shares of Tonbo Imaging India, a defence electronics maker, on Friday listed with a premium of 66% against the issue price of Rs 700.
The stock made its debut at Rs 1,162 apiece, registering a premium of 66% from the issue price on the BSE.
Later, it traded at Rs 1,059.05, down 8.86% from its listing price, still maintaining a premium of 51.28% over its issue price.
On the NSE, the shares opened at Rs 1,160 apiece, a jump of 65.71% over the issue price. It was later trading at Rs 1,058.30, down by 3.64% from the opening level, but 51.18% higher than the issue price.
Following the listing, the company's market capitalisation stood at Rs 6,191.91 crore on the BSE and Rs 6,060.45 crore on the NSE.
The broader equity market was trading in the red, with the BSE Sensex falling 409.06 points, or 0.56%, to 72,840.33, while the NSE Nifty dropped 173.65 points, or 0.77%, to 22,514.

articles.title: Quest Diagnostics confirms data breach exposed patient records
articles.text:
American clinical laboratory company Quest Diagnostics disclosed that patient records have been exposed after a threat actor gained unauthorized access to its Quanum LSM system.
The company learned about the breach on October 21 and deployed its incident response protocol "to contain the activity, assess and investigate the nature and scope of the incident and implement appropriate remedial measures."
“On October 21, 2026, Quest Diagnostics Incorporated learned of unauthorized access to its Quanum LSM system, which certain clients use to place test orders, receive and look up results,” the company says in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
Quest Diagnostics is a major clinical laboratory company in the United States, providing diagnostic testing and services for a wide range of medical conditions.
It operates 7,700 points across North America, employs 65,000 people, and generates more than $11 billion in annual revenue. The company says it serves one in three U.S. adults each year.
Quanum LSM (Lab Services Manager) is the firm’s online platform that physicians, hospital personnel, and medical office staff use to manage laboratory services, access test results, track status, and order supplies.
The company disclosed the breach to the SEC and provided more information in an alert on its website.
The company is still investigating the incident but believes some patient records were exposed. The types of data affected have yet to be determined.
External experts are aiding the ongoing investigation, and Quest Diagnostics has also informed the applicable law enforcement authorities.
The company says that the incident has not disrupted its customer-facing operations and users of direct-customer LIS interfaces or EMRs were not impacted.
As a cautionary measure, Quest Diagnostics has temporarily paused access to other systems, including Essential Insights and LabHQ.
Currently, the Quanum LSM system has been stopped, and customers are recommended to use paper requisitions or Quanum eLabs to place orders and receive results.
As of writing, BleepingComputer could not find a threat group claiming the attack on Quest Diagnostics.
In 2019, data of about 11.9 million Quest Diagnostics patients was compromised in a breach at billing collection provider American Medical Collection Agency (AMCA).
Following the disclosure, at least 19 class-action lawsuits were filed against Quest Diagnostics. The cases were consolidated into multidistrict litigation, which remains ongoing and unresolved.

articles.title: Windows 11 : Microsoft travaille sur une alternative à Recall moins intrusive
articles.text:
Microsoft envisagerait très sérieusement de remplacer sa très controversée fonction Recall par une nouvelle solution plus respectueuse de la vie privée. La firme de Redmond travaille actuellement sur une application expérimentale animée par l’intelligence artificielle et conçue pour fonctionner comme un « second cerveau ».
Project Pantheon, c’est le nom de code de ce projet, propose une application nommée Context Vault qui est capable de stocker et d’exploiter des données personnelles sans pour autant procéder à un enregistrement complet des actions réalisées à l’écran comme le fait Recall.
Un remplaçant de Recall moins intrusif
Nos confrères de Windows Latest, qui rapportent l’information, ont pu accéder à cette application et la tester durant plusieurs semaines. Ils ont en effet pu récupérer l’application directement sur le Microsoft Store via un lien non répertorié. L’application, qui ne requiert aucune invitation préalable, n’est pour l’heure qu’une simple version de test non finalisée utilisée a priori uniquement en interne chez Microsoft.
Cette application Context Vault est a priori bien différente de Recall dans son mode de fonctionnement. Contrairement à Recall, qui capture l’écran automatiquement à intervalles réguliers, Context Vault n’enregistre que les contenus sélectionnés explicitement par l’utilisateur. Il est ainsi possible d’enregistrer des pages web, des fichiers, des captures d’écran, des fragments de textes copiés ou encore des flux audio et vidéo sous la forme de « souvenirs ».
L’interface de l’application s’articule autour d’une page Collections au sein de laquelle les éléments enregistrés sont classés. Les éléments non classés sont quant à eux automatiquement dirigés dans une section « souvenirs non catégorisés ». L’outil est par ailleurs capable de regrouper automatiquement certains contenus. L’application embarque en outre un onglet de discussion qui permet d’échanger avec l’IA de Microsoft sur les éléments sauvegardés. Vous pouvez, par exemple, demander à l’IA de résumer, lister ou rédiger un brouillon à partir des éléments disponibles dans une collection.
Une fonction intégrée dans Windows 11 accessible sur toutes les configurations
Context Vault n’aurait a priori pas besoin d’être exécuté directement dans Windows 11 pour ajouter un souvenir. Microsoft aurait visiblement choisi de l’intégrer directement dans le système d’exploitation, en la rendant par exemple accessible depuis plusieurs endroits dans son OS. L’appli est accessible depuis le menu de partage de l’Explorateur de fichiers, via une extension de navigateur, au sein du presse-papiers, dans l’Outil Capture d’écran et même dans la fonction Click to Do.
Autre différence avec Recall, Context Vault intègre a priori un serveur MCP (Model Context Protocol), un standard ouvert qui permet à des modèles et des outils tiers d’accéder aux données sauvegardées.
Surtout, contrairement à Recall, Context Vault serait utilisable sur tous les PC, quelle que soit leur configuration. L’appli, qui n’exige en effet pas de PC équipé d’un processeur neuronal, s’appuie sur des modèles d’IA hébergés sur le Cloud pour fonctionner. Par ailleurs, Microsoft aurait intégré une option Token usage permettant de surveiller la consommation des jetons IA nécessaire pour interroger les serveurs en ligne sur lesquels les IA tournent.
En adoptant cette nouvelle approche pour la sauvegarde des données assistée par l’IA, Microsoft garantirait une maîtrise totale de la confidentialité et du respect de la vie privée. Le mode de fonctionnement de Context Vault reste néanmoins plus contraignant puisqu’il oblige l’utilisateur à penser à sauvegarder manuellement chaque élément.

articles.title: Lua hoje: confira a fase da Lua deste sábado 24/10/2026
articles.text:
Hoje, 24 de outubro de 2026, a Lua está na fase crescente e 97% visível. Confira o calendário completo de fases da Lua deste mês, de acordo com o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet).
Confira as próximas fases
As fases da Lua no mês de outubro de 2026 começam no dia 3 com a chegada da Lua Minguante, às 10h26 (horário de Brasília). Depois disso, no dia 10, foi a vez da Lua Nova, que chegou às 12h50. A Lua Crescente surgiu às 13h13 do dia 18. Por fim, vem a Lua Cheia, dia 26, à 1h13.
Leia mais:
- Entenda o que é a Lua, como e quando ela se formou
- Saiba como tirar a melhor foto possível com uma câmera de celular
- 7 dicas para fotografar a lua com seu celular
Calendário fases da Lua em outubro de 2026
- Lua Minguante: dia 3, às 10h26
- Lua Nova: dia 10, às 12h50
- Lua Crescente: dia 18, às 13h13
- Lua Cheia: dia 26, à 1h13
O que é o ciclo lunar?
Uma lunação ou ciclo lunar, como é chamado o intervalo de tempo entre luas novas, é sutilmente variável, com média de duração de 29,5 dias. Durante esse período, ela passa pelas quatro fases principais (nova, crescente, cheia e minguante), e cada uma se prolonga por aproximadamente sete dias.
Também existem as “interfases”: quarto crescente e crescente gibosa (entre as fases nova e cheia) e minguante gibosa e quarto minguante (entre a cheia e a minguante).
Entenda cada fase da Lua
Lua Nova
Na Lua Nova, o satélite se posiciona entre a Terra e o Sol. Isso faz com que o lado iluminado da Lua fique voltado para o Sol, enquanto o lado escuro fica voltado para nós. Por esse motivo, a Lua não é visível no céu noturno. Essa fase marca o início de um novo ciclo lunar e está relacionada ao recomeço e a novas possibilidades.
Lua Crescente
Depois da Lua Nova, surge a fase Crescente. Aos poucos, uma pequena faixa iluminada começa a aparecer no céu, aumentando noite após noite. No início, vemos apenas um fino arco de luz, mas com o passar dos dias a parte iluminada cresce até que metade da Lua esteja visível, momento chamado de Quarto Crescente. Essa fase simboliza crescimento, desenvolvimento e a construção de novos caminhos.
Lua Cheia
Na Lua Cheia, a Terra se encontra entre o Sol e a Lua. Isso permite que o lado lunar voltado para nós receba luz por completo, tornando-se totalmente visível e brilhante no céu. É o período de maior intensidade luminosa, quando a Lua nasce no horizonte exatamente no momento em que o Sol se põe. A Lua Cheia é associada à plenitude, ao auge de processos e à energia em seu ponto máximo.
Lua Minguante
Após a Lua Cheia, a luz da Lua começa a diminuir gradualmente. A cada noite, vemos menos da sua superfície iluminada. Quando apenas metade dela está visível, ocorre o Quarto Minguante, fase oposta ao Quarto Crescente. A Lua continua a perder luminosidade até chegar novamente à Lua Nova, reiniciando o ciclo. A fase Minguante simboliza reflexão, encerramento e preparação para novos começos.
Qual a fase da Lua hoje?
Hoje a Lua está na fase Crescente.
Flávia Correia é jornalista do Olhar Digital, cobrindo Ciência e Espaço.

articles.title: 300 glaciares han desaparecido del oeste americano desde mediados del siglo XX. Los supervivientes tienen algunas cosas en común
articles.text:
Nuestros paisajes están cambiando radicalmente con el paso de los años, y las altas cumbres estadounidenses no han sido una excepción, puesto que el oeste de Estados Unidos siempre ha sido un referente por la cantidad de glaciares con los que cuenta. Y hablamos en pasado porque un artículo publicado en la revista PNAS apunta a que ya se ha perdido aproximadamente una cuarta parte de los glaciares.
Un inventario. Para entender exactamente lo que está ocurriendo aquí, los científicos se han apoyado en comparar los mapas topográficos históricos del Servicio Geológico de los Estados Unidos, elaborados con fotografías aéreas tomadas entre 1955 y 1990, con el inventario más reciente finalizado en 2015. Aunque obviamente no todo lo que se ve es glaciar, puesto que para los expertos ganarse esta distinción requiere que estemos ante una masa perenne de nieve e hielo en constante movimiento.
Y a simple vista, las cifras netas podrían llegar a confusión, puesto que los mapas antiguos registraban 1453 glaciares, mientras que el inventario más reciente contabiliza 1.331 glaciares. Aquí la confusión es que, aunque a priori parece que se han perdido 122 glaciares, la realidad es que han desaparecido 300 glaciares.
¿Por qué? La respuesta a esta discrepancia está en la fragmentación, puesto que a medida que los grandes glaciares menguan por el calor, muchos se parten en pedazos más pequeños, inflando artificialmente el número de glaciares individuales a pesar de que la cantidad total de hielo se desploma.
El resultado final es que el área total de hielo ha caído un 35 % y el volumen un 33 %. Y algunas regiones se han llevado la peor parte, como la región de Beartooth-Absaroka, donde se ha visto una pérdida de hasta el 77%. .
Hay supervivientes. Con este panorama, la pregunta que surge es: ¿cómo es posible que el resto de los glaciares sigan existiendo en un clima regional cada vez más hostil? La respuesta, según los expertos, radica paradójicamente en el propio retroceso. Y es que, a medida que los glaciares del oeste de Estados Unidos se encogen, se van replegando hacia los rincones más protegidos de las montañas.
De esta manera, los supervivientes se mantienen con vida gracias a la topografía local, puesto que al volverse tan pequeños consiguen refugiarse en cuencas, barrancos profundos o bajo la sombra de grandes picos que los aíslan de la insolación directa.
Una muerte anunciada. A pesar de esta heroica resistencia basada en el terreno, el futuro a medio plazo es poco alentador. Aquí tenemos un estudio previo del mismo equipo que analizó al detalle la península Olímpica, en el estado de Washington. Allí, de la vasta superficie helada documentada en 1900, ya ha desaparecido la mitad, y desde 1980 se esfumaron 35 glaciares y 16 neveros perennes, una pérdida atribuida directamente al calentamiento del aire.
Con estos datos encima de la mesa, lo que se espera es que finalmente buena parte de los glaciares terminen por desaparecer hacia el año 2070. Pero no es un problema solo de Estados Unidos, sino que este retroceso es un reflejo de la situación global. Aquí los datos publicados a principios de 2025 son claros al apuntar que todo el planeta perdió 273 gigatoneladas de hielo al año entre el año 2000 y 2023, por lo que el futuro no augura de momento nada positivo.

Flutterwave employees can now borrow against their shares
Startup shares can make employees and early investors look rich on paper. But that wealth is usually locked up until the company is sold or someone else agrees to buy the shares. Flutterwave, Africa’s largest payment company, is trying to give some shareholders another way to get cash out of their paper wealth without selling the shares.
What happened? Flutterwave has partnered with Techdollar, a US-based private-credit startup, to let its employees borrow money using their Flutterwave shares as collateral. Shareholders keep their shares while borrowing against their value.
Explain like I’m new here: Startup employees are sometimes paid partly in equity, particularly at young companies. That means someone who joined early can end up owning shares that are worth a lot on paper as the company raises money and its valuation climbs. Normally, if a shareholder wants to turn those shares into cash, they need a buyer. This can happen through a secondary share sale, where another investor buys shares directly from an existing shareholder and the shareholder gets cash.
When Nigerian fintech Moniepoint raised $110 million in 2024, at least two senior employees sold portions of their shares, receiving $850,000 and $20,000 respectively. Flutterwave’s arrangement with Techdollar is different.
How does it work? The shareholder pledges eligible Flutterwave shares as collateral and receives a loan from Techdollar. They own the shares, but the lender has a claim on them if the borrower fails to repay.
Why it matters? Flutterwave’s $3.25 billion valuation gives the arrangement some serious numbers to play with. For employees, the access to cash now without giving up exposure to how big Flutterwave grows is an appeal.

CANAL+ gets bigger, but MultiChoice is still shrinking
CANAL+ is now a much bigger company because it owns MultiChoice. The awkward part is that the business it bought is still getting smaller where it matters most.
What happened? MultiChoice revenue fell 3% on a like-for-like basis in the nine months to September, dragged down by lower subscription income in South Africa. Reported revenue still rose 0.4% to €1.81 billion ($2.03 billion), but that increase came largely from favourable currency movements rather than stronger underlying performance.
There was some improvement. The decline slowed to 2% in the third quarter from 3.4% in the first half. CANAL+ cautioned that easier comparisons with last year’s sports calendar also helped, so it is too early to credit the turnaround.
Explain like I’m new here: CANAL+ completed its takeover of MultiChoice because it wanted scale across Africa, but the two businesses entered the deal from very different positions. CANAL+’s operations outside MultiChoice are still growing strongly in French-speaking Africa. MultiChoice, by contrast, is dealing with falling subscription revenue in its biggest market.
CANAL+ has started responding. In September, DStv launched several unbundled packages in South Africa, after shutting down Showmax in April. The group is also spending on sports rights, including UEFA club competitions and the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.
Between the lines: CANAL+’s strongest African business and its newest acquisition are moving in opposite directions. Revenue from its Africa and Asia operations, excluding MultiChoice, grew 10.2% like-for-like, helped by French-speaking Africa. MultiChoice declined.
CANAL+ is targeting €250 million ($281 million) in synergies, but cutting duplicated costs can only do so much. If fewer South Africans pay for DStv, the group eventually has to fix demand, not just expenses.
What to watch: Subscriber numbers. CANAL+ did not disclose them this quarter. Sports rights, unbundled packages, and more content sound promising, but the proof of a turnaround will be whether DStv can keep more customers and stabilise subscription revenue.

South Africa asks ICASA to rewrite telecom infrastructure sharing rules
Building a telecom network is expensive, and building one next to an existing network can be redundant. South Africa wants to make it easier for operators to share the on-ground infrastructure.
What happened? Solly Malatsi, South Africa’s communications minister, has asked the Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA), the country’s communications regulator, to rewrite its rules for how telecom companies share infrastructure.
Explain like I’m new here: South Africa already has rules for infrastructure sharing, but the framework was introduced in 2010 and has not kept pace with the industry. The government says the framework needs to be updated to reflect how the telecoms market works.
Why it matters: In July, operators told ICASA that getting wayleaves (permission to use public land or existing infrastructure for network deployment) can take 6–12 months in some municipalities. This can slow fibre expansion, mobile network upgrades, and make network expansion more complicated.
What’s changing? ICASA is being asked to speed up leasing negotiations and create a clearer process for resolving disputes between operators and other parties, including landowners. It will also be expected to build a central map of the country’s telecoms infrastructure. Operators would provide information on fibre routes, ducts, poles, and base stations, giving the regulator a better picture of what infrastructure already exists and where new networks are being planned.
What happens next? The regulator has to work through the policy direction and develop the new rules. It is expected to publish final rapid-deployment regulations during the 2026/2027 financial year. If the new framework works as intended, operators should have a clear route to accessing existing infrastructure and fewer deployment delays.

articles.title: Un hydropulseur sans fil et une brosse à dents électrique : le coffret Philips Sonicare est à 129,99 €
articles.text:
Le coffret dentaire Philips Sonicare Power Flosser 3000 et DiamondClean 9000 est à 129,99 € (-41 %)
Le coffret Philips Sonicare HX3886/41 associe un hydropulseur sans fil à deux modes de nettoyage et une brosse à dents électrique DiamondClean 9000.
Amazon propose le coffret Philips Sonicare HX3886/41 à 129,99 €, contre un ancien prix affiché de 218,87 €. L’économie atteint 88,88 €, soit environ 41 %. Par rapport au prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, de 208,34 €, la baisse représente 78,35 €, soit environ 38 %. L’ensemble est vendu et expédié par Amazon, avec la livraison gratuite proposée.
Un hydropulseur sans fil avec deux modes de nettoyage
L’hydropulseur Philips Sonicare Power Flosser 3000 utilise un jet d’eau pour nettoyer les espaces interdentaires en complément du brossage. Son réservoir est intégré au manche : l’appareil se manipule ainsi sans tuyau le reliant à une station posée sur le lavabo.
Deux modes sont disponibles. Clean délivre un débit continu, tandis que Deep Clean produit des pulsations, avec une intensité réglable. La technologie Pulse Wave marque le passage d’un espace interdentaire à l’autre. Deux canules sont fournies : une F1 standard et une F3 Quad Stream, dont l’embout répartit le jet en forme de croix.
Une brosse à dents DiamondClean 9000 et ses accessoires
Le coffret comprend également une brosse à dents électrique Philips Sonicare DiamondClean 9000 blanche, accompagnée d’une tête de brossage. Elle repose sur une technologie sonique et dispose d’un capteur de pression pour signaler un appui trop important. Les deux appareils remplissent donc des fonctions distinctes au sein de la routine quotidienne.
Un verre de recharge et un étui de voyage avec fonction de charge complètent l’ensemble. Le premier permet de recharger la brosse à dents dans la salle de bains, tandis que le second facilite son transport et sa recharge en déplacement. Ce coffret s’adresse surtout aux personnes qui souhaitent s’équiper simultanément d’une brosse électrique et d’un hydropulseur.

articles.title: Microsoft is emailing Xbox owners to trade in their consoles, less than a year after raising prices
articles.text:
WTF?! Do you have an Xbox Series X or Series S sitting in the corner gathering dust, unused for months or even years, a constant reminder that maybe a PS5 would have been a better choice (assuming you've already got a PC)? If you're undecided about trading it in, consider this: even Microsoft thinks you should do it, and is sending out emails to owners encouraging them to get rid of the consoles.
X user Nintendeal posted an email they received from Microsoft. "Haven't played on your console in a while? If you've moved on to XBOX on PC or another way to play XBOX games, it may be time to trade in your console to Best Buy for up to $375 back," the message read.
 – Nintendeal (@Nintendeal) October 19, 2026
Microsoft isn't sending these messages out because it wants people to have some extra money over the holidays. The Redmond giant increased the price of Xbox consoles by $100 and $150 for the 512GB and 1TB models, respectively, less than a year after the previous increase.
In its announcement, Microsoft also revealed it was working with retail partners on new programs to provide previously played consoles at lower prices. As it needs older consoles to refurbish and sell, the company suggested at the time that owners who don't play their Xboxes anymore trade them in for cash or store credit.
Unfortunately for those who, for some reason, are looking to buy an Xbox console, a refurbished Series X is currently around $650, which is $150 more than what the console cost at launch six years ago.
If you are trading in an Xbox, you might want to consider its condition first. That $375 the email promises is only for those consoles in excellent condition with the power cable, controller, and stand all included. Anything in "poor" condition will likely bring around $150. Really, you're probably better off buying and selling them theough eBay, though buyers don't get the security of refurbishment and guarantees.
The average price a consumer has paid for a new Xbox console in 2026 YTD ending August is $529, 26% higher than a year ago, while the average PlayStation console has sold for $597, 20% higher than last year. Both prices are at all-time US highs. Price sensitivity is becoming a real problem.
– Mat Piscatella (@matpiscatella.bsky.social) 9 October 2026 at 15:02
According to figures shared by Circana's Mat Piscatella earlier this month, consumers bought 559,000 consoles in August, down 15% from a year earlier and the lowest August total since 2013. With even refurbished consoles more expensive than new models were at launch, don't expect this trend to change anytime soon.

articles.title: iPhone Duo : des écrans pliables endommagés à la charnière dès les premières livraisons — Frandroid
articles.text:
Apple commercialise enfin un iPhone pliable, sept ans après les premiers modèles de la concurrence. Nous l’avons reçu et vous pouvez lire nos premières impressions à son sujet. Si nous avons apprécié sa charnière, il semblerait que certains modèles soient défaillants car des premiers signalements de dommages sont apparus presque immédiatement. Ils proviennent de Reddit et des forums de MacRumors.
Le cas le plus détaillé vient d’Australie. Selon son propriétaire, l’appareil avait servi environ six heures et avait été ouvert moins de vingt fois. En le montrant à un ami, il dit avoir senti un mouvement sous la dalle, près de la charnière. Un craquement audible a suivi, puis l’écran interne s’est fendu sur une partie de la pliure.
    Pour aller plus loin
iPhone Duo : Apple a transformé la protection de son écran pliable en pièce d’usure
            
Toujours d’après lui, aucune trace de choc n’était visible, ni sur l’écran ni sur la charnière extérieure. Les photos publiées montrent une bande de pixels lumineux qui traverse l’affichage.
Par ailleurs, des clichés d’appareils de démonstration en Chine, où l’iPhone Duo est sorti quelques heures avant les États-Unis, présentent des symptômes comparables.
On y voit des lignes verticales le long de la pliure, croisées par des bandes lumineuses horizontales et des pixels défectueux.
Ces images ont été publiées sur Reddit et Xiaohongshu. Les conditions de ces incidents restent toutefois floues. Il est donc impossible de savoir si le défaut est commun ou si certains appareils ont subi des manipulations brutales dans des magasins très fréquentés.
Une conception complexe et des essais contrastés
Selon Apple, l’écran interne est composé de dix couches ultrafines. Elles associent verre, polymères, titane et adhésifs spécifiques, afin de mieux répartir les contraintes mécaniques. Cette conception pourrait avoir des ratés sur certains exemplaires.
Plus tôt dans la semaine, une vidéo Weibo relayée par le leaker Ice Universe montrait la dalle s’enfoncer sous le doigt près de l’axe de pliage. Des plis temporaires apparaissaient alors.
En laboratoire, les résultats sont plus rassurants. La journaliste Joanna Stern a fait réaliser 32 640 pliages. À l’issue du test, la charnière demande un peu plus de force, mais aucune différence notable n’apparaît à l’usage. Le YouTubeur Tim Pan a quant à lui testé 11 500 pliages. La pliure centrale devient plus visible, mais la charnière reste fluide.
Ces résultats contrastent avec les pannes décrites ci-dessus. En effet, elles surviennent après quelques heures d’usage seulement, et non après des milliers de cycles. Cela fait plutôt penser à un défaut de fabrication sur certains exemplaires qu’à de l’usure, mais rien ne le confirme pour l’instant.
Du côté de la concurrence, le premier Galaxy Fold avait connu un lancement difficile en 2019. Des écrans d’exemplaires prêtés à la presse avaient cédé en quelques jours, et Samsung avait repoussé sa sortie d’avril à septembre. Apple a donc pu observer les erreurs de Samsung pendant plusieurs années. Les écrans pliables de la marque coréenne, désormais plus anciens, ont accumulé davantage de recul à l’usage.
Réaction d’Apple et prudence de rigueur
Dans le cas le mieux documenté, celui de l’acheteur australien, Apple a remplacé l’appareil. Par téléphone, on lui a d’abord proposé un échange qui exigeait, selon lui, une empreinte bancaire équivalente au prix complet du téléphone, sans délai garanti. Il s’est donc rendu directement en Apple Store, où son iPhone Duo a été remplacé immédiatement.
Rappelons que quelques unités défectueuses ne suffisent pas à prouver un défaut généralisé. Certains testeurs ont ouvert l’appareil de très nombreuses fois sans problème. On est encore loin d’un « crackgate », terme que MacRumors a déjà mis en titre de son article, suivi d’un point d’interrogation.
Pour les acheteurs, une casse de la charnière liée à un usage normal relève de la garantie, d’un an chez Apple, à laquelle s’ajoute en France la garantie légale de conformité de deux ans. Les clients qui viennent de recevoir leur iPhone Duo disposent aussi de deux semaines pour le retourner. Si Apple attribue en revanche les dégâts à une mauvaise manipulation, le remplacement de l’écran pliable est facturé 1 149 euros sans AppleCare+, pour un smartphone vendu à partir de 2 339 euros en France.
Cependant, il n’est pas impossible qu’un problème de production puisse expliquer certains cas. Cependant, aucune explication officielle n’a été donnée à ce stade.
Il faudra donc attendre davantage de retours pour savoir si ces incidents restent isolés.

articles.title: Cloudflare Brings On-Demand CPU and Memory Profiling to Production Workers
articles.text:
Cloudflare has introduced on-demand CPU and memory profiling for Workers and Durable Objects, allowing developers to investigate performance bottlenecks in production using interactive flamegraphs. Announced on October 9, 2026, the feature generates interactive flamegraphs through the Workers Observability dashboard or the cf CLI, helping teams identify expensive functions and memory allocations without relying solely on logs and aggregate metrics.
Developers can capture CPU or heap-allocation profiles for a deployed Worker version and inspect the results as a flamegraph, where wider sections indicate functions responsible for a larger share of CPU time or sampled memory allocations. Profiles can also be downloaded for offline analysis.
The key distinction is that profiling targets an already-running isolate rather than starting a fresh one. This allows developers to examine code executing under real production traffic. Durable Objects receive additional support for profiling a specific named instance, which is useful when investigating problems tied to stateful workloads. However, the target must receive sufficient traffic during the capture window, and TypeScript developers should enable source maps to make function names easier to interpret.
The implementation must account for Workers running across Cloudflare’s distributed edge infrastructure, where a script may have multiple isolates across data centres and physical machines. A profiling request therefore needs to identify the requested Worker version and locate a suitable active isolate. Durable Objects add another challenge because they are stateful and can move between locations; Cloudflare routes profiling requests to the machine hosting the specific object.
The runtime does not hold an isolate lock for the entire capture. For CPU profiling, it starts a V8 profiler that samples at one-millisecond intervals, releases the lock while requests continue executing, and reacquires it to stop profiling and collect results. This lets the platform observe live execution without suspending normal request processing during the capture.
CPU and memory profiles also answer different questions. CPU profiling samples call stacks to reveal where execution time is being spent, helping identify expensive functions, redundant computation, and potential optimisation opportunities. Memory profiling, by contrast, highlights allocations associated with functions, helping developers find code that creates excessive objects or contributes to memory pressure.
This is important when diagnosing performance issues: a function may consume significant CPU without allocating much memory, while another may generate substantial allocations without dominating execution time. Examining the appropriate profile helps narrow the investigation to the relevant resource bottleneck.
Cloudflare used the feature internally to identify unnecessary computation and memory consumption. Profiling an R2 binding Worker revealed a recursive JSON replacer that repeatedly traversed nested data, making the function perform redundant work. Correcting the implementation made it a claimed 2.7 times faster. Another profile exposed an unnecessary duplicate metrics call that accounted for approximately 1% of CPU time.
Memory profiling identified a separate problem in which partially disabled Prometheus instrumentation was reportedly still consuming substantial memory. Cloudflare claims that removing the remaining code reduced the Worker's 99.9th-percentile memory usage from 133 MB to 118 MB, bringing it below the 128 MB limit.
Cloudflare’s offering complements established tools rather than replacing them. Chrome DevTools supports local CPU profiling, making it useful during development, but reproducing production traffic and data can be difficult. pprof, widely used in Go and other supported profiling workflows, provides powerful offline profile analysis; Cloudflare also allows downloaded profiles to be examined with pprof. Its main differentiator is the ability to initiate profiling against live Workers and Durable Objects through the platform's existing operational interface.
The feature also complements logs, metrics and distributed tracing. These tools help identify when a service is slow or consuming excessive resources, while a profile can help pinpoint the functions responsible. Together, they provide a more complete picture of application behaviour.
On-demand capture is not continuous monitoring. Short profiling windows can miss intermittent problems, while heap profiles record allocations during capture rather than providing a complete picture of retained memory. Cloudflare says it is working towards continuous profiling, which could make it easier to investigate rare performance problems without having to anticipate when they occur.
For teams running production workloads on Cloudflare Workers, the release adds a practical debugging capability: moving from detecting resource pressure to identifying the code responsible, without first having to reproduce the issue locally.

articles.title: Mila, federal researchers develop AI tool to better predict wildfire behaviour | BetaKit
articles.text:
Mila and the Canadian government have co-created a new AI tool to predict the spread and intensity of wildfires across the country.
The news: Researchers from Montréal AI research institute Mila and the forestry division of Natural Resources Canada have partnered on an AI model that maps wildfire hazards—tracking how likely an area is to burn, how quickly it will spread, and how intense it might become.
It’s meant to replace NRCan’s existing simulator tool, BurnP3+, which relies on physical fire behaviour data and must be updated constantly depending on factors like climate and vegetation.
From the source: The AI model runs between 800 and 3,400 times faster than BurnP3+, Mila said, depending on what kind of computing hardware is used.
“The emulator generates imperfect approximations, but with high fidelity and at speeds incomparably faster” than the existing tool, NRCan researcher and forest systems modelling specialist Tom Swystun said in a release. “The initial reaction to the model’s speed was simply ‘wow.’”
The context: Canada’s 2026 wildfire season is set to be the country’s fourth-worst on record. According to Public Safety Canada’s October update, more than 5,400 wildfires burned approximately 4.5 million hectares of land this year, forcing 33,750 people to evacuate their homes, including more than 8,800 people from First Nations communities.
NRCan’s fire division expects wildfires to only worsen in frequency and intensity, which is why it reached out to Mila’s applied research team to see if an AI model could improve the speed of its hazard mapping. The new AI tool was trained on data from physical fire simulation maps recorded this year, meaning it’s built on a similar database as the BurnP3+ tool but can map hazards within hours instead of months.
Final thought: This is another example of an open-source AI tool developed by Mila, which has been tapped by the federal government to deliver on the open-source section of its federal AI strategy—meaning it’s responsible for building AI models and software that are free to use and build upon. The hub is also negotiating new federal funding for these efforts.
Feature image courtesy Unsplash. Photo by Malachi Brooks.

articles.title: Greece passes under-15 social media ban, and every user may soon have to prove their age
articles.text:
Greece passes under-15 social media ban, and every user may soon have to prove their age
Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok must check users’ ages, with the state-backed Kids Wallet app put forward as a privacy-friendly option
- Greece’s parliament has passed a law banning children under 15 from social media, starting January 1, 2027.
- Platforms must verify users’ ages, and the government is pointing to its Kids Wallet app as the privacy-friendly way to do it.
- Greece follows Australia’s lead, while France’s attempt was struck down and the UK is preparing its own rules.
Greece has passed a law banning children under 15 from social media, making it one of the first European countries to turn a teen social media ban into law.
The restrictions take effect on January 1, 2027, and cover platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok.
Lawmakers approved the bill late on October 22 after a debate lasting more than 16 hours. Only the governing New Democracy party voted in favor, while PASOK abstained and five other opposition parties voted against.
Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis first announced the plan in April, calling it a “difficult but necessary measure,” and blaming social media for rising anxiety, poor sleep, and addictive design.
As with similar laws elsewhere, the job of checking ages falls on the platforms. That has privacy advocates worried, and it’s likely to spark the usual surge of interest in the best VPN apps.
How Greece’s ban will work
The law is short but strict. Parents can’t give their children permission to sign up, and accounts created before January won’t be exempt.
Which services are covered depends on how they work rather than what they’re called, with LinkedIn named alongside the big three. Messaging apps remain available to under-15s.
When a platform can’t confirm a user’s age, it will display a QR code to be scanned with Kids Wallet, a government app.
The app only tells the platform whether the user is over or under 15; it doesn't reveal the age of the individual or any other personal information. “We do not give platforms any of our children’s personal data whatsoever,” said Digital Governance Minister Dimitris Papastergiou.
Greece’s broadcasting council and data protection authority will supervise compliance, with the European Commission handling the largest platforms under the Digital Services Act.
When the plans were announced in May, 25 organizations warned that, in practice, everyone in Greece could have to prove their age, chipping away at online anonymity.
This criticism likely doesn't bother the Greek government, however, since it is also considering plans to end anonymous social media profiles altogether. While online anonymity is important, the situation does change depending on the type of online activity: private or public.
Greece joins a growing list
Australia’s under-16 ban took effect on December 10, 2025, the first of its kind. France passed its own under-15 ban, but its Constitutional Council struck it down in August on freedom of expression grounds.
The UK plans to ban under-16s from social media from spring 2027, though it has ruled out restricting VPNs to enforce it. Slovenia, Spain, and Austria are working on similar measures, and the EU is drafting its own Kids Act, which Greece says it will adapt to.

articles.title: Apple quedó a solo USD 42.000 millones de superar a Nvidia como la empresa más valiosa del mundo
articles.text:
Apple cerró el jueves a un récord de USD 348,22 por acción, lo que llevó su valor bursátil a USD 5,082 billones: apenas USD 42.000 millones menos que los USD 5,124 billones de Nvidia. Una suba de 0,83% bastaría para que la compañía supere a Nvidia y se convierta en la empresa más valiosa del mundo.
La acción de Apple subió 1,23% y llegó a tocar un máximo intradía de USD 348,36. La de Nvidia cayó 4,40%, hasta USD 212,21. Una semana antes, Apple necesitaba una ganancia de 7% para alcanzar a Nvidia; ahora alcanza con 0,83%, equivalente a un precio de USD 351,10 por acción.
El achicamiento de la brecha se dio en medio de una fuerte venta en el sector tecnológico. El Nasdaq Composite cayó 2,60%, su peor jornada desde comienzos de junio, y el índice de semiconductores de Filadelfia perdió 6,7%, su caída más pronunciada desde el 23 de junio.
“Esta es la venta más generalizada que vimos en el rubro de la inteligencia artificial en todo el año”, dijo Michael O’Rourke, de la correduría Jones Trading, sobre el desplome conjunto de los fabricantes de chips y memoria.
El trasfondo de la caída en los chips
El jueves, el director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, dijo que la demanda de las empresas de computación en la nube dedicadas a inteligencia artificial, conocidas como neoclouds, está “fuera de serie”, pero advirtió que “el capital es escaso”.
Huang explicó que esa demanda solo se traduce en pedidos de chips cuando los compradores pueden pagarlos. Si esas empresas no consiguen financiamiento suficiente, las ventas de Nvidia podrían toparse con un techo, aunque el interés por sus productos siga siendo alto.
Apple se mantuvo al margen de la carrera por la IA
Apple ganó 1,82% en la última semana y acumula una suba de 28,44% en lo que va del año. Nvidia, en cambio, cayó 2,31% en la semana y 7,28% en el mes, aunque todavía suma 14,05% de alza en 2026.
Jay Woods, de Freedom Capital Markets, señaló que la postura cautelosa de Apple frente al gasto en inteligencia artificial terminó jugando a su favor. “Antes criticada por no invertir más en IA, logró evitar algunos de los riesgos de ese gasto”, dijo.
Woods habló el 27 de julio, el día en que Apple superó por última vez a Nvidia en valor bursátil, con unos USD 4,94 billones contra USD 4,75 billones de la fabricante de chips.
El lanzamiento del iPhone Duo, el primer plegable de Apple, también sostuvo el ánimo de los inversores. El dispositivo, que arranca en USD 1.999, se agotó en minutos y la mayoría de los pedidos online muestra ahora entregas recién para el 25 de enero, lo que podría correr parte de los ingresos hacia el trimestre siguiente.
Alphabet, con USD 3,965 billones, y Microsoft, con USD 3,869 billones, quedaron lejos de la disputa por el primer puesto. Amazon, con USD 2,701 billones, también está fuera de la pelea, que por ahora es cosa de dos compañías.
Los balances de noviembre pueden definir todo
Apple presentará su balance del cuarto trimestre fiscal el 2 de noviembre, la primera presentación de resultados a cargo del director ejecutivo John Ternus. En julio, la compañía había anticipado un crecimiento de ingresos de entre 9% y 11% y advirtió que la oferta de sus productos se volvería más ajustada.
La acción cotiza a 45 veces sus ganancias después de tocar un récord histórico. Un balance débil probablemente pondría fin a la persecución a Nvidia.
Nvidia reportará resultados alrededor del 18 de noviembre, después de que sus ingresos crecieran 105,8% en el último trimestre. La fabricante de chips cotiza a 43 veces ganancias, una cifra menor que la de Apple pese a crecer mucho más rápido. Si las ventas en el sector de inteligencia artificial se calman, Nvidia podría volver a ampliar la distancia frente a Apple.

articles.title: The European startups defending Ukraine in 2026, and the VCs funding them | EU-Startups
articles.text:
As Ukraine continues to defend itself against Russia’s invasion, European startups are developing technologies ranging from autonomous drones and air-defence systems to satellite intelligence, with venture capital playing an increasingly important role in supporting defence innovation.
EU-Startups’ reporting on European DefenceTech and adjacent dual-use technologies has identified more than €1.8 billion in financing across 22 European startups in 2026, as of October.
Drawing on EU-Startups’ coverage, we’ve put together a list of European startups that secured funding in 2026 and are contributing to Ukraine’s defence efforts, alongside the investors backing them. Together, this list represents over €1 billion of funds raised for direct intervention in Ukraine.
And stay tuned: we have an upcoming EU-Startups Podcast episode featuring one of the startups on this list!
The Defenders
DOD Solution – Estonia/Ukraine: Founded in 2023, DOD Solution is an Estonian-Ukrainian DefenceTech startup developing AI-powered autonomy for unmanned systems. Its AURA AI platform combines onboard computing and software to provide autonomous navigation, target recognition and tracking, even when GPS signals or communications are unavailable. Unlike technologies still awaiting frontline validation, AURA AI has already been used in combat in Ukraine.
In September 2026, the company raised €1.8 million in pre-Seed funding from Angel One Fund, Better Angle, Defence Builder Fund, Network VC, Newfund, UAID Fund, WildField Ventures and 4C-Next Holding AG, alongside strategic investor Draganfly. The financing will support product development and further integrations with Ukrainian drone manufacturers.
Frankenburg Technologies – Estonia: Founded in 2024 and headquartered in Tallinn, Frankenburg Technologies develops affordable, mass-manufacturable missile defence systems intended to counter drones and other aerial threats. Co-founded by Taavi Madiberk and Marko Virkebau, the startup is developing its Mark I short-range interceptor missile, with an emphasis on reducing production costs and increasing manufacturing capacity. Its operations extend across eight countries, including Ukraine, reflecting its ambition to manufacture defensive systems closer to where they are needed.
In February 2026, Frankenburg secured €30 million in Series A funding led by Plural, with participation from SmartCap, bringing its reported total funding to €40 million.
ICEYE – Finland: Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Espoo, ICEYE develops and operates synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites capable of capturing high-resolution imagery regardless of weather conditions or daylight. Its technology supports defence intelligence and battlefield monitoring, including for Ukraine’s armed forces, which benefit from satellite imagery to improve situational awareness.
In January 2026, ICEYE expanded its cooperation with Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence to provide additional space-based intelligence. In June, the company announced a €450 million primary Series F investment led by General Atlantic, with investors including Solidium, Tesi, Varma, Ilmarinen, Lifeline Ventures, Nokia, QIA and TCV. The Scaleup Europe Fund, managed by EQT, was subsequently identified as a co-lead. Including secondary transactions, the financing exceeded €1 billion.
Occam Industries – United Kingdom: Founded in 2025 and based in London, Occam Industries develops autonomous drone technology designed to reduce reliance on human pilots in battlefield conditions. Its OccamX platform uses computer vision to enable FPV drones to navigate and track targets without continuous manual control or GPS connectivity. Occam has also completed initial testing through Ukraine’s Brave1 defence innovation cluster, opening the door to integration trials with Ukrainian drone manufacturers and potential deployment with the country’s armed forces.
In February 2026, the startup raised €3 million in pre-Seed funding led by Presto Tech Horizons, with participation from Antler, Freedom Fund, TYR.vc and defence-sector angel investors.
PDKINEMATICS – Lithuania: Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Vilnius, PDKINEMATICS develops precision-guidance systems for unmanned aerial vehicles, helping drones operate more accurately in environments affected by electronic warfare. Its flagship Gannet technology enables UAVs to release munitions from higher altitudes without sacrificing accuracy. The startup has partnered with Ukrainian drone manufacturer Bavovna.ai, integrating its systems into platforms already deployed in battlefield conditions.
In June 2026, PDKINEMATICS secured €2 million in Seed funding co-led by Coinvest Capital and Iron Wolf Capital, bringing its total funding to €3 million. The investment will support increased manufacturing capacity and further deployments across Ukraine and European defence markets.
Quantum Systems – Germany: Founded in 2015 and based near Munich, Quantum Systems develops AI-powered unmanned aerial systems and software for military reconnaissance and autonomous operations. The company has an established presence in Ukraine, where its drones reportedly completed more than 19,000 missions during 2025.
In July 2026, it announced a €1 billion Series D round co-led by Blackstone, Noteus, Airbus and Advent, with backing from BOND, Fidelity, Wellington Management, A.P. Moller Holding, Elephant Lake Ventures, Balderton and HV Capital. Its Ukrainian operations are also expanding: in October 2026, EU-Startups reported plans for tens of thousands of Germany-funded interceptor drones to be manufactured in Ukraine.
Shotling – Denmark: Danish DefenceTech startup Shotling develops short-range counter-drone systems designed to protect military personnel, vehicles and infrastructure against FPV drones and loitering munitions. Its electrically driven rotary shotgun system uses a high-capacity magazine and is designed for integration into mobile or stationary defence platforms. The technology addresses a challenge encountered by Ukrainian forces: intercepting inexpensive attack drones without relying on disproportionately costly defensive systems.
In February 2026, Shotling announced €700k in pre-Seed financing led by Myriad Defense Fund, with participation from IPO CLUB’s Fund II America 2030 and a non-dilutive match-loan from EIFO. The startup has reportedly received support from Ukrainian frontline units and defence companies, although operational deployment details have not been disclosed.
Special Mention
Varangians – Sweden: Beyond the startups developing defence technologies, Stockholm-based Varangians represents a more direct route for European venture capital into Ukraine’s DefenceTech ecosystem. Co-founded by Pär Lager, Andreas Flodström and Jonas Rydin alongside a Swedish family office, the investment fund announced a close of more than €10 million in June 2026, specifically to support Ukrainian defence innovation.
Its portfolio includes Norda Dynamics, which develops autonomous drone piloting technology for communications-denied environments; Himera, specialising in electronic-warfare-resistant secure communications; and Sine Engineering, which builds UAV communication and positioning systems capable of operating under jamming and interference.
